children.translated_text:
<s>Nyāyadarśana</s> (The System of Logic)
<s>Vātsyāyana</s>'s Commentary (<s>Bhāṣya</s>)
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.1]

Since from a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) there arises the apprehension of an object, and from that apprehension arises the capacity for purposeful activity — therefore <s>pramāṇa</s> is meaningful (i.e., has real purpose).

children.text:
% p.21
pramāṇam antareṇa nārthapratipattiḥ, nārhtapratipattim antareṇa pravṛttisāmarthyam/ pramāṇena khalv ayaṃ jñātārtham abhīpsati jihāsati vā/ tasyepsājihāsāprayuktasya samīhā pravṛttir ity ucyate/ sāmrthyaṃ punar asyāḥ phalenābhisambandhaḥ/ samīhamānas tam artham abhīpsan jihāsan vā tam artham āpnoti jahāti vā/ arthas tu sukhaṃ sukhahetuś ca, duḥkhaṃ duḥkhahetuś ca/
children.translated_text: Without a <s>pramāṇa</s> there is no apprehension of an object; without the apprehension of an object there is no capacity for purposeful activity. For indeed, having known an object through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, one either desires it or wishes to avoid it. The endeavor of one who is impelled by desire or aversion is called <s>pravṛtti</s> (purposeful activity). And the capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) of this (activity) is its connection with a result. One who endeavors — desiring or wishing to avoid that object — either obtains or abandons that object. And the object is either pleasure or the cause of pleasure, or pain or the cause of pain.

children.text:
% p.22
so 'yaṃ pramāṇārtho 'parisaṅkhyeyaḥ, prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṅkhyeyatvāt/ arthavati ca pramāṇe pramātā prameyaṃ pramitir ity arthavanti bhavanti/ kasmāt? anyatamāpāye 'rthasyānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: This purpose of <s>pramāṇa</s> is innumerable, because the variety of living beings is innumerable. And when <s>pramāṇa</s> is meaningful, then the knower (<s>pramātā</s>), the knowable (<s>prameya</s>), and the resultant cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) also become meaningful. Why? Because if any one of these is absent, the (valid knowledge of the) object would not be established.

children.text:
% p.24
tatra yasyepsājihāsāprayuktasya pravṛttiḥ sa pramātā, sa yenārthaṃ pramiṇoti tat pramāṇam, yo 'rthaḥ pramīyate tat prameyam, yad arthavijñānaṃ sā pramitiḥ, catasṛṣu caivaṃvidhāsv arthatattvaṃ parisamāpyate/
kiṃ punas tattvam? sataś ca sadbhāvo 'sataśüEcāsadbhāvaḥ/ sat sad iti gṛhyamāṇaṃ yathābhūtam aviparītaṃ tattvaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text:
Among these, the one who, impelled by desire or aversion, engages in activity — that is the knower (<s>pramātā</s>); that by means of which he cognizes the object — that is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge); the object that is cognized — that is the <s>prameya</s> (knowable); the cognition of the object — that is <s>pramiti</s> (resultant knowledge). And in these four, the truth of the object is fully encompassed.
What then is truth (<s>tattva</s>)? The real existence of what exists and the non-existence of what does not exist. When what exists is apprehended as existing — that is truth, as it really is, without error.

children.text:
% yathābhūtam aviparītaṃ tattvaṃ bhavati/] p.25
asac cāsad iti gṛhyamāṇaṃ yathābhūtam aviparītaṃ tattvaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: And when what does not exist is apprehended as not existing — that too is truth, as it really is, without error.

children.text:
% p.26
katham uttarasya pramāṇenopalabdhir iti? saty upalabhyamāne tadanupalabdheḥ pradīpavat/ yathā darśakena dīpena dṛśye gṛhyamāṇe tad iva yan na gṛhyate, tan nāsti/ yady abhaviṣyad idam iva vyajñāsyata, vijñānābhāvān nāstīti/ evaṃ pramāṇena sati gṛhyamāṇe tad iva yan na gṛhyate,
children.translated_text: How is the latter (non-existence) apprehended by a <s>pramāṇa</s>? When something existent is being perceived, that which is not perceived (alongside it) is (known to be) non-existent — like a lamp. Just as when a visible object is being perceived by an illuminating lamp, that which is not perceived in the same way does not exist. If it had existed, it would have been cognized just like this (visible object); since there is no cognition (of it), it does not exist. Similarly, when something existent is being perceived by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that which is not perceived in the same way,

children.text:
% p.27
tan nāsti/ yady abhaviṣyad idam iva vyajñāsyata, vijñānābhāvān nāstīti/ tad evaṃ sataḥ prakāśakaṃ pramāṇam asad api prakāśayatīti/
children.translated_text: that does not exist. If it had existed, it would have been cognized just like this (perceived object); since there is no cognition (of it), it does not exist. Thus, a <s>pramāṇa</s> that illuminates what exists also illuminates what does not exist.

children.text:
% p.28
sac ca khalu ṣoḍaśadhā vyūḍham upadekṣyate/ tāsāṃ khalv āsāṃ sadvidhānām---
children.translated_text: And indeed, the existent, arranged in sixteen categories, will be taught. Of these categories of the existent —

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.1: From the true knowledge of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), <s>avayava</s> (members of a syllogism), <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning), <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment), <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reasons), <s>chala</s> (quibbling), <s>jāti</s> (futile objections), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) — there arises the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).

children.text:
% p.29
nirdeśe yathāvacanaṃ vigrahaḥ/ cārthe dvandvasamāsaḥ/ pramāṇādīnāṃ tattvam iti śaiṣikī ṣaṣṭhī/
children.translated_text: In the enumeration, the analysis is according to the words (as stated). The <s>dvandva</s> compound is in the sense of 'and.' 'Of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest, the truth' — here the sixth case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) is in the possessive (<s>śaiṣikī</s>) sense.

children.text:
% p.31
tattvasya jñānaṃ niḥśreyasasyādhigama iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhau/ ta etāvanto vidyamānārthāḥ, yeṣām aviparītajñānārtham ihopadeśaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Knowledge of truth' and 'attainment of the highest good' — in both these (expressions), the sixth case is in the objective (<s>karmaṇi</s>) sense. These are the actually existing categories, for whose correct understanding the instruction is given here.

children.text:
% vidyamānārthā, ...] p/32
so 'yam anavayavena tantrārtha uddiṣṭo veditavyaḥ/ ātmādeḥ khalu prameyasya tattvajñānān niḥśreyasādhigamaḥ/
children.translated_text: This entire subject-matter of the treatise, stated without division into parts, should be understood. Indeed, from the true knowledge of <s>prameya</s> (the knowable) beginning with the <s>ātman</s> (self), the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) follows.

children.text:
% p.33
tac caitad uttarasūtreṇānūdyata iti/ heyam, tasya nirvartakaṃ hānam ātyantikam, tasyopāyo 'dhigantavya ity etāni catvāry arthapadāni samyag buddhvā niḥśreyasam adhigacchati/
children.translated_text: And this is reiterated in the next <s>sūtra</s>. What is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>), its complete cessation (<s>hāna</s>) as the means of elimination, the absolute (cessation), and the means to attain it (<s>adhigantavya</s>) — having properly understood these four objects of inquiry, one attains the highest good.

children.text:
% p.34
tatra saṃśayādīnāṃ pṛthagvacanam anarthakam --- saṃśayādayo yathāsambhavaṃ pramāṇeṣu prameyeṣu cāntarbhavanto na vyatiricyanta iti? satyam etat, imās tu catasro vidyāḥ pṛthakprasthānāḥ prāṇabhṛtām anugrahāyopadiśyante, yāsāṃ caturthīyam ānvīkṣikī nyāyavidyā/
children.translated_text: Here, the separate mention of <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) and the rest is purposeless — since doubt and the others, as the case may be, are included within the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) and <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) and do not stand apart? True, this is so. But these four sciences, having separate domains, are taught for the benefit of living beings, and this science of logic (<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>) — the <s>Nyāya</s> science — is the fourth among them.

children.text:
% -prasthānāḥ prāṇabhṛtām ... ] p.35
tasyāḥ pṛthakprasthānāḥ saṃśayādayaḥ padārthāḥ/ teṣāṃ pṛthagvacanam antareṇādhyātmavidyāmātram iyaṃ syāt, yathopaniṣadaḥ/ tasmāt saṃśayādibhiḥ padārthaiḥ pṛthak prasthāpyate/ tatra nānupalabdhe na nirṇīte 'rthe nyāyaḥ pravartate, kiṃ tarhi? saṃśayite 'rthe/ yathoktaṃ --- ``vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ'' iti/ vimarśaḥ --- saṃśayaḥ/ pakṣapratipakṣau --- nyāyapravṛttiḥ/ arthāvadhāraṇaṃ --- nirṇayas tattvajñānam iti/ sa ca ``ayaṃ kiṃsvid'' iti vastuvimarśamātram anavadhāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ, prameye 'ntarbhavann evam arthaṃ pṛthag ucyate/
children.translated_text: Its separate domains are the categories beginning with <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt). Without their separate mention, this (science) would be merely the science of the inner self (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), like the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. Therefore, it is distinguished separately by the categories beginning with doubt. Among these, the method of <s>Nyāya</s> (logical reasoning) does not operate with respect to an object that is unperceived, nor with one that is already ascertained — but rather with respect to an object that is in doubt. As has been stated: 'The ascertainment of an object after deliberation from thesis and counter-thesis is <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination).' Deliberation is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>). Thesis and counter-thesis constitute the operation of <s>Nyāya</s>. Ascertainment of the object is <s>nirṇaya</s> — that is, true knowledge (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). And that (doubt) — being merely the deliberation 'What is this?' — is an indeterminate cognition, a mere questioning about a thing; though included within <s>prameya</s>, it is mentioned separately for this purpose.

children.text:
% p.37
atha prayojanam --- yena prayuktaḥ pravartate, tat prayojanam/ yam artham abhīpsan jihāsan vā karmārabhate,
children.translated_text: Now, <s>prayojana</s> (purpose): that by which one is impelled to act — that is <s>prayojana</s>. The object which one undertakes action to obtain or avoid —

children.text:
% karmārabhate] p.38
tenānena sarve prāṇinaḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi sarvāś ca vidyā vyāptāḥ, tadāśrayaś ca nyāyaḥ pravartate/ kaḥ punar ayaṃ nyāyaḥ? pramāṇair arthaparīkṣaṇaṃ nyāyaḥ/
children.translated_text: by this, all living beings, all actions, and all sciences are pervaded; and <s>Nyāya</s> (logical method), which depends on that (purpose), operates. But what is this <s>Nyāya</s>? The examination of objects by means of <s>pramāṇas</s> is <s>Nyāya</s>.

children.text:
% p.39
pratyakṣāgamāśritam anumānam, sānvīkṣā/ pratyakṣāgamābhyām īkṣitasyānvīkṣaṇam anvīkṣā/ tayā pravarttata ity ānvīkṣikī --- nyāyavidyā --- nyāyaśāstram/ yat punar anumānaṃ pratyakṣāgamaviruddhaṃ nyāyābhāsaḥ sa iti/
children.translated_text: Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) that is based on perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>) constitutes <s>ānvīkṣā</s> (critical examination). The re-examination (<s>anvīkṣaṇa</s>) of what has been examined through perception and scripture is <s>anvīkṣā</s>. That which proceeds by means of this is <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> — the <s>Nyāya</s> science — the <s>Nyāya</s> treatise. And that inference which contradicts perception and scripture is a semblance of <s>Nyāya</s> (<s>nyāyābhāsa</s>).

children.text:
% p.44
tatra vādajalpau saprayojanau/ vitaṇḍā tu parīkṣyate/ vitaṇḍayā pravartamāno vaitaṇḍikaḥ/ sa prayojanam anuyukto yadi pratipadyate so 'sya pakṣaḥ so 'sya siddhānta iti, vaitaṇḍikatvaṃ jahāti/ atha na pratipadyate nāyaṃ laukiko na parīkṣaka ity āpadyate/ athāpi parapakṣapratiṣedhajñāpanaṃ prayojanaṃ bravīti, etad api tādṛg eva/ yo jñāpayati yo jānāti yena jñāpyate yac ca jñāpyate etac ca pratipadyate yadi, tadā vaitaṇḍikatvaṃ jahāti/ atha na pratipadyate, parapakṣapratiṣedhajñāpanaṃ prayojanam ity etad asya vākyam anarthakaṃ bhavati/ vākyasamūhaś ca sthāpanāhīno vitaṇḍā, tasya yady abhidheyaṃ pratipadyate, so 'sya pakṣaḥ sthāpanīyo bhavati/ atha na pratipadyate, pralāpamātram anarthakaṃ bhavati, vitaṇḍātvaṃ nivartata iti/
atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratyakṣaviṣayo 'rthaḥ, yatra laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ darśanaṃ na vyāhanyate/
children.translated_text:
Among these, <s>vāda</s> (debate) and <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) have purpose. But <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) is to be examined. One who engages in <s>vitaṇḍā</s> is called a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s> (caviler). If, when asked about his purpose, he acknowledges 'this is my thesis, this is my established doctrine,' then he abandons the status of a caviler. But if he does not acknowledge this, then he falls into the position of being neither a worldly person nor a critical examiner. And even if he says 'the purpose is to make known the refutation of the opponent's thesis,' that too is the same. He who makes known, he who knows, that by which it is made known, and that which is made known — if he accepts these, then he abandons the status of a caviler. But if he does not accept, then his statement 'the purpose is to make known the refutation of the opponent's thesis' becomes meaningless. And a collection of statements lacking a thesis (<s>sthāpanā</s>) is <s>vitaṇḍā</s>; if he accepts the meaning of that (collection), then his thesis becomes something to be established. But if he does not accept, it becomes mere prattle, meaningless, and the nature of <s>vitaṇḍā</s> ceases.
Now, <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example): an object that is the domain of perception, regarding which the understanding of ordinary people and critical examiners is not contradicted.

children.text:
% p.45
sa ca prameyam/ tasya pṛthagvacanaṃ ca tadāśrayāv anumānāgamau, tasmin sati syātām anumānāgamau asati ca na syātām/ tadāśrayā ca nyāyapravṛttiḥ/ dṛṣṭāntavirodhena ca parapakṣapratiṣedho vacanīyo bhavati, dṛṣṭāntasamādhinā ca svapakṣaḥ sādhanīyo bhavati/ nāstikaś ca dṛṣṭāntam abhyupagacchann āstikatvaṃ jahāti/ anabhyupagacchan kiṃsādhanaḥ param upālabheteti/ niruktena ca dṛṣṭāntena śakyam abhidhātuṃ ``sādhyasādharmyāt taddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam'' ``tadviparyayād viparītam'' iti/
children.translated_text: And that (example) is a <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge). Its separate mention (is justified because): inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>) depend on it — when it exists, inference and scripture would be valid; when it does not exist, they would not. And the operation of <s>Nyāya</s> depends on it. The refutation of an opponent's thesis must be stated through contradiction with the example, and one's own thesis must be established through concordance with the example. And a skeptic (<s>nāstika</s>) who accepts the example abandons his skepticism. (For) without accepting it, on what basis would he criticize others? And with a properly defined example, it is possible to state: 'An example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is that which, by virtue of possessing the same properties as what is to be proved, implies the possession of those properties (in the subject)' and 'the opposite, by virtue of the opposite (properties).'

children.text:
% p.46
asty ayam ity anujñāyamāno 'rthaḥ siddhāntaḥ/ sa ca prameyam/ tasya pṛthagvacanaṃ satsu siddhāntabhedeṣu vādajalpavitaṇḍāḥ pravartante, nāto 'nyatheti/
children.translated_text: An object that is acknowledged as 'this exists' is a <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine). And that too is a <s>prameya</s>. Its separate mention (is justified because): when the distinctions of <s>siddhānta</s> exist, <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) operate — and not otherwise.

children.text:
% p.47
sādhanīyārthasya yāvati śabdasamūhe siddhiḥ parisamāpyate tasya pañcāvayavāḥ pratijñādayaḥ, samūham apekṣyāvayavā ucyante/
children.translated_text: The five members (<s>avayavas</s>) beginning with the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) are the collection of words in which the establishment of the object to be proved is fully accomplished. They are called members with reference to the collection (as a whole).

children.text:
% p.48
teṣu pramāṇasamavāyaḥ, āgamaḥ pratijñā/ hetur anumānam/
children.translated_text: Among these, that which involves the coordination of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge): scripture (<s>āgama</s>) corresponds to the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>). The reason (<s>hetu</s>) corresponds to inference (<s>anumāna</s>).
The example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) corresponds to perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). The application (<s>upanaya</s>) corresponds to comparison (<s>upamāna</s>).

children.text:
% p.52
sarveṣām ekārthasamavāye sāmarthyapradarśanaṃ nigamanam iti/ so 'yaṃ paramo nyāya iti/ etena vādajalpavitaṇḍāḥ pravartante nāto 'nyatheti/
children.translated_text: The demonstration of the capacity (of all these) when coordinated toward a single purpose is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>). This is the supreme method of <s>Nyāya</s>. Through this, <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) operate — and not otherwise.

children.text:
% p.53
tadāśrayā ca tattvavyavasthā/ te caite 'vayavāḥ śabdaviśeṣāḥ santaḥ prameye 'ntarbhūtā evamarthaṃ pṛthag ucyanta iti/
tarko na pramāṇasaṃgṛhīto, na pramāṇāntaram, pramāṇānām anugrāhakas tattvajñānāya kalpate/ tasyodāharaṇam --- kim idaṃ janma kṛtakena hetunā nirvartyate, āhosvid akṛtakena, athākasmikam iti?
children.translated_text:
And the determination of truth depends on this. And these members, being specific words, though included within <s>prameya</s>, are mentioned separately for this purpose.
<s>Tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is not included within the <s>pramāṇas</s>, nor is it a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>; it serves as an aid to the <s>pramāṇas</s> and is conducive to true knowledge. An illustration of this: Is this birth produced by a created cause, or by an uncreated cause, or is it causeless?

children.text:
% -ākasmikam iti?] p.54
evam avijñāte 'rthe kāraṇopapattyā ūhaḥ pravarttate --- yadi kṛtakena hetunā nirvartyate, hetūcchedād upapanno 'yaṃ janmocchedaḥ/ athākṛtakena hetunā, tato hetūcchedasyāśakyatvād anupapanno janmocchedaḥ/ athākasmikam, ato 'kasmān nirvartyamānaṃ na punar nivartsyatīti nivṛttikāraṇaṃ nopapadyate, tena janmānuccheda iti/ etasmiṃs tarkaviṣaye karmanimittaṃ janmeti pramāṇāni pravarttamānāni tarkeṇānugṛhante,
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding an unknown object, reasoning (<s>ūha</s>) proceeds through the fitness of causes: If (birth) is produced by a created cause, then through the cessation of the cause, the cessation of birth is established. But if by an uncreated cause, then since the cessation of (such) a cause is impossible, the cessation of birth is not established. And if it is causeless, then since what is produced without cause will not cease again, a cause of cessation is not established — hence there would be no cessation of birth. In this domain of <s>tarka</s>, (the doctrine that) birth is caused by <s>karma</s> — the <s>pramāṇas</s> operating (to establish this) are aided by <s>tarka</s>,

children.text:
% p.55
tattvajñānaviṣayasya vibhāgāt tattvajñānāya kalpate tarka iti/ so 'yam itthambhūtas tarkaḥ pramāṇasahito vāde sādhanāyopālambhāya cārthasya bhavatīty evam arthaṃ pṛghag ucyate prameyāntarbhūto 'pīti/
children.translated_text: and since it distinguishes the domain of true knowledge, <s>tarka</s> is conducive to true knowledge. This <s>tarka</s>, being of such a nature, when combined with <s>pramāṇas</s> in debate serves both for the establishment and the criticism of a position — hence it is mentioned separately, even though included within <s>prameya</s>.

children.text:
% p.56
nirṇayas tattvajñānaṃ pramāṇānāṃ phalam, tadavasāno vādaḥ, tasya pālanārthaṃ jalpaviṭaṇḍe/ tāv etau tarkanirṇayau lokayātrāṃ vahata iti/ so 'yaṃ nirṇayaḥ prameyāntarbhūta evamarthaṃ pṛthag uddīṣṭa iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment) is true knowledge (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), the fruit of the <s>pramāṇas</s>; debate (<s>vāda</s>) culminates in it; and <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) serve to protect it. These two — <s>tarka</s> and <s>nirṇaya</s> — sustain the conduct of worldly life. This <s>nirṇaya</s>, though included within <s>prameya</s>, is mentioned separately for this purpose.

children.text:
% p.57
vādaḥ khalu nānāpravaktṛkaḥ pratyadhikaraṇasādhano 'nyatarādhikaraṇanirṇayāvasāno vākyasamūhaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Vāda</s> (debate) is indeed a collection of statements made by different proponents, each establishing (something) with respect to a given subject, and culminating in the ascertainment of one side or the other.

children.text:
% vākyasamūhaḥ/] p.58
pṛthag uddiṣṭa upalakṣaṇārtham/ upalakṣitena vyavahāras tattvajñānāya bhavatīti/ ``tadviśeṣau jalpavitaṇḍe tattvādhyavasāyasaṃrakṣaṇārtham'' ity uktam/
children.translated_text: It is mentioned separately for the purpose of characterization. Through what is thus characterized, the practice (of reasoning) serves the purpose of true knowledge. As stated: '<s>Jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> are its (vāda's) two variants, for the purpose of protecting the conviction arrived at through true knowledge.'

children.text:
% p.59
nigrahasthānebhyaḥ pṛthag uddhiṣṭā hetvābhāsā vāde codanīyā bhaviṣyantīti/
children.translated_text: <s>Hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons), mentioned separately from <s>nigrahasthānas</s> (points of defeat), are to be challenged in (legitimate) debate.
But in <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s>, the <s>nigrahasthānas</s> (points of defeat) (apply).

children.text:
% p.63
chalajātinigrahasthānānāṃ pṛthagupadeśa upalakṣaṇārtham iti/ upalakṣitānāṃ svavākye parivarjanam, chalajātinigrahasthānānāṃ paravākye paryanuyogaḥ/ jāteś ca pareṇa prayujyamānāyāḥ sulabhaḥ samādhiḥ, svayaṃ ca sukaraḥ prayoga iti/
children.translated_text: The separate instruction of <s>chala</s> (quibbling), <s>jāti</s> (futile objections), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) is for the purpose of characterization. The avoidance of the characterized (fallacies) in one's own speech, and the censure of <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> in the opponent's speech. And when a <s>jāti</s> (futile objection) is employed by an opponent, its resolution is easy; and its own employment (by oneself) is also easily accomplished.

children.text:
% p.64
seyam ānvīkṣikī pramāṇādibhiḥ padārthair vibhajyamānā ---
pradīpaḥ sarvavidyānām upāyaḥ sarvakarmaṇām/
āśrayaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ vidyoddeśe prakīrtitā//
children.translated_text:
This <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (science of critical inquiry), being divided into categories beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s> —
is proclaimed in the exposition of knowledge as a lamp for all sciences, a means for all actions, and a foundation for all <s>dharmas</s> (duties).

children.text:
% p.65
tad idaṃ tattvajñānaṃ niḥśreyasādhigamārthaṃ yathāvidyaṃ veditavyam/ iha tv adhyātmavidyāyām ātmādijñānaṃ tattvajñānam/ niḥśreyasādhigamo 'pavargaprāptiḥ//1//
children.translated_text: This true knowledge (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) is to be understood as taught, for the purpose of attaining the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). And here, in the science of the inner self (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), true knowledge is the knowledge of the <s>ātman</s> (self) and the rest. The attainment of the highest good is the attainment of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). // 1 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.2]

children.text:
% p.67
tat khalu niḥśreyasaṃ kiṃ tattvajñānāntaram eva bhavati? nety ucyate/ kiṃ tarhi? tattvajñānāt ---
children.translated_text: Does that highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) arise immediately upon true knowledge? No, it is said. What then? From true knowledge —
[Page break]

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.2: Through the successive cessation of pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), birth (<s>janma</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), defect (<s>doṣa</s>), and false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) — each one ceasing upon the cessation of the one immediately following it — there is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).
Among these, regarding the objects of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>) ranging from the self (<s>ātman</s>) to liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) of many kinds prevails.

children.text:
% p.71
ātmani tāvan nāstīti, anātmani ātmeti duḥkhe sukham iti anitye nityam ity atrāṇe trāṇam iti,
children.translated_text: Regarding the self (<s>ātman</s>), first: 'it does not exist'; regarding what is not the self: 'this is the self'; regarding suffering: 'this is pleasure'; regarding what is impermanent: 'this is permanent'; regarding what offers no protection: 'this provides protection';

children.text:
% atrāṇe trāṇam iti] p.76
sabhaye nirbhayam iti, jugupsite 'bhimatam iti, hātavye apratihātavyam iti, pravṛttau nāsti karma, nāsti karmaphalam iti, doṣeṣu nāyaṃ doṣanimittaḥ saṃsāra iti, pretyabhāve nāsti jantur jīvo vā sattva ātmā vā, yaḥ preyāt, pretya ca bhaved iti, animittaṃ janma, animitto janmoparama ity ādimān pretyabhāvaḥ, anantaś ceti, naimittikaḥ sann akarmanimittaḥ pretyabhāva iti, dehendriyabuddhivedanāsantānocchedapratisandhānābhyāṃ nirātmakaḥ pretyabhāva iti/ apavarge bhīṣmaḥ khalv ayaṃ sarvakāyoparamaḥ, sarvaviprayoge 'pavarge bahu ca bhadrakaṃ lupyata iti kathaṃ buddhimān sarvasukhocchedam acaitanyam amum apavargaṃ rocayed iti/
etasmān mithyājñānād anukūleṣu rāgaḥ, pratikūleṣu dveṣaḥ/ rāgadveṣādhikārāc cāsatyerṣyamāyālobhādayo doṣā bhavanti/ doṣaiḥ prayuktaḥ śarīreṇa pravarttamāno hiṃsāsteyapratiṣiddhamaithunāny ācarati, vācānṛtaparuṣasūcanāsambaddhāni, manasā paradrohaṃ paradravyābhīpsāṃ nāstikyaṃ ceti/ seyaṃ pāpātmikā pravṛttir adharmāya/
atha śubhā --- śarīreṇa dānaṃ paritrāṇaṃ paricaraṇaṃ ca, vācā satyaṃ hitaṃ priyaṃ svādhyāyaṃ ceti, manasā dayām aspṛhāṃ śraddhāṃ ceti/ seyaṃ dharmāya/
atra pravṛttisādhanau dharmādharmau pravṛttiśabdenoktau, yathānnasādhanāḥ prāṇāḥ ``annaṃ vai prāṇinaḥ prāṇā''iti/
children.translated_text:
regarding what offers no protection: 'this provides protection'; regarding what is fearful: 'this is free from fear'; regarding what is disgusting: 'this is desirable'; regarding what should be abandoned: 'this should not be given up'; regarding action: 'action does not exist, the fruit of action does not exist'; regarding faults (<s>doṣa</s>): 'this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth) is not caused by faults'; regarding the after-death state (<s>pretyabhāva</s>): 'there is no living being, no <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), no <s>sattva</s> (sentient being), no <s>ātman</s> (self) that transmigrates and, having transmigrated, comes into existence again'; 'birth is without cause, the cessation of birth is without cause' — such is the beginning of the after-death state, 'and it is endless'; 'though the after-death state is caused, it is not caused by action (<s>karma</s>)'; 'the after-death state is without a self, operating through the continuity and interruption of body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensations.' Regarding liberation (<s>apavarga</s>): 'truly frightful is this cessation of the entire body; in liberation, with the disconnection from everything, much that is good is also destroyed — how could an intelligent person relish this liberation that is the destruction of all pleasure and devoid of consciousness?'
From this false knowledge arises attachment (<s>rāga</s>) toward what is agreeable, and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) toward what is disagreeable. And from the dominion of attachment and aversion arise faults such as envy, deceit, greed, and the like. Impelled by these faults, one engages through the body in violence, theft, and prohibited sexual intercourse; through speech in falsehood, harshness, calumny, and incoherent talk; and through the mind in malice toward others, coveting others' property, and nihilism — this is the sinful activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), leading to <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
Now the meritorious (activity): through the body — giving, rescue, and service; through speech — truth, what is beneficial, what is pleasant, and self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>); through the mind — compassion, non-covetousness, and faith. This leads to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness).
Here, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, being the means of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), are denoted by the word '<s>pravṛtti</s>' — just as the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>), being the means of food, (are called by the name of what they sustain): 'food indeed is the life-breath of living beings.'

children.text:
% p.77
seyaṃ pravṛttiḥ kutsitasyābhipūjitasya ca janmanaḥ kāraṇam/ janma punaḥ śarīrendriyabuddhīnāṃ nikāyaviśiṣṭaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ, tasmin sati duḥkham/ tat punaḥ pratikūlavedanīyaṃ bādhanā pīḍā tāpa iti/ ta ime mithyājñānādayo duḥkhāntā dharmā avicchedenaiva pravartamānāḥ saṃsāra iti/
children.translated_text: This activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is the cause of birth — both despicable and honored. Birth, moreover, is the manifestation of body, sense-organs, and intellect in a specific bodily form (<s>nikāya</s>); when that occurs, there is suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). That suffering is adverse sensation — affliction, torment, anguish. These properties, beginning with false knowledge and ending with suffering, proceeding in an unbroken sequence, constitute <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of transmigration).

children.text:
% p.78
yadā tu tattvajñānān mithyājñānam apaiti, tadā mithyājñānāpāye doṣā apayanti, doṣāpāye pravṛttir apaiti,
children.translated_text: But when, through the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), false knowledge is removed, then upon the removal of false knowledge, the faults are removed; upon the removal of faults, activity ceases;

children.text:
% pravṛttir apaiti,] p.80
pravṛttyapāye janmāpaiti, janmāpāye duḥkham apaiti, duḥkhāpāye ca ātyantiko 'pavargo niḥśreyasam iti/
children.translated_text: upon the cessation of activity, birth ceases; upon the cessation of birth, suffering ceases; and upon the cessation of suffering, there is absolute liberation (<s>ātyantika apavarga</s>) — the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).

children.text:
% p.82
tattvajñānaṃ tu khalu mithyājñānaviparyayeṇa vyākhyātam/ ātmani --- tāvad astīti, anātmani --- anātmeti, evaṃ duḥkhe 'nitye 'trāṇe sabhaye jugupsite hātavye ca yathāviṣayaṃ veditavyam, pravṛttau --- asti karma, asti karmaphalam iti, doṣeṣu --- doṣanimitto 'yaṃ saṃsāra iti, pretyabhāve khalu --- asti jantur jīvaḥ sattva ātmā vā, yaḥ pretya bhaved iti, nimittavaj janma, nimittavān janmoparama ity anādiḥ pretyabhāvo 'pavargānta iti, naimittikaḥ san pretyabhāvaḥ pravṛttinimitta iti, sātmakaḥ san dehendriyabuddhivedanāsantānocchedapratisandhānābhyāṃ pravarttata iti, apavarge śāntaḥ khalv ayaṃ sarvaviprayogaḥ sarvoparamo 'pavargaḥ, bahu ca kṛcchaṃ ghoraṃ pāpakaṃ lupyata iti kathaṃ buddhimān sarvaduḥkhocchedaṃ sarvaduḥkhāsaṃvidam apavargaṃ na rocayed iti,
children.translated_text: The knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) is explained as the reverse of false knowledge. Regarding the self: 'it exists'; regarding what is not the self: 'this is not the self'; likewise regarding suffering, impermanence, non-protection, danger, disgust, and what should be abandoned — each should be understood according to its proper object. Regarding activity: 'action exists, the fruit of action exists'; regarding faults: 'this <s>saṃsāra</s> is caused by faults'; regarding the after-death state: 'there exists a living being, a <s>jīva</s>, a <s>sattva</s>, an <s>ātman</s> that transmigrates and comes into existence again'; 'birth has a cause, the cessation of birth has a cause'; 'the after-death state is beginningless and ends with liberation'; 'the after-death state, being caused, is caused by activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>)'; 'possessing a self, it operates through the continuity and interruption of body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensations.' Regarding liberation: 'peaceful indeed is this complete disconnection, this complete cessation — liberation; and much that is wretched, terrible, and sinful is destroyed. How could an intelligent person not relish this liberation that is the destruction of all suffering and the absence of all awareness of suffering?'

children.text:
% -m apavargaṃ na rocayed iti,] p.83
tad yathā madhuviṣasampṛktānnam anādeyam iti, evaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhānuṣaktam anādeyam iti//2//
children.translated_text: Just as food mixed with honey and poison is not to be accepted, so too pleasure conjoined with suffering is not to be accepted. // 2 //

children.text: trividhā cāsya śāstrasya pravṛttiḥ, --- uddeśo lakṣaṇaṃ parīkṣā ceti/ tatra nāmadheyena padārthamātrasyābhidhānam uddśaḥ/
children.translated_text: The engagement with this treatise is threefold: enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>), definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and examination (<s>parīkṣā</s>). Of these, <s>uddeśa</s> is the mere designation of the category (<s>padārtha</s>) by name.

children.text:
% nāmadheyena ... uddeśaḥ/] p.84
tatroddiṣṭasya tattvavyavacchedako dharmao lakṣaṇam/ lakṣitasya yathālakṣaṇam upapadyate na veti pramāṇair avadhāraṇaṃ parīkṣā/ tatroddiṣṭasya pravibhaktasya lakṣaṇam ucyate,
children.translated_text: Of the enumerated (category), the property (<s>dharma</s>) that discriminates its true nature is the <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (definition). The ascertainment by means of the instruments of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) as to whether the defined (category) is established in accordance with its definition or not — that is <s>parīkṣā</s> (examination). Of these, the definition of what has been enumerated and distinguished is stated,

children.text:
% -ddiṣṭasya pravibhaktasya lakṣaṇam ucyate,] p.85
yathā --- pramāṇānāṃ prameyasya ca/ uddhiṣṭasya lakṣitasya ca vibhāgavacanam, yathā --- chalasya ``vacanavighāto 'rthavikalpopapattyā cchalam'', ``tat trividham'' iti/ athoddiṣṭasya vibhāgavacanam ---
children.translated_text: as for instance — the definitions of the instruments of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>). The statement of division regarding what has been enumerated and defined — as for instance, regarding <s>chala</s> (quibble): 'the obstruction of discourse through a shift of meaning is <s>chala</s>,' 'it is of three kinds.' Now, the statement of division regarding what has been enumerated:

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.3: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) are the instruments of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

children.text:
% p.86
akṣasyākṣasya prativiṣayaṃ vṛttiḥ pratyakṣam/ vṛttis tu --- sannikarṣaḥ, jñānaṃ vā/
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is the functioning of each sense-organ (<s>akṣa</s>) with respect to its own object. And 'functioning' means either contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) or cognition (<s>jñāna</s>).

children.text:
% p.87
yadā sannikarṣas tadā jñānaṃ pramitiḥ, yadā jñānam, tadā hānopādānopekṣābuddhayaḥ phalam/
children.translated_text: When it is contact, then cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) is the result (<s>pramiti</s>); when it is cognition, then the cognitions of avoidance (<s>hāna</s>), acquisition (<s>upādāna</s>), and indifference (<s>upekṣā</s>) are the fruit.

children.text:
% p.88
anumānaṃ --- mitena liṅgena liṅgino 'rthasya paścān mānam anumānam/
children.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the subsequent cognition (<s>māna</s>) of the object characterized by the inferential mark (<s>liṅgin</s>) through the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that has been (previously) cognized.

children.text:
% p.90
upamānaṃ --- sāmīpyajñānaṃ --- yathā gaur evaṃ gavaya iti/ sāmīpyaṃ tu sāmānyayogaḥ/ śabdaḥ --- śabdyate 'nenārtha ity abhidhīyate jñāpyate/
children.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) is the knowledge of proximity (similarity) — as in 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.' And proximity means the possession of a common property. <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is that by which an object is verbally communicated — it is said to be that which makes known.

children.text:
% p.91
upalabdhisādhanāni pramāṇāni samākhyānirvacanasāmarthyāt boddhavyam/ pramīyate 'neneti karaṇārthābhidhāno hi pramāṇaśabdaḥ/ tadviśeṣasamākhyāyā api tathaiva vyākhyānam/
kiṃ punaḥ pramāṇāni prameyam abhisaṃplavante? atha pratiprameyaṃ vyavatiṣṭhanta iti?
children.translated_text:
That the <s>pramāṇas</s> (instruments of valid knowledge) are the means of apprehension (<s>upalabdhi-sādhana</s>) should be understood from the force of the naming and etymological derivation. For the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' denotes an instrument — 'that by which one cognizes (<s>pramīyate</s>).' The explanation of the specific names (of each <s>pramāṇa</s>) follows the same method.
Now, do the <s>pramāṇas</s> converge upon (the same) object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>)? Or do they stand separately, each for its own <s>prameya</s>?

children.text:
% p.92
ubhayathā darśanam, ``asty ātmā'' ity āptopadeśāt pratīyate, tatrānumānam --- ``icchādveṣaprayatnasukhaduḥkhajñānāny ātmano liṅgam'' iti, pratyakṣaṃ --- yuñjānasya yogasamādhijam ``ātmamanasoḥ saṃyogaviśeṣād ātmā pratyakṣa'' iti/ agnir āptopadeśāt pratīyate ``atrāgniḥ''iti, pratyāsīdatā dhūmadarśanenānumīyate, pratyāsannena ca pratyakṣata upalabhyate/ vyavasthā punaḥ --- ``agnihotra juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ'' iti, laukikasya svarge na liṅgadarśanam, na pratyakṣam/ stanayitnuśabde śrūyamāṇe śabdahetor anumānam, tatra na pratyakṣam, nāgamaḥ/ pāṇau pratyakṣata upalabhyamāne nānumānam, nāgama iti/
sā ceyaṃ pramitiḥ pratyakṣaparā/ jijñāsitam artham āptopadeśāt pratipadyamāno liṅgadarśanenāpi bubhutsate,
children.translated_text:
Both views are observed. 'The self exists' — this is known from the reliable testimony (<s>āptopadeśa</s>) of the trustworthy. Regarding the same, inference: 'desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain, and cognition are the inferential marks of the self.' And perception: for the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, born of meditative absorption (<s>yogasamādhi</s>) — 'through a special connection of the self and the mind, the self is perceptible.' Fire is known from reliable testimony: 'there is fire here.' By one approaching, it is inferred through the perception of smoke; and by one close at hand, it is directly perceived. On the other hand, the restricted application: 'one who desires heaven should offer the <s>agnihotra</s>' — for the worldly person, there is no inferential mark for heaven, nor perception. When a thunder-sound is heard, there is inference from the auditory cause — there is no perception, no scriptural testimony. When something is perceived by hand through direct perception, there is no inference, no scriptural testimony.
And this valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) culminates in perception. One who apprehends the desired object through reliable testimony also wishes to ascertain it through the observation of inferential marks;

children.text:
% bubhutsate,] p.93
liṅgadarśanānumitaṃ ca pratyakṣato didṛkṣate, upalabdhe 'rthe jijñāsā nivarttate/ pūrvoktam udāharaṇam ``agniḥ'' iti/ pramātuḥ pramāṇānāṃ sambhavo 'bhisaṃplavaḥ, asambhavo vyavastheti//3//
children.translated_text: and what has been inferred through the observation of inferential marks, one wishes to see directly through perception. When the object is directly apprehended, inquiry ceases. The previously stated example is 'fire.' The convergence (<s>abhisaṃplava</s>) of the <s>pramāṇas</s> for the knower occurs when they are applicable; their restricted application (<s>vyavasthā</s>) occurs when they are not. // 3 //
Thus ends the commentary on the three sūtras (<s>trisūtrībhāṣya</s>).
Now the statement of definitions for the distinguished (categories):

children.text: NyS_1,1.4: indriyārthasannikarṣottpannaṃ jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyātmakaṃ pratyakṣam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.4: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) that arises from the contact of a sense-organ with its object, that is non-verbal (<s>avyapadeśya</s>), non-errant (<s>avyabhicāri</s>), and of the nature of determinate judgment (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>).

children.text: indriyasyārthena sannikarṣād utpadyate yaj jñānaṃ tat pratyakṣam/
children.translated_text: The cognition that arises from the contact of a sense-organ with an object — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).

children.text:
% p.94
na tarhīdānīm idaṃ bhavati, ātmā manasā saṃyujyate, mana indriyeṇa, indriyam artheneti?
children.translated_text: But then, does this not (also) occur: the self (<s>ātman</s>) is conjoined with the mind (<s>manas</s>), the mind with the sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>), and the sense-organ with the object?

children.text:
% p.98
nedaṃ kāraṇāvadhāraṇam --- etāvat pratyakṣe kāraṇam iti, kiṃ tu viśiṣṭakāraṇavacanam iti/ yat pratyakṣajñānasya viśiṣṭakāraṇaṃ tad ucyate, yat tu samānam anumānādijñānasya, na tannivarttata iti/
manasas tarhīndriyeṇa saṃyogo vaktavyaḥ?
children.translated_text:
(This sūtra) is not a determination of the totality of causes — (stating) 'this much alone is the cause of perception'; rather, it is a statement of the distinguishing cause. What is the distinguishing cause of perceptual cognition is stated; but what is common (also) to inferential and other cognitions is not thereby excluded.
Then should the conjunction of the mind with the sense-organ be stated?

children.text:
% p.100
bhidyamānasya pratyakṣajñānasya nāyaṃ bhidyata iti samānatvān nokta iti/
children.translated_text: Since this (conjunction of mind and sense-organ) does not differ when perceptual cognition differs (from other types), it is not stated, being common (to all cognitions).

children.text:
% p.109
yāvad arthaṃ vai nāmadheyaśabdās tair arthasampratyayaḥ, arthasampratyayāc ca vyavahāraḥ/ tatredam indriyārthasannikarṣād utpannam arthajñānaṃ ``rūpam'' iti vā, ``rasaḥ'' ity evaṃ vā bhavati, rūparasaśabdāś ca viṣayanāmadheyam/ tena vyapadiśyate jñānaṃ --- rūpam iti jānīte, rasa iti jānīte/ nāmadheyaśabdena vyapadiśyamānaṃ sat śābdaṃ prasajyate, ata āha --- avyapadeśyam iti/
children.translated_text: Words that are names have their meaning only insofar as they serve their purpose; from them comes the understanding of meaning, and from the understanding of meaning comes practical usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>). Now, this cognition of an object arising from the contact of a sense-organ with its object occurs as 'color' or as 'taste' and so on; and the words 'color,' 'taste,' etc. are the names of the (sense-)objects. Through these, cognition is designated — 'he knows color,' 'he knows taste.' But being designated by a name-word, it would follow that it is verbal (<s>śābda</s>); therefore (the sūtra) says: <s>avyapadeśya</s> (non-verbal).

children.text:
% p.110
yad idam anupayukte śabdārthasanbandhe 'rthajñānam, na tat nāmadheyaśabdena vyapadiśyate, gṛhīte 'pi ca śabdārthasambandhe 'syārthasyāyaṃ śabdo nāmadheyam iti/ yadā tu so 'rtho gṛhyate,
children.translated_text: This cognition of an object, when the relationship between word and meaning has not been employed, is not designated by a name-word. Even when the relationship between word and meaning has been grasped — 'this word is the name of this object' —

children.text:
% gṛhyate,] p.111
tadā tat pūrvasmād arthajñānān na viśiṣyate, tad arthavijñānaṃ tādṛg eva bhavati/ tasya tv arthajñānasyānyaḥ samākhyāśabdo nāstīti, yena pratīyamānaṃ vyavahārāya lakpeta/ na cāpratīyamānena vyavahāraḥ/ tasmāj jñeyasyārthasya saṃjñāśabdenetikaraṇayuktena nirdiśyate --- rūpam iti jñānam, rasa iti jñānam iti/ tad evam arthajñānakāle sa na samākhyāśabdo vyāpriyate, vyavahārakāle tu vyāpriyate/ tasmād aśābdam arthajñānam indriyārthasannikarṣotpannam iti/
children.translated_text: when that object is apprehended (perceptually), the resulting cognition is not different from the earlier object-cognition; the cognition of the object is of the same kind. But for that object-cognition there is no other designation-word by which it could be known and employed for practical usage. And there is no practical usage without what is being cognized. Therefore, the object to be known is indicated by the conventional name-word with the instrumental suffix — 'the cognition of color,' 'the cognition of taste.' Thus, at the time of object-cognition, the designation-word does not function; but at the time of practical usage, it functions. Therefore, object-cognition arising from sense-object contact is non-verbal (<s>aśābda</s>).

children.text:
% p.112
grīṣme marīcayo bhaumenoṣmaṇā saṃsṛṣṭāḥ spandamānā dūrasthasya cakṣuṣā sannikṛṣyante,
children.translated_text: In summer, mirages — heat-shimmer from the ground's warmth, flickering — come into contact with the eye of a distant observer.

children.text:
% p.113
tatrendriyārthasannikarṣād udakam iti jñānam utpadyate, tac ca pratyakṣaṃ prasajyata ity ata āha --- avyabhicārīti/ yad atasmiṃs tad iti tad vyabhicāri pratyakṣam iti/
children.translated_text: There, from the contact of the sense-organ with the object, the cognition 'this is water' arises. And this would follow as perception — therefore (the sūtra) says: <s>avyabhicāri</s> (non-errant). That which (cognizes) something as something it is not — that is errant, (and therefore) not perception.

children.text:
% p.121
dūrāc cakṣuṣā hy ayam arthaṃ paśyan nāvadhārayati dhūma iti vā reṇur iti vā/ tad etad indriyārthasannikarṣotpannam anavadhāraṇajñānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ prasajyata ity ata āha --- vyavasāyātmakam iti/ na caitan mantavyam --- ātmamanaḥsannikarṣajam evānavadhāraṇajñānam iti/ cakṣuṣā hy ayam arthaṃ paśyan nāvadhārayati,
children.translated_text: One who sees an object from afar with the eye cannot determine whether it is smoke or dust. This cognition, arising from sense-object contact yet being indeterminate, would follow as perception — therefore (the sūtra) says: <s>vyavasāyātmaka</s> (of the nature of determinate judgment). And this should not be thought — that indeterminate cognition arises only from the contact of the self and the mind (without sense-organ involvement). For one sees an object with the eye yet cannot determine it;

children.text:
% hy ayam arthaṃ paśyan nāvadhārayati,] p.122
yathā cendriyeṇopalabdham arthaṃ manasopalabhate, evam indriyeṇānavadhārayan manasā nāvadhārayati/ yac ca tadindriyānavadhāraṇapūrvakaṃ manasānavadhāraṇaṃ tad viśeṣāpekṣaṃ vimarśamātraṃ saṃśayaḥ, na pūrvam iti/ sarvatra pratyakṣaviṣaye jñātur indriyeṇa vyavasāyaḥ,
children.translated_text: and just as the mind apprehends the object perceived by the sense-organ, so too, when the sense-organ fails to determine, the mind also fails to determine. And that indetermination by the mind, preceded by the sense-organ's indetermination, which depends on (awaiting) specific differentiation — that is merely deliberation, that is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), not a prior (determinate) cognition. In every case within the domain of perception, the determination (<s>vyavasāya</s>) by the knower is through the sense-organ.

children.text:
% vyavasāyaḥ,] p.123
paścān manasāanuvyavasāyaḥ, upahatendriyāṇām anuvyavasāyābhāvād iti/
ātmādiṣu sukhādiṣu ca pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam, anindriyārthasannikarṣajaṃ hi tad iti/ indriyasya vai sato manasa indriyebhyaḥ pṛthagupadeśo dharmabhedāt, bhautikānīndriyāṇi niyataviṣayāṇi,
children.translated_text:
[Note: vyavasāyaḥ,] p.123
Afterwards there is <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective cognition) by <s>manas</s> (mind); for those with impaired sense organs, there is no <s>anuvyavasāya</s>.
The definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) must be stated with respect to <s>ātman</s> and the like, and <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) and the like, for that [perception of these] does not arise from the contact of sense organs with objects. Indeed, though <s>manas</s> is a sense organ, the separate mention of <s>manas</s> from the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) is due to a difference in properties: the sense organs are material (<s>bhautika</s>) and have delimited objects,

children.text:
% -nīndriyāṇi niyataviṣayāṇi,] p.124
saguṇānāṃ caiṣām indriyabhāva iti, manas tv abhautikaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ ca, nāsya saguṇasyendriyabhāva iti/ sati cendriyārthasannikarṣe sannidhim asannidhiṃ cāsya yugapajjñānānutpattikāraṇaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: -nīndriyāṇi niyataviṣayāṇi,] p.124
and the status of these as sense organs is because they possess qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>); but <s>manas</s> is non-material (<s>abhautika</s>) and has all things as its object, and being possessed of qualities does not make it a sense organ. And we shall explain that, even when there is contact between sense organs and objects, the proximity or non-proximity of <s>manas</s> is the cause of the non-arising of simultaneous cognitions.

children.text:
% -m asannidhiṃ ... vakṣyāmaḥ iti/] p.129
manasaś cendriyabhāvān na vācyaṃ lakṣaṇāntaram iti/ tantrāntarasamācārāc caitat pratyetavyam iti/ paramatam apratiṣiddham anumatam iti hi tantrayuktiḥ/ vyākhyātaṃ pratyakṣam//4//
children.translated_text:
[Note: -m asannidhiṃ ... vakṣyāmaḥ iti/] p.129
And because <s>manas</s> has the nature of a sense organ, a separate definition need not be stated. This should be understood from the practice of other systems. For it is a principle of systematic reasoning (<s>tantrayukti</s>) that a rival doctrine not refuted is [tacitly] approved. Thus <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) has been explained. //4//
[Section: NySBh_1,1.5]
[Note: p.132]

children.text: NyS_1,1.5: atha tatpūrvakaṃ trividham anumānaṃ pūrvavac cheṣavat sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: NyS_1,1.5: Now, <s>anumāna</s> (inference), which is preceded by that [perception], is threefold: <s>pūrvavat</s> (based on prior [cause]), <s>śeṣavat</s> (based on remainder), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (based on what is commonly observed). ||

children.text:
% p.142
tatpūrvakam ity anena liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandhadarśanaṃ liṅgadarśanaṃ cābhisambadhyate/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.142]
By the word 'preceded by that' (<s>tatpūrvaka</s>), the perception of the relation between the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) and <s>liṅgin</s> (the thing marked), and the perception of the <s>liṅga</s>, are connected.

children.text:
% p.146
liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambaddhayor darśanena liṅgasmṛtir abhisambadhyate/ smṛtyā liṅgadarśanena cāpratyakṣo 'rtho 'numīyate/
pūrvavad iti --- yatra kāraṇena kāryam anumīyate, yathā meghonnatyā bhaviṣyati vṛṣṭir iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.146]
From the observation of the <s>liṅga</s> and <s>liṅgin</s> in conjunction, the recollection of the <s>liṅga</s> is connected. Through recollection and the observation of the <s>liṅga</s>, an imperceptible object is inferred.
<s>Pūrvavat</s> means — where an effect is inferred from its cause, as when from the rising of clouds one infers 'there will be rain.'

children.text:
% p.148
śeṣavat tad --- yatra kāryeṇa kāraṇam anumīyate, pūrvodakaviparītam udakaṃ nadyāḥ pūrṇatvaṃ śīghratvañ ca dṛṣṭvā srotaso 'numīyate bhūtā vṛṣṭir iti/ sāmānyatodṛṣṭam --- vrajyāpūrvakam anyatra dṛṣṭasya ṇyatra darśanam iti,
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.148]
<s>Śeṣavat</s> is that — where a cause is inferred from its effect; having observed that the water of a river is different from its former state, and seeing its fullness and swiftness, one infers from the current that 'there has been rain.' <s>Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> — the perception elsewhere of something previously seen in one place, preceded by movement;

children.text:
% dṛṣṭasya ṇyatra darśanam iti,] p.149
tathā cādityasya, tasmād asty apratyakṣāpy ādityasya vrajyeti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: dṛṣṭasya anyatra darśanam iti,] p.149
and so too of the sun; therefore, even though imperceptible, there is movement of the sun.

children.text:
% p.152
atha vā pūrvavad iti --- yatra yathāpūrvaṃ pratyakṣabhūtayor anyataradarśanenānyatarasyānumānam,
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.152]
Alternatively, <s>pūrvavat</s> means — where, of two things previously perceived together, by the observation of one the other is inferred,

children.text:
% p.155
'pratyakṣasyānumānam, yathā dhūmenāgnir iti/ śeṣavan nāma pariśeṣaḥ, sa ca prasaktapratiṣedhe ṇyatrāprasaṅgāc chiṣyamāṇe sampratyayaḥ, yathā sad anityam evamādinā dravyaguṇakarmaṇām aviśeṣeṇa sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyebhyo vibhaktasya śabdasya, tasmin dravyakarmaguṇasaṃśaye, na dravyam, ekadravyatvāt, na karma, śabdāntarahetutvāt, yas tu śiṣyate so .yam iti śabdasya guṇatvapratipattiḥ/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.155]
the inference of what was [previously] perceived, as fire from smoke. <s>Śeṣavat</s> means elimination (<s>pariśeṣa</s>), and that is, when what has been proposed is negated, the conviction that falls upon what remains where there is no [such] proposal; as when, by [the reasoning] 'what exists is non-eternal' and so forth, <s>śabda</s> (word/sound) has been distinguished from <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karma</s> (action) without distinction from <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), and when there is doubt whether it is substance, action, or quality — it is not substance, because it inheres in a single substance; it is not action, because it is the cause of another sound; what remains, that it is — thus the cognition of the quality-nature of <s>śabda</s>.

children.text:
%śabdasya guṇatvapratipattiḥ/] p.156
sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ nāma --- yatrāpratyakṣe liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandhe kenacid arthena liṅgasya sāmānyād apratyakṣo liṅgī gamyate, yathecchādibhir ātmā, icchādayo guṇāḥ,
children.translated_text:
[Note: śabdasya guṇatvapratipattiḥ/] p.156
<s>Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> means — where, when the relation between <s>liṅga</s> and <s>liṅgin</s> is imperceptible, the imperceptible <s>liṅgin</s> is cognized through the generality (<s>sāmānya</s>) of the <s>liṅga</s> with some [known] object; as <s>ātman</s> [is inferred] from desire (<s>icchā</s>) and the like — desire and the rest are qualities (<s>guṇa</s>),

children.text:
% guṇāḥ,] p.157
guṇāś ca dravyasaṃsthānāḥ, tad tad eṣāṃ sthānaṃ sa ātmeti/
vibhāgavacanād eva trividham iti siddhe trividhavacanaṃ mahato mahāviṣayasya nyāyasya laghīyasā sūtreṇopadeśāt paraṃ vākyalāghavaṃ manyamānasyānyasmin vākyalāghave 'nādaraḥ/ tathā cāyam itthaṃbhūtena vākyavikalpena pravṛttaḥ siddhānte chale śabdādiṣu ca bahulaṃ samācāraḥ śāstra iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: guṇāḥ,] p.157
and qualities inhere in a substance (<s>dravya</s>); therefore their locus is the <s>ātman</s>.
Since the threefold [division] is already established by the statement of division itself, the [explicit] statement 'threefold' [is explained thus]: one who considers the supreme verbal economy to consist in the instruction of a great <s>nyāya</s> (logical method) of vast scope through the most concise <s>sūtra</s>, shows disregard for verbal economy elsewhere. And thus this practice is abundant in the <s>śāstra</s> — proceeding with such variation of expression — in <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), <s>chala</s> (quibbling), <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony), and the like.

children.text:
% p.158
sadviṣayaṃ ca pratyakṣaṃ sadasadviṣayaṃ cānumānam/ kasmāt?/ traikālyagrahaṇāt ---
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.158]
And <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) has existent things as its object, while <s>anumāna</s> (inference) has both existent and non-existent things as its object. Why? Because of the apprehension of the three times (<s>traikālyagrahaṇa</s>) —

children.text:
% p.161
trikālayuktā arthā anumānena gṛhyante, bhaviṣyatīty anumīyate, bhavatīti, cābhūd iti ca, asac ca khalv attam anāgataṃ ceti//5//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.161]
Objects connected with the three times are grasped by inference: 'it will be' is inferred, and 'it is,' and 'it was'; and indeed the past and the future are non-existent [at present]. //5//
[Note: p.168]
[Section: NySBh_1,1.6]
Now <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) —
NyS_1,1.6: <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) is the means of establishing what is to be proved through similarity with something well-known. ||

children.text: prajñātena sāmānyāt prajñāpanīyasya prajñāpanam upamānam iti/ yathā gaur evaṃ gavaya iti/
children.translated_text: The making known of what is to be made known, through the generality [shared] with what is [already] known — that is <s>upamāna</s>. As [when one says]: 'A <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.'

children.text:
% p.169
kiṃ punar atropamānena kriyate? yadā khalv ayaṃ gavā samānadharmaṃ pratipadyate tadā pratyakṣatas tam arthaṃ pratipadyata iti, samākhyāsambandhapratipattir upamānārtha ity āha/ yathā gaur evaṃ gavaya ity upamāne prayukte gavā samānadharmam artham indriyārthasannikarṣād upalabhamāno 'sya gavayaśabdaḥ saṃjñeti saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandhaṃ pratipadyata iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.169]
But what is accomplished here by <s>upamāna</s>? When this person apprehends something possessing properties in common with a cow, then he apprehends that object through perception — [so what is the role of comparison?] The apprehension of the relation between a name and the thing named is the purpose of <s>upamāna</s>, he [<s>Vātsyāyana</s>] says. When the comparison 'a <s>gavaya</s> is like a cow' has been employed, the person perceiving through sense-object contact an object similar in properties to a cow, understands that 'this word <s>gavaya</s> is the name [of this animal]' — thus he apprehends the relation of <s>saṃjñā</s> (name) and <s>saṃjñin</s> (the named object).

children.text:
% gaur evaṃ gavaya ... pratipadyata iti] p.170
yathā mudgas tathā mudgaparṇī,
children.translated_text:
[Note: gaur evaṃ gavaya ... pratipadyata iti] p.170
Just as [one says] 'a <s>mudgaparṇī</s> is like a <s>mudga</s> (mung bean),'

children.text:
% -parṇī,] p.171
yathā māṣas tathā māṣaparṇīty upamāne prayukte upamānāt saṃjñāsaṃjñisanbandhaṃ pratipadyamānas tām oṣadhīṃ bhaiṣajyāyāharati/
children.translated_text:
[Note: -parṇī,] p.171
or 'a <s>māṣaparṇī</s> is like a <s>māṣa</s> (black gram)' — when the comparison has been employed, one who apprehends the relation of name and named object through comparison gathers that herb for medicinal use.

children.text:
% p.172
evam anyo 'py upamānasya loke viṣayo bubhutsitavya iti//6//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.172]
Thus other domains of <s>upamāna</s> in worldly [practice] too should be investigated. //6//
[Section: NySBh_1,1.7]

[Note: p.173]
Now <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) —
NyS_1,1.7: <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is the instruction of a trustworthy person (<s>āptopadeśa</s>). ||

children.text: āptaḥ khalu sākṣātkṛtadharmā yathādṛṣṭasyārthasya cikhyāpayiṣayā prayukta upadeṣṭā/
children.translated_text: An <s>āpta</s> (trustworthy person) is indeed one who has directly realized <s>dharma</s>, a teacher who is motivated by the desire to communicate an object as it has been seen.

children.text:
% p.174
sākṣātkaraṇam arthasyāptiḥ, tayā pravartata ity āptaḥ/ ṛṣyāryamlecchānāṃ samānaṃ lakṣaṇam/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.174]
The direct realization of an object is <s>āpti</s> (attainment); one who proceeds by that [attainment] is an <s>āpta</s>. The definition is the same for <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), <s>āryas</s> (noble persons), and <s>mlecchas</s> (foreigners).

children.text:
% samānaṃ lakṣaṇam/] p.176
tathā ca sarveṣāṃ vyavahārāḥ pravarttanta iti/ evam ebhiḥ pramāṇair devamanuṣyatiraścāṃ vyavahārāḥ prakalpante, nāto 'nyatheti//7//
children.translated_text:
[Note: samānaṃ lakṣaṇam/] p.176
And thus the transactions of all [these] proceed. In this way, through these <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), the transactions of gods, humans, and animals are established, and not otherwise. //7//
[Section: NySBh_1,1.8]
[Note: p.179]
NyS_1,1.8: That [verbal testimony] is twofold, because its object may be seen or unseen. ||

children.text: yasyeha dṛśyate 'rthaḥ sa dṛṣṭārthaḥ/ yasyāmutra pratīyate so 'dṛṣṭārthaḥ/ evam ṛṣilaukikavākyānāṃ vibhāga iti/ kimarthaṃ punar idam ucyate? sa na manyeta dṛṣṭārtha evāptopadeśaḥ pramāṇam, arthasyāvadhāraṇād iti, adṛṣṭārtho 'pi pramāṇam arthasyānumānād iti//8//
children.translated_text: That whose object is seen here [in this world] is <s>dṛṣṭārtha</s> (having a seen object). That whose [object] is understood in the hereafter is <s>adṛṣṭārtha</s> (having an unseen object). Thus is the division of the statements of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) and ordinary people. But for what purpose is this said? Lest one think that only <s>āptopadeśa</s> (trustworthy instruction) with a seen object is a valid means of knowledge, because the object can be ascertained [directly] — [it is stated that] that with an unseen object is also a valid means of knowledge, because the object can be inferred. //8//
[Section: NySBh_1,1.9]

children.text:
% p.180
kiṃ punar anena pramāṇenārthajātaṃ pramātavyam iti? ---
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.180]
But what class of objects is to be known through these means of valid knowledge? —

NyS_1,1.9: <s>Ātman</s> (self), <s>śarīra</s> (body), <s>indriya</s> (sense organs), <s>artha</s> (objects), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity), <s>doṣa</s> (defects), <s>pretyabhāva</s> (transmigration), <s>phala</s> (fruit), <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — these are the objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>). ||

children.text:
% p.182
tatrātmā sarvasya draṣṭā sarvasya bhoktā sarvajñaḥ sarvānubhāvī/ tasya bhogāyatanaṃ śarīram/ bhogasādhanānīndriyāṇi/ bhoktavyā indriyārthāḥ/ bhogo buddhiḥ/ sarvārthopalabdhau nendriyāṇi prabhavantīti sarvaviṣayam antaḥkaraṇaṃ manaḥ/ śarīrendriyārthabuddhisukhavedanānāṃ nivṛttikāraṇaṃ pravṛttiḥ, doṣāś ca/ nāsyedaṃ śarīram apūrvam anuttaraṃ ca, pūrvaśarīrāṇām ādir nāsti, uttareṣām apavargo 'nta iti pretyabhāvaḥ/ sasādhanasukhaduḥkhopabhogaḥ phalam/ duḥkham iti nedam anukūlavedanīyasya sukhasya pratīteḥ pratyākhyānam/ kiṃ tarhi? janmana evedaṃ sasukhasādhanasya duḥkhānuṣaṅgāt duḥkhenāviprayogād vividhabādhanāyogād duḥkham iti samādhibhāvanam upadiśyate/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.182]
Therein, <s>ātman</s> is the seer of all, the experiencer of all, omniscient, all-experiencing. Its locus of experience is the <s>śarīra</s> (body). The instruments of experience are the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs). The objects of the senses are what is to be experienced. Experience is <s>buddhi</s> (cognition). Since the sense organs are not capable of apprehending all objects, <s>manas</s> (mind) is the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) that has all things as its object. <s>Pravṛtti</s> (activity) and <s>doṣas</s> (defects) are the cause of the cessation of body, sense organs, objects, cognition, and the experience of pleasure. This body of his is neither the first nor the last; there is no beginning to prior bodies, and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) is the end of subsequent ones — this is <s>pretyabhāva</s> (transmigration). The experience of pleasure and pain together with their means is <s>phala</s> (fruit). <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) — this is not a rejection of the perception of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), which is experienced as agreeable. What then? Rather, this is an instruction in meditative contemplation (<s>samādhibhāvana</s>): that birth itself, because of its inseparable connection with suffering along with the means of pleasure, because of the impossibility of separation from suffering, and because of the conjunction with manifold afflictions, is suffering.

children.text:
% -yogād duḥkham ... upadiśyate/] p.183
samāhito bhāvayati, bhāvayan nirvidyate, nirviṇṇasya vairāgyam, viraktasyāpavarga iti/ janmamaraṇaprabandhocchedaḥ sarvaduḥkhaprahāṇam apavarga iti/ asty anyad api dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyāḥ prameyam, tadbhedena cāparisaṅkhyeyam; asya tu tattvajñānād apavargo mithyājñānāt saṃsāra ity ata etad upadiṣṭaṃ viśeṣeṇeti//9//
children.translated_text:
[Note: -yogād duḥkham ... upadiśyate/] p.183
One who is concentrated contemplates; contemplating, one becomes disenchanted; for the disenchanted there is dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>); for the dispassionate there is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). <s>Apavarga</s> is the cutting off of the continuum of birth and death, the abandonment of all suffering. There are also other objects of knowledge — <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — and by their subdivisions they are innumerable; but from the true knowledge of these [twelve <s>prameyas</s>] there is <s>apavarga</s>, and from false knowledge there is <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth) — therefore these have been specially taught. //9//
[Section: NySBh_1,1.10]

children.text:
% p.184
tatrātmā tāvat pratyakṣato na gṛhyate/ sa kim āptopadeśamātrād eva pratipadyata iti? nety ucyate/ anumānāc ca pratipattavya iti/ katham?
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.184]
Therein, <s>ātman</s> is first of all not grasped through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). Is it then to be apprehended solely through <s>āptopadeśa</s> (trustworthy instruction)? No, it is said — it is also to be apprehended through <s>anumāna</s> (inference). How?

NyS_1,1.10: Desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), and cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) are the inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>ātman</s>. ||

children.text:
% p.185
yajjātīyasyārthasya sannikarṣāt sukham ātmopalabdhavān, tajjātīyam evārthaṃ paśyann upādātum icchati, seyam ādātum icchā ekasyānekārthadarśino darśanapratisandhānād bhavati liṅgam ātmanaḥ/ niyataviṣaye hi buddhibhedamātre na sambhavati, dehāntaravad iti/ evam ekasyānekārthadarśino darśanapratisandhānāt duḥkhahetau dveṣaḥ,
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.185]
Having experienced pleasure from contact with an object of a certain kind, <s>ātman</s>, when seeing an object of the same kind, desires to take it — this desire to take, which arises in a single [self] that has seen many objects, from the connecting together of [past] perceptions, is an inferential mark of <s>ātman</s>. For in a mere difference of cognitions restricted to [particular] objects, this [connecting of perceptions] would not be possible — as in the case of different bodies. Similarly, for a single [self] that has seen many objects, aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) toward what causes suffering arises from the connecting together of perceptions;

children.text:
% -nekārthadarśino ... dveṣaḥ,] p.187
yajjātīyo 'syārthaḥ sukhahetuḥ prasiddhas tajjātīyam arthaṃ paśyann ādātuṃ prayatate/ ekam anekārthadarśinaṃ darśanapratisandhātāram antareṇa na syāt/ niyataviṣaye buddhimātre na sambhavati, dehāntaravad iti/ etena duḥkhahetau prayatno vyākhyātaḥ/ sukhaduḥkhasmṛtyā cāyaṃ tatsādhanam ādadānaḥ sukham upalabhate duḥkham upalabhate, sukhaduḥkhe vedayate/ pūrvokta eva hetuḥ/ bubhutsamānaḥ khalv ayaṃ vimṛśati kiṃsvid iti, vimṛśaṃś ca jānīte idam iti, tad idaṃ jñānaṃ bubhutsāvimarśābhyām abhinnakartṛkaṃ gṛhyamāṇam ātmaliṅgam/ pūrvokta eva hetur iti/ tatra dehāntaravad iti vibhajyate yathānātmavādino dehāntareṣu niyataviṣayā buddhibhedā na pratisandhīyante tathaikadehaviṣayā api na pratisandhīyeran, aviśeṣāt/
children.translated_text:
[Note: -nekārthadarśino ... dveṣaḥ,] p.187
when one whose object of a certain kind is well-known as a cause of pleasure sees an object of that kind, one makes effort (<s>prayatna</s>) to take it. Without a single [self] that has seen many objects and that connects perceptions, this would not be possible. In a mere cognition restricted to [particular] objects, this would not be possible — as in the case of different bodies. By this, effort toward what causes suffering is also explained. And this one, taking the means to [pleasure and pain] through the memory of pleasure and pain, experiences pleasure and experiences pain — experiences pleasure and pain. The reason is as stated before. And this one, desiring to know, deliberates 'what is this?', and deliberating, knows 'it is this' — this <s>jñāna</s> (cognition), apprehended as having a single agent inseparable from the desire to know and deliberation, is an inferential mark of <s>ātman</s>. The reason is as stated before. Therein, 'as in the case of different bodies' is elaborated: just as, for those who deny <s>ātman</s>, cognitions restricted to [particular] objects in different bodies are not connected together, so too cognitions pertaining to even a single body would not be connected together, there being no difference [in principle].

children.text:
% tathaikadehaviṣayā api na pratisandhīyeran, aviśeṣāt/] p.188
so 'yam ekasattvasya samācāraḥ svayaṃdṛṣṭasya smaraṇam, nānyaddṛṣṭasya, nādṛṣṭasyeti/ evaṃ khalu nānāsattvānāṃ samācāro 'nyadṛṣṭam anyo na smaratīti/ tad etad ubyayam aśakyam anātmavādinā vyavasthāpayitum ity evam upapannam asty ātmeti//10//
children.translated_text:
[Note: tathaikadehaviṣayā api na pratisandhīyeran, aviśeṣāt/] p.188
This is the practice of a single being: the remembering of what was seen by oneself, not of what was seen by another, and not of what was not seen. And thus is the practice of different beings: one does not remember what another has seen. Both of these cannot be accounted for by one who denies <s>ātman</s> — thus it is established that <s>ātman</s> exists. //10//
[Section: NySBh_1,1.11]

[Note: p.193]
Its [the self's] seat of experience —
NyS_1,1.11: The <s>śarīra</s> (body) is the locus of <s>ceṣṭā</s> (voluntary action), <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), and <s>arthas</s> (objects [of experience]). ||

children.text: kathaṃ ceṣṭāśrayaḥ? īpsitaṃ jihāsitaṃ vārtham adhikṛtyepsājihāsāprayuktasya tadupāyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇā samīhā ceṣṭā, sā yatra varttate tac charīram/
children.translated_text: How is it the locus of <s>ceṣṭā</s> (voluntary action)? With regard to an object that is desired or to be avoided, the purposeful activity (<s>samīhā</s>) that has the character of undertaking the means [to obtain or avoid] it, impelled by desire to obtain or desire to avoid — that is <s>ceṣṭā</s>; and that in which it occurs is the <s>śarīra</s> (body).

children.text:
% tadupāyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇā ... tac charīram/] p.194
katham indriyāśrayaḥ? yasyānugraheṇānugṛhītāni upaghāte copahatāni svaviṣayeṣu sādhvasādhuṣu vartante sa eṣām āśrayaḥ tac charīram/ katham arthāśrayaḥ/
children.translated_text:
[Note: tadupāyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇā ... tac charīram/] p.194
How is it the locus of the sense organs? That by whose support the [sense organs] when supported function in their respective objects, whether good or bad, and by whose impairment they are impaired — that is their locus, that is the <s>śarīra</s> (body). How is it the locus of objects?

children.text:
% sa eṣām āśrayaḥ tac charīram/ katham arthāśrayaḥ/] p.195
yasminn āyatane indriyārthasannikarṣād utpannayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ pratisaṃvedanaṃ pravartate sa eṣām āśrayaḥ,
children.translated_text: That is their substratum, and that is the body. How is it the substratum of objects? That in which the experience of pleasure and pain, produced from the contact of the sense organ and object at a given locus, operates — that is their substratum,

children.text:
% sukhaduḥkhayoḥ pratisaṃvedanaṃ pravartate sa eṣām āśrayaḥ,] p.196
tac charīram iti//11//
children.translated_text: the experience of pleasure and pain operates — that is their substratum; that is the <s>śarīra</s> (body). //11//
Now, the instruments of experience —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.12: The nose, tongue, eye, skin, and ear are the sense organs, [arising] from the elements.

children.text: jighraty aneneti ghrāṇaṃ gandhaṃ gṛhṇātīti/ rasayaty aneneti rasanaṃ rasaṃ gṛhṇātīti/ caṣṭe 'neneti cakṣū rūpaṃ paśyatīti/ tvaksthānam indriyaṃ tvak/ tadupacāraḥ sthānād iti/
children.translated_text: That by which one smells is the <s>ghrāṇa</s> (nose) — it apprehends odor. That by which one tastes is the <s>rasana</s> (tongue) — it apprehends flavor. That by which one sees is the <s>cakṣus</s> (eye) — it perceives form. The sense organ located in the skin is <s>tvak</s> (the tactile sense); the designation is by metonymy from the location.

children.text:
% tadupacāraḥ sthānād iti/] p.198
śṛṇoty aneneti śrotraṃ śabdaṃ gṛhṇātīti/ evaṃ samākhyānirvacanasāmarthyād bodhyaṃ svaviṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇānīndriyāṇīti/
children.translated_text: That by which one hears is the <s>śrotra</s> (ear) — it apprehends sound. Thus, by the force of etymological analysis, it should be understood that the sense organs are characterized by the apprehension of their respective objects.

children.text:
% p.199
bhūtebhya iti/ nānāprakṛtīnām eṣāṃ satāṃ viṣayaniyamaḥ, naikaprakṛtīnām/ sati ca viṣayaniyame svaviṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇatvaṃ bhavatīti//12//
children.translated_text: "From the elements" — since these [sense organs] have different material causes, there is a restriction of [their] objects; this is not the case for those having a single material cause. And when there is restriction of objects, the characteristic of apprehending one's own object obtains. //12//
Now, what are the causes of the sense organs?

children.text: NyS_1,1.13: pṛthivy āpas tejo vāyur ākāśam iti bhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.13: Earth, water, fire, air, and space — these are the elements.

children.text: saṃjñāśabdaiḥ pṛthagupadeśo bhūtānāṃ vibhaktānāṃ suvacaṃ kāryaṃ bhaviṣyatīti//13//
children.translated_text: By designating them separately with their proper names, the task of explaining the elements as distinct will be easy to accomplish. //13//
Now indeed these —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.14: Smell, taste, form, touch, and sound are the qualities of earth and the rest, and are their objects.

children.text: pṛthivyādīnāṃ yathāviniyogaṃ guṇā indriyāṇāṃ yathākramam arthā viṣayā iti//14//
children.translated_text: They are the qualities of earth and the rest in their respective assignment, and the objects — that is, the sense-objects — of the sense organs in their respective order. //14//

children.text:
% p.213
acetanasya karaṇasya buddher jñānaṃ vṛttiḥ cetanasyākartur upalabdhir iti yuktiviruddham arthaṃ pratyācakṣāṇaka ivedam āha ---
children.translated_text: As if rejecting a meaning that contradicts reason — namely, that cognition or knowledge is the function of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), which is an unconscious instrument, while apprehension belongs to the conscious non-agent — he says this:

children.text: NyS_1,1.15: buddhir upalabdhir jñānam ity anarthāntaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.15: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) are synonymous.

children.text: nācetanasya karaṇasya buddher jñānaṃ bhavitum arhati, tad dhi cetanaṃ syāt, ekaś cāyaṃ cetano dehendriyasaṃghātavyatirikta iti/
children.translated_text: Knowledge cannot belong to <s>buddhi</s> as an unconscious instrument, for then it would be conscious; and this one conscious entity is distinct from the aggregate of body and sense organs.

children.text:
% dehendriyasaṃghātavyatirikta iti/] p.214
prameyalakṣaṇārthasya vākyasyānyārthaprakāśanam upapattisāmarthyād iti//15//
children.translated_text: The illumination of another meaning from a sentence whose [primary] meaning defines the <s>prameya</s> (object of valid knowledge) [is possible] by the force of logical reasoning. //15//

children.text:
% p.215
smṛtyanumānāgamasaṃśayapratibhāsvapnajñānohāḥ sukhādipratyakṣam icchādayaś ca manaso liṅgāni/ teṣu satsv ayam api ---
children.translated_text: Memory, inference, verbal testimony, doubt, intuition, dream, cognition, and conjecture, as well as the perception of pleasure and the like, and desire and the rest, are the marks of <s>manas</s> (mind). Among these, there is also this —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.16: The non-origination of simultaneous cognitions is the mark of <s>manas</s> (mind).

children.text: anindriyanimittāḥ smṛtyādayaḥ karaṇāntaranimittā bhavitum arhantīti/ yugapac ca khalu ghrāṇādīnāṃ gandhādīnāṃ ca sannikarṣeṣu satsu yugapaj jñānāni notpadyante,
children.translated_text: Memory and the rest, which are not caused by the [external] sense organs, must be caused by another instrument. And indeed, when there is contact of the nose and other [sense organs] with odor and other [objects] simultaneously, simultaneous cognitions do not arise;

children.text:
% khalu ghrāṇādīnāṃ ... yugapajjñānāni notpadyante, ] p.216
tenānumīyate, asti tat tad indriyasaṃyogi sahakāri nimittāntaram avyāpi, yasyāsannidher notpadyate jñānaṃ sannidheś cotpadyata iti/
children.translated_text: from this it is inferred: there exists another auxiliary cause, connected with each sense organ, which is non-pervasive, from whose absence cognition does not arise, and from whose presence it does arise.

children.text:
% jñānaṃ sannidheś cotpadyata iti/] p.217
manaḥsaṃyogānapekṣasya hīndriyārthasannikarṣasya jñānahetutve yugapad uptadyeran jñānānīti//16//
children.translated_text: For if the contact of sense organ and object were the cause of cognition without depending on connection with <s>manas</s> (mind), cognitions would arise simultaneously. //16//
Now, in due order —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.17: Activity is the initiation of speech, mind, and body.

children.text: mano 'tra buddhir ity abhipretam, budhyate 'neneti buddhiḥ/ so 'yam ārambhaḥ śarīreṇa vācā manasā ca puṇyaḥ pāpaś ca daśavidhaḥ/ tad etat kṛtabhāṣyaṃ dvitīyasūtra iti//17//
children.translated_text: Here, by '<s>buddhi</s>' (intellect), <s>manas</s> (mind) is intended — that by which one cognizes is <s>buddhi</s>. This initiation, through body, speech, and mind, is tenfold — meritorious and sinful. This has been commented upon in the second <s>sūtra</s>. //17//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.18: The <s>doṣas</s> (faults) are characterized by causing activity.

children.text: pravartanā pravṛttihetutvam, jñātāraṃ hi rāgādayaḥ pravartayanti puṇye pāpe vā/ yatra mithyājñānaṃ tatra rāgadveṣāv iti/ pratyātmavedanīyā hīme doṣāḥ kasmāl lakṣaṇato nirdiśyanta iti? karmalakṣaṇāḥ khalu raktadviṣṭamūḍhāḥ, rakto hi tat karma kurute yena karmaṇā sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā labhate, tathā dviṣṭas tathā mūḍha iti/ rāgadveṣamohā ity ucyamāne bahu noktaṃ bhavatīti//18//
children.translated_text: Causing activity means being the cause of <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity), for <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest impel the knower toward merit or sin. Where there is false knowledge, there arise <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion). Now, since these <s>doṣas</s> (faults) are known to each person individually, why are they defined by their characteristics? Because those who are attached, averse, or deluded are characterized by their actions — for the attached person performs that action by which he obtains pleasure or pain, and likewise the averse and the deluded. If one merely said '<s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s>' much would remain unsaid. //18//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.19: Rebirth is the state of being born again after death.

children.text: utpannasya kvacit sattvanikāye mṛtvā yā punarutpattiḥ sa pretyabhāvaḥ/ utpannasya --- sambaddhasya/ sambandhas tu dehendriyamanobuddhivedanābhiḥ/ punarutpattiḥ --- punar dehādibhiḥ sambandhaḥ/ punar ity abhyāsābhidhānam/ yatra kvacit prāṇabhṛnnikāye vartamānaḥ pūrvopāttān dehādīn jahāti tat praiti/
children.translated_text: The re-origination of one who has been born in some class of beings after dying — that is <s>pretyabhāva</s> (post-mortem existence). 'Of one who has been born' means 'of one who is connected.' And the connection is with body, sense organs, mind, intellect, and sensations. 'Re-origination' means connection again with body and the rest. The word 'again' denotes repetition. One who exists in any class of living beings abandons the previously acquired body and the rest — that is 'departing';

children.text:
% pūrvopāttān dehādīn jahāti tat praiti/] p.222
yat tatrānyatra vā dehādīn anyān upādatte tad bhavati/ pretyabhāvaḥ --- mṛtvā punarjanma, so 'yaṃ janmamaraṇaprabandhābhyāso 'nādir apavargāntaḥ pretyabhāvo veditavya iti//19//
