children.translated_text: when one takes up another body and the rest, there or elsewhere — that is 'coming into being.' <s>Pretyabhāva</s> (post-mortem existence) — that is, rebirth after death — this continuous cycle of birth and death, which is beginningless and ends with <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), is to be understood as <s>pretyabhāva</s>. //19//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.20: The fruit is the object produced by activity and faults.

children.text: sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanaṃ phalam/ sukhavipākaṃ karma duḥkhavipākaṃ ca/ tat punar dehendriyaviṣayabuddhiṣu satīṣu bhavatīti saha dehādibhiḥ phalam abhipretam/ tathā hi pravṛttidoṣajanito 'rthaḥ phalam etat sarvaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: The experience of pleasure and pain is the <s>phala</s> (fruit). <s>Karma</s> (action) has either a pleasurable or painful ripening. Moreover, this occurs only when body, sense organs, objects, and intellect are present; thus the fruit is understood together with the body and the rest. For thus it is: all this arises as the fruit produced by activity and faults.

children.text:
% pravṛttidoṣajanito 'rthaḥ phalam etat sarvaṃ bhavati/] p.223
tad etat phalam upātam upātaṃ heyam, tyaktaṃ tyaktam upādeyam iti nāsya hānopādānayor niṣṭhā paryavasānaṃ vāsti, sa khalv ayaṃ phalasya hānopādānasrotasohyate loka iti//20//
children.translated_text: This fruit, each time it is taken up, is to be abandoned; each time it is abandoned, it is taken up again — thus there is no finality or conclusion to its abandonment and acquisition. Indeed, the world is carried along in this stream of abandoning and acquiring the fruit. //20//
Now, this very —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.21: Suffering is characterized by affliction.

children.text: bādhanā pīḍā tāpa iti/ tayānuviddham anuṣaktam avinirbhāgena vartamānaṃ duḥkhayogād duḥkham iti/ so 'yaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhenānuviddham iti paśyan duḥkhaṃ jihāsur janmani duḥkhadarśī nirvidyate, nirviṇṇo virajyate, virakto vimucyate//21//
children.translated_text: <s>Bādhanā</s> means pain, torment. That which is pervaded by it, attached to it, existing inseparably from the connection with suffering — that is <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). Thus, one who sees that everything is pervaded by suffering, desiring to abandon suffering, seeing suffering in birth, becomes disenchanted; being disenchanted, becomes dispassionate; being dispassionate, becomes liberated. //21//

children.text:
% p.225
yatra tu niṣṭhā yatra tu paryavasānaṃ so .yam ---
children.translated_text: But where there is finality, where there is conclusion, that is —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.22: The absolute release from that [suffering] is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text: tena --- duḥkhena janmanā atyantaṃ vimuktir apavargaḥ/ katham? upāttasya janmano hānam, anyasya cānupādānam/ etām avasthām aparyantam apavargaṃ vedayante 'pavargavidaḥ/ tad abhayam ajaram amṛtyupadaṃ brahma kṣemaprāptir iti/
children.translated_text: Absolute freedom from that suffering, from birth, is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). How? The abandonment of the acquired birth, and the non-acquisition of another. Those who know <s>apavarga</s> declare this state to be without limit — that is <s>apavarga</s>. It is fearless, ageless, the state free from death, <s>Brahman</s>, the attainment of security.

children.text:
% p.226
nityaṃ sukham ātmano mahattvavan mokṣe vyajyate, yenābhivyaktenātyantaṃ vimuktaḥ sukhī bhātīti kecin manyante/ teṣāṃ pramāṇābhāvād anupapattiḥ/ na pratyakṣaṃ nānumānaṃ nāgamo vā vidyate nityaṃ sukham ātmano mahattvavan mokṣe 'bhivyajyata iti/
nityasyābhivyaktiḥ --- saṃvedanam, tasya hetuvacanam/ nityasyābhivyaktiḥ ---saṃvedanam --- jñānam iti, tasya hetur vācyo yatas tad utpadyata iti/
children.translated_text: Some think that an eternal happiness inherent in the <s>ātman</s> (self), like its greatness, is manifested in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), whereby the one who is absolutely freed appears as happy. This is untenable due to the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). There is neither perception, nor inference, nor verbal testimony that an eternal happiness inherent in the <s>ātman</s>, like its greatness, is manifested in <s>mokṣa</s>. The manifestation of what is eternal means its experience, and its cause must be stated. The manifestation of what is eternal means experience, that is, knowledge — and its cause, from which it arises, must be stated.

children.text:
% p.227
sukhavan nityam iti cet? saṃsārasthasya muktenāviśeṣaḥ/ yathā muktaḥ sukhena tatsaṃvedanena ca sannityenopapannas tathā saṃsārastho 'pi prasajyata iti, ubhayasya nityatvāt/
children.translated_text: If [one claims that it is] eternal like happiness? Then there would be no difference between one in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and one who is liberated. Just as the liberated person is endowed with eternal happiness and its experience, so too would be the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>, since both are eternal.

children.text:
% p.228
abhyanujñāne ca dharmādharmaphalena sāhacaryaṃ yaugapadyaṃ gṛhyeta/ yad idam utpattisthāneṣu dharmādharmaphalaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā saṃvedyate paryāyeṇa, tasya ca nityasaṃvedanasya ca sahabhāvo yaugapadyaṃ gṛhyeta, na sukhābhāvo nānabhivyaktir asti, ubhayasya nityatvāt/
anityatve hetuvacanam/ atha mokṣe nityasya sukhasya saṃvedanam anityam? yata utpadyate sa hetur vācyaḥ/
ātmamanaḥsaṃyogasya nimittāntarasahitasya hetutvam/ ātmamanaḥsaṃyogo hetur iti cet? evam api tasya sahakāri nimittāntaraṃ vacanīyam iti/
dharmasya kāraṇavacanam/ yadi dharmo nimittāntaram? tasya hetur vācyo yataḥ utpadyata iti/ yogasamādhijasya kāryāvasāyavirodhāt prakṣaye saṃvedananivṛttiḥ/ yadi yogasamādhijo dharmo hetuḥ?
children.translated_text: And if this is accepted, coexistence and simultaneity with the fruits of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) would follow. The pleasure or pain that is experienced alternately as the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> in the places of birth — there would be coexistence and simultaneity of that with the eternal experience; there would be neither absence of happiness nor non-manifestation, since both are eternal. Regarding the statement of a cause for impermanence: if the experience of eternal happiness in <s>mokṣa</s> is impermanent, then the cause from which it arises must be stated. Regarding the causality of the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> together with another auxiliary cause: if the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is the cause, then its auxiliary cause, another condition, must also be stated. Regarding the statement of the cause of <s>dharma</s>: if <s>dharma</s> is the auxiliary cause, then its cause, from which it arises, must be stated. If <s>dharma</s> born of <s>yoga</s> and <s>samādhi</s> is the cause — due to its conflict with the determination of effects,

children.text:
% -samādhijo dharmo hetuḥ?] p.229
tasya kāryāvasāyavirodhāt prakṣaye saṃvedanam atyantaṃ nivartate/
asaṃvedane cāvidyamānenāviśeṣaḥ/ yadi dharmakṣayāt saṃvedanoparamo nityaṃ sukhaṃ na saṃvedyata iti? kiṃ vidyamānaṃ na saṃvedyate, athāvidyamānam iti nānumānaṃ viśiṣṭe 'stīti/
aprakṣayaś ca dharmasya niranumānam utpattidharmakatvāt/ yogasamādhijo dharmo na kṣīyata iti nāsty anumānam/ utpattidharmakam anityam iti viparyayasya tv anumānam/ yasya tu saṃvedanoparamo nāsti tena saṃvedanahetur nitya ity anumeyam/
nitye ca muktasaṃsārasthayor aviśeṣa ity uktam/ yathā muktasya nityaṃ sukhaṃ tatsaṃvedanahetuś ca, saṃvedanasya tūparamo nāsti, kāraṇasya nityatvāt, tathā saṃsārasthasyāpīti/ evaṃ ca sati dharmādharmaphalena sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanena sāhacaryaṃ gṛhyeteti/
śarīrādisambandhaḥ pratibandhahetur iti cet? na, śarīrādīnām upabhogārthatvāt viparyayasya cānanumānāt/
children.translated_text: upon its exhaustion, the experience ceases absolutely. And in the absence of experience, there is no difference from what is non-existent. If, due to the exhaustion of <s>dharma</s>, there is cessation of experience and the eternal happiness is not experienced — is it existent and not experienced, or non-existent? Thus there is no inference that it exists as something distinct. And the non-exhaustion of <s>dharma</s> is without inferential support, since what is subject to origination is impermanent; there is no inference that <s>dharma</s> born of <s>yoga</s> and <s>samādhi</s> does not exhaust. Rather, there is an inference of the contrary: what is subject to origination is impermanent. But for that whose experience does not cease, it should be inferred that the cause of experience is eternal. And if it is eternal, it has been stated that there is no difference between the liberated and the one in <s>saṃsāra</s> — just as the liberated person has eternal happiness and its cause of experience, and there is no cessation of experience since the cause is eternal, so too for the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>; and in that case, coexistence with the experience of pleasure and pain as fruits of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> would follow.

children.text:
% viparyayasya cānanumānāt/] p.230
syān matam --- saṃsārāvasthasya śarīrādisambandho nityasukhasaṃvedanahetoḥ pratibandhakaḥ, tenāviśeṣo nāstīti/ etac cāyuktam, śarīrādayaḥ upabhogārthās te bhogapratibandhaṃ kariṣyantīty anupapannam; na cāsty anumānam aśarīrasyātmano bhogaḥ kaścid astīti/
children.translated_text: One might think: the connection with body and the rest, for one in <s>saṃsāra</s>, is an obstructing cause [of eternal happiness], and therefore there is no lack of distinction. But this is untenable, since body and the rest are for the purpose of experience — it is absurd that they would obstruct experience; and there is no inference that the <s>ātman</s> (self) without a body has any experience whatsoever.

children.text:
% p.231
iṣṭādhigamārthā pravṛttir iti cet? na, aniṣṭoparamārthatvāt/ idam anumānam --- iṣṭādhigamārtho mokṣopadeśaḥ pravṛttiś ca mumukṣūṇām, nobhayam anarthakam iti/ etac cāyuktam, aniṣṭoparamārtho mokṣopadeśaḥ pravṛttiś ca mumukṣūṇām iti/ neṣṭam aniṣṭenānanuviddhaṃ sambhavatīti iṣṭam apy aniṣṭaṃ sampadyate, aniṣṭahānāya ghaṭamāna iṣṭam api jahāti, vivekahānasyāśakyatvād iti/
dṛṣṭātikramaś ca dehādiṣu tulyaḥ/ yathā dṛṣṭam anityaṃ sukhaṃ parityajya nityaṃ sukhaṃ kāmayate, evaṃ dehendriyabuddhīr anityā dṛṣṭā atikramya muktasya nityā dehendriyabuddhayaḥ kalpayitavyāḥ, sādhīyaś caivaṃ muktasya caikātmyaṃ kalpitaṃ bhavatīti/
upapattiviruddham iti cet? samānam/ dehādīnāṃ nityatvaṃ pramāṇaviruddhaṃ kalpayitum aśakyam iti? samānaṃ sukhasyāpi nityatvaṃ pramāṇaviruddhaṃ kalpayitum aśakyam iti/
ātyantike ca saṃsāraduḥkhābhāve sukhavacanād āgame 'pi saty avirodhaḥ/ yady api kaścid āgamaḥ syāt muktasyātyantikaṃ sukham iti?
children.translated_text:
If it is objected that activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is for the purpose of attaining the desired? No, because it is for the purpose of the cessation of the undesired. This is the inference: 'The instruction on <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is for the purpose of attaining the desired, and the activity of those seeking liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) likewise — neither of these two is purposeless.' But this is incorrect, (because) the instruction on <s>mokṣa</s> and the activity of those seeking liberation are for the purpose of the cessation of the undesired. Since the desired cannot exist without being pervaded by the undesired, even the desired becomes undesired; one who strives to abandon the undesired abandons even the desired, because the abandonment of discrimination is impossible.
And the transgression of what is observed is the same with regard to the body and the rest. Just as, having abandoned observed impermanent pleasure, one desires permanent pleasure — so too, having transcended the body, sense-organs, and intellects that are observed to be impermanent, the liberated one's body, sense-organs, and intellects must be posited as permanent; and in this way, the identity of the liberated one is also better posited.
If it is objected that this contradicts reasoning? The same (objection applies to you). That the permanence of body and the rest is impossible to posit because it contradicts the means of valid knowledge? Equally, the permanence of pleasure is impossible to posit because it contradicts the means of valid knowledge.
And when there is the absolute absence of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), there is no contradiction even if a scripture uses the word 'pleasure.' Even if some scripture should say 'the liberated one has absolute pleasure' —

children.text:
% kaścid āgamaḥ syāt muktasyātyantikaṃ sukham iti?] p.232
sukhaśabda ātyantike duḥkhābhāve prayukta ity evam upapadyate, dṛṣṭo hi duḥkhābhāve sukhaśabdaprayogo bahulaṃ loka iti/
nityasukharāgasyāprahāṇe mokṣādhigamābhāvaḥ, rāgasya bandhanasamājñānāt/ yady ayaṃ mokṣo nityaṃ sukham abhivyajyata iti, nityasukharāgeṇa mokṣāya ghaṭamāno na mokṣam adhigacchet, nādhigantum arhatīti/ bandhanasamājñāto hi rāgaḥ/ na ca bandhane saty api kaścin mukta ity upapadyata iti/
prahīṇanityasukharāgasyāpratikūlatvam/ athāsya nityasukharāgaḥ prahīyate, tasmin prahīṇe nāsya nityasukharāgaḥ pratikūlo bhavati? yady evam, muktasya nityaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati, athāpi na bhavati, nāsyobhayoḥ pakṣayor mokṣādhigamo vikalpyate iti//22//
children.translated_text:
some scripture should say 'the liberated one has absolute pleasure'? — it can be explained that the word 'pleasure' (<s>sukha</s>) is used in the sense of the absolute absence of suffering, for the use of the word 'pleasure' in the absence of suffering is seen to be common in the world.
If the craving for permanent pleasure is not abandoned, there is no attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), because craving is recognized as bondage. If one thinks 'this <s>mokṣa</s> manifests permanent pleasure,' then one who strives for <s>mokṣa</s> with a craving for permanent pleasure would not attain <s>mokṣa</s>, nor would he deserve to attain it. For craving is recognized as bondage. And it is not established that anyone is liberated while bondage still exists.
For one who has abandoned the craving for permanent pleasure, (that pleasure) is not adverse. Now, if his craving for permanent pleasure is abandoned — when that is abandoned, is his craving for permanent pleasure not adverse (to him)? If so, then the liberated one has permanent pleasure; but if not, neither in either of these two positions is the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> to be conceived. // 22 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.23]

children.text:
% p.233
sthānavata eva tarhi saṃśayasya lakṣaṇaṃ vācyam iti tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Then the definition of doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) must be stated only for that which has a legitimate basis — and so it is stated:
[Page break]

children.text: NyS_1,1.23: samānānekadharmopapatter vipratipatter upalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthātaś ca viśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.23: Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) is an inquiry that depends on a specific difference, arising from the apprehension of common and multiple properties, from conflicting testimony, and from the irregularity of perception and non-perception.

children.text:
samānadharmopapatter viśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśaya iti/ sthāṇupuruṣayoḥ samānaṃ dharmam ārohapariṇāhau paśyan pūrvadṛṣṭaṃ ca tayor viśeṣam bubhutsamānaḥ kiṃsvid ity anyataraṃ nāvadhārayati, tadanavadhāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ/ samānam anayor dharmam upalabhe viśeṣam anyatarasya nopalabha ity eṣā buddhir apekṣā ---
% nopalabha ity eṣā buddhir apekṣā ---] p.240
saṃśayasya pravṛttikā vartate, tena viśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ/
anekadharmopapatter iti/ samānajātīyam asamānajātīyaṃ cānekam/ tasyānekasya dharmopapatteḥ ---
children.translated_text:
Doubt is an inquiry that depends on a specific difference, arising from the apprehension of common properties. Perceiving the common properties of height and girth in a post and a person, and wishing to know the difference between them that was previously observed, one does not ascertain either one, (thinking) 'What is it?' — that non-ascertainment, that cognition, is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>). 'I perceive the common property of these two; I do not perceive the specific property of either one' — this cognition is the expectation (<s>apekṣā</s>) — it operates as the cause of doubt; hence, doubt is an inquiry that depends on a specific difference.
'Arising from the apprehension of multiple properties' (<s>anekadharmopapatti</s>): the 'multiple' means both of the same kind (<s>samānajātīya</s>) and of different kinds (<s>asamānajātīya</s>). From the apprehension of those multiple properties —

children.text:
% dharmopapatteḥ ---] p.244
viśeṣasyobayathā dṛṣṭatvāt/ samānajātīyebhyo 'samānajātīyebyaś cārthā viśiṣyante, gandhavattvāt pṛthivy abādhibyo viśiṣyate guṇakarmabhyaś ca / asti ca śabde vibhāgajanyatvaṃ viśeṣaḥ/ tasmin dravyaṃ guṇaḥ karma veti sandehaḥ, viśeṣasyobayathā dṛṣṭatvāt/
children.translated_text: because the specific difference is seen in both ways. Objects are distinguished from those of the same kind and from those of different kinds: earth is distinguished from other (elements) by possessing smell (<s>gandhavatva</s>), and also from qualities and actions. And in sound there exists the specific property of being produced by disjunction (<s>vibhāgajanyatva</s>). Regarding that (sound), the doubt arises: 'Is it a substance, a quality, or an action?' — because the specific difference is seen in both ways.

children.text:
% -tvāt] p.249
kiṃ dravyasya sato guṇakarmabhyo viśeṣaḥ, āhosvid guṇasya sata iti, atha karmaṇaḥ sata iti? viśeṣāpekṣā --- anyatamasya vyavasthāpakaṃ dharma nopalaba iti buddhir iti/
vipratipatter iti/ vyāhatam ekārthadarśanaṃ vipratipattiḥ, vyāghātaḥ --- virodho 'sahabhāva iti/ asty ātmety ekaṃ darśanam, nāsty ātmety aparam, na ca sadbhāvāsadbhāvau sahaikatra sambhavataḥ, na cānyatarasādhako hetur upalabhyate, tatra tattvānavadhāraṇaṃ saṃśaya iti/
upalabdhyavayavasthātaḥ khalv api sac codakam upalabhyate taḍāgādiṣu, marīciṣu cāvidyamānam udakam iti, ataḥ kvacid upalabhyamāne tattvavyavasthāpakasya pramāṇasyānupalabdheḥ kiṃ sad upalabhyate 'thāsad iti saṃśayo bhavati/
anupalabdhyavyavasthātaḥ/ sac ca nopalabyate mūlakīlakodakādi, asac cānutpannaṃ niruddhaṃ vā,
children.translated_text:
Is it the specific difference of a substance that exists, or of a quality, or of an action? The expectation of a specific difference — the cognition 'I do not perceive the property that would establish any one of them' — (this is the basis of doubt).
'From conflicting testimony' (<s>vipratipatti</s>): conflicting testimony is contradictory perception of a single object; the contradiction is incompatibility (<s>asahabhāva</s>). 'The <s>ātman</s> (self) exists' is one view; 'the <s>ātman</s> does not exist' is another; and existence and non-existence cannot co-exist in a single (entity); and no reason establishing either one is perceived — there, the non-ascertainment of the truth is doubt.
Also from the irregularity of perception: water is indeed perceived to exist in ponds and the like, and in mirages, water that does not exist (appears to be perceived). Therefore, when something is perceived somewhere, since the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) that would establish the truth is not perceived — the doubt arises: 'Is what is perceived real or unreal?'
From the irregularity of non-perception: what exists is also sometimes not perceived — such as underground water and buried stakes —

children.text:
% nuruddhaṃ vā,] p.250
tataḥ kvacid anupalabhyamāne saṃśayaḥ, kiṃ san nopalabyate utāsad iti saṃśayo bhavati/ viśeṣāpekṣā pūrvavat/
pūrvaḥ samāno 'nekaś ca dharmo jñeyasthaḥ, upalabdhyanupalabdhī punar jñātṛsthe, etāvatā viśeṣeṇa punarvacanam/
children.translated_text:
and what does not exist — being either unproduced or destroyed — (is also not perceived). Therefore, when something is not perceived somewhere, the doubt arises: 'Is what is not perceived existent or non-existent?' The expectation of a specific difference is as before.
The first, common, and multiple properties pertain to the object of knowledge; perception and non-perception, however, pertain to the knower — with this distinction, the restatement (is made).

children.text:
% viśeṣeṇa punarvacanam/] p.255
samānadharmādhigamāt samānadharmopapatter viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣo vimarśa iti//23//
children.translated_text: From the apprehension of common properties, (doubt is) an inquiry that depends on the recollection of a specific difference, arising from the apprehension of common properties. // 23 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.24]
The same (principle applies): the definition is for those that have a legitimate basis.

children.text: NyS_1,1.24: yam arhtam adhikṛtya pravartate tat prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.24: That object with reference to which one acts is <s>prayojana</s> (purpose).

children.text: yam artham āptavyaṃ hātavyaṃ vā vyavasāya tadāptihānopāyam anutiṣṭhati, prayojanaṃ tad veditavyam, pravṛttihetutvāt/ imam artham āpsyāmi hāsyāmi veti vyavasāyo 'rthasyādhikāraḥ, evaṃ vyavasīyamāno 'rtho 'dhikriyata iti//24//
children.translated_text: That object which one resolves to obtain or abandon, and in accordance with which one follows the means of obtaining or abandoning it — that is to be known as <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), because it is the cause of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). The resolution 'I shall obtain this object' or 'I shall abandon it' is the dedication (<s>adhikāra</s>) to the object; an object that is thus resolved upon is 'dedicated to' (<s>adhikriyate</s>). // 24 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.25]

children.text: NyS_1,1.25: laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasminn arthe buddhisāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.25: That object in which the understanding of ordinary people and critical examiners is the same is <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example).

children.text: lokasāmānyam anatītā laukikā naisargikaṃ vainayikaṃ buddhyatiśayam aprāptāḥ/ tadviparītāḥ parīkṣakāḥ/ tarkeṇa pramāṇair arthaṃ parīkṣitum arhantīti/ yathā yam arthaṃ laukikā budhyante tathā parīkṣakā api,
children.translated_text: Ordinary people (<s>laukika</s>) are those who have not transcended worldly commonality and have not attained the superior intellect — whether innate or acquired through training. Critical examiners (<s>parīkṣaka</s>) are the opposite of these — those who are capable of examining objects by reasoning and by means of valid knowledge. That object which critical examiners understand in the same way as ordinary people —

children.text:
% yam arthaṃ laukikā ...] p.259
so 'rtho dṛṣṭāntaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntavirodhena hi pratipakṣāḥ pratiṣeddhavyā bhavantīti, dṛṣṭāntasamādhinā ca svapakṣāḥ sthāpanīyā bhavantīti, avayaveṣu codāharaṇāya kalpata iti//25//
children.translated_text: that object is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). For opposing positions must be refuted through contradiction with the example, and one's own positions must be established through concordance with the example; and it serves as illustration in the members (of the syllogism). // 25 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.26]

children.text:
% p.260
atha siddhāntaḥ, idam itthambhūtañ cety abhyanujñāyamānam arthajātaṃ siddham, siddhasya saṃsthitiḥ siddhāntaḥ, saṃsthitir itthambhāvavyavasthā dharmaniyamaḥ/
sa khalv ayam ---
children.translated_text:
Now, <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine): the body of objects that is acknowledged as 'this exists' and 'this is of such a nature' is <s>siddha</s> (established); the settled state (<s>saṃsthiti</s>) of what is established is <s>siddhānta</s>; the settled state is the definitive determination (<s>itthambhāvavyavasthā</s>), the delimitation of properties (<s>dharmaniyama</s>).
Now this (is stated) —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.26: <s>Siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) is the settled position (derived from) a system (<s>tantra</s>), a topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), or an assumption (<s>abhyupagama</s>).

children.text:
% p.261
tantrārthasaṃsthitiḥ tantrasaṃsthitiḥ, tantram itaretarābhisambaddhasyārthasamūhasyopadeśaḥ śāstram/ adhikaraṇānuṣaktārthasaṃsthitir adhikaraṇasaṃsthitiḥ, abhyupagamasaṃsthitir anavadhāritārthaparigrahaḥ, tadviśeṣaparīkṣaṇāyābhyupagamasiddhāntaḥ/
children.translated_text: The settled position of the meaning of a system is <s>tantrasaṃsthiti</s>; a system (<s>tantra</s>) is a treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) — the instruction of a body of interrelated subject-matter. The settled position of meaning connected to a topic is <s>adhikaraṇasaṃsthiti</s>. The settled position of an assumption is the provisional acceptance of an undetermined matter — for the purpose of examining its particular (aspects), there is the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (assumption-based doctrine).
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.27]

children.text:
tantrabhedāt tu khalu
  NyS_1,1.27: sa caturvidhaḥ sarvatantrapratitantrādhikaraṇābhyupagamasaṃsthityarthāntarabhāvāt ||
children.translated_text:
And indeed, due to the differentiation of systems —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.27: That (<s>siddhānta</s>) is of four kinds, because of the difference between <s>sarvatantra</s> (universally accepted), <s>pratitantra</s> (system-specific), <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic-based), and <s>abhyupagamasaṃsthiti</s> (assumption-based) settled positions.
Among these, these four settled positions are real entities (<s>arthabhūta</s>). // 27 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.28]
Of these —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.28: An object that is acknowledged in a system and is not contradicted by any system is <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s> (universally accepted doctrine).

children.text: yathā ghrāṇādīnīnindriyāṇi gandhādaya indriyārhāḥ pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni pramāṇair arthasya grahaṇam iti//28//
children.translated_text: For example: the sense-organs beginning with smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), the sense-objects beginning with smell (<s>gandha</s>), the elements beginning with earth, and the apprehension of objects by means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). // 28 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.29]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.29: That which is established in a cognate system but not established in the specific system is <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (system-specific doctrine).

children.text: yathā nāsata ātmalābhaḥ, na sata ātmahānam, niratiśayāś cetanāḥ dehendriyamanaḥsu viṣayeṣu tattatkāraṇeṣu ca viśeṣa iti sāṅkhyānām, puruṣakarmādinimitto bhūtasargaḥ, karmahetavo doṣāḥ pravṛttiś ca, svaguṇaviśiṣṭāś cetanāḥ, asad utpadyate utpannaṃ nirudhyata iti yogānām//29//
children.translated_text: For example: 'There is no origination from non-existence; there is no destruction of what exists; consciousnesses are unsurpassed; and there is a specific difference among the body, sense-organs, mind, sense-objects, and their respective causes' — these are (doctrines) of the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>. 'The creation of beings is caused by the <s>karma</s> (action) of the individual (<s>puruṣa</s>); defects (<s>doṣa</s>) and activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) are caused by <s>karma</s>; consciousnesses are distinguished by their own specific qualities; what does not exist arises (into existence), and what has arisen is destroyed' — these are (doctrines) of the <s>Yogas</s>. // 29 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.30]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.30: That whose establishment leads to the establishment of another topic is <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (topic-based doctrine).

children.text: yasyārhtasya siddhāv anye 'rthā anuṣajyante, na tair vinā so 'rthaḥ sidhyati te 'rthā yadadhiṣṭhānāḥ so 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntaḥ,
children.translated_text: That object whose establishment is accompanied by other objects — that object cannot be established without them — those objects which are its foundation constitute the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s>,

children.text:
% -ṣṭhānāḥ so 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntaḥ,] p.265
yathā dehendriyavyatirikto jñātā ``darśanasparśanābhyām ekārthagrahaṇād'' iti atrānuṣaṅgiṇo 'rthā indriyanānātvaṃ niyataviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi svaviṣayagrahaṇaliṅgāni jñātur jñānasādhanāni, gandhādiguṇavyatiriktaṃ dravyaṃ guṇādhikaraṇam aniyataviṣayāś cetanā iti pūrvārthasiddhāv ete 'rhāḥ sidhyanti na tair vinā so 'rthaḥ sambhavatīti//30//
children.translated_text: for example: 'The knower is distinct from the body and sense-organs, because of the apprehension of a single object by sight and touch.' Here the ancillary objects are: the plurality of sense-organs, that the sense-organs have determinate objects, that the sense-organs are the marks of the apprehension of their own objects, that they are the instruments of knowledge for the knower, that substance is distinct from qualities such as smell etc. and is the substratum of qualities, and that consciousnesses have indeterminate objects. Upon the establishment of the primary object, these objects are established; and without them, that object is not possible. // 30 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.31]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.31: The examination of the specific (aspects) of what has been provisionally accepted without examination is <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (assumption-based doctrine).

children.text: yatra kiñcid arthajātam aparīkṣitam abhyupagamyate, astu dravyaṃ śabdaḥ sa tu nityo 'thānitya iti? dravyasya sato nityatānityatā vā tadviśeṣaḥ parīkṣyate, so 'bhyupagamasiddhāntaḥ svabuddhyatiśayacikhyāpayiṣayā parabuddhyavajñānāc ca pravartata iti//31//
children.translated_text: Where a certain body of objects is provisionally accepted without examination — 'Let it be that sound is a substance — but is it permanent or impermanent?' — the specific aspect of the substance that exists, whether its permanence or impermanence, is examined. That is the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s>; it proceeds from the desire to display one's own intellectual superiority and from the disdain for the opponent's intellect. // 31 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.32]
Now the members (<s>avayavas</s>) (of the syllogism) —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.32: The members (of the syllogism) are thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>).

children.text: daśāvayavān eke naiyāyikā vākye sañcakṣate, jijñāsā saṃśayaḥ śakyaprāptiḥ prayojanaṃ saṃśayavyudāsa iti, te kasmān nocyanta iti/ tatrāpratīyamāne 'rthe pratyayārthasya pravartikā jijñāsā/
children.translated_text: Some <s>Naiyāyikas</s> maintain that there are ten members in a sentence — adding inquiry (<s>jijñāsā</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), capacity of attainment (<s>śakyaprāpti</s>), purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), and removal of doubt (<s>saṃśayavyudāsa</s>). Why are these not stated (as separate members)? Among these, inquiry (<s>jijñāsā</s>) is that which, when an object is not being cognized, impels toward the cognition of that object.

children.text:
% jijñāsā/]ü@p.270
apratīyamānam arthaṃ kasmāj jijñāsate? taṃ tattvato jñātaṃ hāsyāmi vopādāsya upekṣiṣye veti/ tā etā hānopādānopekṣābuddhayas tattvajñānasyārthaṣ tadartham(corr.; -rthaḥ, stadartham, ed.) ayaṃ jijñāsate/ sā khalv ayam asādhanam arthasyeti/ jijñāsādhiṣṭhānaṃ saṃśayaś ca vyāhatadharmopasaṅghātāt tattvajñāne pratyāsannaḥ, vyāhatayor hi dharmayor anyataratattvaṃ bhavitum arhatīti/ sa pṛthag upadiṣṭo 'py asādhanam arthasyeti/ pramātuḥ pramāṇāni prameyādhigamārthāni, sā śakyaprāptir na sādhakasya vākyasya bhāgena yujyate pratijñādivad iti/ prayojanaṃ tattvāvadhāraṇam arthasādhakasya vākyasya phalaṃ naikadeśa iti/ saṃśayavyudāsaḥ pratipakṣopavarṇanaṃ tatpratiṣedhena tattvajñānābhyanujñānārtham, na tv ayaṃ sādhakavākyaikadeśa iti/ prakaraṇe tu jijñāsādayaḥ samarthā avadhāraṇīyārthopakārāt/
children.translated_text: Why does one inquire about an object that is not yet perceived? 'Having truly known it, I will either abandon it, or adopt it, or disregard it.' These cognitions of abandonment, adoption, and disregard are the purpose of true knowledge — it is for this purpose that one inquires. That (inquiry) indeed is not the means of establishing the object. And <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), the basis of inquiry, is proximate to true knowledge due to the conjunction of contradictory properties, for of two contradictory properties, one must be the truth. That (doubt), though mentioned separately, is not the means of establishing the object. The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) of the knower are for the purpose of apprehending the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge); this attainment is possible (only through them) and is not fittingly a part of the establishing statement, like the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) and the rest. <s>Prayojana</s> (purpose) — namely, the ascertainment of truth — is the fruit of the statement that establishes the object, not a constituent part. The removal of doubt through the description of the counter-position and its refutation is for the sake of granting assent to true knowledge, but this too is not a constituent part of the establishing statement. However, in the context (of a treatise), inquiry and the rest are efficacious because they contribute to the object to be ascertained.

children.text:
% tu jijñāsadayaḥ samarthā avadhāraṇīyārthopakārāt/] p.271
tattvārthasādhakabhāvāt tu pratijñādayaḥ sādhakavākyasya bhāgā ekadeśā avayavā iti// 32 //
children.translated_text: But because they serve to establish the true object, the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) and the rest are parts — constituent portions — members of the establishing statement. // 32 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.33]
Of these, as they are to be individually distinguished —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.33: The statement of what is to be proved is the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>).

children.text: prajñāpanīyena dharmeṇa dharmiṇo viśiṣṭasya parigrahavacanaṃ pratijñā sādhyanirdeśaḥ anityaḥ śabda iti//33//
children.translated_text: The statement of acceptance of the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) as qualified by the property (<s>dharma</s>) that is to be established is the thesis — the statement of what is to be proved. (Example:) 'Sound is impermanent.' // 33 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.34]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.34: The <s>hetu</s> (reason) is what accomplishes the proof of what is to be proved, by virtue of similarity with the example.

children.text: udāharaṇena sāmānyāt sādhyasya dharmasya sādhanaṃ prajñāpanaṃ hetuḥ, sādhye pratisandhāya dharmam udāharaṇe ca pratisandhāya tasya sādhanatāvacanaṃ hetuḥ utpattidharmakatvād iti/
children.translated_text: The <s>hetu</s> (reason) is the means of establishing — that is, making known — the property to be proved, through what is common with the example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>). Having connected the property with what is to be proved and also having connected it with the example, the statement of its capacity to establish is the reason — (for example:) 'because it has the property of being produced.'

children.text:
% pratisandhāya dharmam ... utpatti-] p.284
% -dharmakatvād iti/] p.288
utpattidharmakam anityaṃ dṛṣṭam iti// 34 //
children.translated_text: What has the property of being produced has been observed to be impermanent. // 34 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.35]

children.text:
% p.290
kim etāvad dhetulakṣaṇam iti? nety ucyate/ kiṃ tarhi?
children.translated_text: Is this the only definition of <s>hetu</s> (reason)? No, it is said. What then?
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.35: Likewise, (it is a reason) by virtue of dissimilarity.

children.text: udāharaṇavaidharmyāc ca sādhyasādhanaṃ hetuḥ/ katham? anityaḥ śabda utpattidharmakatvāt, anutpattidharmakaṃ nityaṃ yathātmādidravyam iti//35//
children.translated_text: The <s>hetu</s> (reason) also accomplishes the proof of what is to be proved through dissimilarity with the example. How? 'Sound is impermanent, because it has the property of being produced. What does not have the property of being produced is permanent — like the <s>ātman</s> (self) and other substances.' // 35 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.36]
[Page break]

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.36: An example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is a case (illustration) which, by virtue of possessing properties in common with what is to be proved, implies the possession of those properties (in the subject).

children.text: sādhyena sādharmyaṃ samānadharmatā/ sādhyasādharmyāt kāraṇāt taddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta iti/
children.translated_text: Similarity with what is to be proved means having the same properties. The example is that which, because of its similarity with what is to be proved, implies the possession of those properties.

children.text:
% dṛṣṭānta iti/] p.308
tasya dharmas taddharmaḥ, tasya --- sādhyasya/ sādhyaṃ ca dvividhaṃ dharmiviśiṣṭo vā dharmaḥ śabdasyānityatvam, dharmaviśiṣṭo vā dharmy anityaḥ śabda iti/ ihottaraṃ tadgrahaṇena gṛhyata iti/ kasmāt? pṛthagdharmavacanāt/ tasya dharmas taddharmas tasya bhāvas taddharmabhāvaḥ sa yasmin dṛṣṭānte vartate sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhyasādharmyād utpattidharmakatvat taddharmabhāvī bhavati, sa codāharaṇam iṣyate/ tatra yad utpadyate tad utpattidharmakam/ tac ca bhūtvā na bhavati ātmānaṃ jahāti nirudhyata ity anityam/ evam utpattidharmakatvaṃ sādhanam anityatvaṃ sādhyam/
children.translated_text: 'Its property' is '<s>taddharma</s>' — 'its' meaning 'of what is to be proved.' And what is to be proved is twofold: either the property as qualified by the subject — namely, the impermanence of sound; or the subject as qualified by the property — namely, impermanent sound. Here, the latter is taken by the pronoun 'tat.' Why? Because the property is mentioned separately. 'Its property' is '<s>taddharma</s>'; 'the existence of that' is '<s>taddharmabhāva</s>'; that in which this exists — that example — is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration). That which, by virtue of similarity with what is to be proved — namely, having the property of being produced — implies the possession of those properties, is the example. There, what is produced has the property of being produced. And that which, having come into being, ceases to be — abandons itself, is destroyed — is impermanent. Thus, the property of being produced is the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), and impermanence is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text:
% p.309
so 'yam ekasmin dvayor dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ sādharmyād vyavasthita upalabhyate, taṃ dṛṣṭānta upalabhamānaḥ śabde 'py anuminoti --- śabdo 'py utpattidharmakatvād anityaḥ sthālyādivad iti, udāhriyate 'nena dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāva ity udāharaṇam//36//
children.translated_text: This relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof, established through similarity in a single (example) for two properties, is perceived. Perceiving this in the example, one then infers the same for sound: 'Sound too is impermanent, because it has the property of being produced — like a pot and similar things.' Since it is through this that the relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof is illustrated, it is called <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration/example). // 36 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.37]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.37: Or the opposite, by virtue of the opposite (properties).

children.text: dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam iti prakṛtam/ sādhyavaidharmyād ataddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam iti/ anityaḥ śabda utpattidharmakatvāt anutpattidharmakaṃ nityam ātmādi, so 'yam ātmādir dṛṭṣṭāntaḥ sādhyavaidharmyād anutpattidharmakatvād ataddharmabhāvī --- yo 'sau sādhyasya dharmo 'nityatvaṃ sa tasmin na bhavatīti/
children.translated_text: 'A case (illustration) which is an example' — this is the subject under discussion. An example which, by virtue of dissimilarity with what is to be proved, implies the non-possession of those properties — that is the (negative) <s>udāharaṇa</s>. (Example:) 'Sound is impermanent, because it has the property of being produced. What does not have the property of being produced is permanent — like the <s>ātman</s> and other substances.' Here, the <s>ātman</s> and the rest constitute the example which, by virtue of dissimilarity with what is to be proved — namely, not having the property of being produced — implies the non-possession of those properties: the property of what is to be proved, namely impermanence, does not exist in it.

children.text:
% dharmo 'nityatvaṃ ...] p.310
atrātmādau dṛṣṭānta utpattidharmakatvasyābhāvād anityatvaṃ na bhavatīty upalabhamānaḥ śabde viparyayam anuminoty utpattidharmakatvasya bhāvād anityaḥ śabda iti/ sādharmyoktasya hetoḥ sādhyasādharmyāt taddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam/ vaidharmyoktasya hetoḥ sādhyavaidharmyād ataddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam/
children.translated_text: In this case, perceiving in the example of the <s>ātman</s> and the rest that due to the absence of the property of being produced, impermanence does not obtain, one infers the contrary for sound: because of the presence of the property of being produced, sound is impermanent. For the reason stated through similarity, the example possessing properties in common with what is to be proved, implying the possession of those properties, is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. For the reason stated through dissimilarity, the example possessing properties contrary to what is to be proved, implying the non-possession of those properties, is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>.

children.text:
% p.311
pūrvasmin dṛṣṭānte yau tau dharmau sādhyasādhanabhūtau paśyati sādhye 'pi tayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvam anuminoti/ uttarasmin dṛṣṭānte tayor dharmayor ekasyābhāvād itarasyābhāvaṃ paśyati tayor ekasya bhāvād itarasya bhāvaṃ sādhye 'numinotīti/ tad etad dhetuvābhāseṣu na sambhavatīty ahetavo hetvābhāsāḥ/
children.translated_text: In the first example, one perceives the two properties as standing in the relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof, and then infers the same relationship of these two properties in the subject to be proved. In the second example, one perceives that due to the absence of one of the two properties, the other is also absent, and infers that due to the presence of the one, the other is present in the subject. This does not occur in <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) — hence they are non-reasons, mere semblances of reasons.

children.text:
% na sambhavatīty ahetavo hetvābhāsāḥ/] p.312
tad idaṃ hetūdāharaṇayoḥ sāmarthyaṃ paramasūkṣmaṃ duḥkhabodhaṃ paṇḍitarūpavedanīyam iti//37//
children.translated_text: This capacity of the reason and the example is extremely subtle, difficult to comprehend, and to be understood (only) by those who have the form of scholars. // 37 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.38]
[Page break]

children.text: NyS_1,1.38: udāharaṇāpekṣas tathety upasaṃhāro na tatheti vā sādhyasyopanayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.38: The <s>upanaya</s> (application) is the subsumption of what is to be proved (under the example), with reference to the example, as 'so it is' or 'it is not so.'

children.text: udāharaṇāpekṣa udāharaṇatantra udāharaṇavaśaḥ/ vaśaḥ sāmarthyam/ sādhyasādharmyayukte udāharaṇe sthālyādi dravyam utpattidharmakam anityaṃ dṛṣṭam, tathā śabda utpattidharmaka iti sādhyasya śabdasyotpattidharmakatvam upasaṃhriyate/
children.translated_text: 'With reference to the example' means 'dependent on the example, governed by the example.' 'Governed' means 'capacity.' In an example connected with similarity to what is to be proved: 'A substance such as a pot, having the property of being produced, has been observed to be impermanent' — 'so too sound has the property of being produced' — thus the property of being produced is subsumed under sound, which is what is to be proved.

children.text:
% utpattidharmaka iti ...] p.314
sādhyavaidharmyayukte punar udāharaṇa ātmādi dravyam anutpattidharmakaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭam, na ca tathā śabda iti, anutpattidharmakatvasyopasaṃhārarapratiṣedhenotpattidharmakatvam upasaṃhriyate/ tad idam upasaṃhāradvaitam udāharaṇadvaitād bhavati/ upasaṃhriyate 'neneti copasaṃhāro veditavya iti//38//
children.translated_text: In an example connected with dissimilarity to what is to be proved: 'A substance such as the <s>ātman</s>, not having the property of being produced, has been observed to be permanent; but sound is not so' — through the denial of the subsumption of 'not having the property of being produced,' the property of being produced is subsumed. This duality of subsumption arises from the duality of examples. And <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (subsumption) should be understood as 'that by which subsumption is made.' // 38 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.39]

children.text:
% p.315
dvividhasya punar hetor dvividhasya codāharaṇasyopasaṃhāradvaite ca samānam ---
children.translated_text: Given the twofold reason and the twofold example, and the duality of subsumption, what is common (to all) —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.39: The restatement of the thesis, on the basis of the reason, is the <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion).

children.text: sādharmyokte vā vaidharmyokte vā yathodāharaṇam upasaṃhriyate, tasmād utpattidharmakatvād anityaḥ śabda iti nigamanam --- nigamyante 'neneti pratijñāhetūdāharaṇopanayā ekatreti nigamanam/ nigamyante --- samarthyante --- sambadhyante/ tatra sādharmokte tāvad dhetau vākyam anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñā/ utpattidharmakatvād iti hetuḥ/ utpattidharmakaṃ sthālyādi dravyam anityam ity udāharaṇam/ tathā cotpattidharmakaḥ śabda ity upanayaḥ/ tasmād utpattidharmakatvād anityaḥ śabda iti nigamanam/ vaidharmyokte 'py anityaḥ śabda utpattidharmakatvāt,
children.translated_text: Whether through the reason stated by similarity or by dissimilarity, after subsumption according to the example — 'Therefore, because of having the property of being produced, sound is impermanent' — this is the <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion). It is 'that by which they are concluded' — the thesis, reason, example, and application are brought together into one — that is the conclusion. 'Concluded' means 'rendered capable,' 'connected.' In the case of the reason stated by similarity, the statement (is as follows): 'Sound is impermanent' — this is the thesis. 'Because it has the property of being produced' — this is the reason. 'A substance such as a pot, having the property of being produced, is impermanent' — this is the example. 'And so too sound has the property of being produced' — this is the application. 'Therefore, because of having the property of being produced, sound is impermanent' — this is the conclusion. Similarly, with the reason stated by dissimilarity: 'Sound is impermanent, because it has the property of being produced;

children.text:
% utpattidharmakatvāt,] p.316
anutpattidharmakam ātmādi dravyaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭam, na ca tathānutpattidharmakaḥ śabdaḥ tasmād utpattidharmakatvād anityaḥ śabda iti/
avayavasamudāye ca vākye sambhūyetaretarābhisambandhāt pramāṇāny arthān sādhayantīti/ sambhavas tāvat śabdaviṣayā pratijñā, āptopadeśasya pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ pratisandhānād anṛṣeś ca svātantryānupapatteḥ/ anumānaṃ hetuḥ, udāharaṇe sādṛśyapratipatteḥ/ tac codāharaṇabhāṣye vyākhyātam/ pratyakṣaviṣayam udāharaṇaṃ dṛṣṭenādṛṣṭasiddheḥ/ upamānam upanayaḥ tathety upasaṃhārāt, na ca tatheti vopamānadharmapratiṣedehe viparītadharmopasaṃhārasiddheḥ/ sarveṣām ekārthapratipattau sāmarthyapradarśanaṃ nigamanam iti/
itaretarābhisambandho 'pi --- asatyāṃ pratijñāyām anāśrayā hetvādayo na pravarteran/
children.translated_text:
a substance such as the <s>ātman</s>, not having the property of being produced, has been observed to be permanent; but sound does not so lack the property of being produced — therefore, because of having the property of being produced, sound is impermanent.'
And in the complete collection of members forming a single statement, the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge), by being mutually connected, establish their objects. The plausibility: the thesis is in the domain of verbal testimony, since the teaching of trustworthy persons is coordinated with perception and inference, and since an unreliable person has no independent validity. Inference is the reason, since similarity is apprehended in the example. And this has been explained in the commentary on the example. The example is in the domain of perception, since what is unseen is established through what is seen. The application is comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), since subsumption is made as 'so it is'; and in the denial 'it is not so' — through the denial of the property of the standard of comparison, the subsumption of the contrary property is established. The demonstration of the capacity of all (members) for apprehending a single meaning is the conclusion.
And their mutual connection: without the thesis, the reason and the rest would have no basis and would not operate.

children.text:
% p.317
asati hetau kasya sādhanabhāvaḥ pradarśyeta/ udāharaṇe sādhye ca kasyopasaṃhāraḥ syāt kasya cāpadeśāt pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ nigamanaṃ syād iti/ asaty udāharaṇe kena sādharmyaṃ vaidharmyaṃ vā sādhyasādhanam upādīyeta, kasya vā sādharmyavaśād upasaṃhāraḥ pravarteta/ upanayaṃ cāntareṇa sādhye 'nupasaṃhṛtaḥ sādhako dharmo nārthaṃ sādhayet/ nigamanābhāve cānabhiyuktasambandhānāṃ pratijñādīnām ekārthena pravartanaṃ tatheti pratipādanaṃ kasyeti/
athāvayavārthaḥ --- sādhyasya dharmasya dharmiṇā sambandhopādānaṃ pratijñārthaḥ/ udāharaṇena samānasya viparītasya vā sādhyasya dharmasya sādhakabhāvavacanaṃ hetvarthaḥ/ dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvapradarśanam ekatrodāharaṇārthaḥ/ sādhanabhūtasya dharmasya sādhyena dharmeṇa sāmānādhikaraṇyopapādanam upanayārthaḥ/ udāharaṇasthayor dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvopapattau sādhye viparītaprasaṅgapratiṣedhārthaṃ nigamanam/ nacaitasyāṃ hetūdāharaṇapariśuddhau satyāṃ sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalyāj jātinigrahasthānabahutvaṃ prakramate/ avyavasthāpya khalu dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvam udāharaṇe jātivādī pratyavatiṣṭhate/ vyavasthite tu khalu dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāve dṛṣṭāntasthe gṛhyamāṇe sādhanabhūtasya dharmasya hetutvenopādānaṃ na sādharmyamātrasya na vaidharmyamātrasya veti// 39 //
children.translated_text:
Without the reason, whose establishing nature would be demonstrated? Without the example and the subject to be proved, whose subsumption would there be, and on the basis of whose statement would there be a restatement of the thesis as the conclusion? Without the example, by what (basis) of similarity or dissimilarity would the means of proof be adopted, and by virtue of whose similarity would the subsumption proceed? Without the application, the establishing property, not being subsumed under the subject, would not establish the object. And in the absence of the conclusion, whose bringing together and whose demonstration of 'so it is' would there be for the thesis and the rest, whose connections are not (yet) established?
Now, the purpose of the members: the purpose of the thesis is the adoption of the connection of the property with the subject. The purpose of the reason is the statement of the establishing nature of a property that is similar to or contrary to (the property in) the example. The purpose of the example is the demonstration of the relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof with respect to the two properties in a single (instance). The purpose of the application is establishing the co-location of the establishing property with the property to be proved. The purpose of the conclusion is, given the establishment of the relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof of the two properties in the example, to preclude the contrary supposition with respect to the subject. And when this purification of reason and example has occurred through both similarity and dissimilarity, the multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> (futile objections) and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) does not arise, since there is no scope for objection. Indeed, the <s>jāti</s>-debater objects without establishing the relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof in the example. But when the relationship of what-is-to-be-proved and its means-of-proof is established and the example is grasped, the adoption of the establishing property as the reason (occurs) — not of mere similarity alone, nor of mere dissimilarity alone. // 39 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 1.1.40]

% p.320
ata ūrdhvaṃ tarko lakṣaṇīya ity athedam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: From this point onward, <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is to be defined; hence this is stated —

children.text: NyS_1,1.40: avijñātatattve 'rthe kāraṇopapattitas tattvajñānārtham ūhas tarkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.40: <s>Tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is the conjectural reasoning (<s>ūha</s>) for the purpose of true knowledge of an object whose truth is unknown, through the fitness of causes.

children.text: avijñāyamānatattve 'rthe jijñāsā tāvaj jāyate jānīyemam artham iti/ atha jijñāsitasya vastuno vyāhatau dharmau vibhāgena vimṛśati ---
children.translated_text: When the true nature of an object is not known, first there arises a desire to know — 'I should know this object.' Then one deliberates upon the two contradictory properties of the object to be known, distinguishing them —

children.text:
% jijñāsitasya vastuno ...] p.321
kiṃsvid ittham āhosvin nettham iti/ vimṛśyamānayor dharmayor ekaṃ kāraṇopapattyānujānāti, sambhavaty asmin kāraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ hetur iti kāraṇopapattyā syād evam etan netarad iti/
tatra nidarśanam --- yo 'yaṃ jñātā jñātavyam arthaṃ jānīte taṃ tattvato jānīyeti jijñāsā/ sa kim utpattidharmako 'thānutpattidharmaka iti vimarśaḥ/ vimṛśyamāne 'vijñātatatte 'rthe yasya dharmasyābhyanujñākāraṇam upapadyate tam anujānāti/ yady ayam anutpattidharmakaḥ, tataḥ svakṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalam anubhavati jñātā, duḥkhajanmapravṛttidoṣamithyājñānānām uttaram uttaraṃ pūrvasya pūrvasya kāraṇam, uttarottarāpāye tadanantarāpāyād apavarga iti syātāṃ saṃsārāpavargau/
children.translated_text: 'Is it thus, or is it not thus?' Of the two properties being deliberated upon, one is accepted through the fitness of a reason — a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), a <s>hetu</s> (reason), is possible in its case — and through the fitness of the reason [one concludes], 'It must be this way, not the other.' An illustration of this: the desire to know is 'May I know in truth that knower who knows the object to be known.' The deliberation is 'Is this [knower] subject to origination, or not subject to origination?' When the true nature of the object being deliberated upon is unknown, one accepts that property for which a reason supporting its acceptance is available. If this [knower] is not subject to origination, then the knower experiences the fruit of self-made <s>karma</s> (action); suffering, birth, activity, faults, and false knowledge — each subsequent one is the cause of the preceding one; and upon the removal of each subsequent one, the one immediately preceding it is also removed, resulting in <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — thus both <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and <s>apavarga</s> would be established.

children.text:
% -pavargau/] p.322
utpattidharmake jñātari punar na syātām/ utpannaḥ khalu jñātā dehendriyabuddhivedanābhiḥ sambadhyata iti nāsyedaṃ svakṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalam utpannaś ca bhūtvā na bhavatīti tasyāvidyamānasya niruddhasya vā svakṛtakarmaṇaḥ phalopabhogo nāsti/ tad evam ekasyānekaśarīrayogaḥ śarīraviyogaś cātyantaṃ na syād iti yatra kāraṇam anupapadyamānaṃ paśyati tan nānujānāti/ so 'yam evaṃlakṣaṇa ūhas tarka ity ucyate/
kathaṃ punar ayaṃ tattvajñānārtho na tattvajñānam eveti? anavadhāraṇāt/ anujānāty ayam ekataraṃ dharmaṃ kāraṇopapattyā, na tv avadhārayati na vyavasyati na niścinoti evam evedam iti/ kathaṃ tattvajñānārtha iti? tattvajñānaviṣayābhyanujñālakṣaṇānugrahabhāvitāt prasannād anatarapramāṇasāmarthyāt tattvajñānam utpadyata ity evaṃ tattvajñānārtha iti/
so 'yaṃ tarkaḥ pramāṇāni pratisandadhānaḥ pramāṇābhyanujñānāt pramāṇasahito vāde 'padiṣṭa ity avijñātatattvam anujānāti/
children.translated_text: But if the knower is subject to origination, neither [<s>saṃsāra</s> nor <s>apavarga</s>] would be established. For a knower who has originated becomes connected with body, sense organs, intellect, and sensations — thus this [experience] is not the fruit of self-made <s>karma</s> for him; and having originated, he ceases to exist — thus for him, being non-existent or destroyed, there is no enjoyment of the fruit of self-made <s>karma</s>. Therefore, in this way, the connection of one [self] with many bodies and the separation from bodies would absolutely not be established — thus where one sees that the reason is untenable, one does not accept [that position]. This, characterized in this manner, is called <s>ūha</s> (reasoning) or <s>tarka</s> (deliberation). But how is this 'for the purpose of knowledge of truth' and not itself 'knowledge of truth'? Because of non-determination. It accepts one of the two properties through the fitness of a reason, but it does not determine, does not ascertain, does not conclude that 'it is definitely thus.' How then is it 'for the purpose of knowledge of truth'? Because knowledge of truth arises from the subsequent force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that has been facilitated by the acceptance — which has the character of a favorable disposition — regarding the subject of knowledge of truth. This <s>tarka</s>, by coordinating the <s>pramāṇas</s>, accepts what is sanctioned by the <s>pramāṇas</s>; combined with <s>pramāṇa</s>, it is prescribed in <s>vāda</s> (debate) — and thus it accepts what is of unknown truth.

children.text:
% vāde 'padiṣṭa ...] p.323
yathā so 'rho bhavati tasya tathābhāvaḥ tattvam, aviparyayo yāthātathyam//40//
children.translated_text: That an object is as it [truly] is — that state of being as it is — is <s>tattva</s> (truth); non-falsity, conformity to reality. //40//
And regarding this subject of <s>tarka</s> (deliberation) —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,1.41: <s>Nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment) is the determination of an object by examining through thesis and counter-thesis.

children.text:
sthāpanā sādhanam, pratiṣedha upālambhaḥ/ tau sādhanopālambhau pakṣapratipakṣāśrayau vyatiṣaktāv anubandhena pravartamānau pakṣapratipakṣāv ity ucyete/ tayor anyatarasya nivṛttir ekatarasyāvasthānam avaśyambhāvi, yasyāvasthānaṃ tasyārthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ/
nedaṃ pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ sambhavatīti --- eko hi pratijñātam arthaṃ hetutaḥ sthāpayati pratiṣiddhaṃ coddharati dvitīyasya/ dvitīyena sthāpanāhetuḥ pratiṣidhyate tasyaiva pratiṣedhahetuś coddhriyate sa nivartate/
children.translated_text: <s>Sthāpanā</s> (establishment) is proof; <s>pratiṣedha</s> (refutation) is censure. These two — proof and censure — being based on thesis and counter-thesis, proceeding in mutual engagement through continuous connection, are called thesis and counter-thesis. Of the two, the cessation of one and the persistence of the other is inevitable; the determination of the object of the one that persists is <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment). This determination of an object through thesis and counter-thesis proceeds as follows: one person establishes the proposed object through a reason and also refutes the counter-thesis of the second; by the second, the reason for the establishment is refuted and its own reason for refutation is also overturned — it ceases.

children.text:
% tasyaiva pratiṣedhahetuś ...] p.330
tasya nivṛttau yo 'vatiṣṭhate tenārthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ/
ubhābhyām evārthāvadhāraṇam ity āha/ kayā yuktyā? ekasya sambhavo dvitīyasyāsambhavaḥ/ tāv etau sambhavāsambhavau vimarśaṃ saha nivarttayataḥ --- ubhayasambhave ubhayāsambhave vānivṛtto vimarśa iti/ vimṛśyeti vimarśaṃ kṛtvā/ so 'yaṃ vimarśaḥ pakṣapratipakṣāv avadyotya nyāyaṃ pravartayatīty upādīyata iti/ etac ca viruddhayor ekadharmisthayor boddhavyam/ yatra tu dharmisāmānyagatau viruddhau dharmau hetutaḥ sambhavataḥ tatra samuccayaḥ, hetuto 'rthasya tathābhāvopapatteḥ/ yathā --- kriyāvad dravyam iti lakṣaṇavacane yasya dravyasya kriyāyogo hetutaḥ sambhavati tat kriyāvat, yasya na sambhavati tad akriyam iti/ ekadharmisthayoś ca viruddhayor dharmayor ayugapadbhāvinoḥ kālavikalpaḥ/ yathā --- tad eva dravyaṃ kriyāyuktaṃ kriyāvat, anutpannoparatakriyaṃ punar akriyam iti/
na cāyaṃ nirṇaye niyamo vimṛśyaiva pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇaya iti, kiṃ tv indriyārthasannikarṣotpannapratyakṣe 'rthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇaya iti, parīkṣāviṣaye tu vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ/ vāde śāstre ca vimarśavarjam// 41 //
children.translated_text: Upon its cessation, the determination of the object by the one that stands — that is <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment). He says the determination of the object is through both [thesis and counter-thesis]. By what reasoning? Because one is possible and the other is impossible. These two — possibility and impossibility — bring the deliberation to an end together: when both are possible or both are impossible, the deliberation remains unresolved. 'Having deliberated' means having conducted the deliberation. This deliberation, by illuminating thesis and counter-thesis, sets the <s>nyāya</s> (logical method) in motion — hence it is employed. And this should be understood regarding two contradictory properties residing in one subject. But where two contradictory properties pertaining to a general class of subjects are both possible on the basis of reasons, there is a combination, since the object's being so is established through reasons. For example, in the definitional statement 'a substance possesses action' — that substance for which the connection with action is possible through a reason possesses action; that for which it is not possible is without action. And regarding two contradictory properties residing in one subject that do not occur simultaneously, there is a temporal distinction. For example, the very same substance, when conjoined with action, possesses action; when the action has not yet arisen or has ceased, it is without action. Nor is there a restriction that <s>nirṇaya</s> must always involve deliberating through thesis and counter-thesis; rather, determination of an object through perception arising from the contact of sense organ and object is also <s>nirṇaya</s>. But in the domain of investigation, the determination of an object by deliberating through thesis and counter-thesis is <s>nirṇaya</s>. In debate and in the treatise, [it occurs] without deliberation. //41//
Thus ends the first lesson of the first chapter in <s>Vātsyāyana</s>'s <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s>.
Second lesson.

children.text: tisraḥ kathā bhavanti --- vādo jalpo vitaṇḍā ceti/ tāsām ---
children.translated_text: There are three kinds of discourse: <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil). Of these —

children.text: NyS_1,2.1: pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pañcāvayavopapannaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraho vādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,2.1: <s>Vāda</s> (debate) is the adoption of thesis and counter-thesis, [supported] by proof and censure through <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) and <s>tarka</s> (reasoning), not contradicting established doctrine, and furnished with the five members [of a syllogism].

children.text: ekādhikaraṇasthau viruddhau dharmau pakṣapratipakṣau pratyanīkabhāvāt, asty ātmā nāsty ātmeti/
children.translated_text: Two contradictory properties residing in one subject are the thesis and counter-thesis, because of their mutual opposition — such as 'the <s>ātman</s> (self) exists' and 'the <s>ātman</s> does not exist.'

children.text:
% -tmeti] p.336
nānādhikaraṇasthau viruddhau na pakṣapratipakṣau, yathā --- nitya ātmā anityā buddhir iti/ parigraho 'bhyupagamavyavasthā/ so 'yam pakṣapratipakṣaparigraho vādaḥ/ tasya viśeṣanaṃ pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ, pramāṇais tarkeṇa ca sādhanam upālambhaś cāsmin kriyata iti/ sādhanaṃ sthāpanā/ upālambhaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ/ tau sādhanopālambhāv ubhayor api pakṣayor vyatiṣaktāv anubaddhau ca yāvad eko nivṛtta ekataro vyavasthita iti nivṛttasyopālambho vyavasthitasya sādhanam iti/
children.translated_text: Two contradictory [properties] residing in different subjects are not thesis and counter-thesis — for example, 'the <s>ātman</s> is eternal' and '<s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is non-eternal.' Adoption means agreement and commitment. This adoption of thesis and counter-thesis is <s>vāda</s> (debate). Its qualification is 'proof and censure through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' — meaning that in it, proof and censure are conducted through <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>tarka</s>. Proof is establishment; censure is refutation. These two — proof and censure — being mutually interlinked and connected with both theses, [continue] until one ceases and the other is established; the censure is of the one that ceases, and the proof is of the one that stands.

children.text:
% ubhayor api ... sādhanam iti/] p.339
jalpe nigrahasthānaviniyogād vāde tatpratiṣedhaḥ/ pratiṣedhe kasyacid abhyanujñānārthaṃ siddhāntāviruddha iti vacanam/
children.translated_text: Since in <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) there is the application of points of defeat, in <s>vāda</s> (debate) there is the prohibition of that. To indicate the acceptance of a certain [restriction] in this prohibition, the expression 'not contradicting established doctrine' is stated.

children.text:
% siddhāntāviruddha iti vacanam/] p.340
``siddhāntam abhyupetya tadvirodhī viruddha'' iti hetvābhāsasya nigrahasthānasyābhyanujñā vāde/ pañcāvayavopapanna iti
children.translated_text: 'That which contradicts an accepted <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) is called viruddha (contradictory)' — this is the acceptance of the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reason) as a point of defeat in <s>vāda</s>. 'Furnished with the five members' —

children.text:
% p.341
``hīnam anyatamenāpy avayavena nyūnam'' ``hetūdāharaṇādhikam adhikam'' iti caitayor abhyanujñānārtham iti/ avayaveṣu pramānatarkāntarbhāve pṛthak pramāṇatarkagrahaṇaṃ sādhanopālambhavyatiṣaṅgajñāpanārtham/ anyathobhāv api pakṣau sthāpanāpravṛttau vāda iti syāt/
children.translated_text: 'That which is deficient by even one member is nyūna (deficient)' and 'that which has more than the reason and example is adhika (redundant)' — this is stated for the purpose of accepting both of these [as points of defeat in <s>vāda</s>]. When <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> are included within the members [of the syllogism], the separate mention of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> is for the purpose of indicating their interlinking with proof and censure. Otherwise, both theses being engaged only in establishment would [also] constitute <s>vāda</s>.

children.text:
% pravṛttau vāda iti syāt/] p.342
antareṇāpi cāvayavasambandhaṃ pramāṇāny arthaṃ sādhayantīti dṛṣṭam, tenāpi kalpena sādhanopālambhau vāde bhavata iti jñāpayati/ ``chalajātinigrahasthānasādhanopālambho jalpa'' iti vacanād vinigraho jalpa iti mā vijñāyi, chalajātinigrahasthānasādhanopālambha eva jalpaḥ pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambho vād eveti mā vijñāyīty evamarthaṃ pṛthak pramānatarkagrahaṇam iti// 1 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is observed that <s>pramāṇas</s> establish an object even without the formal connection of syllogistic members; he indicates that proof and censure in <s>vāda</s> can also proceed in that manner. The separate mention of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> serves this purpose: lest it be understood from the statement '<s>jalpa</s> is proof and censure through <s>chala</s> (quibble), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat)' that any [discourse with] refutation is <s>jalpa</s>; and lest it be understood that only proof and censure through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> constitutes <s>jalpa</s>, while proof and censure through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> constitutes only <s>vāda</s>. //1//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,2.2: <s>Jalpa</s> (disputation) is that which is furnished as described [for <s>vāda</s>], with proof and censure through <s>chala</s> (quibble), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat).

children.text: yathoktopapanna iti, pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pañcāvayavopapannaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahaḥ/ chalajātinigrahasthānasādhanopālambha iti, chalajātinigrahasthānaiḥ sādhanam upālambhaś cāsmin kriyata iti evaṃviśeṣaṇo jalpaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Furnished as described' means: [having] proof and censure through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>, not contradicting established doctrine, furnished with the five members, and involving the adoption of thesis and counter-thesis. 'Proof and censure through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>' means: in it, proof and censure are conducted through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> — thus qualified, it is <s>jalpa</s>.

children.text:
% p.358
na khalu vai chalajātinigrahasthānaiḥ sādhanaṃ kasyacid arthasya sambhavati, pratiṣedhārthataivaiṣāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇe viśeṣalakṣaṇe ca śrūyate --- ``vacanavighāto 'rthavikalpopapattyā chalam'' iti ``sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānaṃ jātiḥ'' ``vipratipattir apratipattiś ca nigrahasthānam'' iti/
children.translated_text: Indeed, proof of any object through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> is not possible; their purpose of refutation alone is heard in both the general definition and the specific definitions: '<s>chala</s> is the disruption of speech through a distorted interpretation of meaning,' '<s>jāti</s> is a rejoinder based on similarity and dissimilarity,' and '<s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) is misunderstanding or failure to understand.'

children.text:
% -sthānam'' iti/] p.359
viśeṣalakṣaṇeṣv api yathāsvam iti/ na caitad vijānīyāt pratiṣedhārthatayaivārthaṃ sādhayantīti, chalajātinigrahasthānopālambho jalpa ity evam apy ucyamāne vijñāyata etad iti/
pramāṇaiḥ sādhanopālambhayoś chalajātinigrahasthānānām aṅgabhāvaḥ svapakṣarakṣaṇārthatvāt/ na svatantrāṇāṃ sādhanabhāvaḥ --- yat tat pramāṇair arthasya sādhanaṃ tatra chalajātinigrahasthānānām aṅgabhāvo rakṣaṇārthatvāt/ tāni hi prayujyamānāni parapakṣavighātena svapakṣaṃ rakṣanti/
children.translated_text: And in the specific definitions as well, each respectively. One should not understand that they prove an object solely through their purpose of refutation — even if one were to say '<s>jalpa</s> is censure through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>,' this [meaning] would be understood. [Rather,] <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> serve as auxiliaries to proof and censure through <s>pramāṇas</s>, since their purpose is the protection of one's own thesis. They do not independently serve as proof — the proof of an object through <s>pramāṇas</s> is where <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> serve as auxiliaries, for the purpose of protection. For when employed, they protect one's own thesis by disrupting the opponent's thesis.

children.text:
% -vighātena svapakṣaṃ rakṣanti/] p.360
tathā coktaṃ ``tattvādhyavasāyasaṃrakṣaṇāthaṃ jalpavitaṇḍe bījaprarohasaṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ kaṇṭakaśākhāvaraṇavat'' iti/ yaś cāsau pramāṇaiḥ pratipakṣasyopālambhas tasya caitāni prayujyamānāni pratiṣedhavighātāt sahakārīṇi bhavanti/ tad evam aṅgībhūtanāṃ chalādīnām upādānaṃ jalpe, na svatantrāṇāṃ sādhanabhāvaḥ/ upālambhe tu svātantryam apy astīti// 2 //
children.translated_text: As it has been said: '<s>Jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> are for the protection of the ascertainment of truth, like a fence of thorny branches for the protection of a growing seed.' And when one censures the counter-thesis through <s>pramāṇas</s>, these [<s>chala</s> etc.], when employed, become auxiliary by disrupting the refutation. Thus, in <s>jalpa</s>, the employment of <s>chala</s> and the rest is as auxiliaries, not as independent means of proof. But in censure, there is also independent [employment]. //2//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,2.3: That [<s>jalpa</s>], devoid of the establishment of a counter-thesis, is <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil).

children.text: sa jalpo vitaṇḍā bhavati/ kiṃviśeṣaṇaḥ? pratipakṣasthāpanayā hīnaḥ/ yau tau samānādhikaraṇau viruddhau dharmau pakṣāv ity uktaṃ tayor ekataraṃ vaitaṇḍiko na sthāpayatīti prapakṣapratiṣedhenaiva pravartata iti/
children.translated_text: That <s>jalpa</s> becomes <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil). With what qualification? Devoid of the establishment of a counter-thesis. Of the two co-located contradictory properties that have been called theses, the caviler does not establish either one — thus he proceeds only by refuting the opponent's thesis.

children.text:
% p.362
astu tarhi sa pratipakṣahīno vitaṇḍā? yad vai khalu tat parapratiṣedhalakṣaṇaṃ vākyaṃ sa vaitaṇḍikasya pakṣaḥ, na tv asau sādhyaṃ kañcid arthaṃ pratijñāya sthāpayatīti/ tasmād yathānyāsam evāstv iti// 3 //
children.translated_text: Then let it be: '<s>vitaṇḍā</s> is that which is devoid of a counter-thesis'? Indeed, that statement which has the character of refuting the opponent — that is the thesis of the caviler; but he does not establish it by proposing some object to be proved. Therefore, let it remain as originally stated. //3//

children.text:
% p.363
hetulakṣaṇābhāvād ahetavo hetusāmānyād dhetuvad ābhāsamānāḥ/ ta ime ---
children.translated_text: Being devoid of the characteristics of a valid reason, they are non-reasons; resembling reasons due to their generic similarity to reasons — these are:

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,2.4: The <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) are: <s>savyabhicāra</s> (erratic), <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (begging the question), <s>sādhyasama</s> (equivalent to what is to be proved), and <s>kālātīta</s> (untimely).
Of these —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1,2.5: The <s>savyabhicāra</s> (erratic) is that which is non-conclusive.

children.text: vyabhicāra ekatrāvyavasthitiḥ/ sahavyabhicāreṇa vartata iti svayabhicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Vyabhicāra</s> (deviation) is non-fixity in one [conclusion]. That which operates with deviation is <s>savyabhicāra</s> (erratic).

children.text:
% -cāraḥ] p.374
nidarśanam --- nityaḥ śabdo 'sparśatvāt, sparśavān kumbho 'nityo dṛṣṭaḥ na ca tathā sparśavān śabdas tasmād asparśatvān nityaḥ śabda iti/
children.translated_text:
[Page 374:]
Illustration: 'Sound is eternal because it is intangible; a pot, being tangible, is observed to be non-eternal; and sound is not likewise tangible — therefore, because of intangibility, sound is eternal.'

children.text:
% tathā sparśavān ...] p.375
dṛṣṭānte sparśavattvam anityatvaṃ ca dharmau na sādhyasādhanabhūtau gṛhyete sparśavāṃś cāṇur nityaś ceti/ ātmādau ca dṛṣṭānte
children.translated_text:
[Page 375:]
In the example, tangibility and non-eternality as properties are not grasped as standing in the relation of provable and prover — for an atom is tangible and yet eternal. And in the case of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) etc. as an example,

children.text:
% dṛṣṭānte] p.376
``udāharaṇasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanaṃ hetuḥ'' ity asparśatvād iti hetur nityatvaṃ vyabhicarati, asparśā buddhir anityā ceti/ evaṃ dvividhe 'pi dṛṣṭānte vyabhicārāt sādhyasādhanabhāvo nāstīti lakṣaṇābhāvād ahetur iti/
nityatvam apy eko 'nto 'nityatvam apy eko ṇta ekasminn ante vidyata iti aikāntikaḥ viparyayād anaikāntika ubhayāntavyāpakatvād iti// 5 //
children.translated_text:
[Page 376:]
'The reason is that which, through the similarity of the example, [establishes] the relation of provable and prover' — thus, the reason 'because of intangibility' deviates from eternality, since intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) is intangible and yet non-eternal. Thus, because there is deviation in both types of examples, the relation of provable and prover does not exist; hence, due to the absence of the defining characteristic, it is a non-reason.
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.6 ****
[Page 377:]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.6: That which, having accepted a <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), contradicts it, is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory).

children.text: taṃ viruṇaddhīti tadvirodhy abhyupetaṃ siddhāntaṃ vyāhantīti/ yathā so 'yaṃ vikāro vyakter apaiti nityatvapratiṣedhāt ---
children.translated_text: It 'contradicts' — that is, opposes — the accepted <s>siddhānta</s>. For example: 'This modification departs from manifestation, because eternality is negated' —

children.text:
% vyakter apaiti nityatvapratiṣedhāt] p.378
na nityo vikāra upapadyata apeto 'pi vikāro 'sti vināśapratiṣedhāt/ so 'yaṃ nityatvapratiṣedhād iti/ hetur vyakter apeto 'pi vikāro 'stīty anena svasiddhāntena virudhyate/ katham? vyaktir ātmalābhaḥ/ apāyaḥ pracyutiḥ/ yady ātmalābhāt pracyuto vikāro 'sti nityatvapratiṣedho nopapadyate/ yad vyakter apetasyāpi vikārasyāstitvaṃ tat khalu nityatvam iti/ nityatvapratiṣedho nāma vikārasyātmalābhāt pracyuter upapattiḥ/
children.translated_text:
[Page 378:]
'A modification is not eternal' is tenable; [but] 'a modification exists even when it has departed [from manifestation]' [follows] because destruction is negated. 'This [modification] because of the negation of eternality' — this reason contradicts his own <s>siddhānta</s> that 'a modification exists even when it has departed.' How? Manifestation means the attainment of [its own] existence. Departure

children.text:
% nāma vikārasyātmalābhāt ...] p.379
yad ātmalābhāt pracyavate tad anityaṃ dṛṣṭam, yad asti na tad ātmalābhāt pracyavate/ astitvaṃ cātmalābhāt pracyutir iti ca viruddhāv etau dharmau na saha sambhavata iti/ so 'yaṃ hetur yaṃ siddhāntam āśritya pravartate tam eva vyāhantīti// 6 //
children.translated_text:
[Page 379:]
means: that which departs from its own attainment of existence is observed to be non-eternal; that which exists does not depart from its own attainment of existence. Existence and departure from the attainment of [its own] existence — these are contradictory properties that cannot co-exist. Thus, this reason, relying on a <s>siddhānta</s> [which it contradicts, proceeds to —]
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.7 ****
[Page 380:]

children.text: NyS_1,2.7: yasmāt prakaraṇacintā sa nirṇayārtham apadiṣṭaḥ prakaraṇasamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.7: That which, being the ground of inquiry, is adduced for the sake of ascertainment, is <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (evenly balanced with the topic).

children.text: vimarśādhiṣṭhānau pakṣapratipakṣāv ubhāv anavasitau prakaraṇam, tasya cintā vimarśāt prabhṛti prāṅ nirṇayād yat samīkṣaṇam,
children.translated_text: The two — the thesis and the counter-thesis — both unresolved, standing as the basis for deliberation, constitute the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (topic of investigation). Its inquiry (<s>cintā</s>) — that examination which extends from the deliberation up to, but prior to, the determination —

children.text:
% prāṅ nirṇayād yat samīkṣaṇam,] p.381
sā jijñāsā yatkṛtā sa nirṇayārthaṃ prayukta ubhayapakṣasāmyāt prakaraṇam anativartamānaḥ prakaraṇasamo nirṇayāya na prakalpate/
prajñāpanaṃ tv anityaḥ śabdo nityadharmānupalabdher iti, anupalabhyamānan ity adharmakaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭam sthālyādi/ nityaḥ śabdo vānityadharmānupalabdheḥ anupalabhyamānānityadharmakaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭam ākāśādi/
yatra samāno dharmaḥ saṃśayakāraṇaṃ hetutvenopādīyate sa saṃśayasamaḥ savyabhicāra eva/
children.translated_text:
[Page 381:]
that investigation for the sake of which [the reason] is employed — due to the equality of both sides, it does not transcend the topic, [and thus] being equally balanced with the topic (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>), it does not serve for determination.
The declaration, however, is: 'Sound is non-eternal because eternal properties are not apprehended' — [that which is] not apprehended, thus [being] a non-property —

children.text:
% p.382
yā tu vimarśasya viśeṣāpekṣitā ubhayapakṣaviśeṣānupalabdhiś ca sā prakaraṇaṃ pravartayati/ yathā śabde nityadharmo nopalabhyata evam anityadharmo 'pi/ seyam ubhayapakṣaviśeṣānupalabdhiḥ prakaraṇacintāṃ pravartayati/
children.translated_text:
[Page 382:]
But the dependence of the deliberation upon a distinguishing feature, and the non-apprehension of distinguishing features of both sides — that sets the investigation in motion. Just as eternal properties are not apprehended in sound, so too non-eternal properties are not [necessarily apprehended]. This non-apprehension of distinguishing features of both sides sets the investigation of the topic in motion.

children.text:
% prakaraṇacintāṃ pravartayati/] p.383
