katham? viparyaye hi prakaraṇanivṛtteḥ --- yadi nityadharmaḥ śabde gṛhyeta na syāt prakaraṇam, yadi na syāt prakaraṇam, yadi vānityadharmo gṛhyeta evam api nivarteta prakaraṇam/ so 'yaṃ hetur ubhau pakṣau pravartayann anyatarasya nirṇayāya na prakalpate// 7 //
children.translated_text:
[Page 383:]
How? Because in the contrary case, the investigation would cease — if an eternal property were grasped in sound, there would be no [open] topic; if there were no [open] topic — or if a non-eternal property were grasped — even so, the investigation would cease. Thus this reason, [equally supporting] both sides, proceeds —
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.8 ****
[Page 384:]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.8: That which is undistinguished from the provable, because of [itself] being provable, is <s>sādhyasama</s> (on a par with the provable).

children.text: dravyaṃ chāyeti sādhyam, gatimattvād iti hetuḥ sādhyenāviśiṣṭaḥ sādhanīyatvāt sādhyasamaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'A substance is a shadow' is the provable; 'because it possesses movement' is the reason — [which is] undistinguished from the provable, because it [itself] needs to be proved; [hence it is] <s>sādhyasama</s>.

children.text:
% sādhyasamaḥ/] p.385
ayam apy asiddhatvāt sādhyavat prajñāpayitavyaḥ/ sādhyaṃ tāvad etat kiṃ puruṣavac chāyāpi gacchaty āhosvid āvarakadravye saṃsarpaty āvaraṇasantānād asannidhisantāno 'yaṃ tejaso gṛhyata iti/
children.translated_text:
[Page 385:]
This too, being unestablished, must be demonstrated like the provable [itself]. For the provable is this: does a shadow move like a person, or does it spread in the obstructing substance, so that from the continuity of obstruction, this [apparent] continuity of absence of the light is grasped?

children.text:
% -sannadhisantāno 'yaṃ tejaso gṛhyata iti/] p.386
sarpatā khalu dravyeṇa yo yas tejobhāga āvriyate tasya tasyāsannidhir evāvicchinno gṛhyata iti/ āvaraṇaṃ tu prāptipratiṣedhaḥ// 8 //
children.translated_text:
[Page 386:]
For when a moving substance covers a given portion of light, only the uninterrupted absence of that [light] is grasped. And obstruction means the prevention of contact. // 8 //
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.9 ****
[Page 388:]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.9: That which is cited [too late], having passed the [proper] time, is <s>kālātīta</s> (time-lapsed).

children.text: kālātyayena yukto yasyārthaikadeśo 'padiśyamānasya sa kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ kālātīta ity ucyate/ nidarśanam --- nityaḥ śabdaḥ saṃyogavyaṅgyatvād rūpavat/
children.translated_text: That which is connected with a lapse of time — when a part of whose thesis is being stated [too late] — is called <s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>, i.e., <s>kālātīta</s> (time-lapsed). Illustration: 'Sound is eternal because it is manifested by contact, like color.'

children.text:
% p.389
prāg ūrdhvaṃ ca vyakter avasthitaṃ rūpaṃ pradīpaghaṭasaṃyogena vyajyate, tathā ca śabdo 'py avasthito bherīdaṇḍasaṃyogena vyajyate dāruparaśusaṃyogena vā, tasmāt samyogavyaṅgyatvān nityaḥ śabda iti; ayam ahetuḥ kālātyayāpadeśāt/ vyañjakasya saṃyogasya kālaṃ na vyaṅgyasya rūpasya vyaktir atyeti/ sati pradīpasaṃyoge rūpasya grahaṇaṃ bhavati, na nivṛtte saṃyoge rūpaṃ gṛhyate/ nivṛtte dāruparaśusaṃyoge dūrasthena śabdaḥ śrūyate vibhāgakāle/ seyaṃ śabdasya vyaktiḥ saṃyogakālam atyetīti na saṃyoganirmitā bhavati/ kasmāt? kāraṇābhāvād dhi kāryābhāva iti/ evam udāharaṇasādharmyasyābhāvād asādhanam ayaṃ hetur hetvābhāsa iti/
children.translated_text:
[Page 389:]
Color, existing prior to and after manifestation, is manifested by the contact of a lamp with a pot; similarly, sound too, existing [latently], is manifested by the contact of a drumstick with a drum, or by the contact of an axe with wood — therefore, because of being manifested by contact, sound is eternal. This is a non-reason because of temporal lapse (<s>kālātyayāpadeśa</s>). Of the manifesting agent —

children.text:
% p.390
avayavaviparyāsavacanaṃ tu na sūtrārthaḥ/ kasmāt?
``yasya yenārthasambandho dūrasthasyāpi tasya saḥ/
arthato hy asamarthānām ānantaryam akāraṇam//''
ity etadvacanād viparyāsenokto hetur udāharaṇasādharmyāt tathā vaidharmyāt sādhyasādhanaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ na jahāti/ ajahaddhetulakṣaṇaṃ na hetvābhāso bhavatīti/
``avayavaviparyāsavacanam aprāptakālam'' iti nigrahasthānam uktam, tad evedaṃ punar ucyata iti, atas tan na sūtrārthaḥ// 9 //
children.translated_text:
[Page 390:]
However, the statement of transposition of component parts is not the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. Why? Because of this statement:
'For that whose meaning-connection exists with something, even if distant, that [connection] holds;
for those that are meaninglessly [related], mere contiguity is not a cause.'
According to this, a reason stated in transposed order, through the similarity or dissimilarity of the example, [remains] the reason establishing the provable —
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.10 ****

[Page 391:]
Now, <s>chala</s> (quibbling):
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.10: The obstruction of [another's] statement through the application of a different interpretation of the meaning is <s>chala</s> (quibbling).

children.text: na sāmānyalakṣaṇe chalaṃ śakyam udāhartum, vibhāge tūdāharaṇāni// 10//
children.translated_text: A general illustration of <s>chala</s> cannot be given; but illustrations [will be given] in the classification. // 10 //
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.11 ****

[Page 392:]
And the classification:

children.text: NyS_1,2.11 : tat trividhaṃ vākchalaṃ sāmānyacchalam upacāracchalam ceti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.11: That [<s>chala</s>] is threefold: <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibbling), <s>sāmānyacchala</s> (quibbling based on generality), and <s>upacāracchala</s> (quibbling based on figurative usage).
Of these:
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.12 ****

children.text: NyS_1,2.12 : aviśeṣābhihite 'rthe vaktur abhiprāyād arthāntarakalpanā vākchalam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.12: When, in a meaning stated without specification, a different meaning is constructed contrary to the speaker's intention, that is <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibbling).

children.text: navakambalo 'yaṃ māṇavaka iti prayogaḥ/ atra navaḥ kambalo 'syeti vaktur abhiprāyaḥ/ vigrahe tu viśeṣaḥ, na samāse/ tatrāyaṃ chalavādī vaktur abhiprāyād avivakṣitam anyam arthaṃ nava kambalā asyeti tāvad abhihitaṃ bhavateti kalpayati,
children.translated_text: The usage: 'This young man is <s>navakambala</s> (possessing a new blanket).' Here, the speaker's intention is 'he has a new blanket' (<s>navaḥ kambalaḥ asya</s>). The specification exists in the compound analysis, not in the compound [itself]. There the quibbler, constructing a meaning different from the speaker's intention — namely, 'he has nine blankets' (<s>nava kambalāḥ asya</s>) — thus posits 'this much has been stated by you,'

children.text:
% nava kambalā asyeti] p.393
kalpayitvā cāsambhavena pratiṣedhati eko 'sya kambalaḥ kuto nava kambalā iti/
tad idaṃ sāmānyaśabde vāci chalaṃ vākchalam iti/
asya pratyavasthānam --- sāmānyaśabdasyānekārthatve 'nyatarābhidhānakalpanāyāṃ viśeṣavacanam/ navakambala ity anekārthābhidhānam, navaḥ kambalo 'syeti nava kambalā asyeti; etasmin prayukte yeyaṃ kalpanā nava kambalā asyety etadbhavatābhihitaṃ tac ca na sambhavatīti, etasyām anyatarābhidhānakalpanāyāṃ viśeṣo vaktavyaḥ/ yasmād viśeṣo 'rthaviśeṣeṣu vijñāyate 'yam artho 'nenābhihita iti/ sa ca viśeṣo nāsti/ tasmān mithyābhiyogamātram etad iti/
prasiddhaś ca loke śabdārthasambandho 'bhidhānābhidheyaniyamaniyogaḥ/ asyābhidhānasyāyam artho 'bhidheya iti samānaḥ sāmānyaśabdasya, viśeṣo viśiṣṭaśabdasya/ prayuktapūrvāś ceme śabdā arthe prayujyante nāprayuktapūrvāḥ/ prayogaś cārthasampratyayārthaḥ/ arthapratyayāc ca vyavahāra iti/
children.translated_text:
[Page 393:]
and having constructed [this meaning], he refutes it by impossibility: 'He has [only] one blanket — where are the nine blankets?'
This is <s>chala</s> (quibbling) in speech — in a word with a general meaning — hence it is called <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibbling).
The rejoinder to this: When a word with a general meaning has multiple meanings, and one [meaning] is [arbitrarily] constructed, a specifying statement [is needed].

children.text:
% iti/] p.394
tatraivam arthagatyarthe śabdaprayoge sāmarthyāt sāmānyaśabdasya prayoganiyamaḥ/ ajāṃ grāmaṃ naya sarpir āhāra brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayeti sāmānyaśabdāḥ santo 'rthāvayaveṣu prayujyante sāmārthyat, yatrārthakriyācodanā sambhavati tatra pravartante nārthasāmānye, kriyādeśanāsambhavāt/ evam ayaṃ sāmānyaśabdo navakambala iti yo 'rthaḥ sambhavati navaḥ kambalo 'syeti tatra pravartate, yas tu na sambhavait nava kambalā asyeti tatra na pravartate/ so 'yam anupapadyamānārthakalpanayā paravākyopālambho na kalpata iti//12//
children.translated_text:
[Page 394:]
Thus, when a word is used with the purpose of conveying a particular meaning, by the force of [contextual] capacity, the general word is restricted in its usage. In 'lead the goat to the village,' 'bring the ghee,' 'feed the Brahmin' — these general words, being applied to specific objects, are employed by force of capacity — where the injunction of purposeful action is possible, there [the word] operates —
**** <s>Nyāyasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.13 ****
[Page 395:]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.13: The construction of an impossible meaning through an over-generalization of a possible meaning is <s>sāmānyacchala</s> (quibbling based on generality).

children.text: aho khalv asau brāhmaṇo vidyācaraṇasampanna ity ukte kaścid āha sambhavati brāhmaṇe vidyācaraṇasampad iti/
children.translated_text: When it is said 'How excellent indeed is this Brahmin, endowed with learning and good conduct!' — someone says, 'It is [merely] possible for a Brahmin to have learning and good conduct.'

children.text:
% vidyācaraṇasampad iti] p.396
asya vacanasya vighāto 'rthavikalpopapattyāsambhūtārthakalpanayā kriyate --- yadi brāhmaṇe vidyācaraṃasampat sambhavati vrātye 'pi sambhavet, vrātyo 'pi brāhmaṇaḥ, so 'py astu vidyācaraṇasampanna iti/ yad vivakṣitam artham āpnoti cātyeti ca tad atisāmānyam/ yathā brāhmaṇatvaṃ vidyācaraṇasampadaṃ kvacid āpnoti kvacid atyeti/ sāmānyanimittaṃ chalaṃ sāmānyacchalam iti/
asya ca pratyavasthānam --- avivakṣitahetukasya viṣayānuvādaḥ praśaṃsārthatvād vākyasya; tad atrāsambhūtārthakalpanānupapattiḥ/ yathā sambhavanty asmin kṣetre śālaya iti anirākṛtam avivakṣitaṃ ca bījajanma, pravṛttiviṣayas tu kṣetraṃ praśasyate; so 'yaṃ kṣetrānuvādaḥ nāsmin śālayo vidhīyanta iti; bījāt tu śālinirvṛttiḥ satī na vivakṣitā/ evaṃ sambhavati brāhmaṇe vidyācaraṇasampad iti sampadviṣayo brāhmaṇatvaṃ na sampaddhetuḥ/ na cātra hetur vivakṣitaḥ/ viṣayānuvādas tv ayaṃ praśaṃsārthatvād vākyasya, sati brāhmaṇatve sampaddhetuḥ samartha iti/ vis'yaṃ ca praśaṃsatā vākyena yathāhetutaḥ phalanirvṛttir na pratyākhyāyate/ tad evaṃ sati vacanavighāto 'sambhūtārthakalpanayā nopapadyata iti//
children.translated_text:
The disruption of this statement is made through the supposition of an unwarranted meaning (<s>asambhūtārthakalpanā</s>) by means of the applicability of an alternative meaning: 'If <s>vidyā</s> (learning) and <s>caraṇa</s> (conduct) are found in a Brahmin, they might also be found in a <s>vrātya</s> (outcaste); the <s>vrātya</s> is also a Brahmin — so let him too be accomplished in learning and conduct.' That which reaches and also surpasses the intended meaning is <s>atisāmānya</s> (over-generalization). Just as Brahmin-hood sometimes reaches and sometimes surpasses the possession of learning and conduct — the quibble based on a general property is called <s>sāmānyacchala</s> (quibble of generality).
The reply to this: the statement about the domain pertains to an unintended cause, since the sentence is for the purpose of praise; therefore, the supposition of an unwarranted meaning is inapplicable. Just as (when one says) 'rice grows in this field' — the birth from seed is neither denied nor intended; the domain of the statement praises the field; this is a statement about the field, not a rule that rice is produced (only) in this (field); the production of rice from seed, though real, is not the intended meaning. Similarly, 'learning and conduct are found in a Brahmin' — Brahmin-hood is the domain of accomplishment, not the cause of accomplishment. And no cause is intended here. This is merely a statement about the domain, since the sentence is for the purpose of praise — (the meaning being that) when Brahmin-hood exists, the cause of accomplishment is effective. And by a sentence that praises the domain, the production of the result from its (actual) cause is not denied. Therefore, the disruption of the statement through the supposition of an unwarranted meaning is not applicable.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.14: In the indication of a variation of property, the denial of the real existence of the meaning is <s>upacāracchala</s> (quibble of figurative usage).

children.text: abhidhānasya dharmo yathārthaprayogaḥ, dharmavikalpo 'nyatra dṛṣṭasyānyatra prayogaḥ, tasya nirdeśe dharmavikalpanirdeśe/ yathā mañcāḥ krośantīti arthasadbhāvena pratiṣedhaḥ,
children.translated_text: The property of an expression is its usage according to its (literal) meaning. A variation of property is the usage elsewhere of what is observed (to be used) in one place. In the indication of such — that is, in the indication of a variation of property. For example, 'the platforms are shouting' — the denial based on the real existence of the meaning (is):

children.text:
% p.398
mañcasthāḥ puruṣāḥ krośanti na tu mañcāḥ krośanti/
kā punar atrārthavikalpopapattiḥ? anyathā prayuktasyānyathārthakalpanam, bhaktyā prayoge prādhānyena kalpanam upacāraviṣayaṃ chalam upacāracchalam/ upacāro nītārthaḥ sahacaraṇādinimittena, atadbhāve tadvad abhidhānam upacāra iti/
atra samādhiḥ --- prasiddhe prayoge vaktur yathābhiprāyaṃ śabdārthayor abhyanujñā pratiṣedhā vā na cchandataḥ/ pradhānabhūtasya śabdasya bhāktasya ca guṇabhūtasya prayoga ubhayor lokasiddhaḥ/ siddhe prayoge yathā vaktur abhiprāyas tathā śabdārthāv anujñeyau pratiṣedhyau vā na cchandataḥ/ yadi vaktā pradhānaśabdaṃ prayuṅkte yathābhūtasyābhyanujñā pratiṣedho vā, na cchandataḥ/ atha guṇabhūtam, tadā guṇabhūtasya/ yatra tu vaktā guṇabhūtaṃ śabdaṃ prayuṅkte pradhānabhūtam abhipretya paraḥ pratiṣedhati, svamanīṣayā pratiṣedho 'sau bhavati na paropālambha iti//
children.translated_text:
the people standing on the platforms are shouting, not the platforms themselves.
What then is the applicability of the alternative meaning here? The supposition of a different meaning for what is used differently — when what is used figuratively (<s>bhakti</s>) is supposed as primary (<s>prādhānya</s>) — this is a quibble in the domain of figurative usage, hence <s>upacāracchala</s>. Figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) has a definite meaning; caused by association and similar grounds — the designation as if it were that, when it is not that, is <s>upacāra</s> (figurative usage).
The resolution of this: in a well-established usage, the acceptance or denial of the relationship between word and meaning should follow the speaker's intention, not one's own whim. The usage of both the primary word and the secondary (figurative) word is well-established in the world. In an established usage, just as the speaker intends, so should the word-meaning relationship be accepted or denied — not at one's own whim. If the speaker uses the primary word, the acceptance or denial is of the real thing, not at whim. If the secondary word (is used), then (acceptance or denial) is of the secondary. But where the speaker uses the secondary word intending the primary meaning, and the opponent denies (it) — that denial is his own arbitrary action, not a legitimate objection to the other.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.15: <s>Upacāracchala</s> (quibble of figurative usage) is just <s>vākcchala</s> (verbal quibble), since there is no distinction between them.

children.text: na vākchalād upacāracchalaṃ bhidyate tasyāpy arthāntarakalpanāyā aviśeṣāt/ ihāpi sthānyartho guṇaśabdaḥ pradhānaśabdaḥ sthānārtha iti kalpayitvā pratiṣidhyata iti//
children.translated_text: <s>Upacāracchala</s> is not different from <s>vākcchala</s>, since there is no distinction in the supposition of an alternative meaning in that case as well. Here too, the meaning of the substitute is the secondary word, and the meaning of the original is the primary word — having so supposed, it is denied.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.16: Not so, because it (<s>upacāracchala</s>) is a different kind (from <s>vākcchala</s>).

children.text: na vākchalam evopacāracchalam, tasyārthasadbhāvapratiṣedhasyārthāntarabhāvāt/ kutaḥ? arthāntarakalpanātaḥ/ anyā hy arthāntarakalpanā, anyo 'rthasadbhāvapratiṣedha iti//
children.translated_text: <s>Upacāracchala</s> is not merely <s>vākcchala</s>, because the denial of the real existence of meaning is a different thing (from the supposition of a different meaning). Why? Because of the difference in the supposition of alternative meaning. For the supposition of an alternative meaning is one thing, and the denial of the real existence of meaning is another.

children.text: NyS_1,2.17 : aviṣeṣe vā kiñcit sādharmyād ekacchalaprasaṅaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.17: Or, if there is no distinction, (then) from some similarity, the consequence would be that there is only one type of quibble.

children.text: chalasya dvitvam abhyanujñāya tritvaṃ pratiṣidhyate kiñcit sādharmyāt/ yathā cāyaṃ hetus tritvaṃ pratiṣedhati tathā dvitvam apy abhyanujñātaṃ pratiṣedhati, vidyate hi kiñcit sādharmyaṃ dvayor apīti/ atha dvitvaṃ kiñcitsādharmyān na nivartate, tritvam api na nivartsyati//
children.translated_text: Having conceded the duality of <s>chala</s> (quibble), the third type is being denied on the basis of some similarity. But just as this reasoning denies the third type, it also denies the conceded duality — for there is indeed some similarity between the two as well. And if the duality is not overturned by some similarity, neither will the third type be overturned.
After the definition of <s>chala</s> (quibble) —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.18: An objection (<s>pratyavasthāna</s>) based on similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) or dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>) is <s>jāti</s> (futile objection).

children.text: prayukte hi hetau yaḥ prasaṅgo jāyate sa jātiḥ/ sa ca prasaṅgaḥ sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānam upālambhaḥ pratiṣedha iti/
children.translated_text: When a reason (<s>hetu</s>) is employed, the consequence that arises is <s>jāti</s>. And that consequence — an objection, a censure, a denial — is based on similarity or dissimilarity.

children.text:
% sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ ...] p.402
``udāharaṇasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanaṃ hetur'' ity asyodāharaṇavaidharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam, ``udāharaṇavaidharmyāt sādhyasādhanaṃ hetur'' ity asyodāharaṇasādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam, pratyanīkabhāvāt/ jāyamāno 'rtho jātir iti//
children.translated_text: Against (the argument) 'a reason establishes what is to be proved through the similarity of the example,' the objection is based on the dissimilarity of the example. Against (the argument) 'a reason establishes what is to be proved through the dissimilarity of the example,' the objection is based on the similarity of the example — because they are mutually opposed. A meaning that arises (as a consequence) is <s>jāti</s> (futile objection).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.19: Misunderstanding (<s>vipratipattti</s>) and non-understanding (<s>apratipattti</s>) are the grounds for defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).

children.text: viparītā vā kutsitā vā pratipattir vipratipattiḥ/ vipratipadyamānaḥ parājayaṃ prāpnoti/ nigrahasthānaṃ khalu parājayaprāptiḥ/ apratipattis tv ārambhaviṣaye anārambhaḥ/ pareṇa sthāpitaṃ vā na pratiṣedhati pratiṣedhaṃ vā noddharati/ asamāsāc ca naite eva nigrahasthāne iti//
children.translated_text: <s>Vipratipattti</s> is understanding that is contrary or faulty. One who misunderstands incurs defeat. A <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (ground for defeat) is indeed the incurrence of defeat. <s>Apratipattti</s> (non-understanding), on the other hand, is the failure to begin regarding the subject at hand. Or: one neither refutes what has been established by the opponent, nor removes the refutation (of one's own position). And from the absence of a comprehensive (statement), these are not the only grounds for defeat.

children.text:
% p.404
kiṃ punar dṛṣṭāntavaj jātinigrahasthānayor abhedo 'tha siddhāntavad bheda ity ata āha ---
children.translated_text: Now, are <s>jāti</s> (futile objection) and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (ground for defeat) without distinction, like illustration (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), or with distinction, like an established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>)? On this, (the sūtra) says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.20: The multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> arises from their respective subdivisions.

children.text: tasya sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalpāj jātibahutvam, tayoś ca vipratipattyapratipattyor vikalpān nigrahasthānabahutvam/ nānā kalpo vikalpaḥ, vividho vā kalpo vikalpaḥ/ tatra ananubhāṣaṇam ajñānam apratibhā vikṣepo matānujñā paryanuyojyopekṣaṇam ity apratipattir nigrasthānam/ śeṣas tu vipratipattir iti/
children.translated_text: From the subdivisions of the objection based on similarity and dissimilarity comes the multiplicity of <s>jāti</s>; and from the subdivisions of misunderstanding and non-understanding comes the multiplicity of <s>nigrahasthāna</s>. A <s>vikalpa</s> (subdivision) is a diverse form or a varied form. Among these, non-response (<s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s>), ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), lack of ready wit (<s>apratibhā</s>), evasion (<s>vikṣepa</s>), admission of the opponent's view (<s>matānujñā</s>), and disregard of what is open to question (<s>paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s>) — these constitute <s>apratipattti</s> as grounds for defeat. The rest constitutes <s>vipratipattti</s>.

children.text:
% p.405
ime pramāṇādayaḥ padārthā uddiṣṭāḥ, yathoddeśaṃ lakṣitāḥ, yathālakṣaṇaṃ parīkṣiṣyanta iti trividhā cāsya śāstrasya pravṛttir veditavyeti//
children.translated_text: These categories (<s>padārtha</s>) beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s> (instruments of valid knowledge) have been enumerated; they have been defined in accordance with their enumeration; they will be examined in accordance with their definitions. Thus, the threefold procedure of this treatise should be understood.

children.text:
iti vātsyāyanīye nyāyabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya dvitīyam āhnikam/
samāptaś cāyaṃ prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ//
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the second <s>āhnika</s> (lesson) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> by <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
And thus the first chapter is complete.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pramāṇādiparīkṣā/ sā ca ``vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ'' ity agre vimarṣa eva parīkṣyate ---
children.translated_text: Hereafter is the examination of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest. And since 'the ascertainment of a matter through deliberation upon the thesis and the counter-thesis is determination (<s>nirṇaya</s>),' the deliberation itself is first examined —

children.text: NyS_2,1.1 : samānānekadharmādhyavasāyād anyataradharmādhyavasāyād vā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.1: Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) does not arise from the ascertainment of a common property or of multiple properties, or from the ascertainment of a property belonging to one (of the alternatives).

children.text: samānasya dharmasyādhyavasāyāt saṃśayo na dharmamātrāt/ atha vā samānam anayor dharmam upalabha iti dharmadharmigrahaṇe saṃśayābhāva iti/
children.translated_text: Doubt arises from the ascertainment of a common property, not from a property as such. Or alternatively: having perceived the common property of these two, since both property and property-bearer are grasped, doubt is absent.

children.text:
% -m upalabha iti] p.409
atha vā samānadharmādhyavasāyād arthāntarabhūte dharmiṇi saṃśayo 'nupapannaḥ, na jātu rūpasyārthāntarabhūtasyādhyavasāyād arthāntarabhūte sparśe saṃśaya iti/ atha vā na adhyavasāyād arthāvadhāraṇād anavadhāraṇajñānaṃ saṃśaya upapadyate kāryakāraṇayoḥ sārūpyābhāvād iti/ etenānekadharmādhyavasāyād iti vyākhyātam/ anyataradharmādhyvasāyāc ca saṃśayo na bhavati, tato hy anyatarāvadhāraṇam eveti//
children.translated_text: Or alternatively: doubt is not possible regarding a property-bearer that is a different entity, merely from the ascertainment of a common property — for never does doubt about touch, which is a different entity, arise from the ascertainment of color, which is (also) a different entity. Or alternatively: doubt, which is non-determinate cognition, cannot arise from ascertainment, which is determinate cognition, because there is no similarity between cause and effect. By this, 'from the ascertainment of multiple properties' is also explained. And doubt does not arise from the ascertainment of a property belonging to one (of the alternatives), because from that there is simply the determination of that one.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.2: And (doubt arises) from conflicting views (<s>vipratipattti</s>), from indeterminacy (<s>avyavasthā</s>), and from ascertainment.

children.text: na vipratipattimātrād avyavasthāmātrād vā saṃśayaḥ/ kiṃ tarhi? vipratipattim upalabhamānasya saṃśayaḥ/ evam avyavasthāyām apīti/ atha vāsty ātmety eke nāsty ātmety apare manyanta ity upalabdheḥ kathaṃ saṃśayaḥ syād iti/ tathopalabdhir avyavasthitā anupalabdhiś cāvyavasthiteti vibhāgenādhyavasite saṃśayo nopapadyata iti//
children.translated_text: Doubt does not arise merely from conflicting views, nor merely from indeterminacy. What then? Doubt arises for one who perceives the conflicting views. Likewise in the case of indeterminacy. Or alternatively: some think 'the self exists' while others think 'the self does not exist' — from such perception, how could doubt arise? Likewise, perception is indeterminate and non-perception is also indeterminate — when these are determined separately, doubt is not possible.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.3: And because in conflicting views there is agreement (<s>sampratipattti</s>).

children.text: yāṃ ca vipratipattiṃ bhavān saṃśayahetuḥ manyate sā sampratipattiḥ, sā hi dvayoḥ pratyanīkadharmaviṣayā/ tatra yadi vipratipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ, sampratipatter eva saṃśaya iti//
children.translated_text: That which you consider the cause of doubt — conflicting views — is itself agreement (<s>sampratipattti</s>), for it concerns the mutually opposed properties of two (alternatives). Therefore, if from conflicting views there is doubt, then from agreement itself there would be doubt.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.4: And because indeterminacy (<s>avyavasthā</s>) is established in a determinate self (<s>avyavasthātman</s>).

children.text:
na saṃśayaḥ/ yadi tāvad iyam avyavasthā ātmani eva vyavasthitā, vyavasthānād avyavasthā na bhavatīty anupapannaḥ saṃśayaḥ/
atha avyavasthātmani na vyavasthitā, evam atādātmyād avyavasthā na bhavatīti saṃśayābhāva iti//
children.translated_text:
There is no doubt. If this indeterminacy is established in the self alone — then, since it is established (i.e., determinate), indeterminacy does not exist, and doubt is unwarranted.
Alternatively, if (the indeterminacy) is not established in a determinate self — then, not having that nature, indeterminacy does not exist, and hence there is no doubt.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.5: Likewise, perpetual doubt would follow, because of the continuity of that property.

children.text: yena kalpena bhavān samānadharmopapatteḥ saṃśaya iti manyate, tena khalv atyantasaṃśayaḥ prasajyate/ samānadharmopapatter anucchedāt saṃśayānucchedaḥ/ na hy ayam ataddharmā dharmī vimṛśyamāṇo gṛhyate, satataṃ tu taddharmā bhavatīti//
children.translated_text: By the very reasoning by which you hold that doubt arises from the obtaining of a common property, thereby perpetual doubt would follow. Since the obtaining of a common property does not cease, doubt does not cease either. For the property-bearer under examination is never apprehended as being without that property; rather, it continuously possesses that property.
The summary extraction of this elaboration of refutations —

children.text: NyS_2,1.6 : yathoktādhyavasāyād eva tadaviśeṣāpekṣāt saṃśaye nāsaṃśayo nātyantasaṃśayo vā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.6: From the ascertainment as previously described — which is expectant of the undifferentiated aspect of that (property) — in doubt, there is neither absence of doubt nor perpetual doubt.

children.text:
na saṃśayānutpattiḥ saṃśayānucchedaś ca prasajyate/ katham? yat tāvat samānadharmādhyavasāyaḥ saṃśayahetuḥ na samānadharmamātram iti, evam etat/ kasmād evaṃ nocyata iti? viśeṣāpekṣa iti vacanāt tatsiddheḥ --- viśeṣasyāpekṣā ākaṅkṣā, sā cānupalabhyamāne viśeṣe samarthā, na coktaṃ samānadharmāpekṣa iti/ samāne ca dharme katham ākaṅkṣā na bhaved yady ayaṃ pratyakṣaḥ syāt/ etena sāmarthyena vijñāyate samānadharmādhyavasāyād iti/
upapattivacanād vā --- samānadharmopapatter ity ucyate na cānyā sadbhāvasaṃvedanād ṛte samānadharmopapattir asti/ anupalabhyamānasadbhāvo hi samāno dharmo 'vidyamānavad bhavatīti/
viṣayaśabdena vā viṣayiṇaḥ pratyayasyābhidhānam --- yathā loke dhūmenāgnir anumīyate ity ukte dhūmadarśanenāgnir anumīyata iti jñāyate/ katham? dṛṣṭvā hi dhūmam athāgnim anuminoti nādṛṣṭveti; na ca vākye darśanaśabdaḥ śrūyate, anujānāti ca vākyasyārthapratyāyakatvam; tena manyāmahe viṣayaśabdena viṣayiṇaḥ pratyayasyābhidhānaṃ boddhānujānāti/ evam ihāpi samānadharmaśabdena samānadharmādhyvasāyam āheti/
children.translated_text:
It is not the case that doubt would fail to arise or that doubt would fail to be resolved. How? As for the claim that apprehension of common properties is the cause of doubt, and that it is not mere common properties [that cause it] — yes, that is so. Why is it not stated thus? Because the expression 'dependent on a differentia' (<s>viśeṣāpekṣa</s>) establishes this — 'dependent on a differentia' means the expectation of a differentia, and this [expectation] is effective when a differentia is not apprehended; nor has it been said 'dependent on common properties.' And when a property is common, how could there not be expectation [of a differentia], if this [common property] were directly perceived? By this implication it is understood that [doubt arises] from the apprehension of common properties.
Or, because of the statement of applicability — it is said 'from the applicability of common properties,' and there is no other applicability of common properties apart from the awareness of their existence. For a common property whose existence is not apprehended becomes as if non-existent.
Or, through the word denoting the object, the cognition that has [that] as its object is referred to — just as in common usage, when it is said 'fire is inferred by smoke,' it is understood that 'fire is inferred by the perception of smoke.' How? For one infers fire after having seen smoke, not without having seen it; yet the word 'seeing' is not heard in the sentence, and one acknowledges the sentence's capacity to convey meaning; therefore we hold that through the word denoting the object, the cognition having [that] as its object is referred to — the knower acknowledges this. Similarly here too, by the word 'common property,' the apprehension of common properties is meant.

children.text:
% p.414
yathohitvā samānamanayor dharmam upalabha iti dharmadharmigrahaṇe saṃśayābhāva iti, pūrvadṛṣṭaviṣayam etat/ yāv aham arthau pūrvam adrākṣaṃ tayoḥ samānaṃ dharmam upalabhe viśeṣaṃ nopalabha iti, kathaṃ nu viśeṣaṃ paśyeyaṃ yenānyataram avadhārayeyam iti/ na caitat samānadharmopalabdhau dharmadharmigrahaṇamātreṇa nivartata iti/
yac coktaṃ nārthāntarādhyavasāyād anyatra saṃśaya iti, yo hy arthāntarādhyavasāyamātraṃ saṃśayahetum upādadīta sa evaṃ vācya iti/
yat punar etat kāryakāraṇayoḥ sārūpyābhāvād iti, kāraṇasya bhāvābhāvayoḥ kāryasya bhāvābhāvau kāryakāraṇayoḥ sārūpyam/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.414]
As for the claim that when one grasps both the property and the property-bearer, setting aside their common property, there is no doubt — this pertains to what was previously observed. 'I apprehend the common property of those two objects I previously perceived, but do not apprehend the differentia' — how then could I perceive a differentia by which I could determine one of them? And this [doubt] is not removed merely by grasping the property and property-bearer when a common property is apprehended.
As for the statement that doubt does not arise from anything other than the apprehension of something different — whoever would adopt the mere apprehension of something different as the cause of doubt should be addressed thus.
As for the objection that there is no resemblance between cause and effect — the existence and non-existence of the effect [following] from the existence and non-existence of the cause constitutes the resemblance between cause and effect.

children.text:
% bhāvābhāvau ...] p.415
yasyotpādād yad utpadyate yasya cānutpādād yan notpadyate tat kāraṇaṃ kāryam itarad ity etat sārūpyam, asti ca saṃśayakāraṇe saṃśaye caitad iti/ etenānekadharmādhyavasāyād iti pratiṣedhaḥ parihṛta iti/
yat punar etad uktaṃ ``vipratipattyavyavasthādhyavasāyāc ca na saṃśaya'' iti, pṛthakpravādayor vyāhatam artham upalabhe viśeṣaṃ ca na jānāmi nopalabhe yenānyataram avadhārayeyam,
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.415 — bhāvābhāvau ...]
That from whose origination something originates, and from whose non-origination something does not originate — the former is the cause, the latter the effect — this is the resemblance, and this obtains between the cause of doubt and doubt itself. By this, the objection 'not from the apprehension of multiple properties' is also refuted.
As for the statement that 'there is no doubt from the apprehension of conflicting assertions and indeterminate apprehension' — I apprehend the mutually contradictory meaning of two different assertions, yet do not know the differentia, nor apprehend [anything] by which I could determine one of them,

children.text:
% -r vyāhatam artham upalabhe ...] p.416
tat ko 'tra viśeṣaḥ syād yenaikataram avadhārayeyam iti saṃśayo vipratipattijanito 'yaṃ na śakyo vipratipattisampratipattimātreṇa nivartayitum iti/evam upalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthākṛte saṃśaye veditavyam iti/
yat punar etat vipratipattau ca sampratipatter iti, vipratipattiśabdasya yo 'rthaḥ tadadhyavasāyo viśeṣāpekṣaḥ saṃśayahetus tasya ca samākhyāntareṇa na nivṛttiḥ/ samāne 'dhikaraṇe vyāhatārthau pravādau vipratipattiśabdasyārthaḥ tadadhyavasāyaś ca viśeṣāpekṣaḥ saṃśayahetuḥ/ na cāsya sampratipattiśabde samākhyāntare yojyamāne saṃśayahetutuvaṃ nivartate/ tad idam akṛtabuddhisammohanam iti/
yat punaḥ ``avyavasthātmani vyavasthitatvāc cāvyavasthāyā'' iti, saṃśayahetor arthasyāpratiṣedhād avyavasthābhyanujñānāc ca nimittāntareṇa śabdāntarakalpanā vyarthā/ śabdāntarakalpanāvyavasthā khalv avyavasthā na bhavaty avyavasthātmani vyavasthitatvād iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.416 — -r vyāhatam artham upalabhe ...]
so what differentia could there be by which I could determine one of them? Thus this doubt, born from conflicting assertions, cannot be removed merely by [pointing to] the existence of agreement and disagreement.
The same should be understood regarding doubt produced by the indeterminacy of apprehension and non-apprehension.
As for the objection that agreement arises even in conflicting assertions — the meaning of the word 'conflicting assertion' (<s>vipratipatti</s>), the apprehension thereof dependent on a differentia, is a cause of doubt, and it is not removed by [substituting] a different designation. Two assertions with mutually contradictory meanings regarding the same subject — that is the meaning of the word <s>vipratipatti</s> (conflicting assertion), and the apprehension thereof, dependent on a differentia, is a cause of doubt. And its status as a cause of doubt is not removed when a different designation, [namely] the word <s>sampratipatti</s> (agreement), is applied. This [objection] does not confuse those whose understanding is formed.
As for the objection 'because indeterminacy is established in what is itself indeterminate' — since the object that is the cause of doubt is not refuted, and since indeterminacy is thereby conceded, the fabrication of a different word for a different reason is pointless. The indeterminacy of fabricating a different word is indeed not indeterminacy, since it is 'established in what is itself indeterminate.'

children.text:
% -kalpanāvyavasthā khalv ...] p.417
nānayor upalabdhyanupalabdhyoḥ sadasadviṣayatvaṃ viśeṣāpekṣaṃ saṃśayahetur na bhvatīti pratiṣidhyate yāvatā cāvyavasthātmani vyavasthitā na tāvatātmānaṃ jahāti, tāvatā hy anujñātāvyavasthā/ evam iyaṃ kriyamāṇāpi śabdāntarakalpanā nārthāntaraṃ sādhayatīti/
yat punar etat ``tathātyantasaṃśayas taddharmasātatyopapatteḥ'' iti, nāyaṃ samānadharmādibhya eva saṃśayaḥ/ kiṃ tarhi? tadviṣayādhyavasāyād viśeṣasmṛtisahitād ity ato nātyantasaṃśaya iti/
anyataradharmādhyavasāyād vā na saṃśaya iti, tan na yuktam; viśeṣāpekṣo vimarṣaḥ saṃśaya iti vacanāt/ viśeṣaś cānyataradharmo na tasminn adhyvasīyamāne viśeṣāpekṣā sambhavatīti//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.417 — -kalpanāvyavasthā khalv ...]
It is not refuted that the having-as-object of existent and non-existent [things] in these two — apprehension and non-apprehension — dependent on a differentia, is a cause of doubt. And inasmuch as [indeterminacy] established in what is itself indeterminate does not abandon its own nature, to that extent indeterminacy is conceded. Thus, even when this fabrication of a different word is carried out, it does not establish a different meaning.
As for the objection 'likewise there would be perpetual doubt, because of the continuity of those properties' — this doubt does not arise from common properties and the like alone. From what then? From the apprehension regarding that object accompanied by the recollection of a differentia — therefore there is no perpetual doubt.
Or [the objection that] there is no doubt from the apprehension of one of the two properties — that is not valid, because of the statement that deliberation dependent on a differentia is doubt. And the differentia is one of the two properties; when that is being apprehended, the dependence on a differentia is not possible. //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.7]
[Note: p.418]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.7: Wherever there is doubt, there in this manner the succession of further and further [objections follows].

children.text: yatra yatra saṃśayapūrvikā parīkṣā śāstre kathāyāṃ vā, tatra tatraivaṃ saṃśaye pareṇa pratiṣiddhe samādhir vācya iti/ ataḥ sarvaparīkṣāvyāpitvāt prathamaṃ saṃśayaḥ parīkṣita iti//
children.translated_text: Wherever there is an examination preceded by doubt — whether in a treatise or in a debate — there, when doubt has been refuted by an opponent, a resolution must be stated. Therefore, because it pervades all examinations, doubt has been examined first. //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.8]

[Note: p.419]
Now, the examination of the means of valid knowledge —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.8: The invalidity of perception and the rest [follows] from the impossibility regarding the three times.

children.text: pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇatvaṃ nāsti traikālyāsiddheḥ pūrvāparasahabhāvānupapatter ity arthaḥ//
children.translated_text: The validity of perception and the rest as means of knowledge does not exist, because of the impossibility regarding the three times — meaning, because of the impossibility of [establishing them as] prior, subsequent, or simultaneous. //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.9]

[Note: p.420]
The analysis of this general statement —

children.text: NyS_2,1.9 : pūrvaṃ hi pramāṇasiddhau nendriyārthasannikarṣāt pratyakṣotpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.9: For if the means of knowledge is established first, then perception does not arise from the contact of sense organ and object.

children.text: gandhādiviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam, tad yadi pūrvam, paścād gandhādīnāṃ siddhiḥ, nedaṃ gandhādisannikarṣād utpadyata iti//
children.translated_text: The cognition having odor and the like as its object is perception. If that [perception] is prior and the establishment of odor and the like is subsequent, then this [perception] does not arise from the contact with odor and the like. //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.10]

children.text: NyS_2,1.10 : paścāt siddhau na pramāṇebhyaḥ prameyasiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.10: If [the object] is established subsequently, then there is no establishment of the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) from the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge).

children.text: asati pramāṇe kena pramīyamāṇo 'rthaḥ prameyaḥ syāt pramāṇena khalu pramīyamāṇo 'rthaḥ prameyam ity etat sidhyati//
children.translated_text: In the absence of a means of knowledge, by what would an object, being measured, become a <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge)? For it is established that an object becomes a <s>prameya</s> only when it is being measured by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge). //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.11]
[Note: p.421]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.11: If [they are] established simultaneously, then because cognitions are restricted to their respective objects, there would be no successive operation of cognitions.

children.text:
yadi pramāṇaṃ prameyaṃ ca yugapadbhavataḥ, evam api gandhādiṣv indriyārtheṣu jñānāni pratyarthaniyatāni yugapatsambhavantīti jñānānāṃ pratyakṣaniyatatvāt kramavṛttitvābhāvaḥ/ yā imā buddhayaḥ krameṇārtheṣu varttante tāsāṃ kramavṛttitvaṃ na sambhavatīti/ vyāghātaś ca ``yugapaj jñānānutpattir manaso liṅgam'' iti/ etāvāṃś ca pramāṇaprameyayoḥ sadbhāvaviṣayaḥ sa cānupapanna iti/ tasmāt pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇatvaṃ na sambhavatīti/
asya samādhiḥ --- upalabdhihetor upalabdhiviṣayasya cārthasya pūrvāparasahabhāvāniyamād yathādarśanaṃ vibhāgavacanam/
children.translated_text:
If the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) and the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) exist simultaneously, even so, since cognitions regarding sense-objects such as odor and the rest are restricted to their respective objects and would occur simultaneously, there would be no successive operation of cognitions — that is, the successive functioning of these cognitions regarding their objects would not be possible. And there would be a contradiction with [the principle] 'the non-origination of simultaneous cognitions is the mark of <s>manas</s> (mind).' And all that pertains to the existence of the relation between <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> is thus untenable. Therefore, the validity of perception and the rest as means of knowledge is not possible.
The resolution to this — since there is no fixed rule that the object which is the cause of apprehension and the object which is the subject of apprehension must be prior, subsequent, or simultaneous, the distinction should be stated according to what is observed.

children.text:
% yathādadarśanaṃ vibhāgavacanam] p.423
kavacid upalabdhihetuḥ, paścād upalabdhiviṣayaḥ, yathādityasya prakāśa utpadyamānānām/ kvacit pūrvam upalabdhiviṣayaḥ paścād upalabdhihetuḥ, yathāvasthitānāṃ pradīpaḥ/ kvacid upalabdhihetur upalabdhiviṣayaś ca saha bhvataḥ, yathā dhūmenāgner grahaṇam iti/ upalabdhihetuś ca pramāṇaṃ prameyaṃ tūpalabdhiviṣayaḥ/ evaṃ pramāṇaprameyayoḥ pūrvāparasahabhāve 'niyate yathārtho dṛśyate tathā vibhajya vacanīya iti tatraikāntena pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ, sāmānyena khalu vibhajya pratiṣedha ukta iti/
samākhyāhetos traikālyayogāt tathābhūtā samākhyā/ yat punar idaṃ paścāt siddhāv asati pramāṇe prameyaṃ na sidhyati, pramāṇena pramīyamāṇo 'rthaḥ prameyam iti vijñāyata iti/ pramāṇam ity etasyāḥ samākhyāyā upalabdhihetutvaṃ nimittam,
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.423 — yathādarśanaṃ vibhāgavacanam]
Sometimes the cause of apprehension is prior and the object of apprehension is subsequent, as the light of the sun for things coming into being. Sometimes the object of apprehension is prior and the cause of apprehension is subsequent, as a lamp for things already present. Sometimes the cause of apprehension and the object of apprehension exist together, as in the apprehension of fire by smoke. The cause of apprehension is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), and the object of apprehension is the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge). Thus, since there is no fixed rule about the priority, posteriority, or simultaneity of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>, one should distinguish and state according to how the object is observed — and therefore a categorical refutation is untenable, since the refutation has been stated in a general way without distinguishing.
Because the naming ground admits of [all] three times, the designation is of that nature. As for the [objection] that when established subsequently, in the absence of a means of knowledge the object of knowledge is not established — 'an object being measured by a <s>pramāṇa</s> is a <s>prameya</s>' — this is understood. The naming ground of the designation '<s>pramāṇa</s>' is its being the cause of apprehension,

children.text:
% m ity etasyāḥ samākhyāyā ...] p.424
tasya traikālyayogaḥ/ upalabdhim akārṣīt, upalabdhiṃ karoti, upalabdhiṃ kariṣyatīti samākhyāhetos traikālyayogāt samākhyā tathābhūtā pramito 'nenārthaḥ pramīyate pramāsyata iti pramāṇam; pramitam, pramīyate, pramāsyate iti ca prameyam/ evaṃ sati bhaviṣyaty asmin hetuta upalabdhiḥ, pramāsyate 'yam arthaḥ prameyam idam ity etat sarvaṃ bhvatīti/ traikālyānabhyanujñāne ca vyavahārānupapattiḥ/ yaś caivaṃ nābhyanujānīyāt tasya pācakam ānaya pakṣyati lāvakam ānaya laviṣyatīti vyavahāro nopapadyata iti/
``pratyakṣādīnām aprāmāṇyaṃ traikālyāsiddher'' ity evamādi vākyaṃ pramāṇapratiṣedhaḥ/ tatrāyaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ, athānena pratiṣedhena bhavatā kiṃ kriyata iti? kiṃ sambhavo nivartyate athāsambhavo jñāpyate iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.424 — m ity etasyāḥ samākhyāyā ...]
and that [cause] admits of [all] three times: 'it caused apprehension, it causes apprehension, it will cause apprehension' — because the naming ground admits of [all] three times, the designation is of that nature: 'the object was measured by this — it is being measured — it will be measured' — thus it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>; 'it was measured, it is being measured, it will be measured' — thus it is a <s>prameya</s>. This being so, 'there will be apprehension in the future based on this as cause; this object will be measured; this is a <s>prameya</s>' — all of this obtains. And if the three times are not conceded, practical usage becomes impossible. And one who would not concede this — for such a person, the practical usage 'bring the cook, he will cook' or 'bring the harvester, he will harvest' would be impossible.
The statement 'the invalidity of perception and the rest because of the impossibility regarding the three times' and so forth is a refutation of the means of knowledge. The [proponent of this refutation] should be asked: what is accomplished by this refutation of yours? Is an [actual] possibility being negated, or is an impossibility being made known?

children.text:
% sambhavo jñāpyate] p.425
tad yadi sambhavo nivartyate sati sambhave pratyakṣādīnāṃ pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ/ athāsambhavo jñāpyate, pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ prāptas tarhi pratiṣedhaḥ pramāṇāsambhavasyopalabdhihetutvād iti//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.425 — sambhavo jñāpyate]
If a possibility is being negated, then since a possibility exists, the refutation of perception and the rest is untenable. If an impossibility is being made known, then the refutation has attained the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), since it is the cause of apprehending the impossibility of the means of knowledge. //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.12]
Moreover, what follows from this?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.12: Because of the impossibility regarding the three times, refutation is untenable.

children.text: asya tu vibhāgaḥ/ pūrvaṃ hi pratiṣedhasiddhāv asati pratiṣedhye kim anena pratiṣidhyate paścāt siddhau pratiṣedhyāsiddhiḥ pratiṣedhābhāvād iti/ yugapatsiddhau pratiṣedhyasiddhyabhyanujñānād anarthakaḥ pratiṣedha iti/
children.translated_text: Here is the analysis of this. For if the refutation is established first, then in the absence of the thing to be refuted, what is being refuted by it? If established subsequently, the thing to be refuted is not established, since there is no refutation [yet]. If established simultaneously, then since the establishment of the thing to be refuted is thereby conceded, the refutation is purposeless.

children.text:
% -jñānād anarthakaḥ ...] p.426
pratiṣedhalakṣaṇe ca vākye 'nupapadyamāne siddhaṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇatvam iti//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.426 — -jñānād anarthakaḥ ...]
And when the statement that constitutes a refutation is itself untenable, the validity of perception and the rest as means of knowledge is established. //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.13]

[Note: p.427]
How?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,1.13: And because of the refutation of all means of knowledge, refutation is untenable.

children.text: traikālyāsiddher ity asya hetor yady udāharaṇam upādīyate hetvarthasya sādhakatvaṃ dṛṣṭānte darśayitavyam iti,
children.translated_text: If an example is adduced for the reason 'because of the impossibility regarding the three times,' the probative force of the reason must be shown in the example —

children.text:
% darśayitavyam iti,] p.428
na ca tarhi pratyakṣādīnām aprāmāṇyam/ atha pratyakṣādīnām aprāmāṇyam, upādīyamānam apy udāharaṇaṃ nārthaṃ sādhayiṣyatīti so 'yaṃ sarvapramāṇavyāhato hetur ahetuḥ; ``siddhāntam abhyupetya tadvirodhī viruddhaḥ'' iti/ vākyārtho hy asya siddhāntaḥ/ sa ca vākyārthaḥ pratyakṣādīni nārthaṃ sādhayantītīdaṃ cāvayavānām upādānam arthasya sādhanāyeti/ atha nopādīyate apradarśitaṃ hetvarthasya dṛṣṭāntena sādhakatvam iti niṣedho nopapadyate hetutvāsiddher iti//
children.translated_text: And if so, then the invalidity of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the other [means of valid knowledge] is not [established]. But if [you maintain] the invalidity of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, then even an example, though adduced, will not establish its object — thus this reason, being opposed by all means of valid knowledge, is a non-reason: 'that which contradicts an accepted <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory).' For the sentence-meaning is his established conclusion. And that sentence-meaning is: '<s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest do not establish the object' — and the adducing of parts [of the argument] is for the establishment of the object. If, on the other hand, [the parts] are not adduced — then the denial that the example does not serve to establish the purpose of the reason, which has not been demonstrated, is not justified, since the status of being a reason is itself unestablished.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.14: Or, if their validity [is accepted], there is no negation of all means of valid knowledge.

children.text: pratiṣedhalakṣaṇe svavākye teṣām avayavāśritānāṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ prāmāṇye 'bhyanujñāyamāne paravākye 'py avayavāśritānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ prasajyate 'viśeṣād iti/ evaṃ ca na sarvāṇi pramāṇāni pratiṣidhyanta iti/ vipratiṣedha iti vīty ayam upasargaḥ sampratipattyarthe, na vyāghāte 'rthābhāvād iti//
children.translated_text: In the prohibitive statement [of the opponent], if the validity of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the other [means of knowledge] presupposed in the parts [of his own statement] is conceded, then in the opponent's statement too, the validity of those [means] presupposed in its parts follows, since there is no distinction. And thus, not all means of valid knowledge are negated. Regarding '<s>vipratiṣedha</s>' (contradiction): the prefix 'vi' here is in the sense of mutual agreement, not in the sense of conflict, since [the latter] would yield no meaning.

children.text: NyS_2,1.15 : traikālyāpratiṣedhaś ca śabdād ātodyasiddhivat tatsiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.15: And [this is so because of] the non-negation of [all] three times, [as established] from sound, like the establishment of a musical instrument.

children.text: kim arthaṃ punar idam ucyate? pūrvoktanibandhanārtham/ yat tāvat pūrvoktam upalabdhihetor upalabdhiviṣayasya cārthasya pūrvāparasahabhāvāniyamād yathādarśanaṃ vibhāgavacanam iti, tad itaḥ samutthānaṃ yathā vijñāyeta/ anityam adarśī khalv ayam ṛṣir niyamena pratiṣedhaṃ pratyācaṣṭe --- traikālyasya cāyuktaḥ pratiṣedha iti/ tatraikāṃ vidhām udāharati śabdād ātodyasiddhivad iti/
children.translated_text: Why is this stated again? For the purpose of what was previously stated. What was stated earlier — that 'due to the non-restriction of temporal priority, posteriority, and simultaneity between the cause of cognition and the object of cognition, the specification should be stated according to observation' — so that its derivation from here may be understood. This sage, seeing the impermanent, certainly rejects the [universal] negation through restriction — and the negation of all three times is unjustified. Among them, he illustrates one type: 'from sound, like the establishment of a musical instrument.'

children.text:
% -d iti] p.431
yathā paścāt siddhena śabdena pūrvasiddham ātodyam anumīyate, sādhyaṃ cātodyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca śabdaḥ, antarhite hy ātodye svanato 'numānaṃ bhavatīti vīṇā vādyate veṇuḥ pūryate iti svanaviśeṣeṇa ātodyaviśeṣaṃ pratipadyate; tathā pūrvasiddham upalabdhiviṣayaṃ paścāt siddhenopalabdhihetunā pratipadyata iti/ nidarśanārthatvāc cāsya śeṣayor vidhayor yathoktam udāharaṇaṃ veditavyam iti/
kasmāt punar iha tan nocyate? pūrvoktam upapādyata iti/ sarvathā tāvad ayam arthaḥ prakāśayitavyaḥ, sa iha vā prakāśyeta tatra vā, na kaścid viśeṣa iti//
children.translated_text: Just as by a sound produced later, a musical instrument produced earlier is inferred — the instrument to be established is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and the sound is the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof); for when the instrument is hidden, there is inference from the sound — 'a <s>vīṇā</s> is being played,' 'a flute is being blown' — one discerns the particular instrument from the particular sound. Similarly, the object of cognition established earlier is understood through the cause of cognition established later. And since this serves as an illustration, for the remaining two types, examples should be understood as stated.

children.text:
% p.432
pramāṇaṃ prameyam iti ca samākhyā samāveśena varttate samākhyānimittavaśāt/ samākhyānimittaṃ tūpalabdhisādhanaṃ pramāṇam upalabdhiviṣayaś ca prameyam iti/ yadā ca upalabdhiviṣayaḥ kvacid upalabdhisādhanaṃ bhavati tadā pramāṇaṃ prameyam iti caiko 'rtho 'bhidhīyate/ asyārthasyāvadyotanārtham idam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: The designations '<s>pramāṇa</s>' (means of valid knowledge) and '<s>prameya</s>' (object of valid knowledge) operate through inclusion, according to the basis of the designation. The basis of the designation is: the means of cognition is <s>pramāṇa</s>, and the object of cognition is <s>prameya</s>. And when the object of cognition somewhere becomes the means of cognition, then a single object is designated as both <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>. To illuminate this point, this is stated:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.16: And [<s>pramāṇas</s> are] knowable, as in the case of the validity of a balance.

children.text: gurutvaparimāṇajñānasādhanaṃ tulā pramāṇam, jñānaviṣayo guru dravyaṃ suvarṇādi prameyam/ yathā suvarṇādinā tulāntaraṃ vyavasthāpyate tadā tulāntarapratipattau suvarṇādi pramāṇam tulāntaraṃ prameyam iti/ evam anavayavena tantrārtha uddiṣṭo veditavyaḥ/ ātmā tāvad upalabdhiviṣayatvāt prameye paripaṭhitaḥ, upalabdhau svātantryāt pramātā/ buddhir upalabdhisādhanatvāt pramāṇam, upalabdhiviṣayatvāt prameyam; ubhayābhāvāt tu pramitiḥ/ evam arthaviśeṣe samākhyāsamāveśo yojyaḥ/ tathā ca kārakaśabdā nimittavaśāt samāveśena varttanta iti/
children.translated_text: A balance is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) as the means of knowing weight and measurement; the heavy substance — gold and the like — whose weight is to be known, is the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge). Just as when gold and the like are used to calibrate another balance, in the determination of that other balance, the gold etc. becomes the <s>pramāṇa</s> and the other balance becomes the <s>prameya</s>. Thus the meaning of the treatise should be understood without remainder. The <s>ātman</s> (self), being an object of cognition, is listed under <s>prameya</s>; being independent in cognition, it is the knower. <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), being the means of cognition, is <s>pramāṇa</s>; being an object of cognition, it is <s>prameya</s>; but having both [aspects absent in a particular instance], it is <s>pramiti</s> (valid cognition). Thus the inclusion of designations should be applied to particular objects. And similarly, the <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic role) terms operate through inclusion according to their basis.

children.text:
% samāveśena vartanta iti/] p.434
vṛkṣas tiṣṭhatīti svasthitau svātantryāt kartā/ vṛkṣaṃ paśyatīti darśanenāptum iṣyamāṇatamatvāt karma/
children.translated_text: 'The tree stands' — being independent in its own state, it is the agent (<s>kartā</s>). 'He sees the tree' — being that which is most desired to be reached through seeing, it is the object (<s>karma</s>).

children.text:
% paśyatīti darśanenāptum ...] p.437
vṛkṣeṇa candramasaṃ jñāpayatīti jñāpakasya sādhakatamatvāt karaṇam/
children.translated_text: 'He indicates the moon by means of the tree' — being the most effective instrument for the indictor, it is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).

children.text:
% sādhakatamatvāt karaṇam/] p.438
vṛkṣāyodakam āsiñcatīti āsicyamānenodakena vṛkṣam abhipraitīti sampradānam/ vṛkṣāt parṇaṃ patatīti ``dhruvam apāye 'pādānam'' ity apādānam/ vṛkṣe vayāṃsi santīti ``ādhāro 'dhikaraṇam'' ity adhikaraṇam/ evam ca sati na dravyamātraṃ kārakam, na kriyāmātram/ kiṃ tarhi? kriyāsādhanaṃ kriyāviśeṣayuktaṃ kārakam/ yat kriyāsādhanaṃ svatantram sa kartā, na dravyamātraṃ na kriyāmātram/ kriyayā vyāptum iṣyamāṇatamaṃ karma,
children.translated_text: 'He pours water for the tree' — directing the water being poured toward the tree, it is the recipient (<s>sampradāna</s>). 'The leaf falls from the tree' — 'the fixed [point] in separation is <s>apādāna</s> (ablative source)' — it is the ablative source. 'The birds are in the tree' — 'the support is <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (locus)' — it is the locus. And in this being so, a <s>kāraka</s> is not mere substance, nor mere action. What then? A <s>kāraka</s> is a means of accomplishing action, possessing a specific relation to action. That which is an independent means of accomplishing action is the agent — it is not mere substance, not mere action. The object is that which is most desired to be pervaded by action,

children.text:
% -m iṣyamāṇatamaṃ karma,] p.439
na dravyamātraṃ na kryāmātram/ evaṃ sādhakatamādiṣv api/ evaṃ ca kārakānvākhyānaṃ yathaiva upapattita evaṃ lakṣaṇataḥ/ kārakānvākhyānam api na dravyamātre na kriyāyām vā/ kiṃ tarhi? kriyāsādhane kriyāviśeṣayukta iti/ kārakaśabdaś cāyaṃ pramāṇaṃ prameyam iti, sa ca kārakadharmaṃ na hātum arhati//16//
children.translated_text: not mere substance, not mere action. The same applies to 'most effective instrument' and the rest. And thus, the explanation of <s>kārakas</s> is justified both from actual usage and from the definitions. The explanation of <s>kārakas</s> pertains not to mere substance nor to action, but rather to the means of accomplishing action possessing a specific relation to action. And this <s>kāraka</s> term [applies to] '<s>pramāṇa</s>' and '<s>prameya</s>' as well, and it should not abandon the property of being a <s>kāraka</s>. //16//

children.text:
% p.440
asti bhoḥ kārakaśabdānāṃ nimittavaśāt samāveṣaḥ/ pratyakṣādīni ca pramāṇāni upalabdhihetutvāt, prameyaṃ copalabdhiviṣayatvāt/ saṃvedyāni ca pratyakṣādīni pramāṇāni, pratyakṣeṇopalabhe anumānenopalabhe upamānenopalabhe āgamenopalabhe/ pratyakṣaṃ me jñānam ānumānikaṃ me jñānam aupamānikaṃ me jñānam āgamikaṃ me jñānam iti viśeṣā gṛhyante/ lakṣaṇataś ca jñāpyamānāni jñāyante viśeṣeṇendriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam ity evamādinā/
children.translated_text: Yes indeed, there is inclusion of <s>kāraka</s> terms according to their bases. And <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the rest are <s>pramāṇas</s> because they are causes of cognition, and they are <s>prameya</s> because they are objects of cognition. And the <s>pramāṇas</s> such as <s>pratyakṣa</s> are themselves cognizable: 'perceived through perception,' 'perceived through inference,' 'perceived through analogy,' 'perceived through testimony.' 'My knowledge is perceptual,' 'my knowledge is inferential,' 'my knowledge is analogical,' 'my knowledge is testimonial' — these specific [distinctions] are grasped. And when made known through definitions, they are known specifically — 'knowledge produced from the contact of sense-organ and object' — and so forth.

children.text:
% p.441
seyam upalabdhiḥ pratyakṣādiviṣayā kiṃ pramāṇāntarataḥ athāntareṇa pramāṇāntaram asādhaneti? kaś cātra viśeṣaḥ?
children.translated_text: Now, this cognition that has <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest as its objects — does it arise from another <s>pramāṇa</s>, or without another <s>pramāṇa</s>? And what difference does it make?

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.17: If [the <s>pramāṇas</s>] are established through [another] <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is the consequence of [requiring] the establishment of the <s>pramāṇas</s> through yet another <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: yadi pratyakṣādīni pramāṇenopalabhyante, yena pramāṇenopalabhyante tat pramāṇāntaram astīti pramāṇāntarasadbhāvaḥ prasajyata iti anavasthām āha tasyāpy anyena tasyāpy anyeneti/
children.translated_text: If <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are cognized through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then the <s>pramāṇa</s> by which they are cognized — another <s>pramāṇa</s> exists for that — thus the existence of yet another <s>pramāṇa</s> follows; he speaks of an infinite regress: 'that too [requires] another, and that too another.'

children.text:
% -m astīti pramāṇāntarasadbhāvaḥ ...] p.442
na cānavasthā śakyānujñātum anupapatter iti//
children.translated_text: And an infinite regress cannot be accepted, since it is untenable.
Then let it be that [<s>pramāṇas</s> are established] without another means — without proof? —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.18: Or, from the cessation of that [regress], the establishment of <s>prameyas</s> would be like the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s>.

children.text: yadi pratyakṣādyupalabdhau pramāṇāntaraṃ nivarttane ātmādyupalabdhāv api pramāṇāntaraṃ nivartsyaty aviśeṣāt//
children.translated_text: If in the cognition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, another <s>pramāṇa</s> is dispensed with, then in the cognition of <s>ātman</s> (self) and the rest too, another <s>pramāṇa</s> would be dispensed with, since there is no distinction.

children.text:
% p.443
evaṃ ca sarvapramāṇavilopa ity ata āha ---
children.translated_text: And thus there would be the annihilation of all <s>pramāṇas</s> — therefore he says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.19: No, because their establishment is like the establishment of light by a lamp.

children.text: yathā pradīpaprakāśaḥ pratyakṣāṅgatvād dṛśyadarśane pramāṇam, sa ca pratyakṣāntareṇa cakṣuṣaḥ sannikarṣeṇa gṛhyate; pradīpabhāvābhāvayor darśanasya tathābhāvād darśanahetur anumīyate, tamasi pradīpam upādadīthā ity āptopadeśenāpi pratipadyate; evaṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ yathādarśanaṃ pratyakṣādibhir evopalabdhiḥ/ indriyāṇi tāvat svaviṣayagrahaṇenaivānumīyante/ arthāḥ pratyakṣato gṛhyante/ indriyārthasannikarṣās tv āvaraṇena liṅgenānumīyante/
children.translated_text: Just as the light of a lamp is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for the seeing of visible things, being an element of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), and it is grasped through another perception — through the contact of the eye; and since seeing is present and absent corresponding to the presence and absence of a lamp, the cause of seeing is inferred; and by the authoritative instruction 'take a lamp in the dark,' [the lamp] is also understood through testimony. Similarly, <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are cognized through <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest themselves, according to observation. The sense-organs are inferred by their grasping of their own objects. Objects are grasped through perception. The contacts of sense-organ and object are inferred through obstruction as a mark.

children.text:
% p.444
indriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam ātmamanasoḥ saṃyogaviśeṣād ātmasamavayāc ca sukhādivad gṛhyate/ evaṃ pramāṇaviśeṣo vibhajya vacanīyaḥ/ yathā ca dṛśyaḥ san pradīpaprakāśo dṛśyāntarāṇāṃ darśanahetur iti dṛśyadarśanavyavasthāṃ labhate, evaṃ prameyaṃ sat kiñcid arthajātam upalabdhihetutvāt pramāṇaprameyavyvasthāṃ labhate/ seyaṃ pratyakṣādibhir eva pratyakṣādīnāṃ yathādarśanam upalabdhir na pramāṇāntarataḥ, na ca pramāṇam antareṇa niḥsādhaneti/
tenaiva tasyāgrahaṇam iti cet, na; arthabhedasya lakṣaṇasāmānyāt --- pratyakṣādīnāṃ pratyakṣādibhir eva grahaṇam ity ayuktam, anyena hy anyasya grahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam iti/ na, arthabhedasya lakṣaṇasāmānyāt --- pratyakṣalakṣaṇenāneko 'rthaḥ saṃgṛhītas tatra kenacit kasyacid grahaṇam ity adoṣaḥ/ evam anumānādiṣv apīti/ yatoddhṛtenodakenāśayasthasya grahaṇam iti/
children.translated_text: The knowledge produced from the contact of sense-organ and object is grasped — like pleasure and the like — from a particular conjunction of the self and mind, and from inherence in the self. Thus, the specific <s>pramāṇas</s> should be distinguished and stated. And just as the light of a lamp, being itself visible, is the cause of seeing other visible things — thus obtaining the arrangement of being both visible and a cause of seeing — similarly, some class of objects, being <s>prameya</s> (knowable), obtains the arrangement of being both <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> because of being a cause of cognition. This cognition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest through <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest themselves, according to observation, is not from another <s>pramāṇa</s>, nor is it without any means — without proof. [Objection:] 'Then the same [<s>pramāṇa</s>] cannot grasp itself!' — No; due to the generality of definition applying to different objects. 'The grasping of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest by <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest themselves is unjustified, since one thing is seen to be grasped by another.' — No; due to the generality of definition applying to different objects — many objects are included under the definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s>; among them, some are grasped by others — so there is no fault. The same applies to inference and the rest. Just as drawn water [can be used to measure] water remaining in a reservoir.

children.text:
% p.445
jñātṛmanasoś ca darśanāt --- ahaṃ sukhī ahaṃ duḥkhī ceti tenaiva jñātrā tasyaiva grahaṇaṃ dṛśyate/ ``yugapajjñānānutpattir manaso liṅgam'' iti ca tenaiva manasā tasyaivānumānaṃ dṛśyate, jñātur jñeyasya cābhedo grahaṇasya grāhyasya cābheda iti/
nimittabhedo 'treti cet samānam --- na nimittāntareṇa vinā jñātā ātmānaṃ jānīte, na ca nimittāntareṇa vinā manasā mano gṛhyata iti samānam etat, pratyakṣādbhiḥ pratyakṣādīnāṃ grahaṃam ity atrāpy arthabhedo na gṛhyata iti/
pratyakṣādīnāṃ cāviṣayasyānupapatteḥ --- yadi syāt kiṃcid arthajātaṃ pratyakṣādīnām aviṣayaḥ yat pratyakṣādibhir na śakyaṃ grahītum, tasya grahaṇāya pramāṇāntaram upādīyeta, tat tu na śakyaṃ kenacid upapādayitum iti/ pratyakṣādīnāṃ yathādarśanam evedaṃ sac cāsac ca sarvaṃ viṣaya iti//
children.translated_text: And from the observation of the knower and the mind — 'I am happy,' 'I am suffering' — the grasping of the very same [self] by that very knower is observed. And 'the non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the mark of the mind' — the inference of that very mind by that very [mind] is observed; the identity of the knower and the knowable, the identity of what grasps and what is to be grasped. [Objection:] 'There is a difference of basis here!' — The response is the same: the knower does not know himself without some other basis, nor is the mind grasped by the mind without some other basis — this is the same; in the statement that <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest grasp <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, no difference of objects is grasped. And since there is nothing that is not an object of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest — if there were some class of objects that were not objects of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, that could not be grasped by <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, then another <s>pramāṇa</s> would be adduced for grasping it; but no one can establish such a thing. According to observation, this entire [domain] of the existent and non-existent — everything — is the object of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest.

children.text: NyS_2,1.20 : kvacin nivṛttidarśanād anivṛttidarśanāc ca kvacid anekāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.20: Due to the observation of cessation in some cases and non-cessation in others, [the result is] inconclusive.

children.text:
kecit tu dṛṣṭāntam aparigṛhītaṃ hetunā viśeṣahetum antareṇa sādhyasādhanāyopādadate; yathā pradīpaprakāśaḥ pradīpāntaraprakāśam antareṇa gṛhyate tathā pramāṇāni pramāṇāntaram antareṇa gṛhyata iti/ sa cāyam ---
yathā cāyaṃ prasaṅgo nivṛttidarśanāt pramāṇasādhāyopādīyate/ evaṃ prameyasādhanāyāpy upādeyo 'viśeṣahetutvāt --- yathā ca sthālyādirūpagrahaṇe pradīpaprakāśaḥ prameyasādhanāyopādīyate,
children.translated_text: But some adduce an example that has not been fully examined, using the reason without a distinguishing reason, for the establishment of what is to be proved: 'Just as the light of a lamp is grasped without the light of another lamp, so too <s>pramāṇas</s> are grasped without another <s>pramāṇa</s>.' And this — just as this illustration is adduced on the basis of the observation of cessation, for the establishment of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, so too it should be adduced for the establishment of a <s>prameya</s>, since there is no distinguishing reason — just as in the grasping of the form of a pot and the like, the light of a lamp is adduced for the establishment of a <s>prameya</s>,

children.text:
% -sādhāyopādīyate,] p.447
evaṃ pramāṇasādhāyāpy upādeyo viśeṣahetvabhāvāt, so 'yaṃ viśeṣahetuparigraham antareṇa dṛṣṭānta ekasmin pakṣe upādeyo na pratipakṣa ity anekāntaḥ/ ekasmiṃś ca pakṣe dṛṣṭānta ity anekānto viśeṣahetvabhāvād iti/
children.translated_text:
[Note: -sādhāyopādīyate,] p.447
Thus, for establishing <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) also, it should be adopted, since there is no distinguishing reason; and this example, without the acceptance of a distinguishing reason, should be adopted in one position but not in the opposing position — this is <s>anekānta</s> (non-absolutism). And that 'the example applies to only one position' is <s>anekānta</s> due to the absence of a distinguishing reason.

children.text:
% p.448
viśeṣahetuparigrahe sati upasaṃhārābhyanujñānād apratiṣedhaḥ --- viśeṣahetuparigṛhītas tu dṛṣṭānta ekasmin pakṣe upasaṃhriyamāṇo na śakyo 'nujñātum/ evaṃ ca saty anekānta ity ayaṃ pratiṣedho na bhavati/
pratyakṣādīnāṃ pratyakṣādibhir upalabdhāv anavastheti ced, na saṃvidviṣayanimittānām upalabdhyā vyavahāropapatteḥ --- pratyakṣeṇārtham upalabhe, anumānenārtham upalabhe, upamānenārtham upalabhe, āgamenārtham upalabhe iti, pratyakṣaṃ me jñānam, ānumānikaṃ me jñānam, aupamānikaṃ me jñānam, āgamikaṃ me jñānam iti saṃvidviṣayaṃ saṃvinnimittaṃ copalabhamānasya dharmārthasukhāpavargaprayojanas tatpratyanīkaparivarjanaprayojanaś ca vyavahāra upapadyate, so 'yaṃ tāvaty eva nivartate/
% tāvaty eva nivartate] p.449
na cāsti vyavahārāntaram anavasthāsādhanīyaṃ yena pratyuktānavasthām upādadīteti//20//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.448]
When a distinguishing reason is accepted, there is no prohibition, because the application is granted — but an example that is accompanied by an accepted distinguishing reason, when applied to one position, cannot be granted. And when this is the case, the prohibition that 'this is <s>anekānta</s>' does not arise.
If it is objected that there is an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) in the apprehension of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the other <s>pramāṇas</s> by <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the others — no, because practical activity is possible through the apprehension of objects of cognition and their causes. 'I apprehend an object by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), I apprehend an object by <s>anumāna</s> (inference), I apprehend an object by <s>upamāna</s> (comparison), I apprehend an object by <s>āgama</s> (testimony)' — and 'my knowledge is perceptual, my knowledge is inferential, my knowledge is analogical, my knowledge is testimonial' — for one who apprehends the object of cognition and the cause of cognition, practical activity with the purpose of <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), as well as the purpose of avoiding their opposites, is possible; and this terminates just at that point.
[Note: tāvaty eva nivartate] p.449
And there is no further practical activity that would require an infinite regress, by which one could adduce a further infinite regress — thus the objection of infinite regress has been answered. // 20 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.21]

children.text: sāmānyena pramāṇāni parīkṣya viśeṣeṇa parīkṣyante/ tatra ---
children.translated_text: Having examined the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) in general, they are now examined in particular. In that regard —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.21: The impossibility of the definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is due to incomplete statement.
For the contact of <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>manas</s> (mind), which is another cause, has not been stated. // 21 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.22]

children.text:
% p.450
na cāsaṃyukte dravye saṃyogajanyasya guṇasyotpattir iti jñānotpattidarśanād ātmamanaḥsannikarṣaḥ kāraṇam/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.450]
And since a quality produced by conjunction does not arise in a substance that is not conjoined, the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is a cause, as knowledge is observed to arise.

children.text:
% -d ātmamanaḥsannikarṣaḥ kāraṇam/] p.451
manaḥsannikarṣānapekṣasya cendriyārthasannikarṣasya jñānakāraṇatve yugapad utpadyeran buddhaya iti manaḥsannikarṣo 'pi kāraṇam/ tad idaṃ sūtraṃ purastāt kṛtabhāṣyam/
children.translated_text:
[Note: -d ātmamanaḥsannikarṣaḥ kāraṇam/] p.451
And if the contact of sense-organ and object, without depending on the contact of <s>manas</s>, were the cause of knowledge, then cognitions would arise simultaneously — therefore the contact of <s>manas</s> is also a cause. This <s>sūtra</s> has already been commented upon earlier.
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.22: In the absence of the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s>, there is no arising of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).

children.text: ātmamanasoḥ sannikarṣābhāve notpadyate pratyakṣam indriyārthasannikarṣābhāvavad iti//22//
children.translated_text: In the absence of the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s>, perception does not arise, just as in the absence of the contact of sense-organ and object. // 22 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.23]

children.text:
% p.452
sati cendriyārthasannikarṣe jñānotpattidarśanāt kāraṇabhāvaṃ bruvataḥ ---
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.452]
When the contact of sense-organ and object exists and knowledge is observed to arise, to one who asserts its causal status —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.23: The same consequence follows with respect to direction, place, time, and space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: digādiṣu satsu jñānabhāvāt tāny api kāraṇānīti? akāraṇabhāve 'pi jñānotpattir digādisannidher avarjanīyatvāt --- yadāpy akāraṇaṃ digādīni jñānotpattau, tadāpi satsu digādiṣu jñānena bhavitavyam,
children.translated_text: Since knowledge occurs in the presence of direction and the rest, are they also causes? Even when they are not causes, the arising of knowledge (still occurs), because the proximity of direction and the rest is unavoidable — even when direction and the rest are not causes of the arising of knowledge, knowledge must occur when direction and the rest are present,

children.text:
% -diṣu jñānena bhavitavyam,] p.453
na hi digādīnāṃ sannidhiḥ śakyaḥ parivarjayitum iti/ tatra kāraṇabhāve hetuvacanam, etasmād dhetor digādīni jñānakāraṇānīti//23//
children.translated_text:
[Note: -diṣu jñānena bhavitavyam,] p.453
for the proximity of direction and the rest cannot be avoided. In that case, the statement of a reason for their causal status (is demanded): 'By this reason, direction and the rest are causes of knowledge.' // 23 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.24]

children.text: ātmamanaḥsannikarṣas tarhy upasaṅkhyeya iti/ tatredam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Then the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> should be additionally enumerated (as a cause). To that, this is said —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.24: Because <s>ātman</s> (self) is indicated by knowledge, there is no exclusion.

children.text:
% p.454
jñānam ātmaliṅgaṃ tadguṇatvāt/ na cāsaṃyukte dravye saṃyogajasya guṇasyotpattir astīti//24//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.454]
Knowledge is the mark of <s>ātman</s>, because it is a quality of <s>ātman</s>. And a quality produced by conjunction does not arise in a substance that is not conjoined. // 24 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.25]
[Note: p.455]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.25: And because the non-simultaneity of those (cognitions) is the mark (of <s>manas</s>), there is no (exclusion) of <s>manas</s> either.

children.text: anavarodha iti varttate/ yugapaj jñānānutpattir manaso liṅgam ity ucyamāne sidhyaty eva manaḥsannikarṣāpekṣa indriyārthasannikarṣo jñānakāraṇam iti//25//
children.translated_text: 'No exclusion' is continued (from the previous <s>sūtra</s>). When the non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is stated as the mark of <s>manas</s>, it is thereby established that the contact of sense-organ and object, depending on the contact of <s>manas</s>, is the cause of knowledge. // 25 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.26]
[Note: p.456]

children.text: NyS_2,1.26: pratyakṣanimittatvāc cendriyārthayoḥ sannikarṣasya svaśabdena vacanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.26: Because the contact of sense-organ and object is the specific cause of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), it is stated by its own term.

children.text: pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdānāṃ nimittam ātmamanaḥsannikarṣaḥ, pratyakṣasyaivendriyārthasannikarṣa ity asamānaḥ, asamānatvāt tasya grahaṇam//26//
children.translated_text: The contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is the common cause of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>upamāna</s> (comparison), and <s>śabda</s> (testimony); the contact of sense-organ and object is specific to <s>pratyakṣa</s> alone — it is different, and because of this difference, it is mentioned (in the definition). // 26 //
[Section: NySBh_2,1.27]
[Note: p.457]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.27: And because for those who are asleep or whose minds are absorbed, the contact of sense-organ and object is the cause.

children.text:
indriyārthasannikarṣasya grahaṇaṃ nātmamanasoḥ sannikarṣasyeti/ ekadā khalv ayaṃ prabodhakālaṃ praṇidhāya suptaḥ praṇidhānavaśāt prabudhyate/ yadā tu tīvrau dhvanisparśau prabodhakāraṇaṃ bhavatas tadā prasuptasyendriyasannikarṣanimittaṃ prabodhajñānam utpadyate/ tatra na jñātur manasaś ca sannikarṣasya prādhānyaṃ bhavati/ kiṃ tarhi? indriyārthayoḥ sannikarṣasya/ na hy ātmā jijñāsamānaḥ prayatnena manas tadā prerayatīti/
ekadā khalv ayaṃ viṣayāntarāsaktamanāḥ saṅkalpavaśād viṣayāntaraṃ jijñāsamānaḥ prayatnapreritena manasā indriyaṃ saṃyojya tad viṣayāntaraṃ jānīte/ yadā tu khalv asya niḥsaṅkalpasya nirjijñāsasya ca vyāsaktamanaso bāhyaviṣayopanipātanāj jñānam utpadyate tadendriyārthasannikarṣasya prādhānyam/
children.translated_text:
