And in a counter-example, an indeterminacy would follow. Just as a horse employed in the place of an ox to draw [a cart] does not become a modification of the ox, so too the <s>ya-kāra</s> employed in the place of the <s>i-kāra</s> is not a modification. But there is no reason for such a restriction here — an example is probative, not a counter-example. //43//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.44]

[Note: p.643]
And the example of substance-modification —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.44: Not so, because there is variation in the original-state of things with unequal natures.

children.text: atulyānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ prakṛtibhāvo vikalpate vikārāś ca prakṛtīr anuvidhīyante/ na tv ivarṇam anuvidhīyate yakāraḥ/ tasmād anudāharaṇaṃ dravyavikāra iti//44//
children.translated_text: For substances that are unequal, the status of being an original form varies, and modifications conform to their originals. But the <s>ya-kāra</s> does not conform to the <s>i-kāra</s>. Therefore, substance-modification is not a [valid] example. //44//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.45]
[Note: p.644]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.45: Just as there is disparity among substance-modifications, so there is variation among phonemic modifications.

children.text: yathā dravyabhāvena tulyāyāḥ prakṛter vikāravaiṣamyam, evaṃ varṇābhāvena tulyāyāḥ prakṛter vikāravikalpa iti//45//
children.translated_text: Just as there is disparity of modification for an original that is equal in substance-nature, so there is variation of modification for an original that is equal in non-phoneme-nature. //45//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.46]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.46: Not so, because the properties of modification do not obtain.

children.text: ayaṃ vikāradharmā dravyasāmānye, yadātmakaṃ dravyaṃ mṛd vā suvarṇaṃ vā tasyātmano 'nvaye pūrvo vyūho nivartate, vyūhāntaraṃ copajāyate; taṃ vikāram ācaṣṭe/ na varṇasāmānye kaścic chabdātmā 'nvayī ya itthaṃ jahāti yatvaṃ cāpadyate/ tatra yathā sati dravyabhāve vikāravaiṣamye nānaḍuho 'śvo vikāro vikāradharmānupapatteḥ, evam ivarṇasya na yakāro vikāro vikāradharmānupapatter iti//46//
children.translated_text: This property of modification [applies] in the general category of substance: when a substance — be it clay or gold — of a certain nature [undergoes modification], its previous configuration ceases while maintaining the continuity of its essence, and a new configuration arises; this is called modification. But in the general category of phonemes, there is no phoneme-essence that persists, abandoning 'i-ness' and attaining 'y-ness.' Just as, given the substance-nature [of things], despite disparity of modification, a horse is not a modification of an ox because the properties of modification do not obtain — so too the <s>ya-kāra</s> is not a modification of the <s>i-kāra</s>, because the properties of modification do not obtain. //46//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.47]

children.text:
% p.645
itaś ca na santi varṇavikārāḥ---
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.645]
Moreover, there are no phonemic modifications because —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.47: Because there is no return of those that have attained modification.

children.text: anupapannā punarāpattiḥ/ katham? punarāpatter ananumānād iti/ ikāro yakāratvam āpannaḥ punar ikāro bhavati, na punar ikārasya sthāne yakārasya prayogo 'prayogaś cety atrānumānaṃ nāsti//47//
children.translated_text: The return [to the original state] is untenable. How? Because there is no inference of return. The <s>i-kāra</s>, having attained <s>ya-kāra</s>-hood, becomes <s>i-kāra</s> again — but there is no inference here that the <s>ya-kāra</s> is employed and then not employed in the place of the <s>i-kāra</s>. //47//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.48]

children.text: ananumānād iti na/ idaṃ hy anumānam---
children.translated_text: [The objection] 'because there is no inference' is not [valid]. For here is the inference —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.48: Because there is return in the case of gold and the like, this is not a valid reason.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ kuṇḍalatvaṃ hitvā rucakatvam āpadyate rucakatvaṃ hitvā punaḥ kuṇḍalatvam āpadyate, evam ikāro 'pi yakāratvam āpannaḥ punar ikāro bhavatīti//48//
children.translated_text: Gold abandons earring-hood and attains bracelet-hood, then abandons bracelet-hood and attains earring-hood again; similarly, the <s>i-kāra</s> too, having attained <s>ya-kāra</s>-hood, becomes <s>i-kāra</s> again. //48//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.49]

children.text:
% p.646
vyabhicārād ananumānam yathā payo dadhibhāvam āpannaṃ punaḥ na payo bhavati kim evaṃ varṇānāṃ na punarāpattiḥ, atha suvarṇavat punarāpattir iti suvarṇodāharaṇopapattiś ca---
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.646]
Because of deviation, there is no inference — just as milk that has become curd does not become milk again. Is it the case that phonemes do not return [to their original form], or is there return as with gold? The justification for the gold-example —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.49: Not so, because the modifications of that [gold] do not deviate from gold-nature.

children.text: avasthitaṃ suvarṇaṃ hīyamānena dharmeṇa upajāyamānena ca dharmi bhavati, naivaṃ kaścic chabdātmā hīyamānena itvenopajāyamānena yatvena dharmī gṛhyate, tasmāt suvarṇodāharaṇaṃ nopapadyata iti//
children.translated_text: Gold persists — it becomes the property-bearer through the property that disappears and the property that arises. But no phoneme-essence is apprehended as a property-bearer through the disappearing 'i-ness' and the arising 'y-ness.' Therefore, the gold-example is untenable.

children.text:
% p.647
varṇatvāvyatirekād varṇavikārāṇām apratiṣedhaḥ/ varṇavikārā api varṇatvaṃ na vyabhicaranti yathā suvarṇavikāraḥ suvarṇatvam iti/
sāmānyavato dharmayogo na sāmānyasya/ kuṇḍalarucakau suvarṇasya dharmau na suvarṇatvasya, evam ikārayakārau kasya varṇātmano dharmau? varṇatvaṃ sāmānyaṃ na tasyemau dharmau bhavitum arhati/ na ca nivartamāno dharma upajāyamānasya prakṛtis tatra nivartamāna ikāro na yakārasyopajāyamānasya prakṛtir iti//49//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.647]
[Objection:] Since phonemic modifications do not deviate from phoneme-hood, there is no refutation of phonemic modifications. Phonemic modifications too do not deviate from phoneme-hood, just as gold-modifications [do not deviate] from gold-hood.
[Reply:] The connection of properties belongs to the possessor of the universal, not to the universal itself. Earring and bracelet are properties of gold, not of gold-hood. Similarly, of which phoneme-essence are <s>i-kāra</s> and <s>ya-kāra</s> the properties? Phoneme-hood is a universal; these two cannot be its properties. And a property that ceases is not the original form of one that arises — the ceasing <s>i-kāra</s> is not the original form of the arising <s>ya-kāra</s>. //49//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.50]
Moreover, phonemic modification is untenable because —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.50: If [phonemes are] permanent, because there is no modification; and if impermanent, because there is no persistence.

children.text: nityā varṇā ity etasmin pakṣe ikārayakārau varṇau ity ubhayor nityatvād vikārānupapattiḥ, nityatve 'vināśitvāt kaḥ kasya vikāra iti/ athānityā varṇā iti pakṣaḥ,
children.translated_text: On the position that phonemes are permanent — since both the <s>i-kāra</s> and <s>ya-kāra</s> are phonemes and both are permanent, modification is untenable; for when [both are] permanent, since they are indestructible, which could be the modification of which? And on the position that phonemes are impermanent,

children.text:
% pakṣaḥ] p.648
evam apy anavasthānaṃ varṇānām/ kim idam anavasthānaṃ varṇānām? utpadya nirodhaḥ/ utpadya niruddhe ikāre yakāra utpadyate yakāre cotpadya niruddhe ikāra utpadyata iti kaḥ kasya vikāraḥ? tad etad avagṛhya sandhāne sandhāya cāvagrahe veditavyam iti//50//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.648 — pakṣaḥ]
even so, there is no persistence of phonemes. What is this non-persistence of phonemes? Cessation after arising. When the <s>i-kāra</s>, having arisen, ceases, the <s>ya-kāra</s> arises; and when the <s>ya-kāra</s>, having arisen, ceases, the <s>i-kāra</s> arises — so which is the modification of which? This should be understood with respect to both separation (<s>avagraha</s>) in <s>sandhi</s> and conjunction (<s>sandhāna</s>) in separation. //50//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.51]
Now, the resolution on the position of permanence —

children.text: NyS_2,2.51: nityānām atīndriyatvāt taddharmavikalpāc ca varṇavikārāṇām apratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.51: Since permanent [entities] are beyond the senses, and because of the variation of their properties, there is no refutation of phonemic modifications.

children.text: nityā varṇā na vikalpanta iti vipratiṣedhaḥ/ yathā nityatve sati kiñcid atīndriyaṃ kiñcid indriyagrāhyam, indriyagrāhyāś ca varṇāḥ, evaṃ nityatve sati kiñcin na vikriyate, varṇās tu vikriyanta iti/
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Permanent phonemes do not vary — this is a contradiction. [Reply:] Just as, permanence being granted, some things are beyond the senses while some are apprehensible by the senses — and phonemes are apprehensible by the senses — so too, permanence being granted, some things do not undergo modification, while phonemes do undergo modification.

children.text:
% p.649
virodhād ahetus taddharmavikalpaḥ/ nityaṃ nopajāyate nāpaity anupajanāpāyadharmakaṃ nityam anityaṃ punar upajanāpāyayuktam, na cāntareṇopajanāpāyau vikāraḥ sambhavati/ tad yadi varṇā vikriyante, nityatvam eṣāṃ nivartate/ atha nityāḥ, vikāradharmatvam eṣāṃ nivartate/ so 'yaṃ viruddho hetvābhāso dharmavikalpa iti//51//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.649]
The variation of properties is not a valid reason, because of contradiction. What is permanent does not come into being and does not perish — having the property of neither arising nor perishing is the nature of the permanent. The impermanent, on the other hand, is subject to arising and perishing. And without arising and perishing, modification is not possible. Therefore, if phonemes undergo modification, their permanence is negated. And if they are permanent, their property of modification is negated. This is the pseudo-reason called <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory) — the variation of properties. //51//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.52]
The resolution on the position of impermanence —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.52: And given non-persistence, the origination of their modification is like the apprehension of phonemes [themselves].

children.text:
yathānavasthāyināṃ varṇānāṃ śravaṇaṃ bhavaty evam eṣāṃ vikāro bhavati/
asambandhād asamarthā arthapratipādikā varṇopalabdhiḥ na vikāreṇa sambandhād asamarthā yā gṛhyamāṇā varṇavikāram anumāpayed iti/ tatra yādṛg idaṃ yathā gandhaguṇā pṛthivy evaṃ śabdasukhādiguṇāpīti, tādṛg etad bhavatīti/
children.translated_text:
Just as there is hearing of phonemes that do not persist, so there is modification of them.
[Objection:] The apprehension of phonemes, being unconnected [with modification], is incapable of establishing phonemic modification — [the apprehension] is not rendered capable by connection [with modification] such that, when apprehended, it could lead one to infer phonemic modification. In this regard, just as [one might argue] 'earth has the quality of odor, therefore [it also has] the qualities of sound, pleasure, etc.' — this would be [equally fallacious].

children.text:
% guṇā pṛthivy evaṃ śabdasukhādiguṇāpīti, tādṛg etad bhavatīti/] p.650
na ca varṇopalabdhir varṇanivṛttau varṇāntaraprayogasya nivartikā/ yo 'yam ivarṇanivṛttau yakārasya prayogo yady ayaṃ varṇopalabdhyā nivartate tadā tatropalabhyamānā ivarṇo yatvam āpadyate iti gṛhyeta/ tasmād varṇopalabdhir ahetur varṇavikārasyeti//52//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.650 — guṇā pṛthivy evaṃ śabdasukhādiguṇāpīti, tādṛg etad bhavatīti/]
And the apprehension of phonemes does not prevent the employment of a different phoneme upon the cessation of one phoneme. If this employment of <s>ya-kāra</s> upon the cessation of <s>i-kāra</s> were prevented by the apprehension of phonemes, then one would apprehend the <s>i-kāra</s> being apprehended there as attaining 'y-ness.' Therefore, the apprehension of phonemes is not a [valid] reason for phonemic modification. //52//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.53]

children.text: NyS_2,2.53: vikāradharmitve nityatvābhāvāt kālāntare vikāropapatteś cāpratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.53: Since there is no permanence when the property of modification obtains, and since modification is possible at a different time, there is no refutation.

children.text: taddharmavikalpād iti na yuktaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ/ na khalv vikāradharmakaṃ kiñcin nityam upalabhyata iti varṇopalabdhivad iti na yuktaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ/ avagrahe hi dadhi atreti prayujya ciraṃ sthitvā tataḥ saṃhitāyāṃ prayuṅkte dadhy atreti/
children.translated_text: The refutation through 'variation of properties' is not valid. For nothing possessing the property of modification is apprehended as permanent. And the refutation through 'like the apprehension of phonemes' is not valid either. For in separation (<s>avagraha</s>), having employed 'dadhi atra' and pausing for a long time, one then employs the conjoined form (<s>saṃhitā</s>) 'dadhy atra.'

children.text:
% prayujya ciraṃ sthitvā tataḥ saṃhitāyāṃ prayuṅkte dadhy atreti/] p.651
ciranivṛtte cāyam ivarṇe yakāraḥ prayujyamānaḥ kasya vikāra iti pratīyate, kāraṇābhāvāt kāryābhāva iti anuyogaḥ prasajyata iti//53//
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.651 — prayujya ciraṃ sthitvā tataḥ saṃhitāyāṃ prayuṅkte dadhy atreti/]
And when this <s>ya-kāra</s> is employed after the <s>i-kāra</s> has long since ceased, the question arises — of what is it a modification? The objection follows that in the absence of a cause, there is absence of the effect. //53//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.54]
Moreover, phonemic modification is untenable because —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.54: Because there is no fixed rule regarding the original form.

children.text: ikārasthāne yakāraḥ śrūyate yakārasthāne khalv ikāro vidhīyate vidhyatīti/ tad yadi syāt prakṛtivikārabhāvā varṇānām, tasya prakṛtiniyamaḥ syāt/ dṛṣṭo vikāradharmitve prakṛtiniyama iti//54//
children.translated_text: A <s>ya-kāra</s> is heard in the place of an <s>i-kāra</s>, and an <s>i-kāra</s> is prescribed in the place of a <s>ya-kāra</s> — so it is said. If there were a relation of original-form and modification among phonemes, there would be a fixed rule regarding the original form. A fixed rule regarding the original form is observed when the property of modification obtains. //54//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.55]
[Note: p.652]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.55: When there is no fixed rule, from the [actual] fixed rule, there is no absence of fixed rule.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ prakṛter aniyama uktaḥ sa niyato yathāviṣayaṃ vyavasthito niyatatvān niyama iti bhavati, evaṃ saty aniyamo nāsti, tatra yad uktaṃ prakṛtyaniyamād iti, etad ayuktam iti//55//
children.translated_text: This absence of fixed rule regarding the original form that has been stated — it is in fact fixed, being established according to its domain; since it is fixed, it constitutes a fixed rule. This being so, there is no absence of fixed rule. Therefore, the statement 'because there is no fixed rule regarding the original form' — this is untenable. //55//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.56]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2,2.56: Because of the contradiction between fixed rule and absence of fixed rule, and because there is a fixed rule even in the absence of fixed rule, there is no refutation.

children.text: niyama ity atrārthābhyanujñā, aniyama iti tasya pratiṣedhaḥ/ anujñātaniṣiddhayoś ca vyāghātād anarthāntaratvaṃ na bhavati/ aniyamaś ca niyatatvāt niyamo na bhavatīti nātrārthasya tathābhāvaḥ pratiṣidhyate/ kiṃ tarhi? tathābhūtasyārthasya niyamaśabdenābhidhīyamānasya niyatatvān niyamaśabda evopapadyate/ so 'yaṃ niyamād aniyame pratiṣedho na bhavatīti//56//
children.translated_text: <s>Niyama</s> (restriction) here means the approval of a meaning, and <s>aniyama</s> (non-restriction) is the negation of that. Since approval and prohibition are contradictory, they are not non-different in meaning. And <s>aniyama</s>, being itself determinate, does not become <s>niyama</s> — thus it is not the case that the meaning itself is negated in its such-ness. What then? The meaning, being such, when denoted by the word <s>niyama</s>, is itself established as determinate — hence only the word <s>niyama</s> is appropriate. Therefore, the negation from <s>niyama</s> to <s>aniyama</s> does not obtain. //56//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.57]

children.text:
% p.653
na ceyaṃ varṇavikāropapattiḥ pariṇāmāt kāryakāraṇabhāvād vā/ kiṃ tarhi?
children.translated_text: [Note: p.653] And this occurrence of <s>varṇavikāra</s> (phonetic modification) is not due to transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) or from a cause-effect relation. What then?

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.57: Phonetic modifications (<s>varṇavikāra</s>) arise from the occurrence of modification through <s>guṇāntarāpatti</s> (acquisition of a different quality), <s>upamarda</s> (effacement), <s>hrāsa</s> (shortening), <s>vṛddhi</s> (lengthening), <s>leśa</s> (attenuation), and <s>śleṣa</s> (augmentation).

children.text: sthānyādeśabhāvād aprayogo vikāraśabdārthaḥ, sa bhidyate/ guṇāntarāpattiḥ udāttasyānudātta ity evamādiḥ/ upamardo nāma ekarūpanivṛttau rūpāntaropajanaḥ/ hrāso dīrghasya hrasvaḥ/ vṛddhir hrasvasya dīrghaḥ, tayor vā plutaḥ/ leśo lāghavam, sta ity aster vikāraḥ/ śleṣa āgamaḥ, prakṛteḥ pratyayasya vā/ eta eva viśeṣā vikārā iti/ eta evādeśāḥ, ete ced vikārā upapadyante tarhi varṇavikārā iti//57//
children.translated_text: The meaning of the word <s>vikāra</s> (modification) is non-usage due to the relation of original form and substitute (<s>sthānin</s> and <s>ādeśa</s>), and that is differentiated as follows: <s>guṇāntarāpatti</s> is such as an <s>udātta</s> (acute accent) becoming <s>anudātta</s> (grave accent), and so forth. <s>Upamarda</s> is the production of a different form upon the cessation of one form. <s>Hrāsa</s> is a long vowel becoming short. <s>Vṛddhi</s> is a short vowel becoming long, or either of them becoming <s>pluta</s> (protracted). <s>Leśa</s> is lightening — 'sta' is the modification of the root 'as'. <s>Śleṣa</s> is augment (<s>āgama</s>), either of the base or the suffix. These very distinctions are the modifications. These very substitutions — if these are modifications, then they are phonetic modifications (<s>varṇavikāra</s>). //57//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.58]
[Note: p.654]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.58: Those [phonemes] ending in inflection (<s>vibhakti</s>) constitute a word (<s>pada</s>).

children.text:
% p.656
yathādarśanaṃ vikṛtā varṇā vibhaktyantāḥ padasaṃjñā bhavanti/ vibhaktir dvayī---nāmiky ākhyātikī ca, brāhmaṇaḥ pacatīty udāharaṇam/
children.translated_text: [Note: p.656] The phonemes modified as observed, ending in inflection, receive the designation <s>pada</s> (word). Inflection is of two kinds — nominal (<s>nāmikī</s>) and verbal (<s>ākhyātikī</s>); the examples are '<s>brāhmaṇaḥ</s>' and '<s>pacati</s>'.
[Note: p.654]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.58: Those [phonemes] ending in inflection (<s>vibhakti</s>) constitute a word (<s>pada</s>).

children.text:
% p.656
yathādarśanaṃ vikṛtā varṇā vibhaktyantāḥ padasaṃjñā bhavanti/ vibhaktir dvayī --- nāmiky ākhyātikī ca, brāhmaṇaḥ pacatīty udāharaṇam/
children.translated_text: [Note: p.656] The phonemes modified as observed, ending in inflection, receive the designation <s>pada</s> (word). Inflection is of two kinds — nominal (<s>nāmikī</s>) and verbal (<s>ākhyātikī</s>); the examples are '<s>brāhmaṇaḥ</s>' and '<s>pacati</s>'.

children.text:
% P.657
upasarganipātās tarhi na padasaṃjñāḥ lakṣaṇāntaraṃ vācyam iti; śiṣyate ca khalu nāmikyā vibhakter avyayāl lopaḥ tayoḥ padasaṃjñārtham iti//58//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.657] Then <s>upasargas</s> (preverbs) and <s>nipātas</s> (particles) would not receive the designation <s>pada</s>, and a separate definition would need to be stated; but indeed the elision (<s>lopa</s>) of the nominal inflection after indeclinables (<s>avyaya</s>) is taught for the purpose of giving them the <s>pada</s> designation. //58//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.59]

children.text:
% p.658
padenārthasampratyaya iti prayojanam, nāmapadaṃ cādhikṛtya parīkṣā, gaur iti padaṃ khalv idam udāharaṇaṃ tadarthe ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.658] The purpose [of defining <s>pada</s>] is the communication of meaning through a word. The inquiry is undertaken with reference to the noun-word (<s>nāmapada</s>). The word '<s>gauḥ</s>' (cow) is the example here, and regarding its meaning —
[Note: p.659]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.59: Doubt arises from figurative usage when <s>vyakti</s> (individual), <s>ākṛti</s> (configuration), and <s>jāti</s> (universal) are co-present.

children.text: avinābhāvavṛttiḥ sannidhiḥ/ avinābhāvena vartamānāsu vyaktyākṛtijātiṣu gaur iti prayujyate, tatra na jñāyate kim anyatamaḥ padārthaḥ utaitat sarvam iti//
children.translated_text: Co-presence (<s>sannidhi</s>) means occurrence without separation (<s>avinābhāva</s>). The word '<s>gauḥ</s>' is used when <s>vyakti</s>, <s>ākṛti</s>, and <s>jāti</s> are present inseparably, and there it is not known whether any one of them is the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>), or all of them together.
[Section: NySBh_2,2.60]
[Note: p.660] The determination of word-meaning is from the capacity of usage of the word. Therefore —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.60: The individual (<s>vyakti</s>) [is the word-meaning], because of the figurative usage in the individual of the relative pronoun (<s>yā</s>-word), collection (<s>samūha</s>), abandonment (<s>tyāga</s>), possession (<s>parigraha</s>), number (<s>saṅkhyā</s>), growth (<s>vṛddhi</s>), diminution (<s>apacaya</s>), colour (<s>varṇa</s>), compound (<s>samāsa</s>), and lineage (<s>anubandha</s>).

children.text: vyaktiḥ padārthaḥ/ kasmāt? yāśabdaprabhṛtīnāṃ vyaktāv upacārāt/ upacāraḥ prayogaḥ/ yā gaus tiṣṭhati yā gaur niṣaṇṇeiti, nedaṃ vākyaṃ jāter abhidhāyakam abhedāt, bhedāt tu dravyābhidhāyakam/
children.translated_text: <s>Vyakti</s> (individual) is the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). Why? Because of the usage of the <s>yā</s>-word and the rest in the individual. Usage means employment. 'Which cow stands, which cow is seated' — this statement does not denote <s>jāti</s> (universal), because there is no difference [in the universal]; but it denotes substance (<s>dravya</s>) because of difference.

children.text:
% dravyābhidhāyakam/] p.661
gavāṃ samūha iti bhedād dravyābhidhānaṃ na jāter abhedāt/ vaidyāya gāṃ dadatīti dravyasya tyāgo na jāter amūrtatvāt pratikramānukramānupapatteeś ca/ parigrahaḥ svatvenābhisambandhaḥ, kauṇḍinyasya gaur brāhmaṇasya gaur iti; dravyābhidhāne dravyabhedāt sambandhabheda ity upapannam, abhinnā tu jātir iti/ saṅkhyā --- daśa gāvo viṃśatir gāva iti bhinnaṃ dravyaṃ saṅkhyāyate, na jātir abhedād iti/ vṛddhiḥ kāraṇavato dravyasyāvayavopacayaḥ avardhata gaur iti; niravayavā tu jātir iti/ etenāpacayo vyākhyātaḥ/ varṇaḥ --- śuklā gauḥ kapilā gaur iti; dravyasya guṇayogo na sāmānyasya/ samāsaḥ --- gohitaṃ gosukham iti, dravyasya sukhādiyogo na jāter iti/ anubandhaḥ --- sarūpaprajananasantāno gaur gāṃ janayatīti, tadutpattidharmatvād dravye yuktaṃ na jātau viparyayād iti/ dravyaṃ vyaktir iti hi nārthāntaram//60//
children.translated_text: [Note: dravyābhidhāyakam/] [Note: p.661] 'A herd of cows' — this denotes substance because of difference, not <s>jāti</s> because of non-difference. 'He gives a cow to the physician' — this is the abandonment of a substance, not of <s>jāti</s>, because [<s>jāti</s>] is incorporeal and because the going forth and coming back [of an incorporeal entity] is impossible. <s>Parigraha</s> (possession) means connection as one's own property — '<s>Kauṇḍinya's</s> cow, the <s>brāhmaṇa's</s> cow'; when substance is denoted, the difference of relation is established because of the difference of substances, but <s>jāti</s> is undifferentiated. <s>Saṅkhyā</s> (number) — 'ten cows, twenty cows': the differentiated substance is counted, not <s>jāti</s>, because of non-difference. <s>Vṛddhi</s> (growth) is the increase of parts in a substance possessing a cause — 'the cow grew'; but <s>jāti</s> is without parts. By this, <s>apacaya</s> (diminution) is explained. <s>Varṇa</s> (colour) — 'a white cow, a tawny cow': it is the substance that has conjunction with qualities, not the universal. <s>Samāsa</s> (compound) — '<s>gohitam</s>' (cow-benefit), '<s>gosukham</s>' (cow-happiness): it is the substance that has connection with happiness and so forth, not <s>jāti</s>. <s>Anubandha</s> (lineage) — the continuity of producing offspring of the same form, 'a cow begets a cow': since it has the property of producing that, it applies to substance, not to <s>jāti</s>, because of the opposite. Substance and <s>vyakti</s> (individual) are indeed not different in meaning. //60//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.61]
[Note: p.662] The refutation of this —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.61: [The individual is] not [the word-meaning], because of non-establishment.

children.text: na vyaktiḥ padārthaḥ/ kasmāt? anavasthānāt/ yāśabdaprabhṛtibhir yo viśeṣyate sa gośabdārtho yā gaus tiṣṭhati yā gaur niṣaṇṇeti, na dravyamātram aviśiṣṭaṃ jātyā vinābhidhīyate/ kiṃ tarhi? jātiviśiṣṭam/ tasmān na vyaktiḥ padārthaḥ / evaṃ samūhādiṣu draṣṭavyam//61//
children.translated_text: <s>Vyakti</s> (individual) is not the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). Why? Because of non-establishment. That which is qualified by the <s>yā</s>-word and the rest is the meaning of the word '<s>gauḥ</s>' — 'which cow stands, which cow is seated' — mere substance without qualification is not denoted without <s>jāti</s> (universal). What then? It is [substance] qualified by <s>jāti</s>. Therefore <s>vyakti</s> is not the word-meaning. The same should be understood regarding collection and the rest. //61//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.62]

children.text: yadi na vyaktiḥ padārthaḥ kathaṃ tarhi vyaktāv upacāra iti? nimittād atadbhāve 'pi tadupacāraḥ/ dṛśyate khalu ---
children.translated_text: If <s>vyakti</s> (individual) is not the word-meaning, then how is there usage in the individual? [Answer:] From a basis (<s>nimitta</s>), even where the thing itself is absent, there is figurative usage of that term. Indeed it is observed —
[Note: p.663]

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.62: From association, location, purpose, conduct, measure, support, proximity, connection, instrumentality, and sovereignty, there is figurative usage of that term even where the thing itself is absent, as in the cases of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, bed, mat, king, barley-flour, sandalwood, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, garment, food, and person.

children.text: atadbhāve 'pi tadupacāra iti atacchabdasya tena śabdenābhidhānam iti/ sahacaraṇād --- yaṣṭikāṃ bhojayeti, yaṣtikāsahacarito brāhmaṇo 'bhidhīyata iti/
children.translated_text: 'Figurative usage of that term even where the thing itself is absent' means the designation of what is not that thing by that word. From association — 'Feed the staffs' means the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> accompanied by staffs are denoted.

children.text:
% p.664
sthānāt --- mañcāḥ krośantīti mañcasthāḥ puruṣā abhidhīyante/ tādarthyāt --- kaṭārtheṣu vīraṇeṣu vyuhyamāneṣu kaṭaṃ karotīti bhavati/ vṛtāt --- yamo rājā kubero rājeti tadvadvartata iti/ mānāt --- āḍhakena mitāḥ saktavaḥ āḍhakasaktava iti/ dhāraṇāt --- tulāyāṃ dhṛtaṃ candanaṃ tulācandanam iti/ sāmīpyāt --- gaṅgāyāṃ gāvaś carantīti deśo 'bhidhīyate sannikṛṣṭaḥ/ yogāt --- kṛṣṇena rāgeṇa yuktaḥ śāṭakaḥ kṛṣṇa ity abhidhīyate/ sādhanāt --- annaṃ prāṇā iti/ ādhipatyāt --- ayaṃ puruṣaḥ kulam ayaṃ gotram iti/ tatrāyaṃ sahacaraṇād yogād vā jātiśabdo vyaktau prayjyata iti//62//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.664] From location — 'the beds are crying' means the persons on the beds are denoted. From purpose (<s>tādarthya</s>) — when <s>vīraṇa</s> grasses intended for a mat are being gathered, one says 'he is making a mat'. From conduct (<s>vṛtta</s>) — '<s>Yama</s> is a king, <s>Kubera</s> is a king' means one who conducts himself like that. From measure (<s>māna</s>) — barley-flour measured by an <s>āḍhaka</s> measure is called '<s>āḍhaka</s>-barley-flour'. From support (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) — sandalwood held on a balance is called 'balance-sandalwood'. From proximity (<s>sāmīpya</s>) — 'cows graze on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' denotes a place nearby [the river]. From connection (<s>yoga</s>) — a garment connected with black dye is called 'black'. From instrumentality (<s>sādhana</s>) — 'food is life'. From sovereignty (<s>ādhipatya</s>) — 'this person is the family, this person is the lineage'. In that context, the <s>jāti</s>-word is used for <s>vyakti</s> through association or connection. //62//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.63]

children.text:
% p.665
yadi gaur ity asya padasya na vyaktir arthaḥ, astu tarhi ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.665] If <s>vyakti</s> (individual) is not the meaning of the word '<s>gauḥ</s>', then let it be —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.63: <s>Ākṛti</s> (configuration) [is the word-meaning], because the establishment of the identity of beings depends on it.

children.text: ākṛtiḥ padārthaḥ/ kasmāt? tadapekṣatvāt sattvavyavasthānisiddheḥ/ sattvāvayavānāṃ tadavayavānāṃ ca niyato vyūha ākṛtiḥ, tasyāṃ gṛhyamāṇāyāṃ sattvavyavasthānaṃ sidhyaty ayam gaur ayaṃ aśva iti, nāgṛhyamāṇāyām/ yasya grahaṇāt sattvavyavasthānaṃ sidhyati taṃ śabdo 'bhidhātum arhati so 'syārtha iti//63//
children.translated_text: <s>Ākṛti</s> (configuration) is the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). Why? Because the establishment of the identity of beings depends on it. The fixed arrangement (<s>vyūha</s>) of the parts of a being and its sub-parts is <s>ākṛti</s>. When that is apprehended, the identification of beings is established — 'this is a cow, this is a horse' — but not when it is not apprehended. That whose apprehension establishes the identification of beings is what the word is fit to denote, and that is its meaning. //63//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.64]

children.text: tad upapadyate yasya jātyā yogas tad atra jātiviśiṣṭam abhidhīyate gaur iti/na
children.translated_text: That is established [only] for what has connection with <s>jāti</s> (universal); it is what is qualified by <s>jāti</s> that is denoted here by '<s>gauḥ</s>'. And

children.text:
% p.666
cāvayavavyūhasya jātyā yogaḥ/ kasya tarhi? niyatāvayavavyūhasya dravyasya/tasmān nākṛtiḥ padārthaḥ/
astu tarhi jātiḥ padārthaḥ ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.666] the arrangement of parts does not have connection with <s>jāti</s>. What then? The substance having a fixed arrangement of parts [has that connection]. Therefore <s>ākṛti</s> is not the word-meaning. Let <s>jāti</s> then be the word-meaning —

children.text: NyS_2,2.64: vyaktyākṛtiyukte 'py aprasṅgāt prokṣādīnāṃ mṛdagavake jātiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.64: <s>Jāti</s> (universal) [is the word-meaning], because sprinkling and other [ritual acts] would not apply to a clay cow, even though it possesses <s>vyakti</s> (individuality) and <s>ākṛti</s> (configuration).

children.text: jātiḥ padārthaḥ/ kasmāt? vyaktyākṛtiyukte 'pi mṛdgavake prokṣaṇādīnām aprasaṅgād iti/ gāṃ prokṣaya gām ānaya gāṃ dehīti naitāni mṛdgavake prayujyante/ kasmāt? jāter abhāvāt/
children.translated_text: <s>Jāti</s> (universal) is the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). Why? Because sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and other [ritual acts] do not apply to a clay cow, even though it possesses <s>vyakti</s> and <s>ākṛti</s>. 'Sprinkle the cow, bring the cow, give the cow' — these are not used with reference to a clay cow. Why? Because of the absence of <s>jāti</s>.

children.text:
% -r abhāvāt/] p.667
asti hi tatra vyaktiḥ asty ākṛtiḥ yadabhāvāt tatrāsampratyayaḥ sa padārtha iti//64//
children.translated_text: [Note: -r abhāvāt/] [Note: p.667] For there exists <s>vyakti</s> (individuality) there, and there exists <s>ākṛti</s> (configuration) there; that whose absence causes non-comprehension there — that is the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). //64//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.65]
[Note: p.670]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.65: [<s>Jāti</s> is] not [the word-meaning], because the manifestation of <s>jāti</s> depends on <s>ākṛti</s> and <s>vyakti</s>.

children.text: jāter abhivyaktir ākṛtivyaktī apekṣate, nāgṛhyamāṇāyām ākṛtau vyaktau ca jātimātraṃ śuddhaṃ gṛhyate; tasmān na jātiḥ padārtha iti//65//
children.translated_text: The manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) of <s>jāti</s> depends on <s>ākṛti</s> and <s>vyakti</s>; when <s>ākṛti</s> and <s>vyakti</s> are not apprehended, mere <s>jāti</s> alone in its pure form is not apprehended. Therefore <s>jāti</s> is not the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). //65//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.66]

children.text: na vai padārthena na bhavituṃ śakyam, kaḥ khalv idānīṃ padārtha iti?
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is not possible for there to be no word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>) at all. What then is the word-meaning?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.66: Rather, <s>vyakti</s> (individual), <s>ākṛti</s> (configuration), and <s>jāti</s> (universal) [together] are the word-meaning.

children.text:
% p.671
tuśabdo viśeṣaṇārthaḥ/ kiṃ viśiṣyate? pradhānāṅgabhāvasyāniyamena padārthatvam iti/ yadā hi bhedavivakṣā viśeṣagatiś ca tadā vyaktiḥ pradhānam aṅgaṃ tu jātyākṛtī/ yadā tu bhedo 'vivakṣitaḥ sāmānyagatiś ca, tadā jātiḥ pradhānam aṅgaṃ tu vyaktyākṛtī/ tad etad bahulaṃ prayogeṣu/ ākṛtes tu pradhānabhāva utprekṣitavyaḥ//66//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.671] The word 'tu' (rather) serves to specify a distinction. What is being distinguished? That word-meaning-hood (<s>padārthatva</s>) obtains without restriction of the principal-subordinate relation. For when differentiation is intended and there is apprehension of the particular, then <s>vyakti</s> is principal and <s>jāti</s> and <s>ākṛti</s> are subordinate. But when differentiation is not intended and there is apprehension of the general, then <s>jāti</s> is principal and <s>vyakti</s> and <s>ākṛti</s> are subordinate. This is abundantly [seen] in usages. As for the principal status of <s>ākṛti</s>, it is to be imagined [in appropriate cases]. //66//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.67]

children.text:
% p.689
kathaṃ punar jñāyate nānā vyaktyākṛtijātaya iti? lakṣaṇabhedāt/ tatra tāvat ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.689] But how is it known that <s>vyakti</s>, <s>ākṛti</s>, and <s>jāti</s> are distinct? From the difference of their definitions. Among these, first —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.67: <s>Vyakti</s> (individual) is a corporeal entity (<s>mūrti</s>) that is the substratum of particular qualities.

children.text:
% p.690
vyajyata iti vyaktir indriyagrāhyeti na sarvaṃ dravyaṃ vyaktiḥ/ yo guṇaviśeṣāṇāṃ sparśāntānāṃ gurutvaghanatvadravatvasaṃskārāṇām avyāpinaḥ parimāṇasyāśrayo yathāsambhavaṃ tad dravyaṃ mūrtiḥ mūrcchitāvayavatvād iti//67//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.690] That which is manifested (<s>vyajyate</s>) is <s>vyakti</s> — meaning it is perceptible to the senses; thus not every substance is <s>vyakti</s>. That substance which is the substratum of particular qualities ending in touch (<s>sparśa</s>) — gravity (<s>gurutva</s>), solidity (<s>ghanatva</s>), fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (dispositional tendency) — and of non-pervasive magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>), as applicable, is a corporeal entity (<s>mūrti</s>), because its parts are congealed. //67//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.68]
[Note: p.691]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.68: <s>Ākṛti</s> (configuration) is that which is called the mark of <s>jāti</s> (universal).

children.text: yayā jātir jātiliṅgāni ca prakhyāyante tām ākṛtiṃ vidyāt/ sā ca nānyā sattvāvayavānāṃ tadavayavānāṃ ca niyatād vyūhād iti/
children.translated_text: One should know <s>ākṛti</s> as that by which <s>jāti</s> and the marks of <s>jāti</s> are made manifest. And it is nothing other than the fixed arrangement (<s>vyūha</s>) of the parts of a being and its sub-parts.

children.text:
% sattvāvayavānāṃ ... iti/] p.692
niyatāvayavavyūhāḥ khalu sattvāvayavā jātiliṅgam, śirasā pādena gām anuminvanti/ niyate ca sattvāvayavānāṃ vyūhe sati gotvaṃ prakhyāyata iti/ anākṛtivyaṅgyāyāṃ jātau mṛtsuvarṇaṃ rajatam ity evamādiṣv ākṛtir nivartate jahāti padārthatvam iti//68//
children.translated_text: [Note: sattvāvayavānāṃ ... iti/] [Note: p.692] The parts of a being, having a fixed arrangement of parts, are the mark of <s>jāti</s> — one infers a cow from its head and foot. And when there is a fixed arrangement of the parts of the being, <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) is made manifest. In the case of <s>jāti</s> that is not manifested through <s>ākṛti</s> — such as in clay, gold, silver, and so on — <s>ākṛti</s> withdraws and relinquishes its status as word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>). //68//
[Section: NySBh_2,2.69]
[Note: p.693]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.69: <s>Jāti</s> (universal) is that which produces a common cognition.

children.text: yā samānaṃ buddhiṃ prasūte bhinneṣv adhikaraṇeṣu, yayā bahūnīteretarato na vyāvartante yo 'rtho 'nekatra pratyayānuvṛttinimittaṃ tat sāmānyam/ yac ca keṣāñcid abhedaṃ kutaścid bhedaṃ karoti tat sāmānyaviśeṣo jātir iti//69//
children.translated_text: That which produces a common cognition in different substrata, by which many things are not distinguished from one another, that object which is the cause of the recurrence of cognition across many [instances] — that is <s>sāmānya</s> (the general/universal). And that which creates non-difference among some and difference from others — that universal-cum-particular is <s>jāti</s>. //69//

children.text: iti vātsyāyanīye nyāyabhāṣye dvitīyādhyāyasya dvitīyam āhnikam//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>āhnika</s> (daily lesson) of the second <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in <s>Vātsyāyana's</s> <s>Nyāya-bhāṣya</s>.
And this second <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) is concluded. //2//
[Note: p.697] Third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter), first <s>āhnika</s> (daily lesson).
[Section: NySBh_3,1.1]

children.text: parīkṣitāni pramāṇāni, prameyam idānīṃ parīkṣyate/ tac cātmādīty ātmā vivicyate, kiṃ dehendriyamanobuddhivedanāsaṅghātamātram ātmā āhosvit tadvayatirikta iti /
children.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) have been examined; now <s>prameya</s> (the object of knowledge) is examined. And that begins with <s>ātman</s> (self) — so <s>ātman</s> is investigated: is the <s>ātman</s> merely an aggregate of body, sense-organs, mind, intellect, and sensation, or is it distinct from these?

children.text:
% p.698
kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ vyapadeśyobhayathā siddheḥ/ kriyākaraṇayoḥ kartrā sambandhasyābhidhānaṃ vyapadeśaḥ/
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.698]
Whence the doubt? Because the verbal designation is established in both ways. The statement of the relation of agent with action and instrument is the designation (<s>vyapadeśa</s>).

children.text:
% vyapadeśaḥ/] p.709
sa dvividhaḥ, avayavena samudāyasya --- mūlair vṛkṣas tiṣṭhati, stambhaiḥ prāsādo dhriyata iti/ anyenānyasya vyapadeśaḥ --- paraśunā vṛścati, pradīpena paśyati/ asti cāyaṃ vyapadeśaḥ cakṣuṣā paśyati manasā vijānāti buddhyā vicārayati śarīreṇa sukhaduḥkham anubhavatīti / tatra nāvadhāryate kim avayavena samudāyasya dehādisaṅghātasya, athānyenānyasya tadvyatiriktasya veti//
children.translated_text:
[Note: vyapadeśaḥ/] p.709
That is of two kinds: (1) of the whole by means of a part — 'the tree stands by its roots,' 'the palace is supported by its pillars'; and (2) the designation of one thing by another — 'he cuts with an axe,' 'he sees by a lamp.' And there is this designation: 'he sees with the eye, he cognizes with the mind, he deliberates with the intellect, he experiences pleasure and pain with the body.' Therein it is not determined whether this is the designation of the whole, namely the body-and-the-rest aggregate, by means of a part, or of another thing, namely one distinct from these, by another.

[Note: p.710]
This is the designation of one thing by another. Why?
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.1: Because a single object is grasped by sight and touch.

children.text: darśanena kaścid artho gṛhītaḥ sparśanenāpi so 'rtho gṛhyate --- yam aham adrākṣaṃ cakṣuṣā taṃ sparśanenāpi spṛśāmīti, yaṃ cāspārkṣaṃ sparśanena taṃ cakṣuṣā paśyāmīti/ ekaviṣayau cemau pratyayāv ekakartṛkau pratisandhīyete,
children.translated_text: An object grasped by sight is also grasped by touch — 'that which I saw with my eye, I also touch by touch,' and 'that which I touched by touch, I also see with my eye.' And these two cognitions, having a single object, are synthesized as having a single agent,

children.text:
% cemau pratyayāv ...] p.711
na ca saṅghātakartṛkau, nendriyeṇaikakartṛkau/ tad yo 'sau cakṣuṣā tvagindriyeṇa caikārthasya grahītā bhinnanimittāv anyakartṛkau pratyayau samānaviṣayau pratisandadhāti so 'rthāntarabhūta ātmā/
children.translated_text:
[Note: cemau pratyayāv ...] p.711
and they do not have the aggregate as agent, nor do they have a single sense-organ as agent. Therefore, that which grasps a single object through eye and tactile sense-organ and synthesizes the two cognitions — which have different causes and would otherwise have different agents — as having the same object, that is the <s>ātman</s>, which is a distinct entity.

children.text:
% yo 'sau cakṣuṣā ...] p.712
kathaṃ punar nendriyeṇaikakartṛkau? indriyaṃ khalu svasvaviṣayagrahaṇam ananyakartṛkaṃ pratisandhātum arhati nendriyāntarasya viṣayāntaragrahaṇam iti/ kathaṃ na saṅghātakartṛkau? ekaḥ khalv ayaṃ bhinnanimittau svātmakartṛkau paryayau pratisaṃhitau vedayate na saṅghātaḥ/ kasmāt? anivṛttaṃ hi saṅghāte pratyekaṃ viṣayāntaragrahaṇasyāpratisandhānam indriyāntareṇeveti//1//
children.translated_text:
[Note: yo 'sau cakṣuṣā ...] p.712
But how do they not have a single sense-organ as agent? A sense-organ, indeed, can synthesize only the grasp of its own object — which has no other agent — but not the grasp of another object by another sense-organ. How do they not have the aggregate as agent? For this single (entity) experiences the two cognitions — which have different causes — as synthesized and as having itself as agent; the aggregate does not. Why? Because in the aggregate, the non-synthesis of each sense-organ's grasp of a different object is not overcome — just as with a different sense-organ. // 1 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.2]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.2: No, because of the fixed assignment of objects (to sense-organs).

children.text: na dehādisaṅghātād anyaś cetanaḥ/ kasmāt? viṣayavyavasthānāt/ vyavasthitaviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi, cakṣuṣy asati rūpaṃ na gṛhyate sati ca gṛhyate/ yac ca yasminn asati na bhavati sati bhavati tasya tad iti vijñāyate/
children.translated_text: There is no conscious entity other than the body-and-the-rest aggregate. Why? Because of the fixed assignment of objects. The sense-organs have fixed objects: when the eye is absent, form is not grasped; when it is present, it is grasped. And that which does not occur when something is absent but occurs when it is present is understood to belong to that.

children.text:
% bhavati sati bhavati ...] p.713
tasmād rūpagrahaṇaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ, cakṣū rūpaṃ paśyati/ evaṃ ghrāṇādiṣv apīti/ tānīndriyāṇīmāni svasvaviṣayagrahaṇāc cetanāni indriyāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvayor viṣayagrahaṇasya tathābhāvāt/ evaṃ sati kim anyena cetanena?
sandhigdhatvād ahetuḥ --- yo 'yam indriyāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvayor viṣayagrahaṇasya tathābhāvaḥ, sa kiṃ cetanatvāt, āhosvic cetanopakaraṇānāṃ grahaṇanimittatvād iti sandihyate/ cetanopakaraṇatve 'pīndriyāṇāṃ grahaṇanimittatvād bhavitum arhati//2//
children.translated_text:
[Note: bhavati sati bhavati ...] p.713
Therefore, the grasping of form belongs to the eye; the eye sees form. Likewise for the nose and the rest. These sense-organs are conscious, because they grasp their own respective objects, and because the grasping of objects corresponds to the presence and absence of the sense-organs. This being so, what need is there for another conscious entity?
(Reply:) This reason is inconclusive because it is doubtful — this correspondence of object-grasping to the presence and absence of the sense-organs: is it because of their being conscious, or because of their being instruments of a conscious entity that are the causes of grasping? This is doubtful. Even if the sense-organs are instruments of a conscious entity, their being the causes of grasping is possible. // 2 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.3]
And as for the statement 'because of the fixed assignment of objects' —
[Note: p.714]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.3: Because of that very fixed assignment, since the existence of <s>ātman</s> (is established), there is no refutation.

children.text: yadi khalv ekam indriyam avyavasthitaviṣayaṃ sarvajñaṃ sarvaviṣayagrāhi cetanaṃ syāt kas tato 'nyaṃ cetanam anumātuṃ śaknuyāt? yasmāt tu vyavasthitaviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi tasmāt tebhyo 'nyaś cetanaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvaviṣayagrāhī viṣayavyavasthitam atīto 'numīyate/ tatredam abhijñānam apratyākhyeyaṃ cetanavṛttam udāhriyate/ rūpadarśī khalv ayaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ vā pūrvagṛītam anuminoti/ gandhapratisaṃvedī ca rūparasāv anuminoti/ evaṃ viṣayaśeṣe 'pi vācyam/ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā (emend.; dṛṣṭā, ed.) gandhaṃ jighrati, ghrātvā ca gandhaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati/ tad evam aniyataparyāyaṃ sarvaviṣayagrahaṇam ekacetanādhikaraṇam ananyakartṛkaṃ pratisandhatte,
children.translated_text: If a single sense-organ had unfixed objects, were omniscient, and grasped all objects as a conscious entity — who could then infer another conscious entity distinct from it? But since the sense-organs have fixed objects, therefore another conscious entity distinct from them — omniscient, grasping all objects, transcending the fixed assignment of objects — is inferred. And here this evidence of conscious activity is cited, which cannot be denied. One who sees form infers a previously grasped taste or smell. One who perceives smell infers form and taste. The same should be stated for the remaining objects. Having seen form, one smells the smell; having smelled the smell, one sees the form. Thus, this grasping of all objects, in no fixed order, having a single conscious entity as its locus and no other agent, is synthesized,

children.text:
% sarvaviṣayagrahaṇam ...] p.715
pratyakṣānumānāgamasaṃśayān pratyayāṃś ca nānāviṣayān svātmakartṛkān pratisandhāya vedayate, sarvaviṣayaṃ ca śāstraṃ pratipadyate, artham aviṣayabhūtaṃ śrotrasya kramabhāvino varṇān śrutvā padavākyabhāvena pratisandhāya śabdārthavyavasthāṃ ca budhyamāno 'nekaviṣayam arthajātam agrahaṇīyam ekaikenendriyeṇa gṛhṇāti/ seyaṃ sarvajñasya jñeyāvyavasthānupadaṃ na śakyā parikramitum/ ākṛtimātraṃ tūdāhṛtam/ tatra yad uktam indriyacaitanye sati kim aneya cetanena tad ayuktaṃ bhavati //3//
children.translated_text:
[Note: sarvaviṣayagrahaṇam ...] p.715
and one experiences perceptual, inferential, testimonial, and dubitative cognitions — having diverse objects — as synthesized and having oneself as agent; and one comprehends an entire treatise covering all objects; and one who hears the phonemes — which are presented successively and are not the object of the ear (as a whole) — synthesizes them into words and sentences, and understanding the determination of word-meaning, grasps the manifold body of meaning that cannot be grasped by any single sense-organ. This (capacity) of the omniscient one, following the non-fixation of objects of knowledge, cannot be completely traversed. Only its general form has been illustrated. Therefore the statement 'if the sense-organs are conscious, what need is there for another conscious entity?' is improper. // 3 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.4]

children.text:
% p.716
itaś ca dehādivyatirikta ātmā, na dehādisaṅghātamātram
children.translated_text:
[Note: p.716]
And for this further reason the <s>ātman</s> is distinct from body and the rest, and is not merely the aggregate of body and the rest —
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.4: Because there would be no sin (<s>pātaka</s>) in burning the body.

children.text: śarīragrahaṇena śarīrendriyabuddhivedanāsaṅghātaḥ prāṇibhūto gṛhyate/ prāṇibhūtaṃ śarīraṃ dahataḥ prāṇihiṃsākṛtapāpaṃ pātakam ity ucyate; tasyābhāvaḥ, tatphalena kartur asambandhāt, akartuś ca sambandhāt/ śarīrendriyabuddhivedanāprabandhe khalv anyaḥ saṅghāta utpadyate anyo nirudhyate,
children.translated_text: By the word 'body,' the living aggregate of body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensation is understood. The sin (<s>pātaka</s>) produced by the violence of killing a living being, committed by one who burns a living body, is so called; (the argument is that there would be) its absence, because the agent would not be connected with its result, while one who is not the agent would be connected.

children.text:
% nirudhyate,] p.717
utpādanirodhasantatibhūtaḥ prabandho nānyatvaṃ bādhate dehādisaṅghātasyānyatvādhiṣṭhānatvāt/ anyatvādhiṣṭhāno hy asau prakhyāyata iti/ evaṃ ca sati yo dehādisaṅghātaḥ prāṇibhūto hiṃsāṃ karoti nāsau hiṃsāphalena sambadhyate, yaś ca sambadhyate na tena hiṃsā kṛtā/ tad evaṃ sattvabhede kṛtahānam akṛtābhyāgamaḥ prasajyate/ sati ca sattvotpāde sattvanirodhe cākarmanimittaḥ sattvasarsargaḥ prāpnoti, tatra muktyartho brahmacaryavāso na syāt/ tad yadi dehādisaṅghātamātraṃ sattvaṃ syāt śarīradāhe pātakaṃ na bhavet, aniṣṭaṃ caitat/ tasmād dehādisaṅghātavyatirikta ātmā nitya iti//4//
children.translated_text:
[Note: nirudhyate,] p.717
In the continuum of body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensation, one aggregate arises and another ceases; the continuum consisting of the succession of arising and cessation does not negate otherness, because the body-and-the-rest aggregate is the basis of otherness. For that (aggregate) is known to be the basis of otherness. And this being so, the body-and-the-rest aggregate that, as a living being, commits violence is not connected with the result of that violence, and the one that is connected did not commit the violence. Thus, when beings are different (at different moments), the consequence of loss of what was done and arrival of what was not done follows. And when there is the origination and cessation of beings, the association of beings without the cause of <s>karma</s> would follow; in that case, the practice of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) for the purpose of liberation would be pointless. Therefore, if the living being were merely the body-and-the-rest aggregate, there would be no sin in burning the body — and this is undesirable. Therefore the <s>ātman</s>, distinct from the body-and-the-rest aggregate, is permanent. // 4 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.5]
[Note: p.720]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.5: The absence of that (sin) would also follow in the burning of that which has a (permanent) <s>ātman</s>, because of its permanence.

children.text: yasyāpi nityenātmanā sātmakaṃ śarīraṃ dahyate tasyāpi śarīradāhe pātakaṃ na bhaved dagdhuḥ/
children.translated_text: Even for one who holds that the body, which has a permanent <s>ātman</s>, is burned — for that person too, there would be no sin in burning the body, for the one who burns.

children.text:
% na bhaved dagdhuḥ/] p.721
kasmāt? nityatvād ātmanaḥ; na jātu kaścin nityaṃ hiṃsitum arhati/ atha hiṃsyate, nityatvam asya na bhavati/ seyam ekasmin pakṣe hiṃsā niṣphalā anyasmiṃs tv anupapanneti//5//
children.translated_text:
[Note: na bhaved dagdhuḥ/] p.721
Why? Because of the permanence of the <s>ātman</s>; no one can ever harm what is permanent. And if it is harmed, its permanence would not hold. Thus, on one view, the harm is without result; on the other, it is impossible. // 5 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.6]
[Note: p.724]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.6: No, because of the destruction of the substratum of effects and of the agents (of cognition).

children.text: na brūmo nityasya sattvasya badho hiṃsā, api tv anucchittidharmakasya sattvasya kāryāśrayasya śarīrasya svaviṣayopalabdheś ca kartṛṇām indriyāṇām upaghātaḥ pīḍā vaikalyalakṣaṇaḥ prabandhocchedo vā pramāpaṇalakṣaṇo vā vadho hiṃseti/ kāryaṃ tu sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanaṃ tasyāyatanam adhiṣṭhānam āśrayaḥ śarīram,
children.translated_text: We do not say that killing is the destruction of a permanent being; rather, the injury — characterized by affliction, impairment, severance of continuity, or killing — of the body, which is the substratum of effects for a being that has the nature of not being annihilated, and of the sense-organs which are the agents of apprehending their own objects, that is violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>). The 'effect' is the experience of pleasure and pain; its seat, abode, and substratum is the body.

children.text:
% tasyāyatanam adhiṣṭhānam ...] p.725
kāryāśrayasya śarīrasya svaviṣayopalabdheś ca kartṛṇām indriyāṇāṃ badho hiṃsā, na nityasyātmanaḥ/ tatra yad uktam --- ``tadabhāvaḥ sātmakapradāhe 'pi tannityatvād'' ity etad ayuktam/ yasya sattvocchedo hiṃsā tasya kṛtahānam akṛtābhyāgamaś ceti doṣaḥ/ etāvac caitat syāt --- sattvocchedo vā hiṃsā, anucchittidharmakasya sattvasya kāryāśrayakartṛvadho vā; na kalpāntaram asti/ sattvocchedaś ca pratiṣiddhaḥ, tatra kim anyat? śeṣaṃ yathābhūtam iti/
atha vā kāryāśrayakartṛvadhād iti, kāryāśrayo dehendriyabuddhisaṅghātaḥ, nityasyātmanas tatra sukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedanam, tasyādhiṣṭhānam āśrayaḥ tadāyatanaṃ tad bhavati na tato 'nyad iti sa eva kartā/ tannimittā hi sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanasya nivṛttiḥ na tam antareṇeti/ tasya vadha upaghātaḥ pīḍā pramāpaṇam vā hiṃsā na nityatvenātmocchedaḥ/ tatra yad uktam --- ``tadabhāvaḥ sātmakapradāhe 'pi tannityatvāt'' etan neti//6//
children.translated_text:
[Note: tasyāyatanam adhiṣṭhānam ...] p.725
The destruction of the body, which is the substratum of effects, and of the sense-organs, which are the agents of apprehending their own objects — that is violence, not (the destruction) of the permanent <s>ātman</s>. Therefore, the statement 'the absence of that (sin) would also follow in the burning of that which has a (permanent) <s>ātman</s>, because of its permanence' is improper. For the one whose view is that violence is the annihilation of a being, the fault of loss of what was done and arrival of what was not done (follows). And the matter amounts to just this: either violence is the annihilation of a being, or it is the destruction of the substratum of effects and the agents (of cognition) for a being that has the nature of not being annihilated — there is no third alternative. And the annihilation of beings has been refuted; so what else (remains)? The remainder is as stated.
Alternatively, 'because of the destruction of the substratum of effects and of the agents' means: the substratum of effects is the aggregate of body, sense-organs, and intellect; the permanent <s>ātman</s>'s experience of pleasure and pain occurs there; its seat, abode, and locus is that (aggregate), and nothing other than that — so it itself is the agent. For the cessation of the experience of pleasure and pain is caused by that (aggregate), not without it. The destruction of that — whether injury, affliction, or killing — is violence, not the annihilation of the <s>ātman</s> through its permanence. Therefore, the statement 'the absence of that (sin) would also follow in the burning of that which has a (permanent) <s>ātman</s>, because of its permanence' is refuted. // 6 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.7]

[Note: p.726]
And for this further reason the <s>ātman</s> is distinct from body and the rest —
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.7: Because of the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) of what was seen by one (eye) through the other.

children.text: pūrvaparayor vijñānayor ekaviṣaye pratisandhijñānaṃ pratyabhijñānam --- tam evaitarhi paśyāmi yam ajñāsiṣam sa evāyam artha iti savyena cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭasyetareṇāpi cakṣuṣā pratyabhijñānād yam adrākṣaṃ tam evaitarhi paśyāmīti/
children.translated_text: Recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) is the synthesizing knowledge of a single object between an earlier and a later cognition — 'I now see that very thing which I knew before; this is that very object.' Because of the recognition through one eye of what was seen by the other eye — 'that which I saw (before), I now see the same thing.'

children.text:
% yam adrākṣaṃ ...] p.727
indriyacaitanye tu nānyadṛṣṭam anyaḥ pratyabhijānātīti pratyabhijñānupapattiḥ/ asti tv idaṃ pratyabhijñanam tasmād indriyavyatiriktaś cetanaḥ//7//
children.translated_text:
[Note: yam adrākṣaṃ ...] p.727
But if consciousness belonged to the sense-organs, then what was seen by one could not be recognized by another — so recognition would be impossible. But this recognition does exist; therefore there is a conscious entity distinct from the sense-organs. // 7 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.8]
[Note: p.728]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.8: (It is) not (the same eye), because the notion of duality arises in what is a single (eye) separated by the nasal bone.

children.text: ekam idaṃ cakṣur madhye nāsāsthivyavahitaṃ tasyāntau gṛhyamāṇau dvitvābhimānaṃ prayojayato madhyavyavahitasya dīrghasyeva//8//
children.translated_text: This eye is one, separated in the middle by the nasal bone; its two extremities, when perceived, give rise to the notion of duality — like a single long thing separated in the middle. // 8 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.9]
[Note: p.729]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.9: Because when one is destroyed the second is not destroyed, there is no unity.

children.text: ekasminn upahate coddhṛte vā cakṣuṣi dvitīyam avatiṣṭhate cakṣuḥviṣayagrahaṇaliṅgam, tasmād ekasya vyavadhānānupapattiḥ//9//
children.translated_text: When one eye is injured or removed, the second one persists — as indicated by the grasping of visual objects — therefore the impossibility of a single (eye) being divided (follows). // 9 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.10]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.10: (This reason is) invalid, because the whole is perceived even when a part is destroyed.

children.text: ekavināśe dvitīyāvināśād ity ahetuḥ/ kasmāt? vṛkṣasya hi kāsucic chākhāsu chinnāsūpalabhyate eva vṛkṣaḥ//10//
children.translated_text: 'Because when one is destroyed the second is not destroyed' — this is invalid. Why? Because even when some branches of a tree are cut, the tree is still perceived. // 10 //
[Section: NySBh_3,1.11]
[Note: p.730]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.11: Because of the contradiction with the example, there is no refutation.

children.text:
na kāraṇadravyasya vibhāge kāryadravyam avatiṣṭate nityatvaprasaṅgāt/ bahuṣv avayaviṣu yasya kāraṇāni vibhaktāni tasya vināśaḥ, yeṣāṃ kāraṇāny avibhaktāni tāni avatiṣṭhante/
atha vā dṛśyamānārthavirodho dṛṣṭāntavirodhaḥ/ mṛtasya hi śiraḥkapāle dvāv avaṭau nāsāsthivyavahitau cakṣuṣaḥ sthāne bhedena gṛhyete na caitad ekasmin nāsāsthivyavahite sambhavati/
atha vā ekavināśasyāniyamād dvāv imāv arthau, tau ca pṛthagāvaraṇopaghātau anumīyete vibhinnav iti/
children.translated_text:
When there is a separation of the causal substance, the effect-substance does not persist — for otherwise permanence would follow. When an entity's causes are separated among multiple wholes (<s>avayavin</s>), that entity is destroyed; those whose causes are not separated persist.
Alternatively, the contradiction with what is observed constitutes the contradiction with the example. For in the skull of a dead person, two hollows separated by the nasal bone are perceived by difference as the place of the eyes; and this is not possible in a single (eye) separated by the nasal bone.
Or alternatively, since the destruction of a single (entity) is not deterministic, there are these two objects; and they are inferred as two separate (entities) by their separate obstructions and destructions.

children.text:
% anumīyete vibhinnav iti/] p.731
avapīḍanāc caikasya cakṣuṣo raśmiviṣayasannikarṣasya bhedād dṛśyabheda iva gṛhyate; tac caikatve virudhyate; avapīḍananivṛttau cābhinnapratisandhānam iti/ tasmād ekasya vyavadhānānupapattiḥ//11//
children.translated_text: And by pressing down one eye, because of the difference in the contact of the visual ray with the sense-object, (the single object) is perceived as if different — as a difference in what is seen. And this is contradicted if there is (only) one (eye). And upon the cessation of pressing down, there is reconnection as undivided. Therefore, the impossibility of an obstruction for a single (entity is established). // 11 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.12]
And this conscious entity is inferred to be distinct from the aggregate of body and the rest —
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.12: Because of the modification of another sense-organ.

children.text: kasyacid amlaphalasya gṛhītatadrasasāhacarye rūpe gandhe vā kenacid indriyeṇa gṛhyamāṇe rasanasyendriyāntarasya vikāraḥ rasānusmṛtau rasagardhivartito dantodakasaṃplavabhūto gṛhyate/ tasyendriyacaitanye 'nupapattiḥ, nānyadṛṣṭam anyaḥ smarati//12//
children.translated_text: When the color or smell of some sour fruit — whose taste has previously been experienced in association (with those properties) — is being perceived by some sense-organ, a modification of another sense-organ, namely the tongue, is perceived — consisting of the recollection of the taste, driven by the craving for that taste, manifesting as salivation. Its impossibility under the (hypothesis of) sense-organ-consciousness (is this): what was experienced by one (sense-organ) is not remembered by another. // 12 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.13]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.13: Not so, because memory (<s>smṛti</s>) has what is to be remembered as its object.

children.text: smṛtir nāma dharmo nimittād utpadyate, tasyāḥ smartavyo viṣayaḥ, tatkṛta indriyāntaravikāro nātmakṛta iti//13//
children.translated_text: Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is a property that arises from a cause (<s>nimitta</s>); its object is what is to be remembered. The modification of another sense-organ is caused by that (memory), not by the <s>ātman</s> (self). // 13 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.14]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.14: Since memory exists as a quality of the <s>ātman</s>, (the <s>ātman</s>) is not denied.

children.text: tasyā ātmaguṇatve sati sadbhāvād apratiṣedha ātmanaḥ/ yadi smṛtir ātmaguṇaḥ, evaṃ sati smṛtir upapadyate nānyad dṛṣṭam anyaḥ samaratīti/ indriyacaitanye tu nānākartṛkāṇāṃ viṣayagrahaṇānām apratisandhānam, pratisandhāne vā viṣayavyavasthānupapattiḥ/ ekas tu cetano 'nekārthadarśī bhinnanimittaḥ pūrvadṛṣṭam artham smaratīti ekasyānekārthadarśino darśanapratisandhānāt smṛter ātmaguṇatve sati sadbhāvaḥ viparyaye cānupapattiḥ/
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> is not denied, because memory exists as a quality of the <s>ātman</s>. If memory is a quality of the <s>ātman</s>, then memory is established — 'what was experienced by one (sense-organ) is not remembered by another.' But under the (hypothesis of) sense-organ-consciousness, perceptions of objects by different agents would have no interconnection (<s>pratisandhāna</s>); or if there were interconnection, the determinate relation of sense-organs to their objects would be impossible. But a single conscious entity, perceiving multiple objects, remembers a previously perceived object due to different occasioning causes — hence, from the interconnection of perceptions by a single perceiver of multiple objects, memory exists as a quality of the <s>ātman</s>; and in the contrary case, it is impossible.

children.text:
% -pratisandhānāt smṛter ...] p.734
smṛtyāśrayāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ sarve vyavahārāḥ/ ātmaliṅgam udāharaṇamātram indriyāntaravikāra iti/
aparisaṅkhyānāś ca smṛtiviṣayasya --- aparisaṅghyāya ca smṛtiviṣayam idam ucyate ``na smṛteḥ smartavyaviṣayatvād'' iti/ yeyaṃ smṛtir agṛhyamāṇe 'rthe ajñāsiṣam aham amum artham iti, etasyā jñātṛjñānaviśiṣṭaḥ pūrvajñāto 'rtho viṣayo nārthamātram, jñātavān aham amum artham,
children.translated_text:
All activities of living beings depend on memory. The modification of another sense-organ is merely an illustration of the inferential mark of the <s>ātman</s>.
And the object of memory is unlimited — this (sūtra) 'not so, because memory has what is to be remembered as its object' is stated without analyzing the full scope of memory's object. This memory — when an object is not being perceived — 'I did not know this object' — its object is the previously-known object qualified by the knower and the knowledge, not just the bare object. 'I knew this object,'

children.text:
% p.735
asav artho mayā jñataḥ, asminn arthe mama jñānam abhūd iti caturvidham etadvākyaṃ smṛtiviṣayajñāpakaṃ samānārtham/ sarvatra khalu jñātā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca gṛhyate/ atha pratyakṣe 'rthe yā smṛtis tayā trīṇi jñānāni ekasminn arthe pratisandhīyante samānakartṛkāṇi, na nānākartṛkāṇi nākartṛkāṇi/ kiṃ tarhi? ekakartṛkāṇi/ adrākṣam amum arthaṃ yam evaitarhi paśyāmi/ adrākṣam iti darśanaṃ darśanasaṃvic ca, na khalv asaṃvidite sve darśane syād etad adrakṣam iti/ te khalv ete dve jñāne, yam evaitarhi paśyāmīti tṛtīyaṃ jñānam, evam eko 'rthas tribhir jñānair yujyamāno nākartṛko na nānākartṛkaḥ kiṃ tarhi?
children.translated_text: 'this object was known by me,' 'I had knowledge regarding this object' — these four statements, being of the same meaning, indicate the object of memory. In every case, the knower, the knowledge, and the knowable are apprehended. Now, regarding a directly perceived object, the memory by which three cognitions are interconnected with respect to a single object — these are of the same agent, not of different agents, not agentless. Rather, they have a single agent. 'I perceived this object which I now perceive.' 'I perceived' — this is the perception and the awareness of that perception; for there could not be (the statement) 'I perceived' without awareness of one's own perception. These indeed are two cognitions. 'Which I now perceive' — this is the third cognition. Thus, a single object, being connected with three cognitions, is neither agentless nor of multiple agents. Rather,

children.text:
% -s tribhir jñānair ...] p.736
ekakartṛka iti/ so 'yaṃ smṛtiviṣayo 'parisaṅkhyāyamāno vidyamānaḥ prajñāto 'rthaḥ pratiṣidhyate --- nāsty ātmā smṛteḥ smartavyaviṣayatvād iti/ na cedaṃ smṛtimātraṃ smartavyamātraviṣayam vā idaṃ khalu jñānapratisandhānavat smṛtipratisandhānam ekasya sarvaviṣayatvāt/ eko 'yaṃ jñātā sarvaviṣayaḥ svāni jñānāni pratisandhatte amum arthaṃ jñāsyāmi amum artham vijānāmy amum artham ajñāsiṣam amum arthaṃ jijñāsamānaś ciram ajñātvādhyavasyaty ajñāsiṣam iti/ evaṃ smṛtim api trikālaviśiṣṭāṃ suṣmūrṣāviśiṣṭāṃ ca pratisandhatte/ saṃskārasantatimātre tu sattve utpadyotpadya saṃskārās tirobhavanti/ sa nāsty eko 'pi saṃskāro yas trikālaviśiṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiṃ cānubhavet/ na cānubhavam antareṇa jñānasya smṛteś ca pratisandhānam ahaṃ mameti cotpadyate dehāntaravat/ ato 'numīyate asty ekaḥ sarvaviṣayaḥ pratidehaṃ svajñānaprabandhaṃ smṛtiprabandhaṃ ca pratisandhatta iti, yasya dehāntareṣu vṛtter abhāvān na pratisandhānaṃ bhavatīti//14//
children.translated_text: it has a single agent. This is the object of memory — the existent, well-known object, which is being denied without proper analysis: 'The <s>ātman</s> does not exist, because memory has what is to be remembered as its object.' This is not merely memory or merely the object of what is to be remembered; this is the interconnection of memory, like the interconnection of knowledge, because a single (entity) has all objects as its domain. This single knower, having all objects as its domain, interconnects its own cognitions: 'I shall know this object, I am knowing this object, I knew this object, wanting to know this object, having not known it for long, I ascertain — I did not know it.' Similarly, it also interconnects memory qualified by three times and qualified by the desire to remember. But in the case of a mere continuum of latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the latent impressions, having arisen, vanish. There is not a single latent impression that would experience knowledge and memory qualified by three times. And without experience, there is no interconnection of knowledge and memory; the notions 'I' and 'mine' arise (only with a self), just as with another body (they do not transfer). Therefore, it is inferred: there exists a single entity having all objects as its domain, which in each body interconnects its own continuum of knowledge and its continuum of memory — and whose activity not occurring in other bodies explains the absence of interconnection (between persons). // 14 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.15]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.15: Not so, because the grounds for the cognition of the <s>ātman</s> are possible in the mind (<s>manas</s>).

children.text: na dehādisaṅghātavyatirikta ātmā/ kasmāt? ātmapratipattihetūnāṃ manasi sambhavāt ---``darśanasparśanābhyām ekārthagrahaṇād'' ity evamādīnām ātmapratipādakānāṃ hetūnāṃ manasi sambhavo yataḥ, mano hi sarvaviṣayam iti/ tasmān na śarīrendriyamanobuddhisaṅghātavyatirikta ātmeti//15//
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> is not distinct from the aggregate of body and the rest. Why? Because the grounds for the cognition of the <s>ātman</s> — such as 'from the apprehension of a single object through sight and touch' and the like — these reasons that prove the <s>ātman</s> are possible in the mind, since the mind has all objects as its domain. Therefore, there is no <s>ātman</s> distinct from the aggregate of body, sense-organs, mind, and intellect. // 15 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.16]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.16: Because the instruments of knowledge are established for a knower, it is merely a difference of designation.

children.text: jñātuḥ khalu jñānasādhanāny upapadyante --- cakṣuṣā paśyati ghrāṇena jighrati sparśanena spṛśati, evaṃ mantuḥ sarvaviṣayasya matisādhanam antaḥkaraṇabhūtaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ vidyate yenāyaṃ manyata iti/ evaṃ sati jñātary ātmasaṃjñā na mṛṣyate manaḥsaṃjñābhyanujñāyate/ manasi ca manaḥsaṃjñā na mṛṣyate matisādhanaṃ tv abhyanujñāyate/ tad idaṃ saṃjñābhedamātraṃ nārthe vivāda iti/
children.translated_text: For the knower, instruments of knowledge are established: he sees with the eye, smells with the nose, touches with the organ of touch. Similarly, for the thinker (<s>mantṛ</s>), who has all objects as its domain, there exists an inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) that serves as the instrument of thought, having all objects as its domain, by which he thinks. This being so, the designation '<s>ātman</s>' is not accepted for the knower, while the designation '<s>manas</s>' (mind) is accepted. And for the mind, the designation '<s>manas</s>' is not accepted, but the role of instrument of thought is accepted. This is merely a difference of designation, not a dispute about the reality.

children.text:
% p.738
pratyākhyāne vā sarvendriyavilopaprasaṅaḥ/ atha mantuḥ sarvaviṣayasya matisādhanaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ pratyākhyāyate nāstīti, evaṃ rūpādiviṣayagrahaṇasādhanāny api na santīti sarvendriyavilopaḥ prasajyata iti//16//
children.translated_text: Or, if (the inner organ is) rejected, the consequence would be the destruction of all sense-organs. If the instrument of thought having all objects as its domain is rejected as not existing for the thinker who has all objects as its domain — then the instruments for the apprehension of visible form and the like would also not exist, and the consequence would be the destruction of all sense-organs. // 16 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.17]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.17: And the restriction (you claim) is without inferential support.

children.text:
yo 'yam niyama iṣyate, rūpādigrahaṇasādhanāny asya santi, matisādhanaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ nāstīti, ayaṃ niyamo niranumānaḥ/ nātrānumānam asti yena niyamaṃ pratipadyāmaha iti/
rūpādibhyaś ca viṣayāntaraṃ sukhādayas tadupalabdhau karaṇāntarasadbhāvaḥ/ yathā cakṣuṣā gandho na gṛhyata iti karaṇāntaraṃ ghrāṇam evaṃ cakṣur ghrāṇābhyāṃ raso na gṛhyata iti karaṇāntaraṃ rasanam/ evaṃ śeṣeṣv api/ tathā cakṣurādibhiḥ sukhādayo na gṛhyanta iti karaṇāntareṇa bhavitavyam/
children.translated_text:
This restriction that is accepted — 'The instruments for the apprehension of visible form and the like exist for it, but an instrument of thought having all objects as its domain does not exist' — this restriction is without inferential support. There is no inference here by which we could establish such a restriction.
And pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like are different objects from visible form and the rest; for their perception, the existence of another instrument (must be admitted). Just as smell is not perceived by the eye — hence another instrument, the nose (exists); just as taste is not perceived by the eye and nose — hence another instrument, the tongue (exists). Similarly for the rest. Likewise, since pleasure and the like are not perceived by the eye and the rest, there must be another instrument.

children.text:
% kāraṇāntareṇa bhavitavyam/] p.739
tac ca jñānāyaugapadyaliṅgam/ yac ca sukhādyupalabdhau karaṇaṃ tac ca jñānāyaugaoadyaliṅgaṃ tasyendriyam indriyaṃ prati sannidher asannidheḥ ca na yugapaj jñānāny utpadyanta iti/ tatra yad uktam ``ātmapratipattihetūnāṃ manasi sambhavāt'' iti tad ayuktam//17//
children.translated_text: And that is marked by the non-simultaneity of cognitions. That instrument for the perception of pleasure and the like is also marked by the non-simultaneity of cognitions (<s>jñānāyaugapadya</s>); it is a sense-organ — because, with respect to this sense-organ, from its proximity and non-proximity, cognitions do not arise simultaneously. Therefore, the statement 'because the grounds for the cognition of the <s>ātman</s> are possible in the mind' is untenable. // 17 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.18]

children.text:
% p.740
kiṃ punar ayaṃ dehādisaṅghātād anyo nityaḥ utānitya iti/ kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? ubhayathā dṛṣṭatvāt saṃśayaḥ/ vidyamānam ubhayathā bhavati nityam anityaṃ ca/ pratipādite ca ātmasadbhāve saṃśayānivṛttir iti/
children.translated_text: Now, is this (self), being other than the aggregate of body and the rest, permanent or impermanent? Whence the doubt? The doubt arises because it is seen in both ways: what exists can be both permanent and impermanent. And when the existence of the <s>ātman</s> has been established, the doubt is not resolved.

children.text:
% p.741
ātmasadbhāvahetubhir evāsya prāg dehabhedād avasthānaṃ siddham ūrddhvam api dehabhedād avatiṣṭhate/ kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: The very reasons that establish the existence of the <s>ātman</s> also establish its persistence prior to the destruction of the body; (the question is whether) it persists even after the destruction of the body. How (is this established)?
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.18: Because a newborn's experience of joy, fear, and grief is established through the connection with memory of what was previously practiced.

children.text: jātaḥ khalv ayaṃ kumārako 'smin janmany agṛhīteṣu harṣabhayaśokahetuṣu harṣabhayaśokān pratipadyate liṅgānumeyān/ te ca smṛtyanubandhād utpadyante nānyathā/ smṛtyanubandhaś ca pūrvābhyāsam antareṇa na bhavati/ pūrvābhyāsaś ca pūrvajanmani sati, nānyatheti sidhyaty etat avatiṣṭhate 'yam ūrdhvaṃ śarīrabhedād iti//18//
children.translated_text: Indeed, this newborn infant, in this life — when the causes of joy, fear, and grief have not yet been apprehended — experiences joy, fear, and grief that are inferred from signs. And these arise from the connection with memory (<s>smṛtyanubandha</s>), not otherwise. And the connection with memory does not occur without prior practice (<s>pūrvābhyāsa</s>). And prior practice (requires) a prior birth; not otherwise. Thus it is established that (the <s>ātman</s>) persists even after the destruction of the body. // 18 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.19]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.19: Like the modifications of blooming and closing in lotuses and the like, such are its modifications.

children.text:
yathā padmādiṣv anityeṣu prabodhaḥ sammīlanaṃ vikāro bhavati evam anityasyātmano harṣabhayaśokasampratipattir vikāraḥ syāt/
hetvabhāvād ayuktam --- anena hetunā padmādiṣu prabodhasammīlanavikāravad anityasyātmano harṣādisampratipattir iti nātrodāharaṇasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanaṃ hetur na vaidharmyād asti hetvabhāvāt asambaddhārthakam apārthakam ucyata iti/
children.translated_text:
Just as in lotuses and the like, which are impermanent, blooming, closing, and modification occur — so too, the experience of joy, fear, and grief would be modifications of an impermanent <s>ātman</s>.
(Reply:) This is untenable because of the absence of a reason. By this reason — that 'the experience of joy etc. of an impermanent <s>ātman</s> is like the modifications of blooming and closing in lotuses and the like' — here, the similarity of the example does not serve as a reason establishing what is to be proved, nor does the dissimilarity. Because of the absence of a reason, (the argument) is stated to be unconnected in meaning, i.e. purposeless.

children.text:
% p.744
dṛṣṭāntāc ca harṣādinimittasyānivṛttiḥ --- yā ceyam āseviteṣu viṣayeṣu harṣādisampratipattiḥ smṛtyanubandhakṛtā pratyātmanaṃ gṛhyate seyaṃ padmādisammīlanadṛṣṭāntena na nivartate/ yathā ceyaṃ na nivarttate tathā jātasyāpīti/ kriyājātau ca parṇavibhāgasaṃyogau prabodhasammīlane, kriyāhetuś ca kriyānumeyaḥ/ evaṃ ca sati kiṃ dṛṣṭāntena pratiṣidhyate//19//
children.translated_text: And from the example, the cause of joy and the like is not negated — this experience of joy and the like in familiar sense-objects, caused by the connection with memory, is perceived in each individual self. This is not negated by the example of the closing of lotuses and the like. And just as this is not negated (in the case of experienced objects), so also for one who is (newly) born. And in the production of the actions (of blooming and closing), the separation and conjunction of petals constitute the blooming and closing; and the cause of action is to be inferred from the action. This being so, what is refuted by the example? // 19 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.1.20]

children.text: atha nirnimittaḥ padmādiṣu prabodhasammīlanavikāra iti matam evam ātmano 'pi harṣādisampratipattir iti/ tac ca ---
children.translated_text: If it is thought that the modifications of blooming and closing in lotuses and the like are without a cause — then the experience of joy and the like by the <s>ātman</s> is also (without a cause). But that too (is refuted) —
<s>NyS</s> 3.1.20: Not so, because the modifications of entities composed of the five elements are caused by the seasons of heat, cold, and rain.

children.text: uṣṇādiṣu satsu bhāvād asatsv abhāvāt tannimittāḥ pañcabhūtānugraheṇa nivṛttānāṃ padmādīnāṃ prabodhasammīlanavikārā iti na nirnimittāḥ/ evaṃ harṣādayo 'pi vikārā nimittad bhavitum arhanti na nimittam antareṇa/
children.translated_text: Because (the modifications) occur when heat and the rest are present, and do not occur when they are absent, the modifications of blooming and closing of lotuses and the like — which are ceased (at other times) through the influence of the five elements — are caused by those (seasonal factors); they are not without a cause. Similarly, the modifications of joy and the like also ought to have a cause, not to be without a cause.

children.text:
% nimittad bhavitum arhanti ...] p.745
na cānyat pūrvābhyastasmṛtyanubandhān nimittam astīti/ na cotpattitirodhakāraṇānumānam ātmano dṛṣṭāntāt, na harṣādīnāṃ nimittam antareṇotpattiḥ, noṣṇādivan nimittāntaropādānaṃ harṣādīnām, tasmād ayuktam etat//20//
children.translated_text: And there is no other cause apart from the connection with the memory of what was previously practiced. There is no inference of a cause that obstructs the origination of the self from the example — for the origination of joy and the like does not occur without a cause, nor is another cause to be adduced for joy and the like as in the case of heat and similar (qualities). Therefore this is untenable. // 20 //
And for this further reason, the self (<s>ātman</s>) is permanent —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.1.21: Because of the desire for milk, which results from the practice of eating in a previous life (<s>pretyāhārābhyāsa</s>).

children.text: jātamātrasya vatsasya pravṛttiliṅgaḥ stanyābhilāṣo gṛhyate/ sa ca nāntareṇāhārābhyāsam/ kayā yuktyā? dṛśyate hi śarīriṇāṃ kṣudhā pīḍyamānānām āhārābhyāsakṛtāt smaraṇānubandhād āhārābhilāṣaḥ/ na ca pūrvaśarīrābhyāsam antareṇāsau jātamātrasyopapadyate/
