From the falling of a discharged arrow, a continuum of actions is apprehended, and because cognitions are restricted to their respective objects, a continuum of cognitions is established, like the continuum of actions. And when what persists is being apprehended, its direct perception ceases due to an intervening obstruction. When a persisting pot is being apprehended, cognition operates as a continuum prior to the obstruction; when it is obstructed, the direct cognition ceases.

children.text:
% santānena iva buddhir ... j,jānaṃ nivartate,] p.882
kālāntarāvasthāne tu buddher dṛśyavyavadhāne 'pi pratyakṣam avatiṣṭheteti/
smṛtiś cāliṅgaṃ buddhyavasthāne saṃskārasya buddhijasya smṛtihetutvāt/ yaś ca manyeta avatiṣṭhate buddhiḥ dṛṣṭā hi buddhiviṣaye smṛtiḥ sā ca buddhāv anityāyāṃ kāraṇābhāvān na syād iti/ tad idam aliṅgam/ kasmāt? buddhijo hi saṃskāro guṇāntaraṃ smṛtihetur na buddhir iti/
children.translated_text:
But if cognition persisted over time, direct perception would persist even when the visible object is obstructed.
And memory is not a mark of the persistence of cognition, because the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born of cognition is the cause of memory. If someone thinks: 'Cognition persists, for memory is observed regarding the object of cognition — and that (memory) would not exist if cognition were impermanent, because of the absence of a cause.' This is not a valid mark. Why? Because the latent impression born of cognition is a different quality that serves as the cause of memory — not cognition itself.

children.text:
% p.884
hetvabhāvād ayuktam iti cet? buddhyavasthānāt pratyakṣatve smṛtyabhāvaḥ/yāvad avatiṣṭhate buddhis tāvad asau boddhavyārthiḥ pratyakṣaḥ pratyskṣe ca smṛtir anupapanna iti//42//
children.translated_text: If it is said that (the argument) is untenable due to the absence of a reason: if cognition persists, then because of the direct perception (of the object), memory would be absent. As long as cognition persists, so long the object to be known is directly perceived; and memory is not established while there is direct perception (of the object). // 42 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.43]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.43: Because of its non-persisting nature, the apprehension (of the object) is indistinct — like the indistinct apprehension of form during a lightning flash.

children.text: yady utpannāpavargiṇī buddhiḥ prāptam avyaktaṃ boddhavyasya grahaṇam, yathā vidyutsampāte vaidyutasya prakāśasyānavasthānād avyaktaṃ rūpagrahaṇam iti; vyaktaṃ tu dravyāṇāṃ grahaṇaṃ tasmād ayuktam etad iti//43//
children.translated_text: If cognition perishes immediately upon arising, then the consequence is that the apprehension of the object to be known is indistinct — just as, during a lightning flash, because the light does not persist, the apprehension of visible form is indistinct. But the apprehension of substances is clearly distinct; therefore, this (view of momentary cognition) is untenable. // 43 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.44]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.44: By adducing the reason, what was to be denied is (actually) accepted.

children.text: utapannāpavargiṇī buddhir iti pratiṣeddhavyaṃ tad eva abhyanujñāyate vidyutsampāte rūpāvyaktagrahaṇavad iti/
children.translated_text: That which was to be denied — 'cognition perishes immediately upon arising' — is actually accepted by (the opponent's own) analogy 'like the indistinct apprehension of form during a lightning flash.'

children.text:
% p.885
yatrāvyaktagrahaṇaṃ tatrotpannāpavargiṇī buddhir iti/ grahaṇahetuvikalpād grahaṇavikalpo na buddhivikalpāt/ yad idaṃ kvacid avyaktaṃ kvacid vyaktaṃ grahaṇam ayaṃ vikalpo grahaṇahetuvikalpāt yatrānavasthito grahaṇahetuḥ tatrāvyaktaṃ grahaṇam yatra avasthitas tatra vyaktam, na tu buddher avasthānānavasthānābhyām iti/ kasmāt? arthagrhaṇaṃ hi buddhiḥ yat tadarthagrahaṇam avyaktaṃ vyaktaṃ vā buddhiḥ sā iti/ viśeṣāgrahaṇe ca sāmānyagrahaṇamātram avyaktagrahaṇaṃ tatra viṣayāntare buddhyanatarānutpattir nimittābhāvāt/ yatra samānadharmayuktaś ca dharmī gṛhyate viśeṣadharmayuktaś ca tad vyaktam grahaṇam, yatra tu viśeṣe 'gṛhyamāṇe sāmānyagrahaṇamātraṃ tad avyaktaṃ grahaṇam/ samānadharmayogāc ca viśiṣthadharmayogo viṣayāntaram, tatra yad grahaṇaṃ na bhavati tad grahaṇanimittābhāvād na buddher anavasthānād iti/
children.translated_text: [Note: p.885] Where there is non-manifest apprehension (<s>avyakta-grahaṇa</s>), there arises a cognition that leads to cessation. The variation in apprehension is due to variation in the cause of apprehension, not due to variation in cognition. This distinction—that apprehension is sometimes non-manifest and sometimes manifest—arises from variation in the cause of apprehension: where the cause of apprehension is unstable, the apprehension is non-manifest; where it is stable, it is manifest—but this is not due to the stability or instability of cognition itself. Why? Because cognition is the apprehension of an object; that apprehension of an object, whether non-manifest or manifest, is cognition. And when particulars are not apprehended, the mere apprehension of universals is non-manifest apprehension; there, no further cognition arises regarding a different object-domain, due to the absence of a cause. Where the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is apprehended as possessing both common properties and distinguishing properties, that is manifest apprehension; but where, the particular not being apprehended, there is mere apprehension of the universal, that is non-manifest apprehension. And since the possession of distinguishing properties over and above common properties constitutes a different object-domain, the fact that apprehension does not occur there is due to the absence of a cause of apprehension, not due to the instability of cognition.

children.text:
% p.886
yathāviṣayaṃ ca grahaṇaṃ vyaktam eva pratyarthaniyatatvāc ca buddhīnām/ sāmānyaviṣayaṃ ca grahaṇaṃ svaviṣayaṃ prati vyaktaṃ viśeṣaviṣayaṃ ca grahaṇaṃ svaviṣayaṃ prati vyaktaṃ pratyarthaniyatā hi buddhayaḥ, tad idam avyaktagrahaṇaṃ deśitaṃ kva viṣaye buddhyanavasthānakāritaṃ syyad iti?
dharmiṇas tu dharmabhede buddhinānātvasya bhāvābhāvābhyāṃ tadupapattiḥ/dharmiṇaḥ khalv arthasya samānāś ca dharmā viśiṣṭāś ca, teṣu pratyarthaniyatā nānābuddayaḥ, tā ubhayo yadi dharmiṇi vartante tadā vyakataṃ grahaṇaṃ dharmiṇam abhipretya/ yadā tu sāmānyagrahaṇamātraṃ tadāvyaktaṃ grahaṇam iti/ evaṃ dharmiṇam abhipretya vyaktāvyakatayor grahaṇayor upapattir iti//44//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.886] And apprehension according to its object is indeed manifest, since cognitions are determined by their respective objects. Apprehension whose object is the universal is manifest with respect to its own object, and apprehension whose object is the particular is manifest with respect to its own object, for cognitions are determined by their respective objects. So where has this non-manifest apprehension been taught—in what object-domain would it be caused by the instability of cognition? The explanation of this is through the presence or absence of plurality of cognitions when there is a difference in properties of the property-bearer. Indeed, the object as property-bearer has both common and distinguishing properties; with respect to these, the various cognitions are determined by their respective objects. If both types of cognition occur regarding the property-bearer, then the apprehension is manifest with respect to the property-bearer. But when there is mere apprehension of the universal, then the apprehension is non-manifest. Thus the explanation of both manifest and non-manifest apprehension is established with reference to the property-bearer. //44//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.45]

children.text:
% p.887
na cedam avyaktaṃ grahaṇaṃ budder boddhavyasya vānavasthāyitvād upapadyate iti/ idaṃ hi ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.887] And this non-manifest apprehension cannot be explained by the instability of cognition or of the object to be cognized. For this reason—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.45: The apprehension of that is not like manifest apprehension through the continuity of lamp-flames.

children.text: anavasthāyitve 'pi buddhes teṣāṃ grahaṇaṃ vyaktaṃ pratipattavyam/ katham? pradīpārciḥsantatyabhivyaktagrahaṇavat/ pradīpārciṣāṃ santatyā vartamānānāṃ grahaṇānavasthānaṃ grāhyānavasthānaṃ ca pratyarthaniyatatvād buddhīnāṃ yāvanti pradīpārcīṃṣi tāvatyo buddaya iti/ dṛśyate cātra vyaktaṃ pradīpārciṣām grahaṇam iti//45//
children.translated_text: Even though cognition is unstable, the apprehension of those [flames] must be understood as manifest. How? Like the manifest apprehension through the continuity of lamp-flames. The instability of apprehension of lamp-flames existing in continuity, and the instability of the apprehended objects—since cognitions are determined by their respective objects, there are as many cognitions as there are lamp-flames. And here, the manifest apprehension of lamp-flames is indeed observed. //45//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.46]

children.text:
% p.888
cetanā śarīraguṇaḥ sati śarīre bhāvād asati ca abhāvād iti
children.translated_text: [Note: p.888] <s>Cetanā</s> (consciousness) is a quality of the body, since it exists when the body exists and is absent when the body is absent—so it is claimed.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.46: There is doubt, because in a substance both its own qualities and the qualities of another are perceived.

children.text: sāṃśayikaḥ sati bhāvaḥ, svaguṇo 'psu dravatvam upalabhyate, paraguṇaś coṣṇatā, tenāyaṃ saṃśayaḥ kiṃ śarīraguṇaś cetanā śarīre gṛhyata atha dravyāntaraguṇa iti//46//
children.translated_text: The existence [of consciousness] when the body exists is doubtful. In water, fluidity is perceived as its own quality (<s>svaguṇa</s>), and heat as the quality of another (<s>paraguṇa</s>). Therefore this doubt arises: is <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness) a quality of the body perceived in the body, or is it a quality of another substance (<s>dravyāntara</s>)? //46//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.47]
<s>Cetanā</s> (consciousness) is not a quality of the body. Why?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.47: Because color and other qualities exist as long as the substance exists.

children.text: na rūpādihīnaṃ śarīraṃ gṛhyate cetanāhīnan tu gṛhyate yathoṣṇatāhīnā āpaḥ, tasmān na śarīraguṇaś cetaneti/
children.translated_text: The body is never perceived without color and other qualities, but it is perceived without <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness)—just as water can be without heat. Therefore, <s>cetanā</s> is not a quality of the body.

children.text:
% p.889
saṃskāravad iti ced na kāraṇānucchedāt/ yathāvidhe dravye saṃskāraḥ tathāvidha evoparamo na, tatra kāraṇocchedād atyantaṃ saṃskārānupapattir bhavati/ yathāvidhe śarīre cetanā gṛhyate tathāvidhe evātyantoparamaś cetanāyā gṛhyate/ tasmāt saṃskāravad ity asamaḥ samādhiḥ/
athāpi śarīrasthaṃ cetanotpattikāraṇaṃ syāt? dravyāntarasthaṃ vā? ubhayasthaṃ vā? tan na, niyamahetvabhāvāt/ śarīrasthena kadācic cetanotpadyate kadācin neti niyame hetur nāstīti/ dravyāntarasthena ca śarīra eva cetanotpadyate na loṣṭādiṣv ity atra na niyame hetur astīti/ ubhayasthasya nimittatve śarīrasamānajātīyadravye cetanā notpadyate śarīra eva cotpadyate iti niyame hetur nāstīti//47//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.889] If one objects that it is like a <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression)—no, because the cause is not destroyed. In whatever type of substance a <s>saṃskāra</s> exists, it ceases only in that same type, and there, due to the destruction of the cause, the <s>saṃskāra</s> becomes completely impossible. But in whatever type of body <s>cetanā</s> is perceived, its complete cessation is also perceived in that very same type. Therefore the analogy 'like <s>saṃskāra</s>' is an unequal rejoinder. Furthermore, would the cause producing <s>cetanā</s> reside in the body? Or in another substance? Or in both? It cannot be so, due to the absence of a reason for the restriction. There is no reason for the restriction that sometimes <s>cetanā</s> arises from something residing in the body and sometimes it does not. And there is no reason for the restriction that <s>cetanā</s> arises only in the body from something residing in another substance, and not in clods of earth and such. If both together were the cause, there is no reason for the restriction that <s>cetanā</s> does not arise in a substance of the same class as the body, yet arises only in the body itself. //47//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.48]

children.text:
% p.890
yac ca manyeta sati śyāmādiguṇe dravye śyāmādyuparamo dṛṣṭaḥ evaṃ cetanoparamaḥ syād iti ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.890] And if one were to think that just as the cessation of dark color and other qualities is observed in a substance possessing such qualities, so too the cessation of <s>cetanā</s> would occur—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.48: No, because a different <s>pākaja</s> (heat-produced) quality arises.

children.text: nātyantaṃ rūpoparamo dravyasya, śyāme rūpe nivṛtte pākajaṃ guṇāntaraṃ raktaṃ rūpam utpadyate, śarīre tu cetanāmātroparamo 'tyantam iti//48//
children.translated_text: The cessation of color in a substance is not absolute: when the dark color ceases, a different <s>pākaja</s> (heat-produced) quality—namely, red color—arises. But in the body, the cessation of <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness) alone is absolute. //48//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.49]
[Note: p.891] Moreover—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.49: There is no negation of <s>pākaja</s> (heat-produced) qualities, because they are established through their counterparts.

children.text: yāvatsu dravyeṣu pūrvaguṇapratidvandvisiddhis tāvatsu pākajotpattir dṛśyate pūrvaguṇaiḥ saha pākajānām avasthānasyāgrahaṇāt/ na ca śarīre cetanāpratidvandvisiddhau sahānavasthāyi guṇāntaraṃ gṛhyate yenānumīyeta tena cetanāyā virodhaḥ/ tasmād apratiṣiddhā cetanā yāvac charīraṃ varteta, na tu vartate, tasmān na śarīraguṇaś cetanā iti//49//
children.translated_text: In as many substances as the counterpart-establishment of prior qualities is found, in those the arising of <s>pākaja</s> qualities is observed, since the co-existence of <s>pākaja</s> qualities with prior qualities is not apprehended. But in the body, when there is the counterpart-establishment of the cessation of <s>cetanā</s>, no co-existing different quality is apprehended by which one could infer a conflict with <s>cetanā</s>. Therefore <s>cetanā</s> is unnegated—it should persist as long as the body persists, yet it does not persist; therefore <s>cetanā</s> is not a quality of the body. //49//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.50]

children.text:
% p.892
itaś ca na śarīraguṇaś cetanā ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.892] And for this further reason, <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness) is not a quality of the body—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.50: Because it would pervade the entire body.

children.text: śarīraṃ śarīrāvayavāś ca sarve cetanotpattyā vyāptā iti na kvacid anutpattiś cetanāyāḥ, śarīravac charīrāvayavāś cetanā iti prāptaṃ cetanabahutvam/ tatra yathā pratiśarīraṃ cetanabahutve sukhaduḥkhajñānānāṃ vyavasthā liṅgam evam ekaśarīre 'pi syāt, na tu bhavati, tasmān na śarīraguṇaś cetaneti//50//
children.translated_text: If the body and all its parts were pervaded by the arising of <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness), then there would be no place where <s>cetanā</s> does not arise; just as the body has parts, each part would have <s>cetanā</s>, and a plurality of conscious entities would follow. In that case, just as the distinction of pleasure, pain, and knowledge is the mark of a plurality of conscious beings across different bodies, so too it should apply within a single body—but it does not. Therefore <s>cetanā</s> is not a quality of the body. //50//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.51]

children.text: yad uktaṃ na kvacic charīrāvayave cetanāyā anutpattir iti sā ---
children.translated_text: What was stated—that there is no part of the body where <s>cetanā</s> does not arise—that [claim is addressed as follows]:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.51: Not so, because it is not perceived in hair, nails, and the like.

children.text: keśeṣu nakhādiṣu cānutpattiś cetanāyā iti anupapannaṃ śarīravyāpitvam iti//51//
children.translated_text: Since <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness) does not arise in hair, nails, and the like, the claim that it pervades the entire body is untenable. //51//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.52]
[Note: p.893]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.52: Since the body extends only up to the skin, the objection regarding hair, nails, and the like does not apply.

children.text: indriyāśrayatvaṃ śarīralakṣaṇam, tvakparyantaṃ jīvamanaḥsukhaduḥkhasaṃvittyāyatanabhūtaṃ śarīram, tasmān na keśādiṣu cetanotpadyate/ arthakāritas tu śarīropanibandhaḥ keśādīnām iti//52//
children.translated_text: The defining characteristic of the body is being the locus of the sense-organs. The body, extending up to the skin, is the abode of the living being (<s>jīva</s>), <s>manas</s> (mind), and the experience of pleasure and pain. Therefore <s>cetanā</s> does not arise in hair and the like. The connection of hair and similar parts to the body is merely functional. //52//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.53]
And for this further reason, <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness) is not a quality of the body—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.53: Because of the dissimilarity from bodily qualities.

children.text:
% p.894
dvividhaḥ śarīraguṇaḥ --- apratyakṣaś ca gurutvam, indriyagrāhyaś ca rūpādiḥ, vidhāntaraṃ tu cetanā, nāpratyakṣā saṃvedyatvāt, nendriyagrāhyā manoviṣayatvāt/ tasmād dravyāntaraguṇa iti//53//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.894] Bodily qualities are of two kinds: imperceptible ones like heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), and sense-perceptible ones like color (<s>rūpa</s>) and the rest. But <s>cetanā</s> is of a different kind: it is not imperceptible, since it is experienced (<s>saṃvedya</s>); nor is it sense-perceptible, since it is an object of <s>manas</s> (mind) alone. Therefore it is a quality of another substance (<s>dravyāntara</s>). //53//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.54]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.54: No, because color and other qualities are also mutually dissimilar.

children.text: yathā itaretaravidharmāṇo rūpādayo na śarīraguṇatvaṃ jahaty evaṃ rūpādivaidharmyāc cetanā śarīraguṇatvaṃ na hāsyatīti//54//
children.translated_text: Just as color and other qualities, though mutually dissimilar, do not thereby cease to be qualities of the body, so too <s>cetanā</s> would not cease to be a quality of the body merely because of its dissimilarity from color and the rest—so the objection runs. //54//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.55]
[Note: p.895]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.55: There is no negation of color and other qualities, because they are sense-perceptible.

children.text:
apratyaksatvāc ceti/ yathetaretaravidharmāṇo rūpādayo na dvaividhyam ativartante tathā rūpādivaidharmyāc cetanā na dvaividhyam ativarteta yadi śarīraguṇaḥ syād iti/ ativarttate tu, tasmān na śarīraguṇa iti/
bhūtendriyamanasāṃ jñānapratiṣedhāt siddhe saty ārambho viśeṣajñāpanārthaḥ, bahudhā parīkṣyamāṇaṃ tattvaṃ suniścitataraṃ bhavatīti//55//
children.translated_text: And because [<s>cetanā</s>] is imperceptible [to the senses]. Just as color and other qualities, though mutually dissimilar, do not go beyond the twofold classification [of imperceptible and sense-perceptible], so too <s>cetanā</s>, being dissimilar from color and the rest, would not go beyond the twofold classification if it were a quality of the body. But it does go beyond it; therefore it is not a quality of the body. Since knowledge has already been negated of the gross elements (<s>bhūta</s>), sense-organs (<s>indriya</s>), and <s>manas</s> (mind), the present undertaking is for the purpose of specifying this further, since a truth examined from many angles becomes more firmly established. //55//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.56]

children.text:
% p.896
parīkṣitā buddhiḥ, manasa idānīṃ parīkṣākramaḥ/ tat kiṃ pratiśarīram ekam anekam iti vicāre ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.896] Cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) has been examined. Now comes the order of examination of <s>manas</s> (mind). In the inquiry whether there is one <s>manas</s> per body or many—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.56: <s>Manas</s> (mind) is singular, because of the non-simultaneity of cognitions.

children.text: asti khalu vai jñānāyaugapadyam ekaikasyendriyasya yathāviṣayam, karaṇasyaikapratyayanirvṛttau sāmarthyāt, na tadekatve manaso liṅgam/ yat tu khalv idam indriyāntarāṇāṃ viṣayāntareṣu jñānāyaugapadyam iti tal liṅgam/ kasmāt? sambhavati khalu vai bahuṣu manaḥsv indriyamanaḥsaṃyogayaugapadyam iti jñānayaugapadyaṃ syāt, na tu bhavati/ tasmād viṣaye pratyayaparyāyād ekaṃ manaḥ//56//
children.translated_text: Indeed there is non-simultaneity of cognitions for each individual sense-organ with respect to its own object, due to the capacity of the instrument to produce only one cognition at a time; but this is not a mark of the singularity of <s>manas</s>. Rather, the non-simultaneity of cognitions of different sense-organs with respect to different objects—that is the mark. Why? Because if there were many <s>manas</s>, the simultaneity of the conjunction of sense-organs and <s>manas</s> would be possible, and thus simultaneity of cognitions would occur—but it does not occur. Therefore, from the succession of cognitions regarding objects, <s>manas</s> is one. //56//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.57]
[Note: p.897]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.57: No [it is not singular], because the perception of multiple simultaneous activities is observed.

children.text: ayaṃ khalv adhyāpako 'dhīte vrajati kamaṇḍaluṃ dhārayati panthānaṃ paśyati śṛṇoty āraṇyajān śabdān bibhyad vyālaliṅgāni bubhutsate smarati ca gantavyaṃ sthānīyam iti/ kramasyāgrahaṇād yugapad etāḥ kriyā iti prāptaṃ manaso bahutvam iti//57//
children.translated_text: Consider this teacher who recites, walks, holds his water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>), watches the road, hears forest sounds, fears when he sees signs of wild animals, desires to know, and remembers the destination he must reach. Since the succession [of these activities] is not apprehended, they appear to be simultaneous—and thus the plurality of <s>manas</s> would follow. //57//
[Section: NySBh_3,2.58]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.58: The perception of those [as simultaneous] is like the perception of a whirling firebrand (<s>alātacakra</s>), due to rapid movement.

children.text: āśusañcārād alātasya bhramato vidyamānaḥ kramo na gṛhyate/ kramasyāgrahaṇād avicchedabuddhyā cakravad buddhir bhavatīti/
children.translated_text: Due to the rapid movement of the whirling firebrand (<s>alāta</s>), the actually existing succession is not apprehended. Because the succession is not apprehended, there arises a cognition as of a circle, through the cognition of non-interruption.

children.text:
% -vicchedabuddhyā cakravad buddhir bhavatīti/] p.898
tathā buddhīnāṃ kriyāṇāṃ cāśuvṛttitvād vidyamānaḥ kramo na gṛhyate kramasyāgrahaṇād yugapat kriyā bhavanntīty abhimāno bhavati/
kiṃ punaḥ kramasyāgrahaṇād yugapat kriyābhimānaḥ, atha yugapadbhāvād eva yugapadanekakriyopalabdhir iti nātra viśeṣapratipatteḥ kāraṇam ucyata iti/ uktam indriyāntarāṇāṃ viṣayāntareṣu paryāyeṇa buddhayo bhavantīti tac cāpratyākhyeyam ātmapratyakṣatvāt/ athāpi dṛṣṭaśrutān arthān cintayataḥ krameṇa buddhayo vartante na yugapad anenānumātavyam iti/ varṇapadavākyabuddhīnāṃ tadarthabuddhīnāṃ cāśuvṛttitvāt kramasyāgrahaṇam/ katham? vākyastheṣu khalu varṇeṣūccaratsu prativarṇaṃ tāvac chravaṇaṃ bhavati, śrutaṃ varṇam ekam anekaṃ vā padabhāvena sa pratisandhatte, pratisandhāya padaṃ vyavasyati, padavyavasāyena smṛtyā padārthaṃ pratipadyate, padasamūhapratisandhānāc ca vākyaṃ vyavasyati, sambaddhāṃś ca padārthān gṛhītvā vākyārthaṃ pratipadyate/ na cāsāṃ krameṇa vartamānānāṃ buddhīnām āśuvṛttitvāt kramo gṛhyate, tad etad anumānam anyatra buddhikriyāyaugapadyābhimānasyeti/ na cāsti muktasaṃśayā yugapad utpattir buddhīnāṃ yayā manasāṃ bahutvam ekaśarīre 'numīyeta iti//58//
children.translated_text:
Similarly, since cognitions and actions are swift in their operation, the existing sequence is not grasped; and from the non-grasping of the sequence, the supposition arises that actions occur simultaneously.
But is the supposition of simultaneity due to the non-grasping of sequence, or is the perception of multiple simultaneous actions due to actual simultaneity? No reason is stated for determining either. It has been said that cognitions of the other sense organs regarding their respective objects occur in sequence — and that cannot be denied, since it is a matter of self-perception (<s>ātmapratyakṣa</s>). And furthermore, since cognitions of seen and heard objects, for one who reflects (on them), occur in sequence and not simultaneously — this is to be inferred. The non-grasping of sequence in the cognitions of phonemes, words, sentences, and their meanings is due to the swiftness of those cognitions. How? When phonemes in a sentence are being uttered, hearing occurs for each phoneme. One connects the heard phoneme — one or many — into a word; having connected them, one determines the word; through the word-determination, one understands the word-meaning by memory; from connecting the collection of words, one determines the sentence; and having grasped the connected word-meanings, one understands the sentence-meaning. But the sequence of these cognitions, which occur in succession, is not grasped due to their swiftness — this is the inference that the supposition of simultaneous cognition and action (is mistaken). And there is no doubt-free simultaneous origination of cognitions by which the plurality of <s>manas</s> (minds) in one body could be inferred. // 58 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.59]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.59: And (mind is) atomic, because of the reason already stated.

children.text: aṇu mana ekaṃ ceti dharmasamuccayo jñānāyaugapadyāt/ mahattve manasaḥ sarvendriyasaṃyogād yugapad viṣayagrahaṇaṃ syād iti//59//
children.translated_text: That <s>manas</s> (mind) is atomic, one, and (so on) — this collection of properties (follows) from the non-simultaneity of cognitions. For if <s>manas</s> were large, due to its conjunction with all sense organs simultaneously, there would be simultaneous apprehension of sense-objects. // 59 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.60]

children.text:
manasaḥ khalu bhoḥ sendriyasya śarīre vṛttilābho nānyatra śarīrāt/ jñātuś ca puruṣasya śarīrāyatanā buddhyādayo viṣayopabhogo jihāsitahānam īpsitāvāptiś ca sarve ca śarīrāśrayā vyavahārāḥ/ tatra khalu vipratipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ --- kim ayaṃ puruṣakarmanimittaḥ śarīrasarga āhosvid bhūtamātrād akarmanimitta iti/ śrūyate khalv atra vipratipattir iti/
tatredaṃ tattvam ---
children.translated_text:
Now indeed, <s>manas</s> (mind), together with the sense organs, obtains its operation in the body and not elsewhere. And for the knowing person (<s>puruṣa</s>), cognition and the like, enjoyment of objects, abandonment of what is to be abandoned, attainment of what is desired, and all activities dependent on the body — all have the body as their locus. Regarding this, from the conflict of views, there is doubt: is this creation of the body caused by the person's <s>karma</s> (actions), or does it arise from the elements alone without <s>karma</s> as a cause? The conflict of views on this is indeed heard.
Here, the truth is —
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.60: The origination of that (body) is due to the connection with the fruits of previously performed (actions).

children.text: pūrvaśarīre yā pravṛttir vāgbuddhiśarīrārambhalakṣaṇā tat pūrvakṛtaṃ karmoktam, tasya phalaṃ tajjanitau dharmādharmau/
children.translated_text: The activity in the previous body — characterized by the initiation of speech, mind, and body — that is called previously performed <s>karma</s> (action). Its fruit is <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) generated by it.

children.text:
% tajjanitau dharmādharmau/] p.900
tatphalasyānubandha ātmasamavetasyāvasthānam, tena prayuktebhyo bhūebyas tasyotpattiḥ śarīrasya, na svatantrebhya iti/ yad adhiṣṭhāno 'yam ātmā 'yam aham iti manyamāno yatrābhiyukto yatropabhogatṛṣṇayā viṣayānupalabhamāno dharmādharmau saṃskaroti tad asya śarīram, tena saṃskāreṇa dharmādharmalakṣaṇena bhūtasahite patite 'smin śarīra uttaraṃ niṣpadyate, niṣpannasya cāsya pūrvaśarīravat puruṣārthakriyā, puruṣasya ca pūrvaśarīravat pravṛttir iti karmāpekṣebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ śarīrasarge saty etad upapadyata iti/
children.translated_text: The continuation (<s>anubandha</s>) of that fruit — its persistence as inherent in the <s>ātman</s> (self) — impelled by that, the body originates from the elements, not from independent (elements). That in which this <s>ātman</s> is located, thinking 'this is my self,' where it is engaged, where, not perceiving objects due to the craving for enjoyment, it accumulates <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — that is its body. By that accumulation — characterized by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — when this body falls, combined with the elements, the next (body) is produced. And for the produced (body), there is purposeful activity for the person, just as for the previous body; and the person's activity (continues) just as in the previous body — this is how (the cycle) is established when the body is created from elements that are dependent on <s>karma</s>.

children.text:
% pravṛttir iti karmāpekṣebhyo ... upapadyata iti/] p.901
dṛṣṭā ca puruṣaguṇena prayatnena prayuktebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ puruṣārthkriyāsamarthānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ rathaprabhṛtīnām utpattiḥ/ tathānumātavyaṃ śarīram api puruṣārthakriyāsamartham utpadyamānaṃ puruṣasya guṇāntarāpekṣebhyo bhūtebhya utpadyata iti//60//
children.translated_text: And it is observed that from elements impelled by human effort — a quality of the person — substances capable of serving human purposes, such as chariots and the like, are produced. Similarly, it should be inferred that the body too, being capable of serving human purposes, when being produced, is produced from elements that are dependent on another quality of the person. // 60 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.61]
Here the materialist (<s>nāstika</s>) says —
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.61: Just as material forms (produced) from the elements are adopted (for human use), so too the body is adopted (from the elements without karma).

children.text: yathā karmanirapekṣebhyo bhūtebhyo nirvṛttā mūrtayaḥ sikatāśarkarāpāṣāṇagairikāñjanaprabhṛtayaḥ puruṣārthakāritvād upādīyante tathā karmanirapekṣebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ śarīram utpannaṃ puruṣārthakāritvād upādīyate iti//61//
children.translated_text: Just as material forms — pebbles, gravel, stones, red ochre, collyrium, and the like — produced from elements independently of <s>karma</s>, are adopted because they serve human purposes, so too the body, produced from elements independently of <s>karma</s>, is adopted because it serves human purposes. // 61 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.62]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.62: No, because of the equality with what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>).

children.text: yathā śarīrotpattir akarmanimittā sādhyā tathā sikatāśarkarāpāṣāṇagairikāñjanaprabhṛtīnām apy akarmanimittaḥ sargaḥ sādhyaḥ sādhyasamatvād asādhanam iti ``bhūtebhyo mūrtyupādānavad'' iti cānena sādhyam//62//
children.translated_text: Just as the origination of the body without <s>karma</s> as a cause is what is to be proved, so too the creation of pebbles, gravel, stones, red ochre, collyrium, and the like without <s>karma</s> as a cause is also what is to be proved. Since it is equal to what is to be proved, it is not a means of proof — and (the claim) 'just as material forms from the elements' is itself what needs to be proved. // 62 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.63]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.63: Not so, because the mother and father are the instrumental cause of origination.

children.text: viṣamaś cāyam upanyāsaḥ/ kasmāt? nirbījā imā mūrtaya utpadyante bījapūrvikā tu śarīrotpattiḥ/ mātāpitṛśabdena lohitaretasī bījabhūte gṛhyete/ tatra sattvasya garbhavāsānubhavanīyaṃ karma pitroś ca putraphalānubhavanīye karmaṇī mātur garbhāśraye śarīrotpattiṃ bhūtebhyaḥ prayojayantīty upapannaṃ bījānuvidhānam iti//63//
children.translated_text: And this comparison is unequal. Why? Because these material forms are produced without a seed, whereas the origination of the body is preceded by a seed. By the words 'mother' and 'father,' the menstrual blood and semen — which serve as the seed — are meant. There, the <s>karma</s> of the being that is to be experienced during the womb-residence, and the <s>karmas</s> of the parents that yield the fruit of having a child, impel the origination of the body from the elements in the mother's womb — thus the conformity to the seed is warranted. // 63 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.64]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.64: Likewise of food.

children.text: utpattinimittatvād iti prakṛtam/ bhuktaṃ pītam āhāraḥ tasya paktinirvṛttaṃ rasadravyaṃ mātṛśarīre copacīyate bīje garbhāśayasthe bījasamānapākam, mātrayā copacayo bīje yāvad vyūhasamarthaḥ sañcaya iti/ sañcitaṃ ca kalalārbudamāṃsapeśīkaṇḍarāśiraḥpāṇyādinā ca vyūhenendriyādhiṣṭhānabhedena vyuhyate, vyūhe ca garbhanāḍyāvatāritaṃ rasadravyam upacīyate yāvat prasavasamartham iti/ na cāyam annapānasya sthālyādigatasya kalpata iti/ etasmāt kāraṇāt karmanimittatvaṃ śarīrasya vijñāyata iti//64//
children.translated_text: 'Because of being the instrumental cause of origination' — this is the ongoing topic. Food that is eaten and drunk — the nutrient substance produced through its digestion — accumulates in the mother's body and in the seed residing in the womb, undergoing digestion similar to the seed, and through the mother the accumulation in the seed (continues) until the collection is capable of forming the bodily structure. And the accumulated (material) is organized through the structure of <s>kalala</s> (embryonic jelly), <s>arbuda</s> (embryonic lump), flesh-mass, tendons, and the differentiation of sense-organ locations into head, hands, and the like; and as the structure (develops), the nutrient substance conveyed through the umbilical cord accumulates until (the fetus) is capable of being born. And this (process) of food and drink placed in a pot and the like cannot (produce such a result). From this reason, it is understood that the body is caused by <s>karma</s>. // 64 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.65]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.65: And because there is no fixed rule regarding the attainment (of conception).

children.text: na sarvo dampatyoḥ saṃyogo garbhādhānahetur dṛśyate tatrāsati karmaṇi na bhavati sati ca bhavatīty anupapanno niyamābhāva iti/ karmanirapekṣeṣu bhūteṣu śarīrotpattihetuṣu niyamaḥ syāt na hy atra kāraṇābhāva iti//65//
children.translated_text: Not every union of husband and wife is observed to be the cause of conception of the embryo. There, when <s>karma</s> is absent, (conception) does not occur; and when it is present, it does occur — this lack of fixed rule is unwarranted (on the materialist view). If the elements, independently of <s>karma</s>, were the causes of the body's origination, there would be a fixed rule — for there is no absence of (elemental) cause (in any union). // 65 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.66]
And furthermore —
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.66: <s>Karma</s> is the cause of the origination of the conjunction (of self and body), just as it is the cause of the origination of the body.

children.text: yathā khalv idaṃ śarīraṃ dhātuprāṇasaṃvāhinīnāṃ nāḍīnāṃ śukrāntānāṃ dhātūnāṃ ca snāyutvagasthiśirāpeśīkalalakaṇḍarāṇāṃ ca śirobāhūdarāṇāṃ sakthnāṃ ca koṣṭhagānāṃ vātapittakaphānāṃ ca mukhahṛdayāmāśayapakvāśayādhaḥsrotasāṃ ca paramaduḥkhasampādanīyena sanniveśena vyūhanam aśakyaṃ pṛthivyādibhiḥ karmanirapekṣair utpādayitum iti karmanimittā śarīrotpattir iti vijñāyate; evaṃ ca pratyātmaniyatasya nimittasyābhāvān niratiśayair ātmabhiḥ sambandhāt sarvātmanāṃ ca samānaiḥ pṛthivyādibhir utpāditaṃ śarīraṃ pṛthivyādigatasya ca niyamahetor abhāvāt sarvātmanāṃ sukhaduḥkhasaṃvittyāyatanaṃ samānaṃ prāptam/ yat tu pratyātmaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate tatra śarīrotpattinimittaṃ karma vyavashtāhetur iti vijñāyate/ paripacyamāno hi pratyātmaniyataḥ karmāśayo yasminn ātmani vartate tasyaivopabhogāyatanaṃ śarīram utpādya vyavasthāpayati/ tad evaṃ ``śarīrotpattinimittavat saṃyoganimittaṃ karma'' iti vijñāyate/ pratyātmavyavasthānaṃ tu śarīrasyātmanā saṃyogaṃ pracakṣmaha iti//66//
children.translated_text: For indeed, this body — with its arrangement of channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>) that carry bodily fluids and vital breaths, of bodily constituents (<s>dhātus</s>) ending in semen, and of tendons, skin, bones, veins, flesh-masses, embryonic jellies, and sinews, and of the head, arms, abdomen, and thighs, and of the internal organs of wind, bile, and phlegm, and of the mouth, heart, stomach, intestines, and lower passages — with an arrangement that is supremely difficult to produce for the purpose of pain, cannot be produced by earth and the like independently of <s>karma</s>. Thus it is known that the origination of the body is caused by <s>karma</s>. And moreover, since in the absence of a cause that is restricted to each individual self, all selves being without surplus (of merit), and from the conjunction with unsurpassed selves, and since the elements — earth and the like — are the same for all selves, and since there is no restricting cause inherent in earth and the like, it would follow that the body produced from earth and the like would be the same locus of pleasure, pain, and consciousness for all selves. But what is individually established for each self — there, <s>karma</s> as the cause of the body's origination is known to be the cause of the individual arrangement. For the <s>karmāśaya</s> (repository of <s>karma</s>) that is restricted to each individual self, as it ripens, produces and establishes the body as the locus of experience for that very self in whom it exists. Thus it is known that '<s>karma</s> is the cause of the origination of the conjunction (of self and body), just as it is the cause of the origination of the body.' And we declare that the individual establishment of the body for a particular self is its conjunction with that self. // 66 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.67]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.67: By this, the (objection about the) absence of a fixed rule has been answered.

children.text: yo .yam akarmanimitte śarīrasarge saty aniyama ity ucyate, ayaṃ ``śarīrotpattinimittavat saṃyogotpattinimittaṃ karma'' iti anena pratyuktaḥ/
children.translated_text: The claim that there is no fixed rule when the body's creation is without <s>karma</s> as a cause — this has been answered by (the statement) '<s>karma</s> is the cause of the origination of the conjunction, just as it is the cause of the origination of the body.'

children.text:
% -nimittavat saṃyogotpattinimittaṃ ... pratyuktaḥ/] p.908
kas tāvad ayaṃ niyamaḥ? yathaikasyātmanaḥ śarīraṃ tathā sarveṣām iti niyamaḥ/ anyasyānyathānyasyānyathety aniyamo bhedo vyāvṛttir viśeṣa iti/
children.translated_text: What then is this fixed rule? That just as one self has a body, so do all — that is the (expected) rule. That one has one kind (of body) and another has another kind — that irregularity, that difference, that distinction, is the absence of a fixed rule.

children.text:
% -ty aniyamo bhedo vyāvṛttir viśeṣa iti/] p.909
dṛṣṭā ca janmavyāvṛttir uccābhijano nikṛṣṭābhijana iti, praśastaṃ nindatam iti, vyādhibahulam arogam iti, samagraṃ vikalam iti, pīḍābahulaṃ sukhabahulam iti, puruṣātiśayalakṣaṇopapannaṃ viparītam iti, praśastalakṣaṇaṃ ninditalakṣaṇam iti, paṭvindriyaṃ mṛḍvindriyam iti/ sūkṣmaś ca bhedo 'parimeyaḥ/ so 'yam janmabhedaḥ pratyātmaniyatāt karmabhedād upapadyate, asati karmabhede pratyātmaniyate niratiśayatvād ātmanāṃ samānatvāc ca pṛthivyādīnāṃ pṛthivyādigatasya niyamahetor ahbāvāt sarvaṃ sarvātmanāṃ prasajyeta, na tv idam itthambhūtaṃ janma/ tasmān nākarmanittā śarīrotpattir iti/
upapannaś ca tadviyogaḥ karmakṣayopapatteḥ/ karmanimitte śarīrasarge tena śarīreṇātmano viyoga upapannaḥ/ kasmāt? karmakṣayopapatteḥ/ upapadyate khalu karmakṣayaḥ samyagdarśanāt prakṣīṇe mohe vītarāgaḥ punarbhavahetukarma kāyavāṅmanobhir na karotīty uttarasyānupacayaḥ pūrvopacitasya vipākapratisaṃvedanāt prakṣayaḥ/ evaṃ prasavahetor abhāvāt patire 'smin śarīre punaḥ śarīrāntarānupapatter apratisandhiḥ/ akarmanimitte tu śarīrasarge bhūtakṣayānupapattes tadviyogānupapattir iti//67//
children.translated_text:
And the distinction in birth is observed: one of noble birth and one of low birth; praiseworthy and blameworthy; disease-ridden and healthy; complete and deficient; affliction-predominant and pleasure-predominant; endowed with marks of human excellence and the opposite; with auspicious marks and with inauspicious marks; with sharp senses and with dull senses. And the subtle differences are immeasurable. This distinction in birth is warranted by the difference in <s>karma</s> that is restricted to each individual self. In the absence of <s>karma</s>-difference restricted to each individual, since all selves are without surplus, since the elements — earth and the like — are the same for all, and since there is no restricting cause inherent in earth and the like — everything would be the same for all selves, and this particular kind of birth would not occur. Therefore, the origination of the body is not without <s>karma</s> as its cause.
And the separation from that (body) is warranted because the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> is possible. When the creation of the body is caused by <s>karma</s>, the separation of the self from that body is warranted. Why? Because the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> is possible. The exhaustion of <s>karma</s> is indeed possible: through correct knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), when delusion (<s>moha</s>) is destroyed, one becomes free from attachment (<s>vītarāga</s>); (being) free from attachment, one does not perform <s>karma</s> that is the cause of further existence through body, speech, and mind — hence no further accumulation. (And) through experiencing the ripening of what was previously accumulated, there is (its) exhaustion. Thus, in the absence of the cause of (further) birth, when this body falls, there is no re-connection with another body — (this is) non-rebirth (<s>apratisandhi</s>). But if the creation of the body were without <s>karma</s> as its cause, since the destruction of elements is impossible, the separation from that (body) would be impossible. // 67 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 3.2.68]
[Page break]

children.text: NyS_3,2.68: tad adṛṣṭakāritam iti cet punas tatprasaṅgo 'pavarge ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 3.2.68: If (it is said that) that (elemental creation) is caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), then the consequence would be the same (karma-dependence) in the case of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).

children.text: adarśanaṃ khalv adṛṣṭam ity ucyata adṛṣṭakāritā bhūtebhyaḥ śarīrotpattiḥ/ na jātv anutpanne śarīre draṣṭā nirāyatano dṛśyaṃ paśyati/ tac cāsya dṛśyaṃ dvividhaṃ viṣayaś ca nānātvaṃ cāvyaktātmanaḥ, tadarthaḥ śarīrasargaḥ/ tasminn avasite caritārthāni bhūtāni na śarīram utpādayantīty upapannaḥ śarīraviyoga ity evaṃ cen manyase, ``punas tat prasaṅgo 'pavarge'' --- punaḥ śarīrotpattiḥ prasajyata iti/ yā cānutpanne śarīre darśanānutpattir adarśanābhimatā yā cāpavarge śarīranivṛttau darśanānutpattir adarśanabhūtā naitayor adarśanayoḥ kvacid viśeṣa ity adarśanasyānivṛtter apavarge punaḥ śarīrotpattiprasaṅga iti/
children.translated_text: Non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>) is indeed called <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (the unseen); the origination of the body from the elements is brought about by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. Never does the seer, having no support (body), see the visible when no body has arisen. And the visible for this (seer) is twofold: objects and the differentiation of the unmanifest self. The creation of the body is for that purpose. When that (purpose) is accomplished, the elements — having fulfilled their function — do not produce a body, and thus the separation from the body is possible. If you think this (is the case), 'there arises again the same contingency in liberation' — that is, the origination of a body would follow again. For the non-origination of seeing when no body has arisen — which is considered 'non-seeing' — and the non-origination of seeing at the time of the cessation of the body in liberation — which constitutes 'non-seeing' — there is no distinction anywhere between these two (types of) non-seeing. Therefore, since non-seeing is not eliminated, in liberation there arises the contingency of body-origination again.

children.text:
% p.910
caritārthatā viśeṣa iti cet na karaṇākaraṇayor ārambhadarśanāt/ caritārthāni bhūtāni darśanāvasānān na śarīrāntaram ārabhanta ity ayaṃ viśeṣa evaṃ ced ucyate; na, karaṇākaraṇayor ārambhadarśanāt --- caritārthānāṃ bhūtānāṃ viṣayopalabdhikaraṇāt punaḥ punaḥ śarīrārambho dṛśyate prakṛtipuruṣayor nānātvadarśanasyākaraṇān nirarthakaḥ śarīrārambhaḥ punaḥ punar dṛśyate/ tasmād akarmanimittāyāṃ bhūtasṛṣṭau na darśanārthā śarīrotpattir yuktā, yuktā tu karmanimitte sarge darśanārthā śarīrotpattiḥ/ karmavipākasaṃvedanaṃ darśanam iti/
children.translated_text: If (you say) the distinction lies in the fulfillment of purpose — not so, because origination is observed both from purposeful and purposeless (activity). If you say 'the elements, having fulfilled their purpose through the completion of seeing, do not commence another body' — this is the distinction — no, because origination is observed from both purposeful and purposeless (activity): (on one hand,) the origination of a body is observed again and again from elements that have fulfilled their purpose of enabling the perception of objects; (on the other hand,) a purposeless origination of a body is observed again and again even when the seeing of the differentiation between <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) and <s>puruṣa</s> (self) has not taken place. Therefore, in a creation by elements that is independent of <s>karma</s> (action), the origination of a body for the purpose of seeing is not justified; but in a creation caused by <s>karma</s>, the origination of a body for the purpose of seeing is justified. 'Seeing' means the experience of the ripening of <s>karma</s>.

children.text:
% p.911
tad adṛṣṭakāritam iti cet? kasyacid darśanam adṛṣṭaṃ nāma paramāṇūnāṃ guṇaviśeṣaḥ kriyāhetus tena preritāḥ paramāṇavaḥ sammūrcchitāḥ śarīram utpādayantīti tan manaḥ samāviśati svaguṇenādṛṣṭena preritaṃ samanaske śarīre draṣṭur upalabdhir bhavatīti/
etasmin vai darśane guṇānucchedāt punas tatprasaṅgo 'pavarge/ apavarge śarīrotpattiḥ paramāṇuguṇasyādṛṣṭasyānucchedyatvād iti//68//
children.translated_text:
If (you say) that (seeing/origination) is brought about by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>? According to certain (Vaiśeṣikas), the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> called 'seeing' is a special quality of the atoms that is the cause of activity; impelled by that, the atoms combine and produce a body. Then <s>manas</s> (mind), impelled by its own quality of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, enters (the body); and in a body endowed with mind, the perception of the seer occurs.
But in this view, since the quality (of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> in the atoms) is not destroyed, the same contingency arises again in liberation. In liberation, the origination of a body (would follow) because the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> — a quality of the atoms — is indestructible. // 68 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.69: And because of the causal role of the mind's <s>karma</s>, there would be no interruption of the conjunction (of mind and body).

children.text: manoguṇenādṛṣṭena samāveśite manasi saṃyogavyucchedo na syāt, tac ca kiṃkṛtaṃ śarīrād apasarpaṇaṃ manasa iti? karmāśayakṣaye tu karmāśayāntarād vipacyamānād apasarpaṇopapattir iti/ adṛṣṭād evāpasarpaṇam iti cet --- yo 'dṛṣṭaḥ śarīropasarpaṇahetuḥ sa evāpasarpaṇahetur apīti? na, ekasya jīvanaprāyaṇahetutvānupapatteḥ --- evaṃ ca saty ekam adṛṣṭaṃ jīvanaprāyaṇayor hetur iti prāptam, naitad upapadyate//69//
children.translated_text: If the mind enters (the body) impelled by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> that is a quality of the mind, there would be no interruption of the conjunction (of mind and body). Then what causes the departure of the mind from the body? Upon the exhaustion of one <s>karmāśaya</s> (accumulated karmic deposit), the departure is possible due to another <s>karmāśaya</s> that is ripening. If (you say that) the departure is from <s>adṛṣṭa</s> itself — (then you claim that) the same <s>adṛṣṭa</s> that is the cause of entering the body is also the cause of departing? No, because it is untenable that a single thing is the cause of both living and dying — for then it would follow that a single <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is the cause of both living and dying, and this is untenable. // 69 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.70: And the consequence would be permanence (of the body), because death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) would be impossible.

children.text: vipākasaṃvedanāt karmāśayakṣaye śarīrapātaḥ prāyaṇam, karmāśayāntarāc ca punarjanma/ bhūtamātrāt tu karmanirapekṣāc charīrotpattau kasya kṣayāc charīrapātaḥ prāyaṇam iti? prāyaṇānupapatteḥ khalu vai nityatvaprasaṅgaṃ vidmaḥ/ yādṛcchike tu prāyaṇe prāyaṇabhedānupapattir iti//70//
children.translated_text: Death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) is the fall of the body upon the exhaustion of the <s>karmāśaya</s> (karmic deposit) through the experience of its ripening, and rebirth is from another <s>karmāśaya</s>. But if the origination of the body is merely from the elements, independent of <s>karma</s> — from the exhaustion of what would the fall of the body, i.e., death, occur? We recognize that from the impossibility of death, the consequence of permanence (of the body) follows. And if death is random, the impossibility of different kinds of death (would follow). // 70 //

children.text:
% p.916
punas tatprasaṅgo 'pavarga ity etat samādhitsur āha ---
children.translated_text: Wishing to resolve the (objection) 'there arises again the same contingency in liberation,' (the opponent) says —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.71: This would be like the permanence of the blackness of an atom.

children.text: yathāṇoḥ śyāmatā nityā agnisaṃyogena pratiṣiddhā na punar utpadyata evam adṛṣṭakāritaṃ śarīram apavarge punar notpadyata iti// 71 //
children.translated_text: Just as the permanent blackness of an atom, having been counteracted by conjunction with fire, does not arise again — so too the body produced by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> does not arise again in liberation. // 71 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.72: Not so, because of the consequence of <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s> (the approach of what has not been done).

children.text:
nāyam asti dṛṣṭāntaḥ/ kasmāt? akṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgāt/ akṛtaṃ pramāṇato 'nupapannam, tasyābhyāgamo 'bhyupapattir vyavasāyaḥ, etacchraddadhānena pramāṇato ṇupapannaṃ mantavyam/ tasmān nāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto na pratyakṣaṃ na cānumānaṃ kiṃcid ucyata iti/ tad idaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya sādhyasamatvam abhidhīyata iti/
atha vā nākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgāt/ aṇuśyāmatādṛṣṭāntenākarmanimittāṃ śarīrotpattiṃ samādadhānasyākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgaḥ/ akṛte sukhaduḥkhahetau karmaṇi puruṣasya sukhaṃ duḥkham abhyāgacchatīti prasajyeta/ om iti bruvataḥ pratyakṣānumānāgamavirodhaḥ/
children.translated_text:
This example is not valid. Why? Because of the consequence of <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s> (accepting what is not established by valid means of knowledge). <s>Akṛta</s> means what is not established by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge); its <s>abhyāgama</s> (approach) means acceptance, commitment. By one who accepts this, what is not established by valid means of knowledge must be believed. Therefore this is not a valid example — neither perception nor any inference is adduced. Hence this is declared to be the defect of the example being equal to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasamatva</s>).
Alternatively: not so, because of the consequence of <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>. For one who, using the analogy of atomic blackness, resolves the problem of the body's origination being independent of <s>karma</s> — the consequence of <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s> arises: when the causal <s>karma</s> for pleasure and pain has not been performed, pleasure and pain would approach (befall) the person. One who says 'yes (to this)' contradicts perception, inference, and scripture.

children.text:
% p.917
pratyakṣavirodhas tāvat --- bhinnam idaṃ sukhaduḥkhaṃ pratyātmavedanīyatvāt pratyakṣaṃ sarvaśarīriṇām/ ko bhedaḥ? tīvraṃ mandaṃ ciram āśu nānāprakāram ekaprakāram ity evam ādir viśeṣaḥ/ na cāsti pratyātmaniyataḥ sukhaduḥkhahetuviśeṣaḥ, na cāsati hetuviśeṣe phalaviśeṣo dṛśyate/ karmanimitte tu sukhaduḥkhayoge karmaṇāṃ tīvramandatopapatteḥ karmasañcayānāṃ cotkarṣāpakarṣabhāvāt nānāvidhaikavidhabhāvāc ca karmaṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhabhedopapattiḥ/ so 'yaṃ hetubhedābhāvād dṛṣṭaḥ sukhaduḥkhabhedo na syād iti pratyakṣavirodhaḥ/
tathānumānavirodhaḥ --- dṛṣṭaṃ hi puruṣaguṇavyavasthānāt sukhaduḥkhavyavasthānam/ yaḥ khalu cetanāvān sādhananirvartanīyaṃ sukhaṃ buddhvā tad īpsan sādhanāvāptaye prayatate sa sukhena yujyate na viparītaḥ/ yaś ca sādhananirvartanīyaṃ duḥkhaṃ buddhvā taj jihāsuḥ sādhanaparivarjanāya yatate sa ca duḥkhena tyajyate na viparītaḥ/ asti cedaṃ yatnam antareṇa cetanānāṃ sukhaduḥkhavyavasthānaṃ tenāpi cetanaguṇāntaravyavasthākṛtena bhavitavyam ity anumānam/
children.translated_text:
The contradiction with perception, first: the pleasure and pain of all embodied beings is different, being individually experienced — this is directly perceived. What is the difference? Intense, mild, prolonged, brief, manifold, uniform — such are the distinctions. And there is no specific cause of pleasure and pain that is fixed for each individual self; and without a specific cause, no specific result is observed. But when pleasure and pain are connected through <s>karma</s>, from the possibility of <s>karmas</s> being intense and mild, from the rise and decline of accumulated <s>karmas</s>, and from <s>karmas</s> being manifold and uniform — the differentiation of pleasure and pain is possible. Therefore, in the absence of a differentiated cause, the observed differentiation of pleasure and pain would not exist — this is the contradiction with perception.
Likewise, the contradiction with inference: it is observed that the arrangement of pleasure and pain is due to the arrangement of the qualities of the person. One who is conscious, having understood that pleasure is to be accomplished by means, desiring it, strives for the attainment of those means — that one is conjoined with pleasure, not the opposite. And one who, having understood that pain is to be accomplished by means, desiring to avoid it, strives for the avoidance of those means — that one is freed from pain, not the opposite. And there is this arrangement of pleasure and pain for conscious beings without (apparent) effort — from that too it must be inferred that it is due to the arrangement of some other quality of the conscious being.

children.text:
% -mānam/] p.918
tad etad akarmanimitte sukhaduḥkhayoge virudhyata iti/ tac ca guṇāntaram asaṃvedyatvād adṛṣṭaṃ vipākakālāniyamāc cāvyavasthitam/ buddhyādayas tu saṃvedyāś cāpavargiṇaś ceti/
athāgamavirodhaḥ --- bahu khalv idam ārṣam ṛṣīṇām upadeśajātam anuṣṭhānaparivarjanāśrayam, upadeśaphalaṃ ca śarīriṇāṃ varṇāśramavibhāgeṇānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇā pravṛttiḥ, parivarjanalakṣaṇā nivṛttiḥ/ tac cobhayam etasyāṃ dṛṣṭau ``nāsti karma sucaritaṃ duścaritaṃ vā? karmanimittaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhayogaḥ'' iti virudhyate/ seyaṃ pāpiṣṭhānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ --- akarmanimittā śarīrasṛṣṭir akarmanimittaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoga iti//72//
children.translated_text:
This (observation) contradicts the view that the conjunction of pleasure and pain is independent of <s>karma</s>. And that other quality, being imperceptible, is <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen <s>karma</s>); and being of indeterminate time of ripening, it is unfixed. But <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest are perceivable and terminate at <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).
Now, the contradiction with scripture (<s>āgama</s>): vast indeed is this body of teachings of the sages (<s>ṛṣis</s>), founded upon the practice and avoidance (of actions). And the fruit of (this) teaching for embodied beings is: activity characterized by practice, according to the division of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>, and cessation characterized by avoidance. Both of these are contradicted by this view: 'does not good or bad <s>karma</s> exist? Is not the conjunction of pleasure and pain for persons caused by <s>karma</s>?' This is the wicked false view of the sinful: that the creation of the body is not caused by <s>karma</s>, and the conjunction of pleasure and pain is not caused by <s>karma</s>. // 72 //

children.text: iti śrīvātsyāyanīye nyāyabhāṣye tṛtīyādhyāyasya dvitīyam āhnikam// 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>āhnika</s> (lesson) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the revered <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> by <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. // 2 //
And thus the third chapter is complete. // 3 //
The <s>Nyāyadarśana</s>. Now begins the first <s>āhnika</s> (lesson) of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter).

children.text: manaso 'nantaraṃ pravṛttiḥ parīkṣitavyā/ tatra khalu yāvad dharmādharmāśrayaśarīrādi parīkṣitam, sarvā sā pravṛtteḥ parīkṣety āha ---
children.translated_text: After mind (<s>manas</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is to be examined. Since all that has been examined — the body and the rest as the substrate of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — all that is the examination of <s>pravṛtti</s>, he says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.1: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is as previously described.
It has been thus examined. // 1 //

children.text:
% p.923
pravṛttyanantarās tarhi doṣāḥ parīkṣyantām ity ata āha ---
children.translated_text: Then let the faults (<s>doṣa</s>), which follow immediately after activity, be examined. On this, he says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.2: Likewise the faults (<s>doṣa</s>).

children.text: parīkṣitā iti/ buddhisamānāśrayatvād ātmaguṇāḥ, pravṛttihetutvāt punarbhavapratisandhānasāmarthyāc ca saṃsārahetavaḥ, saṃsārasyānāditvād anādinā prabandhena pravartante, mithyājñānanivṛttis tattvajñānāt tannivṛttau rāgadveṣaprabandhocchyede 'pavarga iti/ prādurbhāvatirodhānadharmakā ityevamādyuktam doṣāṇām iti//2//
children.translated_text: They have been examined. Being qualities of the self (<s>ātman</s>) — having the same substrate as <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — and being the causes of activity, and having the power to reconnect to further existence (<s>punarbhava</s>), they are the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of transmigration). Since <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless, they operate in a beginningless succession. False knowledge ceases through the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>); upon its cessation, when the succession of attachment and aversion is cut off, there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). (The faults) have the property of manifestation and concealment — and so forth has been stated regarding the faults. // 2 //

children.text:
% p.924
pravartanālakṣaṇā doṣā ity uktam, tathā ceme mānerṣyāsūyāvicikitsāmatsarādayaḥ, te kasmān nopasaṅkhyāyante ity ata āha ---
children.translated_text: It was stated that the faults are characterized by causing activity. Now, pride (<s>māna</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), malice (<s>asūyā</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), jealousy (<s>matsara</s>), and the like are also such. Why are they not separately enumerated? On this, he says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.3: They form three groups (<s>trairāśya</s>), because <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) are each a distinct category.

children.text: teṣāṃ doṣāṇāṃ trayo rāśayas trayaḥ pakṣāḥ/ rāgapakṣaḥ --- kāmo matsaraḥ spṛhā tṛṣṇā lobha iti/ dveṣapakṣaḥ --- krodha īrṣyā asūyā droho 'marṣa iti/ mohapakṣo
children.translated_text: These faults have three groups, three classes. The <s>rāga</s> (attachment) class: desire (<s>kāma</s>), jealousy (<s>matsara</s>), craving (<s>spṛhā</s>), thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), and greed (<s>lobha</s>). The <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) class: anger (<s>krodha</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), malice (<s>asūyā</s>), ill-will (<s>droha</s>), and resentment (<s>amarṣa</s>). The <s>moha</s> (delusion) class:

children.text:
% p.925
mithyājñānaṃ vicikitsā mānaḥ pramāda iti/ trairāśyān nopasaṅkhyāyante iti/ lakṣaṇasya tarhy abhedāt tritvam anupapannam? nānupapannam, rāgadveṣamohārthāntarabhāvāt;
children.translated_text: false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and carelessness (<s>pramāda</s>). Because of the three groups, they are not separately enumerated. But if the definition is undifferentiated, how is the threefold division justified? It is not unjustified, because <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s> are each a distinct category (<s>arthāntarabhāva</s>).

children.text:
% p.926
āsaktilakṣaṇo rāgaḥ, amarṣalakṣaṇo dveṣaḥ, mithyāpratipattilakṣaṇo moha iti/ etat pratyātmavedanīyaṃ sarvaśarīriṇām --- vijānāty ayaṃ śarīrī rāgam utpannam ``asti me 'dhyātmaṃ rāgadharma'' iti/ virāgaṃ ca vijānāti ---``nāsti me 'dhyātmaṃ rāgadharma'' iti/ evam itarayor apīti/ mānerṣyāsūyāprabhṛtayas tu trairāśyam anupatitā iti nopasaṅkhyāyante//3//
children.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) is characterized by clinging (<s>āsakti</s>); <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) is characterized by resentment (<s>amarṣa</s>); <s>moha</s> (delusion) is characterized by false apprehension (<s>mithyāpratipatti</s>). This is individually experienced by all embodied beings: the embodied being recognizes the arisen attachment — 'there is in me internally the property of attachment.' And recognizes the absence of attachment — 'there is no property of attachment in me internally.' Likewise for the other two as well. But pride, envy, malice, and the rest, having fallen under the three groups, are not separately enumerated. // 3 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.4: Not (distinct categories), because they have a single antidote (<s>ekapratyanīka</s>).

children.text: nārthāntaraṃ rāgādayaḥ/ kasmāt? ekapratyanīkabhāvāt --- tattvajñānaṃ samyaṅmatir āryaprajñā sambodha ity ekam idaṃ pratyanīkaṃ trayāṇām iti//4//
children.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> and the rest are not distinct categories. Why? Because they have a single antidote: the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), right cognition (<s>samyaṅmati</s>), noble wisdom (<s>āryaprajñā</s>), awakening (<s>sambodha</s>) — this single thing is the antidote for all three. // 4 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.5: (This argument is) invalid because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>).

children.text: ekapratyanīkāḥ pṛthivyāṃ śyāmādayo 'gnisaṃyogenaikena, ekayonayaś ca pākajā iti//5//
children.translated_text: Dark color and the like in earth have a single antidote — conjunction with fire; and the heat-born (colors) have a single origin. // 5 //
If they are indeed distinct categories —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.6: Among them, <s>moha</s> (delusion) is the worst, because the other two do not arise in one who is not deluded.

children.text: mohaḥ pāpaḥ, pāpataro vā dvāv abhipretyoktam/ kasmāt? nāmūḍhasyetarotpatteḥ ---
children.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> is sinful, or rather the most sinful — both senses are intended. Why? Because the other two do not arise in one who is not deluded —

children.text:
% -tarotpatteḥ ---] p.929
amūḍhasya rāgadveṣā notpadyante mūḍhasya tu yathāsaṅkalpam utpattiḥ, viṣayeṣu rañjanīyāḥ saṅkalpā rāgahetavaḥ, kopanīyāḥ saṅkalpā dveṣahetavaḥ, ubhaye ca saṅkalpā na mithyāpratipattilakṣaṇatvān mohād anye, tāv imau mohayonī rāgadveṣāv iti/ tattvajñānāc ca mohanivṛttau rāgadveṣānutpattir ity ekapratyanīkabhāvopapattiḥ/ evaṃ ca kṛtvā tattvajñānād ``duḥkhajanmapravṛttidoṣamithyājñānānām uttarottarāpāye tadanantarābhāvād apavarga'' iti vyākhyātam iti//6//
children.translated_text: In one who is not deluded, attachment and aversion do not arise; but in one who is deluded, they arise according to one's volitions (<s>saṅkalpa</s>). Volitions that lead to fascination with objects are the causes of attachment; volitions that lead to anger are the causes of aversion; and both types of volition, being characterized by false apprehension, are not different from <s>moha</s> (delusion). Thus these two — attachment and aversion — have delusion as their source. And from the cessation of delusion through the knowledge of reality, the non-arising of attachment and aversion (follows) — thus the possibility of a single antidote is established. Therefore, it has been explained that through the knowledge of reality, 'from the successive removal of false knowledge, faults, activity, birth, and suffering — each (ceasing) upon the absence of the one (immediately) preceding it — there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).' // 6 //
[Section: NySBh_4,1.7]
[Note: p.930] Then the following is obtained —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.7: Because of the relation of cause and effect, (delusion) is a different entity from the defects (<s>doṣas</s>).

children.text: anyad dhi nimittam anyac ca naimittikam iti doṣanimittatvād adoṣo moha iti//7//
children.translated_text: For the cause is one thing and the effect is another; therefore, since delusion (<s>moha</s>) is caused by the defects, it is not (itself) a defect. //7//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.8]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.8: (This is) not (so), because delusion is included within the definition of defects.

children.text: pravarttanālakṣaṇā doṣā ity anena doṣalakṣaṇenāvarudhyate doṣeṣu moha iti//8//
children.translated_text: The defects are defined as that which causes activity (<s>pravartanā</s>) — by this definition of defect, delusion is included among the defects. //8//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.9]
[Note: p.931]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.9: And because the relation of cause and effect is justified among things of the same class, there is no exclusion (of delusion from the defects).

children.text: dravyāṇāṃ guṇānāṃ vānekavidhavikalpo nimittanaimittikabhāve tulyajātīyānāṃ dṛṣṭa iti//9//
children.translated_text: The manifold variety of substances or qualities is observed in the relation of cause and effect among things of the same class. //9//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.10]

children.text: doṣānantaraṃ pretyabhāvaḥ, tasyāsiddhir ātmano nityatvāt --- na khalu nityaṃ kiṃcij jāyate mriyate vā iti janmamaraṇayor nityatvād ātmano 'nupapattiḥ, ubhayaṃ ca pretyabhāva iti tatrāyaṃ siddhānuvādaḥ ---
children.translated_text: After the defects comes transmigration (<s>pretyabhāva</s>). Its establishment (is questioned) on account of the permanence of the self — for indeed nothing permanent is born or dies; thus, from the permanence of the self, both birth and death are unjustified, and both constitute transmigration. On this, here is a statement of what is already established —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.10: Transmigration (<s>pretyabhāva</s>) is established given the permanence of the self.

children.text: nityo 'yam ātmā praiti pūrvaśarīraṃ jahāti mriyate iti, pretya ca pūrvaśarīraṃ hitvā
children.translated_text: This self is permanent — it departs, abandons the former body, and dies; and having departed, having left the former body,

children.text:
% p.932
bhavati jāyate śarīrāntaram upādatta iti/ tac caitad ubhayaṃ ``punar utpattiḥ pretyabhāvaḥ'' ity atroktaṃ pūrvaśarīraṃ hitvā śarīrāntaropādānaṃ pretyabhāvaḥ iti tac caitannityatve sambhavatīti/ yasya tu sattvotpādaḥ sattvanirodhaḥ pretyabhāvaḥ tasya kṛtahānam akṛtābhyāgamaś ca doṣaḥ/ ucchedahetuvāde ṛṣyupadeśāś cānarthakā iti//10//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.932] it comes into being, is born, and takes up another body. And both of these have been stated in the (definition) 'transmigration is re-birth': leaving the former body and taking up another body is transmigration — and this is possible given permanence. But for one for whom transmigration is the origination and cessation of a being, there is the defect of loss of what was done and the arrival of what was not done. And in the doctrine that posits annihilation as the cause, the teachings of the sages (<s>ṛṣis</s>) would also be purposeless. //10//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.11]
[Note: p.933] If (one asks) how does origination (occur)? —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.11: Because of the authority of perception regarding (the origination of) manifest (things) from the manifest.

children.text: kena prakāreṇa kiṃdharmakāt kāraṇād vyaktaṃ śarīrādy utpadyata iti? vyaktād bhūtasamākhyātāt pṛthivyāditaḥ paramasūkṣmān nityād vyaktaṃ śarīrendriyaviṣayopakaraṇādhāraṃ prajñātaṃ dravyam utpadyate/ vyaktaṃ ca khalv indriyagrāhyaṃ tatsāmānyāt kāraṇam api vyaktam/ kiṃ sāmānyam? rūpādiguṇayogaḥ rūpādiguṇayuktebhyaḥ pṛthivyādibhyo nityebhyo rūpādiguṇayuktaṃ śarīrādy utpadyate/
children.translated_text: In what manner, from a cause of what nature, does a manifest (thing) such as the body originate? From the manifest — that is, from earth and the rest, which are designated as elements (<s>bhūtas</s>), which are supremely subtle and permanent — a manifest substance that is known (as) the body, sense organs, objects, instruments, and their support originates. And since the manifest is indeed graspable by the sense organs, the cause too is manifest, by virtue of their commonality. What is the commonality? The possession of qualities such as color and the rest — from earth and the rest, which are permanent and possess qualities such as color, the body and the rest, which possess qualities such as color, originate.

children.text:
% -vyādibhyo nityebhyo rūpādiguṇayuktaṃ śarīrādy utpadyate/] p.934
pratyakṣaprāmāṇyāt --- dṛṣṭo hi rūpādiguṇayuktebhyo mṛtprabhṛtibhyas tathābhūtasya dravyasyotpādaḥ, tena cādṛṣṭasyānumānam iti/ rūpādīnām anvayadarśanāt prakṛtivikārayoḥ, pṛthivyādīnāṃ nityānām atīndriyāṇāṃ kāraṇabhāvo 'numīyata iti//11//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.934] Because of the authority of perception — for the origination of a substance of that nature from (substances) such as clay and the rest that possess qualities such as color is observed; and from that, the unobserved (cause) is inferred. From the observation of the continuity of color and the rest in the material cause and its transformation, the causal nature of earth and the rest — which are permanent and beyond the senses — is inferred. //11//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.12]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.12: (This is valid) because a pot is not produced from (another) pot.

children.text: idam api pratyakṣam --- na khalu vyaktād ghaṭād vyakto ghaṭa utpadyamāno dṛśyate iti, vyaktād vyaktasyānutpattidarśanān na vyaktaṃ kāraṇam iti//12//
children.translated_text: This too is a matter of perception — for indeed a manifest pot is not seen being produced from a manifest pot; therefore, from the observation that a manifest (thing) is not produced from a manifest (thing of the same kind), the manifest is not the (direct) cause. //12//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.13]
[Note: p.935]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.13: There is no refutation (of the view that the manifest originates) from the manifest, because a pot is (indeed) produced from a manifest (substance).

children.text: na brūmaḥ sarvaṃ sarvasya kāraṇam iti, kin tu yad utpadyate vyaktaṃ dravyaṃ tat tathābhūtād evotpadyate iti/ vyaktaṃ ca tanmṛddravyaṃ kapālasaṃjñakaṃ yato ghaṭa utpadyate/ na caitannihnuvānaḥ kvacid abhyanujñāṃ labdhum arhatīti/ tad etat tattvam//13//
children.translated_text: We do not say that everything is the cause of everything; rather, whatever manifest substance is produced, it is produced only from (a cause) of the same nature. And that clay substance called a potsherd (<s>kapāla</s>), from which a pot is produced, is itself manifest. And one who denies this does not deserve to gain assent anywhere. This is the truth of the matter. //13//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.14]
Hereafter, the views of the debaters are presented —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.14: An existent thing originates from the non-existent — not, because (production occurs) by destroying (the prior form) and then manifesting.

children.text:
% p.936
asataḥ sad utpadyate ity ayaṃ pakṣaḥ/ kasmāt? upamṛdya prādurbhāvāt/ upamṛdya bījam aṅkura utpadyate nānupamṛdya, na ced vījopamardo 'ṅkurakāraṇam anupamarde 'pi bījasyāṅkurotpattiḥ syād iti//14//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.936] The thesis is: the existent originates from the non-existent. Why? Because (production occurs) by destroying and then manifesting. The sprout originates by destroying the seed, not without destroying (it); if the destruction of the seed were not the cause of the sprout, then the sprout would originate even without the destruction of the seed. //14//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.15]
To this it is said —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.15: Because of contradiction, the usage is improper.

children.text: upamṛdya prādurbhāvād ity ayuktaḥ prayogo vyāghātāt/ yad upamṛdnāti na tad upamṛdya prādurbhavitum arhati vidyamānatvāt/ yac ca prādurbhavati na tenāprādurbhūtenāvidyamānenopamarda iti//15//
children.translated_text: The usage 'by destroying and then manifesting' is improper because of contradiction. That which destroys cannot, after destroying, come into manifestation, since it (still) exists (as the destroyer). And that which comes into manifestation, not having previously manifested and being non-existent, cannot perform the destruction. //15//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.16]
[Note: p.937]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.16: (This is) not (a valid objection), because of the use of agent-words (<s>kāraka</s>) for past and future (non-existent things).

children.text: atīte cānāgate cāvidyamāne kārakaśabdāḥ prayujyante/ putro janiṣyate, janiṣyamāṇaṃ putram abhinandati, putrasya janiṣyamāṇasya nāma karoti, abhūt kumbhaḥ, bhinnaṃ kumbham anuśocati, bhinnasya kumbhasya kapālāni, ajātāḥ putrāḥ pitaraṃ tāpayantīti bahulaṃ bhāktāḥ prayogā dṛśyante/ kā punar iyaṃ bhaktiḥ? ānantaryaṃ bhaktiḥ, ānantaryasāmarthyād upamṛdya prādurbhāvārthaḥ, prādurbhaviṣyann aṅkura upamṛdnātīti bhāktaṃ kartṛtvam iti//16//
children.translated_text: Agent-words are applied to what is past and future, which are non-existent: 'A son will be born,' 'he rejoices at the son who is about to be born,' 'he gives a name to the son who is about to be born,' 'the pot existed,' 'he grieves over the broken pot,' 'the potsherds of the broken pot,' 'unborn sons torment their father' — such figurative usages are seen abundantly. What then is this figurative usage? Figurative usage is based on immediate succession (<s>ānantarya</s>); by the force of immediate succession, (the expression) 'by destroying and then manifesting' has meaning — 'the sprout that is about to manifest destroys (the seed)' — this is figurative agency. //16//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.17]
[Note: p.938]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.17: (This is) not (valid), because there is no production from what has been destroyed.

children.text: na vinaṣṭād bījād aṅkura utpadyate iti tasmān nābhāvād bhāvotpattir iti//17//
children.translated_text: The sprout is not produced from a destroyed seed; therefore, there is no origination of an existent from the non-existent. //17//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.18]
[Note: p.939]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.18: There is no refutation, because of the indication of a sequence.

children.text: upamardaprādurbhāvayoḥ paurvāparyaniyamaḥ kramaḥ, sa khalv abhāvād bhāvotpatter hetur nirdiśyate; sa ca na pratiṣidhyate iti/ vyāhatavyūhānām avayavānāṃ pūrvavyūhanivṛttau vyūhāntarād dravyaniṣpattir nābhāvāt/ bījāvayavāḥ kutaścin nimittāt prādurbhūtakriyāḥ pūrvavyūhaṃ jahati vyūhāntaraṃ cāpadyante vyūhāntarād aṅkura utpadyate/ dṛśyante khalu avayavās tatsaṃyogāś cāṅkurotpattihetavaḥ/ na cānivṛtte pūrvavyūhe bījāvayavānāṃ śakyaṃ vyūhāntareṇa bhavitum ity upamardaprādurbhāvayoḥ paurvāparyaniyamaḥ kramaḥ,
children.translated_text: The fixed order of priority and posteriority between destruction and manifestation is the sequence (<s>krama</s>), and that is indicated as the basis for the origination of the existent from the non-existent; and it is not refuted. When the parts of the re-arranged constituents cease their prior arrangement, a substance is produced from the new arrangement, not from non-existence. The parts of the seed, due to some cause, having their activity initiated, abandon their prior arrangement and assume a new arrangement; from the new arrangement, the sprout is produced. For the parts and their conjunctions are observed to be the causes of the sprout's origination. And without the cessation of the prior arrangement of the seed's parts, a new arrangement is not possible — hence the fixed order of priority and posteriority between destruction and manifestation constitutes the sequence.

children.text:
% -m ity upamardaprādurbhāvayoḥ paurvāparyaniyamaḥ kramaḥ,] p.940
tasmān nābhāvād bhāvotpattir iti/ na cānyad bījāvayavebhyo 'ṅkurotpattikāraṇam ity upapadyte bījopādānaniyama iti//18//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.940] Therefore, there is no origination of the existent from the non-existent. And no other cause of the sprout's origination apart from the seed's parts is justified — hence the rule that the seed is the material cause. //18//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.19]
Now another says —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.19: <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is the cause, because it is observed that a person's actions do not (always) produce results.

children.text: puruṣo 'yaṃ samīhamāno nāvaśyaṃ samīhāphalaṃ prāpnoti tenānumīyate parādhīnaṃ puruṣasya karmaphalārādhanam iti, yadadhīnaṃ sa īśvaraḥ/ tasmād īśvaraḥ kāraṇam iti//19//
children.translated_text: This person, though striving, does not necessarily obtain the result of his effort; from this it is inferred that the obtainment of the fruit of a person's action is dependent on another — the one on whom it depends is <s>Īśvara</s>. Therefore, <s>Īśvara</s> is the cause. //19//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.20]
[Note: p.942]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.20: (This is) not (valid), because in the absence of a person's action, the result would not be produced.

children.text: īśvarādhīnā cet phalaniṣpattiḥ syād api tarhi puruṣasya samīhām antareṇa phalaṃ niṣpadyeteti//20//
children.translated_text: If the production of the result were dependent on <s>Īśvara</s> alone, then surely the result should be produced even without the person's effort. //20//
[Section: NySBh_4,1.21]
[Note: p.943]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.21: (The objection in 4.1.20) is not a valid reason, because (the result) is brought about by that (<s>Īśvara</s>).

children.text:
puruṣakāram īśvaro 'nugṛhṇāti, phalāya puruṣasya yatamānasyeśvaraḥ phalaṃ sampādayatīti/ yadā na sampādayati tadā puruṣakarmāphalaṃ bhavatīti/ tasmād īśvarakāritatvāt ahetuḥ puruṣakarmābhāve phalāniṣpatter iti/
guṇaviśiṣṭam ātmāntaram īśvaraḥ/ tasya ātmakalpāt kalpāntarānupapattiḥ, adharmamithyājñānapramādahānyā dharmajñānasamādhisampadā ca viśiṣṭam ātmāntaram īśvaraḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> supports a person's effort — <s>Īśvara</s> brings about the result for the person who strives for it. When he does not bring it about, then the person's action becomes fruitless. Therefore, because (the result) is brought about by <s>Īśvara</s>, the absence of result in the absence of a person's action is not a valid reason (against <s>Īśvara</s>'s being the cause). <s>Īśvara</s> is a different self distinguished by special qualities. Since he is of the nature of a self, a nature different from that of the self is unjustified; <s>Īśvara</s> is a different self distinguished by the absence of <s>adharma</s> (demerit), false knowledge, inadvertence, and negligence, and by the fullness of <s>dharma</s> (merit), knowledge, and <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration),

children.text:
% p.944
tasya ca dharmasamādhiphalam aṇimādyaṣṭavidham aiśvaryam/ saṅkalpānuvidhāyī cāsya dharmaḥ pratyātmavṛttīn dharmādharmasañcayān pṛthivyādīni ca bhūtāni pravartayati/ evaṃ ca svakṛtābhyāgamasyālopena nirmāṇaprākāmyam īśvarasya svakṛtakarmaphalaṃ veditavyam/ āptakalpaś cāyam --- yathā pitāpatyānāṃ tathā pitṛbhūta īśvaro bhūtānām/ na cātmakalpād anyaḥ kalpaḥ sambhavati/ na tāvad asya buddhiṃ vinā kaścid dharmo liṅgabhūtaḥ śakya upapādayitum/ āgamāc ca draṣṭā boddhā sarvajñātā īśvara iti/ buddhyādibhiś cātmaliṅgair nirupākhyam īśvaraṃ pratyakṣānumānāgamaviṣayātītaṃ kaḥ śakta upapādayitum/
