There is no reason here [to establish that] what is not subject to origination is non-eternal. //66//
But this is the resolution —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4,1.67: No, and because <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the like are caused by mental construction.

children.text: karmanimittatvād itaretaranimittatvāc ceti samuccayaḥ/ mithyāsaṅkalpebhyo rañjanīyakopanīyamohanīyebhyo rāgadveṣamohā utpadyante, karma ca sattvanikāyanirvartakaṃ naiyamikān rāgadveṣamohān nirvarttayati, niyamadarśanāt/ dṛśyate hi kaścit sattvanikāyo rāgabahulaḥ kaścid dveṣabahulaḥ kaścin mohabahula iti/ itaretaranimittā ca rāgādīnām utpattiḥ/ mūḍho rajyati mūḍhaḥ kupyati rakto muhyati kupito muhyati/
children.translated_text: This is a conjunction [of reasons]: because they are caused by <s>karma</s>, and because they are mutually caused. <s>Rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) arise from false mental constructions — those that are attractive, provocative, and deluding. And <s>karma</s>, which produces [particular] classes of beings, produces the fixed [patterns of] <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s>, as seen from the observed restriction. For it is observed that a certain class of beings is predominated by <s>rāga</s>, another by <s>dveṣa</s>, and another by <s>moha</s>. And the origination of <s>rāga</s> and the like is mutually caused: the deluded person becomes attached, the deluded person becomes angry, the attached person becomes deluded, the angry person becomes deluded.

children.text:
% p.1033
sarvamithyāsaṅkalpānāṃ tattvajñānād anutpattiḥ kāraṇānutpātau ca kāryānutpatter iti rāgādīnām atyantam anutpattir iti/ anādiś ca kleśasantatir ity ayuktam, sarve ime khalv ādhyātmikā bhāvā anādinā prabandhena pravarttante śarīrādayaḥ, na jātv atra kaścid anutpannapūrvaḥ prathamata utpadyate 'nyatra tattvajñānāt/ na caivaṃ saty anutpattidharmakaṃ kiñcid avyayadharmakaṃ pratijñāyate iti/ karma ca sattvanikāyanirvartakaṃ tattvajñānakṛtān mithyāsaṅkalpavighātān na rāgādyutpattinimittaṃ bhavati, sukhaduḥkhasaṃvittiḥ phalaṃ tu bhavatīti//67//
children.translated_text: Through knowledge of truth, all false mental constructions do not arise; and when the cause does not arise, the effect does not arise — hence the absolute non-origination of <s>rāga</s> and the like. And [the claim that] the continuum of afflictions is beginningless is unreasonable, for all these internal states — body and the like — proceed in a beginningless continuum. Never does anything here that has not previously originated arise for the first time, except through knowledge of truth. Yet even so, nothing is claimed to be not subject to origination or not subject to destruction. And <s>karma</s>, which produces classes of beings — through the destruction of false mental constructions brought about by knowledge of truth — does not become the cause of the origination of <s>rāga</s> and the like; but the experience of pleasure and pain remains as its fruit. //67//
Now, the second lesson of the fourth chapter.

children.text: kiṃ nu khalu bhoḥ yāvanto viṣayās tāvatsu pratyekaṃ tattvajñānam utpadyate, atha kvacid utpadyata iti/ kaś cātra viśeṣaḥ? na tāvad ekaikatra yāvad viṣayam utpadyate jñeyānām ānantyāt/ nāpi kvacid utpadyate, yatra notpadyate tatrānivṛtto moha iti mohaśeṣaprasaṅgaḥ/ na cānyaviṣayeṇa tattvajñānenānyaviṣayo mohaḥ śakyaḥ pratiṣeddhum iti/
children.translated_text: Now then, does knowledge of truth arise with respect to each of as many objects as there are, or does it arise with respect to some particular [set of objects]? And what is the distinction here? It does not arise with respect to each and every object, since the objects to be known are infinite. Nor does it arise with respect to some particular [objects], for wherever it does not arise, delusion remains unremoved — and the consequence would be residual delusion. And delusion regarding one object cannot be prevented by knowledge of truth regarding another object.

children.text:
% p.1036
mithyājñānaṃ vai khalu moho na tattvajñānasyānutpattimātram/ tac ca mithyājñānaṃ yatra viṣaye pravartamānaṃ saṃsārabījaṃ bhavati sa viṣayas tattvato jñeya iti/
kiṃ punas tan mithyājñānam? anātmany ātmagrahaḥ, aham asmīti moho 'haṅkāra iti/ anātmānaṃ khalv aham asmīti paśyato dṛṣṭir ahaṅkāra iti/ kiṃ punas tadarthajātaṃ yadviṣayo 'haṅkāraḥ? śarīrendriyamanovedanābuddhayaḥ/ kathaṃ tadviṣayo 'haṅkāraḥ saṃsārabījaṃ bhavati?
children.translated_text: False knowledge is indeed delusion — not the mere non-origination of knowledge of truth. And that false knowledge, operating in whatever object it becomes the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — that object must be known in truth. What then is that false knowledge? The apprehension of self in what is not self — the delusion 'I am,' the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (egoism). Indeed, one who sees what is not the self as 'I am' — that view is <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. What then is the class of objects regarding which <s>ahaṅkāra</s> operates? Body, sense organs, mind, sensations, and cognitions. How does <s>ahaṅkāra</s> regarding these become the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>?

children.text:
% bhavati?] p.1037
ayaṃ khalu śarīrādyarthajātam aham asmīti vyavasitaḥ taducchedenātmocchedaṃ manyamāno 'nucchedatṛṣṇāpariplutaḥ punaḥ punas tad upādatte, tad upādadāno janmamaraṇāya yatate, tenāviyogān nātyantaṃ duḥkhād vimucyata iti/ yas tu duḥkhaṃ duḥkhāyatanaṃ duḥkhānuṣaktaṃ sukhaṃ ca sarvam idaṃ duḥkham iti paśyati sa duḥkhaṃ parijānati/ parijñātaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ prahīṇaṃ bhavaty anupādānāt saviṣānnavat/ evaṃ doṣān karma ca duḥkhahetur iti paśyati/ na cāprahīṇeṣu doṣeṣu duḥkhaprabandhocchedena śakyaṃ bhavitum iti doṣān jahāti, prahīṇeṣu ca doṣeṣu na pravṛttiḥ pratisandhānāyety uktam/
pretyabhāvaphaladuḥkhāni ca jñeyāni vyavasthāpayati karma ca doṣāṃś ca praheyān/ apavargo 'dhigantavyas tasyādhigamopāyas tattvajñānam/ evaṃ catasṛbhir vidhābhiḥ prameyaṃ vibhaktam āsevamānasyābhyasyato bhāvayataḥ samyagdarśanaṃ yathābhūtāvabodhas tattvajñānam utpadyate/
evaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text:
This person, indeed, having identified with the body and the rest as 'I am this,' thinking that upon their destruction the <s>ātman</s> is destroyed, and overwhelmed by the craving for non-destruction, repeatedly grasps at them; grasping at them, he strives toward birth and death; and because of non-separation from these, he is not absolutely liberated from suffering. But one who sees that all this — suffering, the abode of suffering, and the pleasure that is accompanied by suffering — is suffering, he fully comprehends suffering. And suffering that has been fully comprehended becomes abandoned, because of the cessation of grasping — like poisoned food. Similarly, he sees that defects (<s>doṣa</s>) and <s>karma</s> are causes of suffering. And since, without the abandonment of defects, it is not possible to cut off the continuum of suffering — he abandons the defects. When the defects are abandoned, there is no activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) for the purpose of reconnection (to <s>saṃsāra</s>) — as has been stated.
The sufferings that result in future existence are to be known; and <s>karma</s> and defects are to be abandoned as what is to be removed. <s>Apavarga</s> (liberation) is to be attained; and the means to its attainment is true knowledge (<s>tattvajñāna</s>). Thus, when the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is divided into four categories and one diligently practices, repeats, and cultivates — right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), the understanding of things as they really are, i.e. true knowledge, arises.
And thus —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.1: From the true knowledge of the occasions of defects, the cessation of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) (follows).

children.text:
% p.1038
śarīrādiduḥkhāntaṃ prameyaṃ doṣanimittaṃ tadviṣayatvān mithyājñānasya/ tad idaṃ tattvajñānaṃ tadviṣayam utpannam ahaṅkāraṃ nivartayati samānaviṣaye tayor virodhāt/ evaṃ tattvajñānād ``duḥkhajanmapravṛttidoṣamithyājñānānām uttarottarāpāye tadanantarābhāvād apavarga'' iti/ sa cāyaṃ śāstrārthasaṃgraho 'nūdyate nāpūrvo vidhīyate iti//1//
children.translated_text: The knowable (<s>prameya</s>), extending from the body to suffering, is the occasion of defects, because false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) has it as its object. This true knowledge, having arisen with that (knowable) as its object, removes the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), because of the mutual opposition between them when they share the same object. Thus, from true knowledge: 'through the successive cessation of suffering, birth, activity, defects, and false knowledge — each one ceasing upon the cessation of the one following it — there is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).' And this is a summary of the teaching of the treatise — it is being restated (<s>anūdya</s>), not being newly prescribed. // 1 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.2]
But the order of contemplation (<s>prasaṅkhyāna</s>) is as follows —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.2: The objects of the senses — visible form and the rest — are the occasions of defects, produced by false ideation (<s>saṅkalpa</s>).

children.text: kāmaviṣayā indriyārthā iti rūpādaya ucyante/ te mithyā saṅkalpyamānā rāgadveṣamohān pravartayanti, tān pūrvaṃ prasañcakṣīta/ tāṃś ca prasañcakṣāṇasya rūpādiviṣayo mithyāsaṅkalpo nivartate/ tannivṛttāv adhyātmaṃ śarīrādi prasañcakṣīta/ tatprasaṅkhyānād adhyātmaviṣayo 'haṅkāro nivartate/
children.translated_text: The objects of desire, the objects of the senses, are called visible form and the rest. When falsely ideated, they activate passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) — one should first contemplate these (external objects). And for one who contemplates them, the false ideation directed at the external objects of visible form and the rest ceases. Upon its cessation, one should contemplate the inner (<s>adhyātma</s>) — the body and the rest. Through that contemplation, the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) directed at the inner (body) ceases.

children.text:
% -d adhyātmaviṣayo 'haṅkāro] p.1040
so 'yam adhyātmaṃ bahiś ca viviktacitto viharan mukta ity ucyate//2//
children.translated_text: This person, whose mind is detached both inwardly and outwardly, dwelling (in equanimity), is called 'liberated' (<s>mukta</s>). // 2 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.3]

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ kācit saṃjñā heyā kācid bhāvayitavyety upadiśyate, nāthanirākaraṇam arthopādānaṃ vā/ katham iti? ---
children.translated_text: Hereafter, certain designations (<s>saṃjñā</s>) are to be abandoned and certain are to be cultivated — this is taught; not the rejection of the object nor the adoption of the object. How so?
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.3: But the cause of those (defects) is the false identification with the whole (<s>avayavin</s>).

children.text: teṣāṃ doṣāṇāṃ nimittaṃ tv avayavyabhimānaḥ/ sā ca khalu strīsaṃjñā sapariṣkārā puruṣasya, puruṣasaṃjñā ca striyāḥ sapariṣkārā nimittasaṃjñā anuvyañjanasaṃjñā ca/
children.translated_text: The cause of those defects is the false identification with the whole (<s>avayavin</s>). The designation 'woman,' together with her adornments, (is the cause) for the man; the designation 'man,' together with his adornments, for the woman — both the designation of primary characteristics and the designation of secondary characteristics.

children.text:
% ca/] p.1041
nimittasaṃjñā --- rasanāśrotram, dantoṣṭham, cakṣurnāsikam/ anuvyañjanasaṃjñā --- itthaṃ daṇḍā ittham oṣṭhāv iti/ seyaṃ saṃjñā kāmaṃ vardhayati tadanuṣaktāṃś ca doṣān vivarjanīyān, varjanaṃ tv asyāḥ/ bhedenāvayavasaṃjñā --- keśalomamāṃsaśoṇitāsthisnāyuśirākaphapittoccārādisaṃjñā;
children.translated_text: The designation of primary characteristics — the tongue and ear, teeth and lips, eyes and nose. The designation of secondary characteristics — 'Such is the tooth-stick, such are the lips.' This designation increases desire and the defects that accompany it — and they are to be rejected; but the rejection is of the designation (not of the object itself). The designation of parts (<s>avayava</s>) — the designation as hair, body-hair, flesh, blood, bone, sinew, vein, phlegm, bile, excrement, and so forth;

children.text:
% -śoṇitāsthi...] p.1042
tām aśubhasaṃjñety ācakṣate/ tām asya bhāvayataḥ kāmarāgaḥ prahīyate/
saty eva ca dvividhe viṣaye kācit saṃjñā bhāvanīyā kācit parivarjanīyety upadiśyate, yathā viṣasampṛkte 'nne 'nnasaṃjñopādānāya viṣasaṃjñā prahāṇāyeti//3//
children.translated_text:
they call this the 'impure designation' (<s>aśubhasaṃjñā</s>). For one who cultivates this (designation), the passion of desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>) is abandoned.
And since both types of object (the desirable and the impure) actually exist, certain designations are to be cultivated and certain are to be rejected — this is what is taught. Just as, in food mixed with poison, the designation 'food' leads to consumption (and is to be rejected), while the designation 'poison' leads to abandonment (and is to be cultivated). // 3 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.4]
Now, in order to refute the object (the whole), the refutation of the <s>avayavin</s> (whole) is presented —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.4: Doubt arises from the twofold nature of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).

children.text: sadasator upalambhād vidyā dvividhā, sadasator anupalambhād avidyāpi dvividhā/ upalambhyamāne 'vayavini vidyādvaividhyāt saṃśayaḥ, anupalabhyamāne cāvidyādvaividhyāt saṃśayaḥ/ so 'yam avayavī *yad upalabhyate (following ṭhakur, yady apalabhyate ṛinsen) athāpi nopalabhyate na kathañcana saṃśayān mucyata iti//4//
children.translated_text: Knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) is twofold, because of the perception of the existent and the existent (i.e. both real aspects); ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is also twofold, because of the non-perception of the existent and the (other) existent. When the <s>avayavin</s> (whole) is perceived, doubt arises from the twofold nature of knowledge; and when it is not perceived, doubt arises from the twofold nature of ignorance. This <s>avayavin</s> — whether it is perceived or whether it is not perceived — in no way is it freed from doubt. // 4 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.5]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.5: There is no doubt about that, because of the well-established nature of the previously stated reasons.

children.text: tasminn anupapannaḥ saṃśayaḥ/ kasmāt? pūrvoktahetūnām apratiṣedhād asti dravyāntarārambha iti//5//
children.translated_text: The doubt about that (the <s>avayavin</s>) is untenable. Why? Because the previously stated reasons have not been refuted — the origination of a different substance (<s>dravyāntarārambha</s>) is established. // 5 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.6]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.6: Also because of the impossibility of function (<s>vṛtti</s>), there is no doubt.

children.text: vṛttyanupapatter api tarhi saṃśayānupapattir nāsty avayavīti//6//
children.translated_text: Since function would be impossible (without a whole), doubt is untenable — (one cannot say) 'the <s>avayavin</s> does not exist.' // 6 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.7]
He analyzes this —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.7: Because the parts do not exist in the whole either in its entirety or in a part, the <s>avayavin</s> (whole) does not exist.

children.text: ekaiko 'vayavo na tāvat kṛtsne 'vayavini vartate, tayoḥ parimāṇabhedād avayavāntarasambandhābhāvaprasaṅgāc ca/ nāpy avayavyekadeśena, na hy asyānye avayavā ekadeśabhūtāḥ santīti//7//
children.translated_text: Each individual part does not exist in the entire <s>avayavin</s> — because of the difference in magnitude between them, and because the consequence would be the absence of connection with other parts. Nor does (the <s>avayavin</s> exist) in a part of the parts, for it has no other parts that constitute a portion of it. // 7 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.8]
Now, suppose the <s>avayavin</s> exists in the parts themselves —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.8: And because of the non-existence of function in them (the parts), the <s>avayavin</s> does not exist.

children.text: na tāvat pratyavayavaṃ vartate, tayoḥ parimāṇabhedād dravyasya caikadravyatvaprasaṅgāt/ nāpy ekadeśaiḥ sarveṣu anyāvayavābhāvāt/ tad evaṃ na yuktaḥ saṃśayo nāsty avayavīti//
children.translated_text: It does not exist in each individual part — because of the difference in magnitude between them, and because the consequence would be the substance's being identical with a single substance. Nor does it exist in all (parts) through portions, because of the absence of other parts (in the parts). Thus, the doubt is unjustified — the <s>avayavin</s> does not exist.
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.9]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.9: And because it does not exist separately from the parts.

children.text: avayavyabhāva iti vartate/ na cāyaṃ pṛthag avayavebhyo vartate agrahaṇāt nityatvaprasaṅgāc ca/ tasmān nāsty avayavīti//
children.translated_text: It is continued: the <s>avayavin</s> does not exist. And it does not exist separately from the parts — because it is not apprehended (apart from them), and because the consequence would be permanence. Therefore, the <s>avayavin</s> does not exist.
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.10]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.10: And the parts are not (the same as) the <s>avayavin</s>.

children.text: na cāvayavānāṃ dharmo 'vayavī/ kasmāt? dharmamātrasya dharmibhir avayavaiḥ pūrvavat sambandhānupapatteḥ/ pṛthak cāvayavebhyo dharmibhyo dharmasyāgrahaṇād iti samānam//10//
children.translated_text: And the <s>avayavin</s> is not a property of the parts. Why? Because the impossibility of the connection between a mere property and the property-bearers (i.e. the parts) is the same as before. And because a property is not apprehended separately from the property-bearers (the parts) — the same (reasoning applies). // 10 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.11]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.11: Because there is no division in a single entity, the use of the word 'division' is untenable — hence no question (arises).

children.text: kiṃ pratyavayavaṃ kṛtsno 'vayavī vartate athaikadeśeneti nopapadyate praśnaḥ/ kasmāt? ekasmin bhedābhāvād bhedaśabdaprayogānupapatteḥ/ kṛtsnam ity anekasyāśeṣābhidhānam, ekadeśa iti nānātve kasyacid abhidhānam/ tāv imau kṛtsnaikadeśaśabdau bhedaviṣayau naikasminn avayaviny uapapadyete bhedābhāvād iti//11//
children.translated_text: The question 'Does the whole <s>avayavin</s> exist in each part entirely, or in a portion?' — this question is untenable. Why? Because there is no division in a single entity, the use of the word 'division' is untenable. 'Entirely' (<s>kṛtsna</s>) designates the entirety of many things; 'a portion' (<s>ekadeśa</s>) designates some one among many. These two words — 'entirely' and 'a portion' — pertain to division, and are not applicable to a single <s>avayavin</s> because there is no division (in it). // 11 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.12]
(The argument that) it does not exist in a portion because of the absence of other parts — this is not a valid reason:
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.12: Even if other parts exist (within the parts), because of non-existence (of the whole in them), the reason is invalid.

children.text: avayavāntarābhāvād iti/ yady api ekadeśo 'vayavāntarabhūtaḥ syāt tathāpy avayave 'vayavāntaraṃ vartate nāvayavīti anyo 'vayavīti/
children.translated_text: (We said) 'because of the absence of other parts.' Even if a portion were constituted by other parts (within the parts), it would still be the case that a part's other part exists within the part, not the <s>avayavin</s> — which is something different from the <s>avayavin</s>.

children.text:
% -vāntaraṃ vartate ...] p.1050
anyāvayavabhāve 'py avṛtter avayavino naikadeśena vṛttir anyāvayavābhāvād ity ahetuḥ/
vṛttiḥ katham iti cet? ekasyānekatrāśrayāśritasambandhalakṣaṇā prāptiḥ/ āśrayāśritabhāvaḥ katham iti cet? yasya yato 'nyatrātmalābhānupapattiḥ sa āśrayaḥ/ na kāraṇadravyebhyo 'nyatra kāryadravyam ātmānaṃ labhate viparyayas tu kāraṇadravyeṣv iti/
nityeṣu katham iti cet, anityeṣu darśanāt siddham, nityeṣu dravyeṣu katham āśrayāśrayibhāva iti cet? anityeṣu dravyaguṇeṣu darśanād āśrayāśritabhāvasya nityeṣu siddhir iti/
children.translated_text:
Even if other parts exist, because of the non-existence of the <s>avayavin</s>'s functioning through a portion — because of the absence of other parts (of the whole in the parts of the parts) — this is not a valid reason.
If one asks: how does 'functioning' (<s>vṛtti</s>) work? The being-in (<s>prāpti</s>) of one entity in many, characterized by the relation of substrate and what is substrated (<s>āśrayāśritasambandha</s>). If one asks: how does the substrate-substrated relation (work)? That without which an entity cannot obtain its existence elsewhere — that is the substrate. The effect-substance does not obtain its existence apart from the causal substances; but the reverse (holds) in causal substances.
If it is asked: how (does this apply) in the case of permanent (substances)? Since it is observed in impermanent (things), it is established; if it is asked: in permanent substances, how does the substrate-substrated relation (exist)? Since the substrate-substrated relation is observed in impermanent substances and qualities, it is established in permanent ones as well.

children.text:
% p.1053
tasmād avayavyabhimānaḥ pratiṣidhyate niḥśreyasakāmasya, nāvayavī, yathā rūpādiṣu mithyāsaṅkalpo na rūpādaya iti//12//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the false identification with the <s>avayavin</s> (whole) is to be denied for one who desires the highest good — not the <s>avayavin</s> itself; just as in the case of visible form and the rest, it is the false ideation that is denied, not visible form and the rest themselves. // 12 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.13]

children.text:
% p.1054
sarvāgrahaṇam avayavyasiddher iti pratyavasthito 'py etad āha ---
children.translated_text: Even one who has taken the opposing position that the non-apprehension of everything (proves the non-existence of the <s>avayavin</s>) says this —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.13: Its perception is like the perception of a mass of hair by one suffering from <s>taimirika</s> (an eye disease).

children.text: yathaikaikaḥ keśas taimirikeṇa nopalabhyate keśasamūhas tūpalabhyate, tathaikaiko 'ṇur nopalabhyate aṇusañcayas tūpalabhyate, tad idam aṇusamūhaviṣayaṃ grahaṇam iti//13//
children.translated_text: Just as an individual hair is not perceived by one with <s>taimirika</s> (but a mass of hair is perceived), so too an individual atom is not perceived (but an aggregate of atoms is perceived). This apprehension has a mass of atoms as its object. // 13 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.14]

children.text: NyS_4,2.14: svaviṣayān atikrameṇendiryasya paṭumandabhāvād viṣayagrahaṇasya tathābhāavo nāviṣaye pravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 4.2.14: Because of the sharpness and dullness of the sense organ, which surpasses its own domain, and because the apprehension of objects is of the same kind, there is no operation in a non-object.

children.text: yathāviṣayam indriyāṇāṃ paṭumandabhāvād viṣayagrahaṇānāṃ paṭumandabhāvo bhavati/ cakṣuḥ khalu prakṛṣyamāṇaṃ nāviṣayaṃ gandhaṃ gṛhṇāti, nikṛṣyamāṇaṃ ca na svaviṣayāt pracyavate/ so 'yaṃ taimirikaḥ kaścic cakṣur viṣayaṃkeśaṃ na gṛhṇāti, kaścid gṛhṇāti keśasamūham/
children.translated_text: Because of the sharpness and dullness of the sense organs with respect to their own objects, the apprehensions of objects also become sharp and dull. The eye, when enhanced, does not apprehend smell, which is not its object; and when diminished, it does not fall away from its own object (color). Thus, the person with <s>taimirika</s> — some (degree of the disease allows) the eye not to apprehend a single hair, (while another degree allows) some (to apprehend) a mass of hair.

children.text:
% p.1055
ubhayaṃ hy ataimimirikeṇa caks.uṣā gṛhyate/ paramāṇavas tv atīndriyā indriyāviṣayabhūtā na kenacid indriyeṇa gṛhyante, samuditās tu gṛhyante, ity aviṣaye pravṛttir indriyasya prasajyeta/ na jātv arthāntaram aṇubhyo gṛhyata iti/ te khalv ime paramāṇavaḥ sannihitā gṛhyamāṇā atīndriyatvaṃ jahati, viyuktāś cāgṛhyamāṇā indriyaviṣayatvaṃ na labhanta iti/ so 'yaṃ dravyāntarānutpattāv atimahān vyāghāta ity upapadyate dravyāantaram yad grahaṇasya viṣaya iti/
sañcayamātraṃ viṣaya iti cen na, sañcayasya saṃyogabhāvāt tasya cātīndriyasyāgrahaṇād ayuktam/ sañcayaḥ khalv anekasya saṃyogaḥ, sa ca gṛhyamāṇāśrayo gṛhyate nātīndriyāśrayaḥ, bhavati hīdam anena saṃyuktam iti/ tasmād yuktam etad iti/
children.translated_text:
For both (the individual hair and the mass) are apprehended by the eye of a non-<s>taimirika</s> person. But atoms, being supersensory and not objects of the senses, are not apprehended by any sense organ; yet in combination they are apprehended — (which would mean) the sense organ operates on a non-object, (and) this is untenable. No other object apart from atoms is ever apprehended (on this view). These very atoms, when proximate and being apprehended, abandon their supersensory nature; but when separated and not being apprehended, they do not acquire the status of sense-objects. This great contradiction in the non-origination of a different substance is established — hence it is established that a different substance is the object of apprehension.
If it is said that the mere aggregate is the object — no, because the aggregate is (nothing but) a conjunction, and since that (conjunction of supersensory entities) is supersensory and not apprehended, it is untenable. An aggregate is the conjunction of many things; and that is apprehended when its substrate is being apprehended, not when the substrate is supersensory. For (it must be the case that) 'this is conjoined with that.'  Therefore, this (position that the whole exists) is justified.

children.text:
% p.1056
gṛhyamāṇasya cendriyeṇa viṣayasyāvaraṇādyanupalabdhikāraṇam upalabhyate/ tasmān nendriyadaurbalyād anupalabdhir aṇūnām, yathā nendriyadaurbalyāc cakṣuṣānupalabdhir gandhādīnām iti//14//
children.translated_text: And for an object that is being apprehended by a sense organ, a cause of non-apprehension such as obstruction is perceived. Therefore, the non-apprehension of atoms is not due to the weakness of the sense organs — just as the non-apprehension of smell and the like by the eye is not due to the weakness of the eye. // 14 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.15]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.15: And in this way, the infinite regress of parts and wholes (would follow) until dissolution.

children.text: yaḥ khalv avayavino 'vayaveṣu vṛttipratiṣedhād abhāvaḥ so 'yam avayavasyāvayaveṣu prasajyamānaḥ sarvapralayāya vā kalpeta, niravayavād vā paramāṇuto nivarteta/ ubhayathā copalabdhiviṣayasyābhāvaḥ, tadabhāvād upalabhyabhāvaḥ/ upalabhyāśrayaś cāyaṃ vṛttipratiṣedhaḥ, sa āśrayaṃ vyāghnan ātmaghātāya kalpata iti//15//
children.translated_text: The non-existence that is the denial of the existence of a whole in its parts — this same (reasoning), when applied to the parts (themselves) in their own parts, would either lead to the dissolution of everything, or would cease (to apply) at the partless <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom). In both cases, the object of perception would be non-existent; from its non-existence, there would be non-existence of the perceivable. And this denial of existence depends on the perceivable; (therefore,) denying its own foundation, it amounts to self-destruction. // 15 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.16]
And furthermore —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.16: There is no (universal) dissolution, because of the continued existence of the atom (<s>aṇu</s>).

children.text: avayavavibhāgam āśritya vṛttipratiṣedhād abhāvaḥ prasajyamāno niravayavāt paramāṇor nivartate na sarvapralayāya kalpate, niravayavatvaṃ tu paramāṇor vibhāgair alpataraprasaṅgasya yato nālpīyas tatrāvasthānāt/ loṣṭasya khalu pravibhajyamānāvayavasyālpataram alpatamam uttaram uttaraṃ bhavati/ sa cāyam alpataraprasaṅgaḥ yasmān nālpataram asti yaḥ paramo 'lpas tatra nivartate, yataś ca nālpīyo 'sti taṃ parama'nuṃ pracakṣmahe iti//16\\
children.translated_text: The non-existence entailed by the denial of the whole's existence through the division of parts, when being applied, ceases at the partless <s>paramāṇu</s> and does not lead to the dissolution of everything. The partlessness of the <s>paramāṇu</s> is because, in the process of division, the tendency toward something smaller comes to rest at that point beyond which nothing smaller exists. For when the parts of a clod are being progressively divided, each successive (result) becomes smaller and smaller. And this tendency toward something smaller ceases at that beyond which nothing smaller exists — that which is the ultimate smallest, that we call the <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom). // 16 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.17]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.17: Or else, beyond division there is nothing (further).
Since the division of parts has no end-point, substances would be innumerable; hence the cessation of divisibility. // 17 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.18]

children.text:
% p.1059
athedānīm ānupalambhikaḥ sarvaṃ nāstīti manyamāna āha ---
children.translated_text: Now, a non-perceptionist (<s>ānupalambhika</s>), thinking 'everything is non-existent,' says —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.18: That (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is untenable, because of the interpenetration of <s>ākāśa</s> (space).

children.text: tasyāṇor niravayavasya nityasyānupapattiḥ/ kasmāt? ākāśavyatibhedāt/ antar bahiś cāṇur ākāśena samāviṣṭo vyatibhinnaḥ, vyatibhedāt sāvayavaḥ, sāvayavatvād anitya iti//18//
children.translated_text: That atom, partless and eternal, is untenable. Why? Because of the interpenetration of <s>ākāśa</s>. The atom is pervaded and interpenetrated by <s>ākāśa</s> both inside and outside; because of the interpenetration, it has parts; because of having parts, it is impermanent. // 18 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.19]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.19: Or (the consequence would be) the non-omnipresence of <s>ākāśa</s> (space).

children.text: athaitan neṣyate --- paramāṇor antar nāsty ākāśam ity asarvagatatvaṃ prasajyata iti//19//
children.translated_text: And if this is not accepted — (that is, if it is maintained that) there is no <s>ākāśa</s> inside the <s>paramāṇu</s> — then the consequence is the non-omnipresence (of <s>ākāśa</s>). // 19 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.20]

children.text: NyS_4,2.20: antar bahiś ca kāryadravyasya kāraṇāntaravacanād akārye tadabhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 4.2.20: 'Inside' and 'outside' refer to a product-substance's being spoken of with reference to another cause; in the non-product, these do not apply.

children.text: ``antar'' iti pihitaṃ kāraṇāntaraiḥ kāraṇam ucyate/ ``bahir'' iti ca vyavadhāyakam avyavahitaṃ kāraṇam evocyate/ tad etat kāryadravyasya sambhavati, nāṇor akāryatvāt/ akārye hi paramāṇāv antar bahir ity asyābhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Inside' refers to a cause that is enclosed by other causes. 'Outside' also refers to a cause that is the covering (cause), the unenclosed (cause). This applies to a product-substance, not to the atom, because it is not a product. For in the <s>paramāṇu</s>, which is not a product, 'inside' and 'outside' do not apply.

children.text:
% hi paramāṇāv ...] p.1061
yatra cāsya bhāvo 'nukāryaṃ tat, na paramāṇuḥ, yato hi nālpataram asti sa paramāṇur iti//20//
children.translated_text: And that of which these (terms) apply is a product of the atom (<s>anukārya</s>), not the <s>paramāṇu</s> (itself) — for that beyond which there is nothing smaller is the <s>paramāṇu</s>. // 20 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.21]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.21: And (space is) omnipresent, because sounds and conjunctions are found (everywhere in it).

children.text: yatra kvacid utpannāḥ śabdā vibhavanty ākāśe --- tadāśrayā bhavanti, manobhiḥ paramāṇubhis tatkāryaiś ca saṃyogā vibhavanty ākāśe, nāsaṃyuktam ākāśena kiñcin mūrtadravyam upalabhyate, tasmān nāsarvagatam iti//21//
children.translated_text: Sounds produced anywhere whatsoever are found in <s>ākāśa</s> — they have it as their substrate. Conjunctions with minds, <s>paramāṇus</s>, and their products are found in <s>ākāśa</s>. No corporeal substance is perceived as uncojoined with <s>ākāśa</s>. Therefore it is not non-omnipresent. // 21 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.22]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.22: Non-displacement, non-obstruction, and pervasiveness are the properties of <s>ākāśa</s> (space).

children.text: saṃsarpatā pratighātinā dravyeṇa na vyuhyate, yathā kāṣṭhenodakam/ kasmāt? niravayavatvāt/ sarpac ca pratighāti na viṣṭambhāti --- nāsya kriyāhetuṃ guṇaṃ pratibadhnāti/
children.translated_text: It is not displaced by a moving, obstructing substance — as water (is displaced) by wood. Why? Because it is partless. And a moving, obstructing (substance) does not obstruct it — does not impede its quality that is the cause of action.

children.text:
% p.1063
kasmāt? asparśatvāt/ viparyaye hi viṣṭambho dṛṣṭa iti sa bhavān sāvayave sparśavati dravye dṛṣṭaṃ dharmaṃ viparīte nāśāṅkitum arhati/
aṇvavayavasyāṇutaratvaprasaṅgād anukāryapratiṣedhaḥ/ sāvayavatve cāṇor aṇvavayavo 'nutara iti prasajyate/ kasmāt? kāryakāraṇadravyayoḥ parimāṇabhedadarśanāt/ tasmād aṇvavayavasyāṇutaratvam, yas tu sāvayavo 'nukāryaṃ tad iti/ tasmād anukāryam idaṃ pratiṣidhyata iti/
kāraṇavibhāgāc ca kāryasyānityatvam, nākāśavyatibhedāt/ loṣṭasyāvayavavibhāgād anityatvam, nākāśasamāveṣād iti//22//
children.translated_text:
Why? Because it is intangible. For in the contrary case, obstruction is observed — and that, sir, has been observed in a substance that has parts and possesses touch; you should not suspect it in the contrary (case).
The denial of atomic products through the consequence that the parts of atoms would be smaller than atoms: if the atom had parts, its parts would be smaller than the atom — this is the consequence. Why? Because of the observed difference in magnitude between product-substance and cause-substance. Therefore, the parts of the atom would be smaller than the atom; but what has parts is a product of the atom — that is (the conclusion). Therefore the atomic product is hereby denied.
And the impermanence of a product is due to the separation of its causes, not due to the interpenetration of <s>ākāśa</s>. The impermanence of a clod is due to the division of its parts, not due to its being pervaded by <s>ākāśa</s>. // 22 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.23]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.23: And because corporeal things can have configurations, the existence of parts (is established).

children.text: paricchinnānāṃ hi sparśavatāṃ saṃsthānaṃ trikoṇaṃ caturasraṃ samaṃ parimaṇḍalam ity upapadyate, yat tat saṃsthānaṃ so 'vayavasanniveṣaḥ, parimaṇḍalāś cāṇavas tasmāt sāvayavā iti//23//
children.translated_text: For bounded, tangible things can have configurations — triangular, quadrangular, even, and spherical. That configuration is the arrangement of parts. And since atoms are spherical, therefore they have parts. // 23 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.24]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.24: And because of the possibility of conjunction.

children.text:
madhye sann aṇuḥ pūrvāparābhyām aṇubhyām saṃyuktas tayor vyavadhānaṃ kurute/ vyavadhānenānumīyate pūrvabhāgena pūrveṇāṇunā saṃyujyate, parabhāgena pareṇāṇunā saṃyujyate, yau tau pūrvāparau bhāgau tāv asyāvayavau, evaṃ sarvataḥ saṃyujyamānasya sarvato bhāgā avayavā iti/
yat tāvan ``mūrtimatāṃ saṃsthānopapatter avayavasadbhāva'' iti? atroktam/ kim uktam? vibhāge 'lpataraprasaṅgasya yato nālpīyas tatra nivṛtter aṇavayavasya cāṇutaratvaprasaṅgād aṇukāryapratiṣedha iti/
children.translated_text:
An atom situated in the middle, conjoined with two atoms — one in front and one behind — creates an intervening space between them. From the intervening space, it is inferred: it is conjoined with the front atom by its front part, and conjoined with the rear atom by its rear part. Those front and rear parts are its parts; thus an (atom) that is conjoined on all sides has parts on all sides.
As for the (argument) 'because corporeal things can have configurations, the existence of parts': the reply has been given. What was said? That in the process of division, the tendency toward something smaller ceases at that beyond which nothing smaller exists; and because the parts of atoms would have to be smaller than atoms, atomic products are denied.

children.text:
% p.1065
yat punar etat saṃyogopapatteś ceti? sparśavattvād vyavadhānam āśrayasya cāvyāptyā bhāgabhaktiḥ/ uktaṃ cātra sparśavān aṇuḥ sparśavator aṇvoḥ pratighātād vyavadhāyako na sāvayavatvāt/ sparśavattvāc ca vyavadhāne saty aṇusaṃyogo nāśrayaṃ vyāpnotīti bhāgabhaktir bhavati bhāgavānn ivāyam iti/ uktaṃ cātra vibhāge 'lpataraprasaṅgasya yato nālpīyas tatrāvasthānāt tadavayavasya cāṇutaratvaprasaṅgād aṇukāryapratiṣedha iti//24//
children.translated_text: And as for the (argument) 'because of the possibility of conjunction': since it is tangible, it creates an intervening space; and from the non-pervasion of the substrate, there is an allocation to parts. And the reply here is: the tangible atom, due to the obstruction by (other) tangible atoms, creates an intervening space — but not because it has parts. And because, given the tangibility, when there is an intervening space, the conjunction of the atom does not pervade its substrate, there is an allocation to parts — it appears as if having parts. And the reply here is: in the process of division, the tendency toward something smaller ceases at that beyond which nothing smaller exists; and because the parts of atoms would be smaller than atoms, atomic products are denied. // 24 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.25]

children.text: mūrtimatāṃ ca saṃsthānopapatteḥ saṃyogopapatteś ca paramāṇūnāṃ sāvayavatvam iti hetvoḥ ---
children.translated_text: Regarding the two reasons — that corporeal things can have configurations and that conjunction is possible — for the conclusion that <s>paramāṇus</s> have parts:
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.25: The denial (of partlessness) does not hold, because (these reasons) lead to an infinite regress, and because an infinite regress is untenable.

children.text: yāvan mūrtimad yāvac ca saṃyujyate tat sarvaṃ sāvayavam ity anavasthākāriṇāv imau hetū, sā cānavasthā nopapadyate/ satyām anavasthāyāṃ satyau hetū syātām, tasmād apratiṣedho 'yaṃ niravayavatvasyeti/
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is corporeal' and 'whatever is conjoined' — all of that has parts: these two reasons lead to an infinite regress, and that infinite regress is untenable. If the infinite regress were tenable, then the reasons would be valid; therefore, this denial of partlessness does not hold.

children.text:
% p.1066
vibhāgasya ca vibhajyamānahānir nopapadyate tasmāt pralayāntatā nopapadyata iti/
children.translated_text: And the dissolution of the divisible through division is untenable; therefore, the termination in dissolution is untenable.

children.text:
% p.1071
anavasthāyāṃ ca pratyadhikaraṇaṃ dravyāvayavānām ānantyāt parimāṇabhedānāṃ gurutvasya cāgraḥaṇam samānaparimāṇatvaṃ cāvayavāvayavinoḥ paramaṇvavayavibhāgād ūrdhvam iti//25//
children.translated_text: And in an infinite regress, since the parts of substance-parts in each successive case would be infinite, there would be no apprehension of differences in magnitude or of heaviness; and there would be equality of magnitude between the part and the whole beyond the division of the <s>paramāṇu</s>. // 25 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.26]

children.text:
% p.1072
yad idaṃ bhavān buddhīr āśritya buddhiviṣayāḥ santīti manyate mithyābuddhaya etāḥ, yadi hi tattvabuddhayaḥ syur buddhyā vivecane yāthātmyaṃ buddhiviṣayāṇām upalabhyeta ---
children.translated_text: Now, you who think, relying on cognitions, that the objects of cognition exist — these cognitions are false. For if they were cognitions of reality, then through discrimination by cognition, the true nature of the objects of cognition would be apprehended —

children.text: NyS_4,2.26: buddhyā vivecanāt tu bhāvānāṃ yāthātmyānupalabdhis tantvapakarṣaṇe paṭasadbhāvānupalabdhivat tadanupalabdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 4.2.26: But the non-apprehension of the true nature of things through discrimination by cognition — like the non-apprehension of the cloth's existence when the threads are separated — is such non-apprehension.

children.text:
% p.1073
yathāyaṃ tantur ayaṃ tantur iti pratyekaṃ tantuṣu vivicyamāneṣu nārthāntaraṃ kiñcid upalabhyate --- yat paṭabuddher viṣayaḥ syāt, yāthātmyānupalabdher asati viṣaye paṭabuddhir bhavantī mithyābuddhir bhavati, evaṃ sarvatreti// 26 //
children.translated_text: When the threads are discriminated one by one — 'this is a thread, this is a thread' — nothing else is apprehended that would be the object of the cognition 'cloth.' Since its true nature is not apprehended, the cognition of cloth occurring in the absence of its object is a false cognition — and so everywhere. // 26 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.27]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.27: This is a non-reason, because it is self-contradictory.

children.text: yadi buddhyā vivecanaṃ bhāvānāṃ na sarvabhāvānāṃ yāthātmyānupalabdhiḥ/ atha sarvabhāvānāṃ yāthātmyānupalabdhir na buddhyā vivecanam/ bhāvānāṃ buddhyā vivecanaṃ yāthātmyānupalabdhiś ceti vyāhanyate/
children.translated_text: If there is discrimination of things by cognition, then there is no non-apprehension of the true nature of all things. And if there is non-apprehension of the true nature of all things, then there is no discrimination of things by cognition. 'The discrimination of things by cognition' and 'the non-apprehension of true nature' — these are mutually contradictory.

children.text:
% yāthātmyānupalabdhiś ceti vyāhanyate/] p.1074
tad uktam --- ``avayavāvayaviprasaṅgaś caivam ā pralayād'' iti// 27 //
children.translated_text: As has been said: 'The consequence of parts having (further) parts, and so on until dissolution.' // 27 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.28]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.28: The non-separate apprehension (of the whole from its parts) is because (the whole) depends on them (the parts) as its substrate.

children.text: kāryadravyaṃ kāraṇadravyāśritaṃ tat kāraṇebhyaḥ pṛthaṅ nopalabhyate, viparyaye pṛthaggrahaṇāt,
children.translated_text: A product-substance depends on the cause-substance as its substrate; that (product) is not apprehended separately from its causes. In the contrary case, there is separate apprehension;

children.text:
% p.1075
yatrāśrayāśritabhāvo nāsti tatra pṛthaggrahaṇam iti/ buddhyā vivecanāt tu bhāvānāṃ pṛthaggrahaṇam atīndriyeṣv aṇuṣu, yad indriyeṇa gṛhyate tad etayā buddhyā vivicyamānam anyad iti// 28 //
children.translated_text: where the substrate-dependent relationship does not exist, there is separate apprehension. But the discrimination of things by cognition (leads to) separate apprehension only in the case of super-sensible atoms; what is apprehended by the sense organs, when discriminated by this cognition, (is seen to be) something different. // 28 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.29]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.29: And because of the apprehension of objects from <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge).

children.text: buddhyā vivecanād bhāvānāṃ yāthātmyopalabdhiḥ, yad asti yathā ca yan nāsti yathā ca tat sarvaṃ pramāṇata upalabdhyā sidhyati, yā ca pramāṇata upaloabdhis tad buddhyā vivecanaṃ bhāvānām, tena sarvaśāstrāṇi sarvakarmāṇi sarve ca śarīriṇāṃ vyavahārā vyāptāḥ/ parīkṣamāṇo hi buddhyādhyavasyatīdam astīdaṃ nāstīti tatra na sarvabhāvānupapattiḥ// 29 //
children.translated_text: Through the discrimination of things by cognition, the true nature is apprehended — what exists as it is, and what does not exist as it is — all this is established through apprehension by <s>pramāṇas</s>. And that apprehension through <s>pramāṇas</s> is the discrimination of things by cognition; by it, all sciences, all actions, and all the activities of embodied beings are pervaded. For one who examines determines by cognition: 'this exists, this does not exist.' Therefore, the non-existence of all things does not follow. // 29 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.30]
[Page break]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.30: And because of the untenability and tenability of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge).

children.text: evaṃ ca sati sarvaṃ nāstīti nopapadyate, kasmāt? pramāṇānupapattyupapattibhyām/ yadi sarvaṃ nāstīti pramāṇam upapadyate, sarvaṃ nāstīti etad vyāhanyate/ atha pramāṇaṃ nopapadyate, sarvaṃ nāstīty asya kathaṃ siddhiḥ? atha pramāṇam antareṇa siddhiḥ, sarvam astīty asya kathaṃ na siddhiḥ?// 30 //
children.translated_text: Given this, the (thesis) 'everything is non-existent' is untenable. Why? Because of the untenability and tenability of <s>pramāṇa</s>. If a <s>pramāṇa</s> is tenable (for establishing that) 'everything is non-existent,' then (the thesis) 'everything is non-existent' is contradicted (since the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself exists). But if a <s>pramāṇa</s> is untenable, how is 'everything is non-existent' established? And if establishment (is possible) without a <s>pramāṇa</s>, how then is 'everything exists' not (equally) established? // 30 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.31]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.31: This supposition of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> is like the supposition of objects in dreams.

children.text: yathā svapne na viṣayāḥ santy atha cābhimāno bhavati, evaṃ na pramāṇāni prameyāṇi ca santy atha ca pramāṇaprameyābhimāno bhavati// 31 //
children.translated_text: Just as in dreams the objects do not exist and yet the supposition (of their existence) occurs, so too <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) and <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) do not exist and yet the supposition of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> occurs. // 31 //
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.32]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.32: Or like illusion (<s>māyā</s>), a celestial city (<s>gandharvanagara</s>), or a mirage (<s>mṛgatṛṣṇikā</s>).
[Page break]
[Commentary on <s>NyS</s> 4.2.33]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.33: (The nihilist thesis) is not established, because of the absence of a reason.

children.text: svapnānte viṣayābhimānavat pramāṇaprameyābhimāno na punar jāgaritānte viṣayopalabdhivad ity atra hetur nāsti/ hetvabhāvād asiddhiḥ/ svapnānte cāsanto viṣayā upalabhyanta ity atrāpi hetvabhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: Just as there is a belief in objects at the end of a dream, so there is a belief in <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) and <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge) — but not like the apprehension of objects at the end of waking' — for this there is no reason. In the absence of a reason, (the thesis) is unestablished. And as for 'in dream, non-existent objects are apprehended' — here too there is an absence of reason.

children.text:
% p.1078
pratibodhe 'nupalambhād iti cet? pratibodhaviṣayopalambhād apratiṣedhaḥ/ yadi pratibodhe ṇupalambhāt svapne viṣayā na santīti, tarhi ya ime pratibuddhena viṣayā upalabhyanta upalambhāt santīti/ viparyaye hi hetusāmarthyam/ upalambhāt sadbhāve saty anupalambhād abhāvaḥ siddhyati, ubhayathā tv abhāve nānupalambhasya sāmarthyam asti, yathā pradīpasyābhāvād rūpasyādarśanam iti, tatra bhāvenābhāvaḥ samarthyata iti/
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1078] If (the objector says) 'because of non-apprehension upon waking' — (we reply:) there is no refutation, because of the apprehension of objects upon waking. If objects in dream do not exist because of non-apprehension upon waking, then those objects which are apprehended by one who is awake exist because of apprehension. For the force of a reason operates in the contrary case (as well). When existence is established through apprehension, non-existence through non-apprehension is (also) established; but if in both cases there is non-existence, non-apprehension has no force — just as the non-seeing of color due to the absence of a lamp; there, existence is made possible by (the presence of) something positive.

children.text:
% p.1080
svapnāntavikalpe ca hetuvacanam/ svapnaviṣayābhimānavad iti bruvatā svapnāntavikalpe hetur vācyaḥ/ kaścit svapno bhayopasaṃhitaḥ, kaścit pramodopasaṃhitaḥ, kaścid ubhayaviparītaḥ, kadācit svapnam eva na paśyatīti/ nimittavatas tu svapnaviṣayābhimānasya nimittavikalpād vikalpopapattiḥ// 33 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1080] And a reason must be stated for the variation in dream-content. One who says 'like the belief in dream-objects' must state the reason for the variation in dream-content. Some dreams are accompanied by fear, some by joy, some are the opposite of both, and sometimes one does not dream at all. But for the belief in dream-objects, which has a cause, the variation is justified by the variation of the cause. //33//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.34]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.34: And the belief in dream-objects is like memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and imagination (<s>saṅkalpa</s>).

children.text: pūrvopalabdhaviṣayaḥ/ yathā smṛtiś ca saṅkalpaś ca pūrvopalabdhaviṣayau na tasya pratyākhyānāya kalpete tathā svapne viṣayagrahaṇaṃ pūrvopalabdhaviṣayaṃ na tasya pratyākhyānāya kalpata iti/
children.translated_text: (It) has previously apprehended objects (as its content). Just as memory and imagination, which have previously apprehended objects as their content, do not serve to deny that (reality), so too the apprehension of objects in dream, which has previously apprehended objects as its content, does not serve to deny that (reality).

children.text:
% kalpata iti] p.1084
evaṃ dṛṣṭaviṣayaś ca svapnānto jāgaritāntena/ yaḥ suptaḥ svapnaṃ paśyati sa eva jāgrat svapnadarśanāni pratisandhatta idam adrākṣam iti/ tatra jāgradbuddhivṛttivaśāt svapnaviṣayābhimāno mithyeti vyavasāyaḥ/ sati ca pratisandhāne yā jāgrato buddhivṛttis tadvaśād ayaṃ vyavasāyaḥ svapnaviṣayābhimāno mithyeti/
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1084] Thus, the dream-state, like the waking state, has (previously) experienced objects (as its content). The very same person who, while sleeping, sees a dream, upon waking, connects the dream-experiences (with waking): 'I saw this.' There, by virtue of the operation of waking cognition, there is the determination that the belief in dream-objects is false. And when there is such connection, this determination — 'the belief in dream-objects is false' — arises by virtue of the operation of the waking cognition.

children.text:
% p.1085
ubhayāviśeṣe tu sādhanānarthakyam/ yasya svapnāntajāgaritāntayor aviśeṣas tasya svapnaviṣayābhimānavad iti sādhanam anarthakaṃ tadāśrayapratyākhyānāt/
atasmiṃs tad iti ca vyavasāyaḥ pradhānāśrayaḥ/ apuruṣe sthāṇau puruṣa iti vyavasāyaḥ, sa pradhānāśrayaḥ, na khalu puruṣe 'nupalabdhe puruṣa ity apuruṣe vyavasāyo bhavati, evaṃ svapnaviṣayasya vyavasāyo hastinam adrākṣaṃ parvatam adrākṣam iti pradhānāśrayo bhavitum arhati// 34 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1085] But if there is no distinction between the dream-state and the waking-state, then the argument is pointless. For one who (holds that) there is no distinction between the dream-state and the waking-state, the proof 'like the belief in dream-objects' is pointless, because the basis (of that proof) has been rejected. And the determination 'this is that in what is not that' has a real basis (<s>pradhāna</s>). The determination 'this is a person' regarding a post (<s>sthāṇu</s>) that is not a person — that has a real basis; for indeed, the determination 'this is a person' regarding a non-person does not occur without a person having been (previously) apprehended. Likewise, the determination regarding dream-objects — 'I saw an elephant, I saw a mountain' — deserves to have a real basis. //34//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.35]
[Note: p.1087] And this being so —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.35: The destruction of false apprehension comes from the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), like the destruction of the belief in dream-objects upon waking.

children.text:
sthāṇau pruṣo 'yam iti vyavasāyo mithyopalabdhiḥ atasmiṃs tad iti jñānam, sthāṇau sthāṇur iti vyavasāyas tattvajñānam/ tattvajjānena ca mithyopalabdhir nivartyate, nārthaḥ sthāṇupuruṣasāmānyalakṣaṇaḥ/ yathā pratibodhe yā jñānavṛttis tayā svapnaviṣayābhimāno nivartyate nārtho viṣayasāmānyalakṣaṇaḥ, tathā māyāgandharvanagaramṛgatṛṣṇikāṇām api yā buddhayo 'tasmiṃs tad iti vyavasāyās tatrāpy anenaiva kalpena mithyopalabdhivināśas tattvajñānān nārthapratiṣedha iti/
upādānavac ca māyādiṣu mithyājñānam/ prajñāpanīyasarūpaṃ ca dravyam upādāya sādhanavān aparasya mithyādhyavasāyaṃ karoti sā māyā, nīhāraprabhṛtīnāṃ nagarasarūpasanniveśe dūrān nagarabuddhir utpadyate viparyaye tadabhāvāt, sūryamarīciṣu bhaumenoṣmaṇā saṃsṛṣṭeṣu spandamāneṣūdakabuddhir bhavati sāmānyagrahaṇāt, antikasthasya viparyaye tadabhāvāt/
children.translated_text: The determination 'this is a person' regarding a post is false apprehension — it is the cognition 'this is that in what is not that'; the determination 'this is a post' regarding a post is knowledge of reality. False apprehension is removed by the knowledge of reality, not the object characterized by the commonality of post and person. Just as, upon waking, the operation of cognition removes the belief in dream-objects but not the object characterized by the commonality of (dream and waking) objects — so too for the cognitions of illusions (<s>māyā</s>), phantom cities (<s>gandharvanagara</s>), and mirages (<s>mṛgatṛṣṇikā</s>) — which are determinations of 'this is that in what is not that' — by this very principle, the destruction of false apprehension comes from the knowledge of reality, not from the denial of the object. And false cognition in illusions and the like arises from a material basis (<s>upādāna</s>). Illusion (<s>māyā</s>) is when someone, having taken up a substance resembling what is to be made to appear, and being equipped with the means, produces a false determination in another; the cognition of a city arises from a distance when mist and the like have a configuration resembling a city, and in the contrary case (at close distance) it is absent; the cognition of water arises regarding sun-rays that are mixed with terrestrial heat and are shimmering, due to the apprehension of a common feature — and this is absent for one nearby, because in the contrary case it does not occur.

children.text:
% p.1088
kvacit kadācit kasyacic ca bhāvān nānimittaṃ mithyājñānam/ dṛṣṭaṃ ca buddhidvaitaṃ māyāprayoktuḥ parasya ca, dūrānikasthayor gandharvanagaramṛgatṛṣṇikāsu, suputapratibuddhayoś ca svapnaviṣaye/ tad etat sarvasyābhāve nirupākhyatāyāṃ nirātmakatve nopapadyata iti// 35 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1088] Since (false cognition occurs) somewhere, sometime, and for someone — false cognition is not without a cause. And a duality of cognition is observed — for the magician and for the other (spectator), for one far away and one nearby regarding phantom cities and mirages, and for one asleep and one awake regarding dream-objects. All this is not possible if everything is non-existent, indescribable, and without a self. //35//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.36]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.36: And because the cause and the existence of cognition are apprehended in this way.

children.text: mithyābuddheś cārthavad apratiṣedhaḥ/ kasmāt? nimittopalambhāt, sadbhāvopalambhāc ca/ upalabhyate hi mithyābuddhinimittaṃ mithyābuddhiś ca pratyātmam utpannā gṛhyate saṃvedyatvāt, tasmān mithyābuddhir apy astīti// 36 //
children.translated_text: And there is no refutation of false cognition being a real entity. Why? Because its cause is apprehended, and because its existence is apprehended. For the cause of false cognition is apprehended, and false cognition, having arisen in each individual, is grasped — because it is experienced (<s>saṃvedya</s>). Therefore, false cognition too exists. //36//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.36]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.37: And because of the distinction between the real and the predominant (object), the twofold nature of false cognition is justified.

children.text: tattvaṃ sthāṇur iti, pradhānaṃ puruṣa iti/ tattvapradhānayor alopād bhedāt sthāṇau puruṣa iti mithyābuddhir utpadyate sāmānyagrahaṇāt/ evaṃ patākāyāṃ balāketi, loṣṭe kapota iti na tu samāne viṣaye mithyābuddhīnāṃ samāveśaḥ sāmānyagrahaṇavyavasthānāt/ yasya tu nirātmakaṃ nirupākhyaṃ sarvaṃ tasya samāveśaḥ prasajyate/
children.translated_text: The real (<s>tattva</s>) is the post; the predominant (<s>pradhāna</s>) is the person. Because both the real and the predominant are not lost — (that is,) because of the distinction (between them) — the false cognition 'this is a person' regarding a post arises from the apprehension of a common feature. Likewise, 'a crane' regarding a flag, 'a pigeon' regarding a clod — but there is no convergence of false cognitions regarding the same object, because of the fixed determination of the apprehension of common features. But for one who (holds that) everything is without a self and indescribable, the consequence of (such random) convergence would follow.

children.text:
% p.1090
gandhādau ca prameye gandhādibuddayo mithyābhimatās tattvapradhānayoḥ sāmānyagrahaṇasya cābhāvāt tattvabuddhaya eva bhavanti/ tasmād ayuktam etat --- pramāṇaprameyabuddhayo mithyeti// 37 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1090] And regarding objects of knowledge such as smell and the rest, the cognitions of smell and the rest, (even if) considered false, are in fact cognitions of reality — because of the absence of a common feature between the real and the predominant. Therefore, this is unjustified — (the claim) that cognitions of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> are false. //37//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.38]

children.text: doṣanimittānāṃ tattvajñānād ahaṅkāranivṛttir ity uktam/ atha kathaṃ tattvajñānam utpadyata iti?
children.translated_text: It has been said that from the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), the cessation of egoism (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), which is caused by defects (<s>doṣas</s>), occurs. Now, how does the knowledge of reality arise?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.38: Through the practice of a special <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration).

children.text: sa tu pratyāhṛtasyendriyebhyo manaso dhārakeṇa prayatnena dhāryamāṇasyātmanā saṃyogas tattvabubhutsāviśiṣṭaḥ/
children.translated_text: That (samādhi) is the conjunction of the mind — which has been withdrawn from the sense organs and is being held by the self through a sustaining effort — with the self, qualified by the desire to know reality.

children.text:
% saṃyogas tattvabubhutsāviśiṣṭaḥ/] p.1091
sati hi tasminn indriyārtheṣu buddhayo notpadyante, tadabhyāsavaśāt tattvabuddhir utpadyate// 38 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1091] For when that (samādhi) is present, cognitions regarding sense-objects do not arise; through the sustained practice of that, the knowledge of reality arises. //38//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.39]

children.text: yad uktaṃ ``sati hi tasminn indriyārtheṣu buddhayo notpadyanta'' ity etat ---
children.translated_text: As for the statement 'when that is present, cognitions regarding sense-objects do not arise' — (the objection is:)
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.39: (This is) not (possible), because of the overpowering force of particular objects.

children.text: anicchato 'pi buddhyutpatter naitad yuktam/ kasmāt? arthaviśeṣaprābalyāt/ abubhutsamānasyāpi buddhyutpattir dṛṣṭā yathā stanayitnuśabdaprabhṛtiṣu; tatra samādhiviśeṣo nopapadyate// 39 //
children.translated_text: Since cognition arises even for one who does not wish it, this is not justified. Why? Because of the overpowering force of particular objects. The arising of cognition is observed even for one who does not desire it, as in the case of sounds like thunder; in that case, the special <s>samādhi</s> is not possible. //39//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.40]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.40: And because of the instigation (of cognition) by hunger and the like.

children.text:
% p.1092
kṣutpipāsābhyāṃ śītoṣṇābhyāṃ vyādhibhiś cānicchato 'pi buddhayaḥ pravartante tasmād aikāgryānupapattir iti// 40 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1092] Cognitions arise even unwillingly due to hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and diseases; therefore, single-pointed concentration (<s>aikāgrya</s>) is not possible. //40//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.41]

children.text: astv etat samādhiṃ vihāya vyutthānaṃ vyutthānanimittaṃ samādhipratyanīkaṃ ca, sati tv etasmin ---
children.translated_text: Let this be so — (let there be) distraction (<s>vyutthāna</s>) from <s>samādhi</s>, and let there be causes of distraction opposed to <s>samādhi</s>; but given this —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.41: Its (<s>samādhi</s>'s) arising is due to the continuation of the fruit of what was previously done.

children.text:
% p.1093
pūrvakṛto janmāntaropacitas tattvajñānahetur dharmapravivekaḥ phalānubandho *yogābhyāsasāmarthyaṃ (corr.; gogābhyāsa-, ed.), niṣphale hy abhyāse nābhyāsam ādriyeran/ dṛṣṭaṃ hi laukikeṣu karmasv abhyāsasāmarthyam// 41 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1093] The discernment of <s>dharma</s>, which was previously cultivated over other lifetimes and which is the cause of the knowledge of reality — its 'continuation of fruit' is the capacity (arising from) the practice of <s>yoga</s>. For if practice were fruitless, no one would value practice. And the capacity of practice is observed in worldly activities. //41//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.42]
And for the purpose of overcoming obstacles —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.42: The instruction to practice <s>yoga</s> in forests, caves, riverbanks, and such places.

children.text: yogābhyāsajanito dharmo janmāntare 'py anuvartate/ pracayakāṣṭhāgate tattvajñānahetau dharme prakṛṣṭāyāṃ samādhibhāvanāyāṃ tattvajñānam utpadyata iti/ dṛṣṭaś ca samādhinārthaviśeṣaprābalyābhibhavaḥ ``nāham etad aśrauṣaṃ nāham etad ajñāsiṣam anyatra me mano 'bhūd'' ity āha laukika iti// 42 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> generated by the practice of <s>yoga</s> continues even in another birth. When <s>dharma</s>, which is the cause of the knowledge of reality, reaches its culmination, and when the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> is at its highest, the knowledge of reality arises. And it is observed that <s>samādhi</s> overcomes the force of particular objects — an ordinary person says: 'I did not hear that, I did not know that — my mind was elsewhere.' //42//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.43]

children.text:
% p.1094
yady arthaviśeṣaprābalyād anicchato 'pi buddhyutpattir anujñāyate ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1094] If it is conceded that cognition arises even unwillingly due to the overpowering force of particular objects —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.43: The same consequence would apply even in liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).
Even for one who is liberated, cognitions would arise due to the force of external objects. //43//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.44]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.44: Not so, because (in embodied existence) it (the arising of cognition) is inevitable.

children.text: karmavaśān niṣpanne śarīre ceṣṭendriyārthāśraye nimittabhāvād avaśyambhāvī buddhīnām utpādaḥ/ na ca prabalo 'pi san bāhyo ṛtha ātmano buddhyutpāde samartho bhavati tasyendriyeṇa saṃyogād buddhyutpāde sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭam iti// 44 //
children.translated_text: When the body — which serves as the basis for activity, sense organs, and objects — has been produced through the force of <s>karman</s>, the arising of cognitions is inevitable because of the causal conditions being present. However, even a powerful external object is not capable of producing cognition in the self (by itself) — it is observed that its capacity to produce cognition comes from conjunction with a sense organ. //44//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.45]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.45: And in liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), that (body and sense organs) is absent.

children.text: tasya buddhinimittāśrayasya śarīrendriyasya dharmādharmābhāvād abhāvo 'pavarge/ tatra yad uktam ``apavarge 'py evaṃ prasaṅga'' iti, tad ayuktam/ tasmāt sarvaduḥkhavimokṣo 'pavargaḥ/ yasmāt sarvaduḥkhabījaṃ sarvaduḥkhāyatanaṃ cāpavarge vicchidyate tasmāt sarveṇa duḥkhena vimuktir apavargaḥ/ na nirbījaṃ nirāyatanaṃ ca duḥkham utpadyata iti// 45 //
children.translated_text: In liberation, that basis of the cause of cognition — namely the body and sense organs — is absent, due to the absence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. Therefore, the statement 'the same consequence would apply even in liberation' is unjustified. Therefore, liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) is the complete release from all suffering. Since in liberation, the seed of all suffering and the basis of all suffering are severed, liberation is the release from all suffering. For suffering does not arise when it is without a seed and without a basis. //45//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.46]

children.text: NyS_4,2.46: tadarthaṃ yamaniyamābhyām ātmasaṃskāro yogāc cādhyātmavidhyupāyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.46: For the attainment of that (liberation), the refinement of the self (<s>ātmasaṃskāra</s>) is through restraint (<s>yama</s>) and observance (<s>niyama</s>), and through the methods of self-knowledge (<s>adhyātmavidhi</s>) derived from <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: tasyāpavargasyādhigamāya yamaniyamābhyām ātmasaṃskāraḥ/ yamaḥ samānam āśramiṇāṃ dharmasādhanam, niyamas tu viśiṣṭam/ ātmasaṃskāraḥ punar adharmahānaṃ dharmopacayaś ca/ yogaśāstrāc cādhyātmavidhiḥ pratipattavyaḥ/ sa punas tapaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ pratyāhāro dhyānaṃ dhāraṇeti/ indriyaviṣayeṣu prasaṃkhyānābhyāso rāgadveṣaprahāṇārthaḥ/ upāyas tu yogācāravidhānam iti// 46 //
children.translated_text: For the attainment of that liberation, the refinement of the self is through restraint (<s>yama</s>) and observance (<s>niyama</s>). <s>Yama</s> (restraint) is the common <s>dharma</s>-practice for all orders of life (<s>āśramin</s>s); <s>niyama</s> (observance) is the specific one. The refinement of the self (<s>ātmasaṃskāra</s>) is the abandonment of <s>adharma</s> and the accumulation of <s>dharma</s>. And the method of self-knowledge (<s>adhyātmavidhi</s>) is to be understood from the <s>Yogaśāstra</s>. That consists of austerity (<s>tapas</s>), breath-control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), withdrawal of the senses (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>). The practice of discernment (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>) regarding sense-objects is for the purpose of abandoning attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). And the means (<s>upāya</s>) is the method of <s>yoga</s> practice. //46//
[Section: NySBh_4,2.47]

children.text: NyS_4,2.47: jñānagrahaṇābhyāsas tadvidyaiś ca saha saṃvādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.47: The practice of acquiring knowledge, and dialogue with those who possess that knowledge.

children.text: tadartham iti prakṛtam/ jñāyate 'neneti jñānam ātmavidyāśāstraṃ tasya grahaṇam adhyayanadhāraṇe, abhyāsaḥ satatakriyādhyayanaśravaṇacintanāni/ tadvidyaiś ca saha saṃvāda iti prajñāparipākārtham, paripākas tu saṃśayacchedanam avijñātārthabodho 'dhyavasitābhyanujñānam iti/ samayāvādaḥ saṃvādaḥ// 47 //
children.translated_text: "For that purpose" — this is the topic under discussion. <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge) is that by which one knows — the science of self-knowledge (<s>ātmavidyā-śāstra</s>); its apprehension consists in study and retention; <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) consists in continuous activity — study, hearing, and reflection. And conversation (<s>saṃvāda</s>) with those learned in that science is for the purpose of maturing one's insight; maturation means the resolution of doubt, the understanding of what was not previously understood, and the confirmation of what has been ascertained. Harmonious discussion is <s>saṃvāda</s>. // 47 //
[Section: NySBh_4,2.48]

children.text: tadvidyaiś ca saha saṃvāda ity avibhaktārthaṃ vacanaṃ vibhajyate ---
children.translated_text: "And conversation (<s>saṃvāda</s>) with those learned in that science" — this statement, whose meaning is undivided, is now analyzed —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.48: One should engage in it with those who seek the highest good, being distinguished as students, teachers, and fellow-students, and who are free from envy.
This is understood simply by its literal statement. // 48 //
[Section: NySBh_4,2.49]

children.text:
% p.1098
yadi ca manyeta pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahaḥ pratikūlaḥ parasyeti ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1098] And if one thinks that the opponent's adoption of thesis and counter-thesis is hostile —

children.text: NyS_4,2.49: pratipakṣahīnam api vā prayojanārhtam arthitve ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.49: Or one may engage even with one lacking a counter-thesis, for a purpose, when there is a desire for that purpose.

children.text: tam abhyupeyād iti vartate/ parataḥ prajñām upāditsamānas tattvabubhutsāprakāśanena svapakṣam anavasthāpayan svadarśanaṃ pariśodhayed iti/ anyonyapratyanīkāni ca prāvādukānāṃ darśanāni// 49 //
children.translated_text: "One should engage" — this carries over from the previous sūtra. Desiring to acquire wisdom from the other, by manifesting a desire for truth without firmly establishing one's own thesis, one should refine one's own view. And the views of debaters are mutually opposed to one another. // 49 //
[Section: NySBh_4,2.50]

children.text:
% p.1099
svapakṣarāgeṇa caike nyāyam ativartante, tatra ---
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1099] And some, through attachment to their own thesis, transgress proper reasoning; in that regard —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.50: <s>Jalpa</s> (disputation) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) serve to protect the ascertainment of truth, just as a covering of thorny branches serves to protect the seed and its sprout.

children.text: anutpannatattvajñānānām aprahīṇadoṣāṇāṃ tadarthaṃ ghaṭamānānām etad iti// 50 //
children.translated_text: This is for those whose knowledge of truth has not yet arisen, whose faults have not yet been abandoned, and who are striving for that purpose. // 50 //
[Section: NySBh_4,2.51]
And when one is being treated with contempt by an opponent through displays of learning and the like —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.2.51: Through these two, one engages in contentious debate.

children.text:
% p.1100
vigṛhyeti vijigīṣayā, na tattvabubhutsayeti/ tad etad vidyāpālārthaṃ na lābhapūjākhyātyartham iti// 51 //
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1100] "Contentiously" means with a desire to win, not with a desire for truth. Thus, this is for the protection of knowledge, not for the sake of gain, honor, or fame. // 51 //
Thus ends the fourth book in the venerable <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. // 4 //

children.text:
% p.1101 (corr.; 1200, ed.)
nyāyadarśanam
atha pañcamādhyāyasyādyam āhnikam
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1101 (corr.; 1200, ed.)] <s>Nyāyadarśana</s>. Now begins the first chapter of the fifth book.
[Section: NySBh_5,1.1]

children.text: sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya ``vikalpāj jātibahutvam'' iti saṅkṣepeṇaoktam, tad vistareṇa vibhajyate --- tāḥ khalv imā jātayaḥ sthāpanāhetau prayukte caturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣedhahetavaḥ/
children.translated_text: The objection through <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) and <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity) was stated in summary as "the multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) arises from alternatives." This is now analyzed in detail — these <s>jātis</s> are twenty-four kinds of counter-reasons employed when a probative reason is advanced:

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.1: <s>Sādharmya</s> (similarity), <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity), <s>utkarṣa</s> (excess), <s>apakarṣa</s> (deficiency), <s>varṇya</s> (the commendable), <s>avarṇya</s> (the non-commendable), <s>vikalpa</s> (alternative), <s>sādhya</s> (the to-be-proved), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>aprāpti</s> (non-attainment), <s>prasaṅga</s> (implication), <s>pratidṛṣṭānta</s> (counter-example), <s>anutpatti</s> (non-origination), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (topic), <s>ahetu</s> (non-reason), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>aviśeṣa</s> (non-distinction), <s>upapatti</s> (cogency), <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension), <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), <s>anitya</s> (impermanence), <s>nitya</s> (permanence), and <s>kāryasama</s> (equivalence to the effect).

children.text:
% p.1102
sādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanāhetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ/ aviśeṣaṃ tatra tatrodāhariṣyāmaḥ/ evaṃ vaidharmyasamaprabhṛtayo 'pi nirvaktavyāḥ//1//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1102] An objection through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) that, being indistinguishable from the probative reason, constitutes a <s>sādharmyasama</s> (futile rejoinder based on similarity). We shall illustrate the lack of distinction in each case. In the same way, <s>vaidharmyasama</s> (futile rejoinder based on dissimilarity) and the rest are also to be explained. // 1 //
[Section: NySBh_5,1.2]
[Note: p.1105] Now the definition —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.2: When there is a positive or negative correlation, since both the property and its opposite are equally possible, these constitute <s>sādharmyasama</s> and <s>vaidharmyasama</s>.

children.text: sādharmyeṇopasaṃhāre sādhyadharmaviparyayopapatteḥ sādharmyeṇaiva pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanāhetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ/ nidarśanam kriyāvān ātmā, dravyasya kriyāhetuguṇayogāt/ dravyaṃ loṣṭaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayuktaḥ kriyāvān, tathā cātmā, tasmāt kriyāvān iti/ evam upasaṃhṛte paraḥ sādharmyeṇaiva pratyavatiṣṭhate niṣkriya ātmā vibhuno dravyasya niṣkriyatvād, vibhu cākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ ca, tathā cātmā, tasmān niṣkriya iti/
children.translated_text: When there is positive correlation through similarity, since the opposite of the property to be proved is equally possible, the objection through similarity alone — being indistinguishable from the probative reason — is the <s>sādharmyasama</s> (futile rejoinder based on similarity) as a counter-reason. An illustration: the <s>ātman</s> (self) possesses action, because a substance possesses qualities that are causes of action. The substance <s>loṣṭa</s> (clod of earth) is seen to possess qualities that are causes of action and to possess action; so too is the <s>ātman</s>; therefore it possesses action. When this positive correlation is made, the opponent objects through similarity alone: the <s>ātman</s> is devoid of action, because a pervasive substance is devoid of action; <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is pervasive and devoid of action; so too is the <s>ātman</s>; therefore it is devoid of action.

children.text:
% -n niṣkriya iti/] p.1106
na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyam, na punar akriyasādharmyād niṣkriyeṇeti/ viśeṣahetvabhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedho bhavati/
atha vaidharmyasamaḥ --- kriyāhetuguṇayukto loṣṭaḥ paricchinno dṛṣṭo na ca tathātmā, tasmān na loṣṭavat kriyāvān iti/ na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na punaḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyād akriyeṇeti, viśeṣahetvabhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ/
vaidharmyeṇa copasaṃhāraḥ --- niṣkriya ātmā vibhutvāt, kriyāvad dravyam avibhu dṛṣṭaṃ yathā loṣṭaḥ, na ca tathātmā, tasmān niṣkriya iti/ vaidharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam --- niṣkriyaṃ dravyam ākāśaṃ kriyāhetuguṇarahitaṃ dṛṣṭam, na ca tathātmā, tasmān na niṣkriya iti/ na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyān niṣkriyeṇa bhavitavyaṃ na punar akriyavaidharmyāt kriyāvateti viśeṣahetvabhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ/
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1106] And there is no distinguishing reason to establish that because of similarity with what possesses action, it must possess action, rather than being devoid of action because of similarity with what lacks action. Due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, it constitutes the <s>sādharmyasama</s> futile rejoinder. Now the <s>vaidharmyasama</s> — the <s>loṣṭa</s> (clod), which possesses qualities that are causes of action, is seen to be limited in size, but the <s>ātman</s> is not like that; therefore it does not possess action like a <s>loṣṭa</s>. And there is no distinguishing reason to establish that because of similarity with what possesses action, it must possess action, rather than being devoid of action because of dissimilarity with what possesses action; due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is <s>vaidharmyasama</s>. And the negative correlation through dissimilarity: the <s>ātman</s> is devoid of action because of its pervasiveness; a substance possessing action is seen to be non-pervasive, like a <s>loṣṭa</s>; the <s>ātman</s> is not like that; therefore it is devoid of action. The objection through dissimilarity: <s>ākāśa</s> (space), a substance devoid of action, is seen to lack qualities that are causes of action; the <s>ātman</s> is not like that; therefore it is not devoid of action. And there is no distinguishing reason to establish that because of dissimilarity with what possesses action, it must be devoid of action, rather than possessing action because of dissimilarity with what lacks action; due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is <s>vaidharmyasama</s>.

children.text:
% p.1107
atha sādharmyasamaḥ --- kriyāvān loṣṭaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayukto dṛṣṭaḥ, tathā cātmā, tasmāt kriyāvān iti/ na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyān niṣkriyo na punaḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvān iti viśeṣahetvabhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1107] Now the <s>sādharmyasama</s> — the <s>loṣṭa</s> (clod) is seen to possess action and to possess qualities that are causes of action; so too the <s>ātman</s>; therefore it possesses action. And there is no distinguishing reason to establish that because of dissimilarity with what possesses action, it is devoid of action, rather than possessing action because of similarity with what possesses action; due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is <s>sādharmyasama</s>. //
[Section: NySBh_5,1.3]
The reply to these two is —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.3: Its establishment is like the establishment of a cow from cowness (<s>gotva</s>).

children.text: sādharmyamātreṇa vaidharmyamātreṇa ca sādhyasādhane pratijñāyamāne syād avyavasthā,
children.translated_text: If the proving and disproving of what is to be established were claimed on the basis of mere similarity or mere dissimilarity alone, there would be indeterminacy.

children.text:
% p.1108
sā tu dharmaviśeṣe nopapadyate, gosādharmyād gotvāj jātiviśeṣād gauḥ sidhyati, na tu sāsnādisambandhāt/ aśvādivaidharmyād gotvād eva gauḥ sidhyati, na guṇādibhedāt/ tac caitat kṛtavyākhyānam avayavaprakaraṇe/ pramāṇānām abhisambandhāc caikārthakāritvaṃ samānaṃ vākya iti/ hetvābhāsāśrayā khalv iyam avyavastheti//
children.translated_text: [Note: p.1108] But that indeterminacy does not arise with respect to a specific property. A cow is established from similarity with cows through <s>gotva</s> (cowness) — the specific universal — not through the connection with dewlap and other features. Through dissimilarity with horses and the like, a cow is established through <s>gotva</s> alone, not through difference in qualities and the like. And this has already been explained in the section on the members of a syllogism. Since the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) are connected and work toward a single purpose, they form a unified statement. This indeterminacy indeed rests on pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>). //
[Section: NySBh_5,1.4]

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.4: Due to the alternation of properties between the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), and because both become what is to be proved, these constitute <s>utkarṣasama</s> (excess-equivalence), <s>apakarṣasama</s> (deficiency-equivalence), <s>varṇyasama</s> (commendable-equivalence), <s>avarṇyasama</s> (non-commendable-equivalence), <s>vikalpasama</s> (alternative-equivalence), and <s>sādhyasama</s> (probandum-equivalence).

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntadharmaṃ sādhye samāsañjayata utkarṣasamaḥ/ yadi kriyāhetuguṇayogāl loṣṭavat kriyāvān ātmā, loṣṭavad eva sparśavān api prāpnoti/ atha na sparśavān, loṣṭavat kriyāvān api na prāpnoti, viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti/
sādhye dharmābhāvaṃ dṛṣṭāntāt prasañjayato 'pakarṣasamaḥ/ loṣṭaḥ khalu kriyāvān avibhur dṛṣṭaḥ,
children.translated_text: The <s>utkarṣasama</s> consists in superimposing a property of the example onto the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum).
